title: The Lotus Sutra
summary: The Buddha says the different paths he taught before were skillful means fitted to each listener; in the end there is only one path, and everyone can become a buddha.
compare: 前半部（第 1–14 章）最要紧的是两个词：upāya-kauśalya 和 yāna。upāya-kauśalya 字面是「在方法上的巧妙」，英文写 skillful means，白话写「善巧方便」；鸠摩罗什只用「方便」两个字，现代中文里「方便」已经是「省事、顺手」的意思，读者很容易把佛陀的苦心看成「图省事」。yāna 是「车、乘具」，英文 vehicle、中文「乘」都保留了「载人走路的东西」这个画面，所以火宅譬喻里的三辆车能直接对上三乘，三种语言在这里难得一致。但怎么配对有出入：梵文是鹿车配声闻乘、羊车配独觉乘、牛车配菩萨乘；鸠摩罗什把前两辆对调成「羊车—声闻、鹿车—辟支佛」，第三乘又写成「佛乘」，汉传的说法都从他来。英文照梵文走。经名也一样：梵文 Saddharmapuṇḍarīka 是「正法的白莲花」，英文照字面写 Lotus of the True Dharma，鸠摩罗什译成「妙法莲华」，「正」变成了「妙」，白色也没有了。

第二个差别在鸠摩罗什本和梵本的出入。最出名的是第 3 章：梵本说佛知道诸法「是什么、怎样、像什么、有什么特征、有什么本性」五项，鸠摩罗什写成「如是相、如是性……如是本末究竟等」十项，后来成了天台宗「十如是」的根据；英文和白话照梵文只有五项。第 12 章梵本把提婆达多和龙女的故事放在宝塔品里，鸠摩罗什通行本另立一品；梵本每章结尾的品次（「第十一品」等）也因此和本站的章号对不上。各处授记（vyākaraṇa，英文 prediction，中文「授记」）里的佛名、劫名、数目，鸠摩罗什常常改写或取整，逐段对照注里都标了出来。

后半部最难对上的是华人最熟的那一品：观世音菩萨普门品。现存梵文是 avalokiteśvara，字面是「俯视（世间）的主」，玄奘照这个形式译「观自在」；鸠摩罗什的「观世音」对应的是更早的写法 avalokitasvara（svara 是「声音」），他还在第一段加了梵文没有的「一心称名，观世音菩萨即时观其音声」，从此中文读者都把名字理解成「听见世间的呼声」。英文照现存梵文写 Avalokiteshvara，白话沿用「观世音」，所以这一品的三语对照几乎每段都在讲「梵文本在这里怎么说、鸠摩罗什又怎么说」：梵文列出十六种化身，罗什本是后来常说的「三十三身」；罗什最初的译本没有偈颂，通行本的偈颂是后人补译编入的；梵文偈颂里的「好眼、慈眼」，到罗什笔下成了「真观、清净观」；梵文末尾还多出七首讲阿弥陀佛和极乐世界的偈颂，汉译完全没有。

第二个现象是数字和章次。如来寿量品是全经的转折：佛说自己其实在极久远以前就已成佛，涅槃只是方便。汉传有名的「五百尘点劫」在梵文里是「五十」；罗什「如来秘密神通之力」的「秘密」是他加的；偈颂里有一句梵文说「我从不对他们说起」，罗什却译成「或时为此众，说佛寿无量」，意思正好相反。章次也不一样：梵本把提婆达多并在见宝塔品里，所以每一品的编号比本站少一（本站把开经算作一章，两者抵消），陀罗尼品、嘱累品的位置也和罗什本不同。英文各章结尾的「第几品完」照梵文的编号写，章名用本站的章号，差别在各章最后一段的对照注里说明。
compareEn: In the first half (chapters 1–14) two words matter most: upāya-kauśalya and yāna. Upāya-kauśalya literally means "skill in method"; the English says "skillful means" and the plain Chinese says 善巧方便 (shànqiǎo fāngbiàn, "skillful expedient"). Kumarajiva uses just 方便 (fāngbiàn), which in modern Chinese has come to mean "convenient, handy," so a Chinese reader can easily mistake the Buddha's careful teaching for taking the easy way. Yāna means "cart, vehicle"; the English "vehicle" and the Chinese 乘 (shèng, "a carriage") both keep the picture of something that carries people along a road, so in the parable of the burning house the three carts map straight onto the three vehicles, and for once all three languages agree. The pairing itself differs, though: in the Sanskrit the deer cart goes with the disciple vehicle, the goat cart with the solitary-buddha vehicle and the ox cart with the bodhisattva vehicle; Kumarajiva swaps the first two, 羊车 (yángchē, "goat cart") for the disciples and 鹿车 (lùchē, "deer cart") for the solitary buddhas, and calls the third 佛乘 (fóshèng, "buddha vehicle"). The usual East Asian telling comes from him; the English follows the Sanskrit. The title is another case: the Sanskrit Saddharmapuṇḍarīka is "the white lotus of the true Dharma," which the English follows as "Lotus of the True Dharma"; Kumarajiva's 妙法莲华 (miàofǎ liánhuá, "lotus flower of the wonderful Dharma") turns "true" into "wonderful" and loses the white.

The second difference lies between Kumarajiva's version and the Sanskrit. The best known case is in chapter 3: the Sanskrit says the Buddha knows five things about all dharmas (what they are, how they are, what they are like, what marks they have, what their nature is), while Kumarajiva lists ten, 如是相、如是性……如是本末究竟等 (rúshì xiàng, rúshì xìng... rúshì běnmò jiūjìng děng, "such marks, such nature... such consistency from beginning to end"), which later became the basis of the Tiantai school's teaching of the "ten suchnesses"; the English and plain Chinese keep the Sanskrit's five. In chapter 12 the Sanskrit tells the story of Devadatta and the naga king's daughter inside the chapter on the stupa, while Kumarajiva's common version gives it a chapter of its own, so the chapter numbers at the end of each Sanskrit chapter ("the eleventh chapter" and so on) do not match the site's numbering. In the many predictions of future buddhahood (vyākaraṇa, English "prediction," Chinese 授记 (shòujì, "conferring a record")), Kumarajiva often rewrites or rounds off the names of buddhas and eons and the numbers; the notes on each passage point these out.

The hardest match in the second half is the chapter Chinese readers know best, the chapter on Avalokiteshvara, “the Gateway Facing Every Direction.” The surviving Sanskrit name is avalokiteśvara, literally “the lord who looks down (on the world),” which Xuanzang follows with 观自在 (Guānzìzài, “the one who observes with mastery”). Kumarajiva’s 观世音 (Guānshìyīn, “the one who observes the world’s sounds”) matches an older spelling, avalokitasvara (svara means “sound”), and in the first verse he adds a line the Sanskrit doesn’t have, 一心称名，观世音菩萨即时观其音声 (“call his name with a single mind, and the bodhisattva at once observes the sound of their voices”). Ever since, Chinese readers have understood the name as “the one who hears the world’s cries.” The English follows the surviving Sanskrit with Avalokiteshvara and the plain Chinese keeps 观世音, so the notes in this chapter keep returning to “what the Sanskrit says here, and what Kumarajiva says”: the Sanskrit lists sixteen forms the bodhisattva takes, Kumarajiva the later famous thirty-three; Kumarajiva’s first translation had no verses at all, and the verses in the common edition were translated and added later; the Sanskrit verses’ “lovely eyes, kind eyes” become “true seeing, pure seeing” in Chinese; and the Sanskrit ends with seven extra verses about the Buddha Amitabha and his Land of Bliss that no Chinese version contains.

The second thing to watch is numbers and chapter order. The chapter on how long the Tathagata lives is the turning point of the whole sutra: the Buddha reveals that he actually became a buddha an immensely long time ago, and that his passing into nirvana is a skillful means. The “five hundred” in the famous Chinese image of eons as many as specks of dust is “fifty” in the Sanskrit; the word 秘密 (mìmì, “secret”) in Kumarajiva’s 如来秘密神通之力 (“the Tathagata’s secret supernatural power”) is his own addition; and where a Sanskrit verse says “I never tell them of this,” Kumarajiva writes 或时为此众，说佛寿无量 (“at times I tell this assembly that the Buddha’s life is immeasurable”), the exact opposite. The chapter numbers differ too: the Sanskrit folds the Devadatta chapter into the stupa chapter, so each of its chapter numbers is one lower than the site’s (the site counts the opening section as a chapter, and the two cancel out for Kumarajiva’s numbering), and the dharani and entrusting chapters sit in different places than in Kumarajiva’s version. The closing line of each English chapter keeps the Sanskrit number, while the chapter title uses the site’s number; the note on each closing line explains the difference.

verses.en: The Lotus of the True Dharma Sutra.

cmp.note: 梵文是「正法（sad-dharma）的白莲（puṇḍarīka）」。英文 Lotus of the True Dharma 照字面；鸠摩罗什译「妙法莲华」，把 sat（真、正、好）译成「妙」，强调的是「奇妙」而不是「真正」；他也没有译出「白」色。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit is "the white lotus (puṇḍarīka) of the true Dharma (sad-dharma)." The English "Lotus of the True Dharma" is literal. Kumarajiva's title 妙法莲华 (Miàofǎ Liánhuá, "lotus flower of the wondrous Dharma") renders sat ("true, real, good") as 妙 (miào, "wondrous"), stressing marvel rather than truth, and leaves out that the lotus is white.

verses.en: Homage to all buddhas and bodhisattvas! Homage to all the Tathagatas, the solitary buddhas (pratyekabuddhas), and the noble disciples of the past, the future, and the present, and to all the bodhisattvas!

This is what I heard. At one time the Blessed One was staying at Rajagriha (the capital of Magadha), on the mountain called Vulture Peak, together with a great community of monks, twelve hundred monks. All of them were arhats (saints who have ended rebirth): their outflows (the defilements that leak out of the mind) were used up, they were free of afflictions, they had mastered themselves, their minds were thoroughly freed, their wisdom was thoroughly freed. They were like thoroughbred horses, like great elephants. They had done what had to be done, finished the work to be finished, put down the burden, and reached their own goal. The fetters that tie one to existence were worn away; by right understanding their minds were thoroughly freed; they had reached the highest perfection in every kind of mastery of the mind; they were well known among the well known. They were great disciples (shravakas).

cmp.note: 梵文把阿罗汉比作「良种马、大象」，ājāneya 是血统好的骏马，mahānāga 可以是大象也可以是大龙。英文 thoroughbred horses, great elephants、白话都保留了这两个比喻；鸠摩罗什译本把整串形容压成「诸漏已尽……心得自在」，比喻全部省掉。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit compares the arhats to "thoroughbreds and great nāgas": ājāneya is a horse of good breeding, and mahānāga can mean a great elephant or a great dragon. The English "thoroughbred horses, great elephants" and the plain Chinese keep both images; Kumarajiva compresses the whole string into 诸漏已尽……心得自在 (zhū lòu yǐ jìn … xīn dé zìzài, "all outflows ended … minds at ease") and drops the comparisons.

cmp.note: 梵文是「一千二百位比丘」；鸠摩罗什译作「万二千人」，人数大了十倍。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says "twelve hundred monks"; Kumarajiva writes 万二千人 (wàn èr qiān rén, "twelve thousand people"), ten times as many.

verses.en: Namely: the venerable Ajnata Kaundinya (the first of the Buddha's five original disciples), the venerable Ashvajit, the venerable Bashpa, the venerable Mahanaman, the venerable Bhadrika, the venerable Mahakashyapa, the venerable Urubilva Kashyapa, the venerable Nadi Kashyapa, the venerable Gaya Kashyapa, the venerable Shariputra, the venerable Mahamaudgalyayana, the venerable Mahakatyayana, the venerable Aniruddha, the venerable Revata, the venerable Kapphina, the venerable Gavampati, the venerable Pilindavatsa, the venerable Bakkula, the venerable Mahakaushthila, the venerable Bharadvaja, the venerable Mahananda, the venerable Upananda, the venerable Sundarananda, the venerable Purna Maitrayaniputra, the venerable Subhuti, and the venerable Rahula (the Buddha's son).

cmp.note: 字面是「有寿命的、长寿的」，是对比丘的尊称。英文 venerable 是「可敬的」，白话「具寿」是旧译；鸠摩罗什干脆不译这个尊称，只列名字。
cmp.en: Literally "possessing long life," a respectful way of addressing a monk. The English "venerable" means "worthy of respect"; the plain Chinese keeps the old rendering 具寿 (jùshòu, "endowed with life"); Kumarajiva leaves the title out and just lists names.

verses.en: With these and other great disciples, and with the venerable Ananda, who was still in training; with two thousand other monks, some still in training and some beyond training; and with six thousand nuns led by Mahaprajapati (the Buddha's aunt and foster mother).

cmp.note: 「还要学的」和「不用再学的」，指尚未和已经成为阿罗汉的人。英文 still in training / beyond training 照字面；鸠摩罗什译「学、无学」，是同一个意思的旧说法。
cmp.en: "One who still has to train" and "one who no longer needs to," meaning those not yet and already arhats. The English "still in training / beyond training" is literal; Kumarajiva's 学、无学 (xué, wúxué, "learning, beyond learning") is the older Chinese way of saying the same thing.

verses.en: And with the nun Yashodhara, Rahula's mother, with her following. And with eighty thousand bodhisattvas, all of them unable to turn back from unsurpassed, perfect awakening, bound to it by just one more birth. They had gained the dharanis (powers of memory that hold the teaching); they stood firm in great eloquence; they turned the wheel of the Dharma that never turns back; they had served many hundreds of buddhas, planted roots of goodness under many hundreds of thousands of buddhas, and been praised by hundreds of thousands of buddhas. Their bodies and minds were steeped in kindness. They were skilled at leading others into the Tathagata's knowledge, great in wisdom, gone all the way to the perfection of wisdom. They were famous in many hundreds of thousands of world systems, and they had carried across many hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas of living beings (koti and nayuta are both huge numbers).

cmp.note: 「只被一生系缚」，即再过一生就成佛。白话「只差这一生」意思对；鸠摩罗什本没有译这一句，只说「不退转」。
cmp.en: "Bound by only one birth," that is, one more life and they will be buddhas. The plain Chinese 只差这一生 ("just this one life to go") has it; Kumarajiva does not translate the phrase and only says 不退转 (bù tuìzhuǎn, "not turning back").

verses.en: Namely: Manjushri the Prince, the bodhisattva, the great being; Avalokiteshvara, Mahasthamaprapta, Sarvarthanaman, Nityodyukta, Anikshiptadhura, Ratnapani, Bhaishajyaraja, Bhaishajyasamudgata, Vyuharaja, Pradanashura, Ratnachandra, Ratnaprabha, Purnachandra, Mahavikramin, Anantavikramin, Trailokyavikramin, Mahapratibhana, Satatasamitabhiyukta, Dharanidhara, Akshayamati, Padmashri, Nakshatraraja, Maitreya the bodhisattva, the great being, and Simha the bodhisattva, the great being; together with sixteen good men led by Bhadrapala.

cmp.note: 字面是「成了童子的」，常用来称文殊，意思近于「王子、法王之子」。英文 the Prince、白话「童子」各取一面；鸠摩罗什在别处译「法王子」。
cmp.en: Literally "one who has become a youth," a standing epithet of Manjushri, close to "crown prince (of the Dharma)." The English "the Prince" and the plain Chinese 童子 (tóngzǐ, "youth") each catch one side; elsewhere Kumarajiva renders it 法王子 (fǎ wángzǐ, "prince of the Dharma King").

verses.en: Namely: Bhadrapala, Ratnakara, Susarthavaha, Naradatta, Guhyagupta, Varunadatta, Indradatta, Uttaramati, Visheshamati, Vardhamanamati, Amoghadarshin, Susamprasthita, Suvikrantavikramin, Anupamamati, Suryagarbha, and Dharanimdhara. With these at their head there were eighty thousand bodhisattvas. There was also Shakra, lord of the gods (Indra), with a following of twenty thousand young gods, namely the young god Chandra (the moon), the young god Surya (the sun), the young god Samantagandha, the young god Ratnaprabha, and the young god Avabhasaprabha; with these at their head, twenty thousand young gods. And there were the Four Great Kings (guardians of the four directions), with a following of thirty thousand young gods.

Namely: the great king Virudhaka, the great king Virupaksha, the great king Dhritarashtra, and the great king Vaishravana. There were the young god Ishvara and the young god Maheshvara, each with a following of thirty thousand young gods. There was Brahma Sahampati (lord of this world) with a following of twelve thousand young gods of Brahma's retinue, namely Brahma Shikhin and Brahma Jyotishprabha; with these at their head, twelve thousand gods of Brahma's retinue. And there were eight naga kings (serpent kings of the waters) with a following of many hundreds of thousands of kotis of nagas, namely the naga king Nanda, the naga king Upananda, Sagara, Vasuki, Takshaka, Manasvin, Anavatapta, and the naga king Utpalaka.

cmp.note: 梵天的称号，意思难定，通常理解为「娑婆世界之主」。英文 lord of this world、白话「娑婆世界之主」都取这个传统说法。
cmp.en: An epithet of Brahma whose meaning is uncertain; it is traditionally taken as "lord of the Saha world." The English "lord of this world" and the plain Chinese 娑婆世界之主 (Suōpó shìjiè zhī zhǔ, "lord of the Saha world") both follow that tradition.

verses.en: There were four kinnara kings (celestial singers), each with a following of many hundreds of thousands of kotis of kinnaras, namely the kinnara king Druma, the kinnara king Mahadharma, the kinnara king Sudharma, and the kinnara king Dharmadhara. There were four young gods of the gandharva host (celestial musicians), with a following of many hundreds of thousands of gandharvas, namely the gandharva Manojna, Manojnasvara, Madhura, and the gandharva Madhurasvara. There were four asura lords (titans who war with the gods), with a following of many hundreds of thousands of kotis of asuras, namely the asura lord Bali, the asura lord Kharaskandha, the asura lord Vemachitrin, and the asura lord Rahu. And there were four garuda lords (giant birds), with a following of many hundreds of thousands of kotis of garudas.
Namely: the garuda lord Mahatejas, Mahakaya, Mahapurna, and the garuda lord Maharddhiprapta. And King Ajatashatru of Magadha, son of Queen Vaidehi, was there too.

At that time the Blessed One, surrounded by the fourfold assembly (monks, nuns, laymen, laywomen), honored, respected, revered, esteemed, worshipped, and venerated by them, had just taught a Dharma discourse, a sutra called The Great Teaching, a very extensive one, an instruction for bodhisattvas, held dear by all buddhas. Then, on that same great Dharma seat, he crossed his legs and entered the samadhi (deep meditative concentration) called The Ground of Endless Teaching, his body unmoving and his mind come to stillness. The moment the Blessed One entered it, a great rain of heavenly flowers poured down, mandarava and great mandarava, manjushaka and great manjushaka, scattering over the Blessed One and the four assemblies.

cmp.note: 梵文这部先讲的经叫「大教示」；鸠摩罗什译作《无量义》，后来汉地把它当成一部独立的《无量义经》，梵本只给了名字。
cmp.en: In the Sanskrit, the sutra taught just before is called "The Great Teaching." Kumarajiva calls it 无量义 (Wúliàngyì, "Immeasurable Meanings"), and later Chinese Buddhism treated it as a separate scripture, the Sutra of Immeasurable Meanings; the Sanskrit gives only the name.

verses.en: And the whole buddha-field shook in six ways: it moved and moved all over, it swayed and swayed all over, it heaved and heaved all over. At that time, gathered and seated in that assembly were monks, nuns, laymen and laywomen; gods, nagas, yakshas (nature spirits), gandharvas, asuras, garudas, kinnaras, mahoragas (great serpent spirits), humans and non-humans; regional kings, wheel-turning kings who rule by force of arms, and wheel-turning kings of the four continents. All of them, with their followings, gazed at the Blessed One, struck with wonder, amazement, and joy.

cmp.note: 「佛的田地」，一位佛教化的整个世界。英文 buddha-field 照字面；白话「佛土」、鸠摩罗什「佛世界」都把「田」的意象换成了「国土」。
cmp.en: "A buddha's field," the whole world a buddha teaches in. The English "buddha-field" is literal; the plain Chinese 佛土 (fó tǔ, "buddha-land") and Kumarajiva's 佛世界 (fó shìjiè, "buddha-world") replace the image of a field with that of a country.

verses.en: Then, at that moment, a single ray of light came out of the tuft of white hair between the Blessed One's eyebrows. It spread through eighteen thousand buddha-fields in the east, and all those buddha-fields were seen lit up clearly by its light, down as far as Avichi, the great hell (the lowest hell), and up as far as the peak of existence (the top of the world). All the beings in those buddha-fields, in the six realms of rebirth, were seen without exception. The buddhas, the blessed ones, who were living, staying, and carrying on in those buddha-fields were all seen too, and the Dharma those buddhas were teaching was heard in full. The monks, nuns, laymen and laywomen in those buddha-fields, the yogis and practitioners of yoga, those who had reached the fruit and those who had not, were all seen as well.

cmp.note: 「存在的顶端」，指轮回世界最高的一层天。英文 peak of existence、白话「有顶天」照字面；鸠摩罗什写成「阿迦尼咤天」，换成了色界最高天的名字。
cmp.en: "The summit of existence," the highest heaven within the cycle of rebirth. The English "peak of existence" and the plain Chinese 有顶天 (yǒudǐng tiān, "heaven at the top of existence") are literal; Kumarajiva writes 阿迦尼咤天 (Ājiānízhà tiān), naming instead the Akanishtha heaven, the top of the form realm.

verses.en: The bodhisattvas, the great beings, in those buddha-fields who were following the bodhisattva path by skillful means, through many different kinds of hearing, objects of attention, inclinations, causes, and reasons, were all seen too. The buddhas, the blessed ones, in those buddha-fields who had passed into final nirvana were all seen too. And the jeweled stupas holding the relics of those buddhas who had passed into final nirvana were all seen as well.

Then this occurred to Maitreya, the bodhisattva, the great being: "Oh, what a great sign, what a wonder the Tathagata has worked! What could be the cause, what the reason, that the Blessed One has worked a great sign, a wonder like this? The Blessed One has entered samadhi, and yet these great marvels of supernatural power, so astonishing and beyond thought, are being seen. Whom should I ask about this? Who would be able to explain it?" Then this occurred to him: "Here is Manjushri the Prince, who did his service under past Victors, who planted roots of goodness and served many buddhas.

"Manjushri the Prince must have seen signs like these before, under the Tathagatas of the past, the arhats, the fully awakened buddhas, and must have taken part in great conversations on the Dharma. Why don't I ask Manjushri the Prince about this?"

And the four assemblies, the monks, nuns, laymen and laywomen, and the many gods, nagas, yakshas, gandharvas, asuras, garudas, kinnaras, mahoragas, humans and non-humans, seeing this great sign of the Blessed One, this glow of wonders, were struck with astonishment, amazement, and curiosity, and they thought: "Whom should we ask about this glow of great supernatural wonder that the Blessed One has shown?"

Then Maitreya, the bodhisattva, the great being, in that very instant knew with his own mind the thoughts in the minds of the four assemblies, and he himself had doubts about the Dharma. So at that moment he said to Manjushri the Prince: "Manjushri, what is the cause, what is the reason, that the Blessed One has shown this astonishing glow of supernatural power, and that these eighteen thousand buddha-fields appear, so varied, lovely, supremely lovely, each led and guided by its Tathagata?"
Then Maitreya, the bodhisattva, the great being, spoke to Manjushri the Prince in these verses:
Why, Manjushri, has the Leader of Men sent out this ray? This single ray shines out from between his brows, from the tuft of white hair.
The gods, overjoyed, let fall a great rain of mandarava flowers, and manjushaka flowers mixed with sandalwood powder, heavenly, fragrant, and delightful.
With these the earth is beautiful all around, and the four assemblies are filled with joy; and this whole field has shaken in six ways, a fearsome sight.
And that ray, in the eastern direction, has lit up eighteen thousand fields, full, in a single instant; all the fields look as if they were the color of gold.
As far as Avichi and up to the highest peak of existence, all the beings in those fields, living in the six realms of rebirth, those who are dying there and those being born,
their deeds, varied and of many kinds, are seen in their realms, happy and painful, low, high, and in between: standing here, I have seen all of this.
And I see the buddhas, lions among the lords of men, making the Dharma plain and opening it up, instructing many kotis of beings, speaking in sweet voices.
Each in his own field, they send forth a deep, noble, wonderful sound, making this Dharma of the buddhas plain with kotis of nayutas of examples and reasons.
To beings crushed by suffering, worn out in mind by birth and old age, who do not understand, they make known the peace of nirvana: "This, monks, is the end of suffering."
To people who have gained great strength, who are endowed with merit and have seen buddhas, they speak of the vehicle of the solitary buddhas, praising this way of the Dharma.

cmp.note: 「独自觉悟者的乘」。英文 the vehicle of the solitary buddhas、白话「独觉乘」照字面；鸠摩罗什译「缘觉」，强调的是「观因缘而觉悟」，是另一种解释。
cmp.en: "The vehicle of those awakened on their own." The English "vehicle of the solitary buddhas" and the plain Chinese 独觉乘 (dújué shèng, "vehicle of solitary awakening") are literal; Kumarajiva's 缘觉 (yuánjué, "awakened through conditions") stresses awakening by contemplating causes and conditions, a different interpretation.

verses.en: And to other sons of the Sugata (the Well-Gone One, a title of the Buddha), who seek unsurpassed knowledge and keep up all kinds of practice at all times, they speak in praise of awakening.
Manjughosha (Gentle Voice, a name of Manjushri), standing here I hear and see such things there, and thousands of kotis of other marvels; I will describe only a small part of them.

cmp.note: 「声音柔美的人」，是文殊的别名。白话译「妙音」，容易和后面另一位妙音菩萨（Gadgadasvara）混淆；鸠摩罗什直接写「文殊师利」。英文保留 Manjughosha 并加注。
cmp.en: "The one with a gentle voice," another name for Manjushri. The plain Chinese 妙音 (Miàoyīn, "wondrous sound") can be confused with the later bodhisattva of the same Chinese name (Gadgadasvara); Kumarajiva simply writes 文殊师利 (Wénshūshīlì, "Manjushri"). The English keeps "Manjughosha" with a gloss.

verses.en: In many fields, too, I see bodhisattvas as many as the sands of the Ganges, many thousands of kotis of them, bringing about awakening through all kinds of effort.
Some of them give gifts: wealth, gold in the raw, silver, gold coin, pearls, jewels, conch shells, crystal, coral, slaves both men and women, carts, horses, and sheep.
They give litters adorned with jewels, giving with glad hearts, and they dedicate the merit to the highest awakening: "May we gain that vehicle!"

cmp.note: 「转向、回向」：把布施的功德转送给觉悟这个目标。英文 dedicate the merit 是解释；白话「回向」是佛教术语。
cmp.en: "Turning over": transferring the merit of giving toward the goal of awakening. The English "dedicate the merit" explains it; the plain Chinese uses the technical term 回向 (huíxiàng, "turning toward").

verses.en: "The best and finest vehicle in the triple world, the buddha vehicle praised by the Sugatas: may I soon gain it too." So they give gifts like these.
Some give chariots yoked to four horses, with railings, adorned with flowers and banners, with victory flags, made of jewels; some give gifts like these.
Some give their sons and their daughters, some give their own dear flesh; when asked, they give their hands and feet, seeking this highest awakening.
Some give their heads, some their eyes, some give their very best bodies; and having given these gifts with a clear and happy mind, they long for the knowledge of the Tathagatas.
Manjushri, in some places I see people giving up flourishing kingdoms, their women's quarters, all their lands, leaving all their ministers and kin,
going to the Guides of the World and asking them about the finest Dharma, for the sake of peace; and they put on ochre robes and shave off their hair and beards.
And I see some bodhisattvas who have become monks living in the woods, keeping to empty wilderness; and some who delight in reciting and studying the texts.
And I see some steadfast bodhisattvas going into mountain caves, reflecting on this knowledge of the buddhas, pondering it, and seeing it clearly.

Others have given up sense pleasures completely; they have trained themselves, their range is pure, they have touched the five higher knowledges (supernormal powers), and they live in the wilderness, sons of the Sugata.
Some steadfast ones stand here, feet even, palms joined, facing the Guides; full of joy, they praise the Victor, king of lords, in thousands of verses.

cmp.note: 梵文是「双脚并齐站着」赞佛；鸠摩罗什译「安禅合掌」，变成坐禅中合掌，姿势不同。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit has them "standing with feet even" as they praise the Buddha; Kumarajiva writes 安禅合掌 (ān chán hézhǎng, "settled in meditation, palms joined"), turning it into a seated meditation posture.

verses.en: Some, mindful, self-controlled, and fearless, understanding the subtle way of practice, ask the Best of the Two-footed (the Buddha) about the Dharma, and having heard it, they become holders of the Dharma.
And here and there I see some sons of the Victor, well trained in themselves, teaching the Dharma to many kotis of living beings with many nayutas of examples and reasons.
Full of joy, they teach the Dharma, encouraging many bodhisattvas; having struck down Mara (the tempter) with his army and his mounts, they beat this drum of the Dharma.
In the Sugata's teaching I see some sons of the Sugata worshipped by humans, gods, yakshas, and rakshasas (demons), yet they are not puffed up, not proud, and they go about calm and at peace.
Others, of another kind, staying in the depths of the forest, send out light from their bodies, draw beings up out of the hells, and encourage them toward awakening.
Some sons of the Victor stand firm in effort; others have thrown off drowsiness entirely and live in the woods, given to walking meditation; by effort they have set out for the highest awakening.
And here some always guard their moral discipline, pure and unbroken like a precious jewel, and they practice it to the full; by discipline they have set out for the highest awakening.
Some sons of the Victor have patience as their strength: they bear the abuse, slander, and threats of monks full of conceit; by patience they have set out for the highest awakening.

cmp.note: 「陷入过高自负的」，指自以为已经证悟的人。英文 full of conceit、白话「傲慢」都略弱；鸠摩罗什「增上慢」是专门术语，正是「未证言证」的意思。
cmp.en: "Fallen into excessive conceit," meaning people who think they have attained what they have not. The English "full of conceit" and the plain Chinese 傲慢 (àomàn, "arrogant") are a little weak; Kumarajiva's technical term 增上慢 (zēngshàng màn, "overreaching conceit") means exactly "claiming an attainment one lacks."

verses.en: And I see some bodhisattvas who have given up all fun and games, who keep away from foolish companions, who delight in the company of the noble ones, collected in mind,
avoiding a scattered mind, with minds on one point in forest caves, meditating for thousands of kotis of years; by meditation they have set out for the highest awakening.
Some, likewise, give gifts in the very presence of the Victors and their communities of disciples: hard food and soft food, food and drink, and many, many medicines for the sick.
They give hundreds of kotis of robes; some give robes worth hundreds of thousands of kotis, some give robes beyond price, in the very presence of the Victors and their communities of disciples.
They have hundreds of kotis of monasteries built, made of jewels and of sandalwood, furnished with plenty of beds and seats, and they hand them over in the very presence of the Sugatas.
Some give parks, clean and lovely, full of fruit and bright with flowers, as places to spend the day, to the Bulls among Men (a title of the buddhas) and their disciples.

cmp.note: 「人中的公牛」，古印度以公牛比喻领袖和最强者。英文 Bulls among Men 照字面；白话「人中牛王」相近；鸠摩罗什这里只写「佛」。
cmp.en: "Bull among men": in ancient India the bull stood for a leader, the strongest of the herd. The English "Bulls among Men" is literal and the plain Chinese 人中牛王 (rén zhōng niúwáng, "bull-king among men") is close; Kumarajiva just writes 佛 (fó, "buddha").

verses.en: Full of joy, they give gifts like these, of every kind and color; and having given, they rouse their effort for awakening; by giving they have set out for the highest awakening.
And some teach the Dharma of peace with many nayutas of examples and reasons; they teach thousands of kotis of living beings; by knowledge they have set out for the highest awakening.
Understanding that things are inactive, that they do not run in twos, that they are like the sky, these sons of the Sugata are untainted; by wisdom they have set out for the highest awakening.

cmp.note: 这半句写法古怪，字面像是「运行于二」，与上下文「不落二边」相反，可能是抄本有误。英文、白话都按「不二」理解；鸠摩罗什译「无有二相」，也是这个意思。
cmp.en: This half-line is oddly worded: literally it looks like "proceeding in two," the opposite of the expected "not falling into duality," so the manuscript may be corrupt. The English and the plain Chinese both read it as "non-dual"; Kumarajiva's 无有二相 (wú yǒu èr xiàng, "without the mark of two") reads it the same way.

verses.en: And again, Manjughosha, I see that in the teaching of the Sugatas who have passed into final nirvana, many steadfast bodhisattvas have arisen, and they honor the relics of the Victors.
I see thousands of kotis of stupas, as many as the sands of the Ganges, with which kotis of fields are always adorned; they were built by those sons of the Victors.

Made of the seven precious things, splendid and tall, a full five thousand yojanas high (a yojana is a day's march, roughly ten kilometers or more), and two thousand around, with thousands of kotis of parasols and banners on them,
with victory flags, always shining, the clusters of bells always ringing; humans, gods, yakshas, and rakshasas worship them with flowers, scents, and music.
The sons of the Sugata have such worship made here for the relics of the Victors, and by it the ten directions are made beautiful, as if by coral trees in full bloom.

cmp.note: 天界的一种花树（刺桐类）。英文 coral trees、白话「波利质多树」；鸠摩罗什译「天树王」，只说是天上的树中之王，没有树名。
cmp.en: A flowering tree of heaven (a kind of Indian coral tree). The English says "coral trees," the plain Chinese transliterates it as 波利质多树 (bōlìzhìduō shù); Kumarajiva writes 天树王 (tiān shù wáng, "king of heavenly trees") without naming it.

verses.en: And I, and these many kotis of living beings standing here, see all this: this world with its gods all in flower. The Victor has sent out this single ray.
Oh, the power of the Bull among Men! Oh, his vast knowledge, free of outflows! His single ray, spreading through the world today, shows many thousands of fields.
We are struck with wonder at seeing this sign, so amazing and beyond measure. Tell us what it means, Manjusvara (Gentle Voice); take away our curiosity, son of the Buddha.
These four assemblies, eager in mind, are looking at you and at me, hero. Give them joy, take away their doubt; you explain it, son of the Sugata.
Why has the Sugata sent out such a light today? Oh, the power of the Bull among Men! Oh, his vast, pure knowledge!
His single ray, spreading through the world today, shows many thousands of fields. There must be some purpose this great for which this vast ray has been sent out.
The highest truths that the Sugata, the Supreme Person, touched back then on the seat of awakening: will the Lord of the World set them out here? Or will he give these bodhisattvas their predictions?

cmp.note: vyākaraṇa 原义是「分别解说」，在这部经里专指佛预言某人将来成佛。英文 give their predictions、白话「授记」都取这个专门意义。
cmp.en: Vyākaraṇa originally means "explaining in detail"; in this sutra it is the technical term for a buddha predicting that someone will become a buddha. The English "give their predictions" and the plain Chinese 授记 (shòujì, "conferring a prediction") both take this special sense.

verses.en: There must be no small reason here, that so many thousands of fields have been shown, brightly colored, adorned with jewels, and that buddhas of boundless vision are seen.
Maitreya is asking, son of the Victor; humans, gods, yakshas, and rakshasas are longing to know; these four assemblies are looking up and waiting: what will Manjusvara explain here?

Then Manjushri the Prince addressed Maitreya, the bodhisattva, the great being, and the whole gathering of bodhisattvas: "Sons of good family, the Tathagata intends to hold a great conversation for the hearing of the Dharma. Today, sons of good family, the Tathagata intends to pour down the great rain of the Dharma, to sound the great drum of the Dharma, to raise the great banner of the Dharma, to light the great torch of the Dharma, to blow the great conch of the Dharma, to beat the great kettledrum of the Dharma, and to give a great teaching of the Dharma. As I see it, sons of good family, I saw a sign like this before under the Tathagatas of the past, the arhats, the fully awakened buddhas: those earlier Tathagatas, arhats, fully awakened buddhas also sent out a ray of light like this.

"That is how I know that the Tathagata wants to hold a great conversation for the hearing of the Dharma, wants to let the great Dharma be heard, since he has shown a sign like this beforehand. Why? Because the Tathagata, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, wants to let a Dharma discourse be heard that goes against the whole world, and so he shows this great wonder, this ray of light, as a sign beforehand."

cmp.note: 「与整个世间相违的」，即世人很难接受、与常识相反的教法。英文 goes against the whole world、白话都照字面；鸠摩罗什译「一切世间难信之法」，把「相违」说成了「难信」。
cmp.en: "Running against the whole world": a teaching the world finds hard to accept, contrary to common sense. The English "goes against the whole world" and the plain Chinese are literal; Kumarajiva's 一切世间难信之法 (yíqiè shìjiān nán xìn zhī fǎ, "a Dharma hard for the whole world to believe") turns "contrary" into "hard to believe."

verses.en: "Sons of good family, I remember that in the past, countless eons (kalpas) ago, more than countless, vast, immeasurable, inconceivable, limitless, beyond reckoning, and further back still beyond that, at that time, on that occasion, a Tathagata named Chandrasuryapradipa (Lamp of Moon and Sun) appeared in the world, an arhat, a fully awakened buddha, perfect in knowledge and conduct, the Sugata, knower of the world, unsurpassed, trainer of people to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a buddha, a blessed one. He taught the Dharma, good in the beginning, good in the middle, good in the end, good in meaning and good in wording, whole, complete, pure, and spotless; he made known the holy life.

"That is, to the disciples he taught the Dharma linked to the four noble truths and unfolding as dependent arising, for getting past birth, old age, sickness, death, grief, lament, pain, sorrow, and despair, and ending in nirvana. And to the bodhisattvas, the great beings, he taught the Dharma linked to the six perfections, aimed at unsurpassed, perfect awakening and ending in all-knowing knowledge.

cmp.note: 梵文只分两类听众：声闻（四谛加缘起）和菩萨（六度）。鸠摩罗什本分成三类，多出「为求辟支佛者说应十二因缘法」，把缘起单独划给了缘觉，形成后来常说的「三乘各有其法」。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit has only two audiences: disciples (the four truths plus dependent arising) and bodhisattvas (the six perfections). Kumarajiva has three, adding 为求辟支佛者说应十二因缘法 ("for those seeking to be solitary buddhas he taught the twelve links of dependent arising"), giving dependent arising to the solitary buddhas alone, the familiar later scheme of three vehicles each with its own teaching.

verses.en: "And after that Tathagata Chandrasuryapradipa, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, further back still, sons of good family, another Tathagata appeared in the world, also named Chandrasuryapradipa, an arhat, a fully awakened buddha. In this way, Ajita (Maitreya's personal name), one after another, there were twenty thousand Tathagatas, arhats, fully awakened buddhas named Chandrasuryapradipa, all of one name, one family and one clan, the Bharadvaja clan. And Ajita, of those twenty thousand Tathagatas, from the first all the way to the last, each was a Tathagata named Chandrasuryapradipa, an arhat, a fully awakened buddha, perfect in knowledge and conduct, the Sugata, knower of the world, unsurpassed, trainer of people to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a buddha, a blessed one.

"He too taught the Dharma, good in the beginning, good in the middle, good in the end, good in meaning and good in wording, whole, complete, pure, and spotless; he made known the holy life. That is, to the disciples he taught the Dharma linked to the four noble truths and unfolding as dependent arising, for getting past birth, old age, sickness, death, grief, lament, pain, sorrow, and despair, and ending in nirvana; and to the bodhisattvas, the great beings, he taught the Dharma linked to the six perfections, aimed at unsurpassed, perfect awakening and ending in all-knowing knowledge.

"Ajita, before this Blessed One Chandrasuryapradipa, the Tathagata, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, left home, when he was still a prince, he had eight sons: a prince named Mati, a prince named Sumati, and princes named Anantamati, Ratnamati, Visheshamati, Vimatisamudghatin, Ghoshamati, and Dharmamati. Ajita, these eight princes, sons of the Blessed One Chandrasuryapradipa, the Tathagata, had great power and wealth. Each of them enjoyed four great continents, and there they ruled their kingdoms.

"When they learned that the Blessed One had left home, and heard that he had awakened to unsurpassed, perfect awakening, they gave up all the pleasures of their kingdoms and followed the Blessed One into homeless life. All of them set out for unsurpassed, perfect awakening and became teachers of the Dharma. Those princes always lived the holy life, and they had planted roots of goodness under many hundreds of thousands of buddhas.

"At that time, Ajita, the Blessed One Chandrasuryapradipa, the Tathagata, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, had taught a Dharma discourse, a sutra called The Great Teaching, a very extensive one, an instruction for bodhisattvas, held dear by all buddhas. Then in that same instant, in that same gathering, on that same great Dharma seat, he crossed his legs and entered the samadhi called The Ground of Endless Teaching, his body still and his mind unmoving. The moment the Blessed One entered it, a great rain of heavenly flowers poured down, mandarava and great mandarava, manjushaka and great manjushaka,

"scattering over the Blessed One and his assembly, and that whole buddha-field shook in six ways: it moved and moved all over, swayed and swayed all over, heaved and heaved all over. At that time, Ajita, on that occasion, the monks, nuns, laymen and laywomen, gods, nagas, yakshas, gandharvas, asuras, garudas, kinnaras, mahoragas, humans and non-humans gathered and seated in that assembly, and the regional kings, the wheel-turning kings who rule by force of arms, and the wheel-turning kings of the four continents, all of them with their followings gazed at that Blessed One, struck with wonder, amazement, and joy. Then, at that moment, a single ray of light came out of the tuft of white hair between the brows of the Blessed One Chandrasuryapradipa, the Tathagata.
"It spread through eighteen thousand buddha-fields in the east, and all those buddha-fields were seen lit up clearly by its light, Ajita, just as these buddha-fields are seen now.

"At that time, Ajita, twenty kotis of bodhisattvas were following that Blessed One. Those in that assembly who had come to hear the Dharma, seeing the world lit up by that great ray of light, were struck with wonder, amazement, and joy, and became curious.

"At that time, Ajita, in that Blessed One's following there was a bodhisattva named Varaprabha (Excellent Light), who had eight hundred pupils. That Blessed One rose from his samadhi and, addressing himself to the bodhisattva Varaprabha, set out the Dharma discourse called the Lotus of the True Dharma. He spoke for sixty full intermediate eons, sitting on a single seat, his body not trembling and his mind unmoving. And that whole assembly, sitting on single seats, listened to the Dharma from that Blessed One for those sixty intermediate eons, and not one being in that assembly grew tired in body or tired in mind.

cmp.note: 「中间劫」，大劫之中的一段。英文 intermediate eons、白话「中劫」照字面；鸠摩罗什译「小劫」，是另一种分法的名称，长短说法不一。
cmp.en: "In-between eon," a subdivision of a great eon. The English "intermediate eons" and the plain Chinese 中劫 (zhōng jié, "middle eon") are literal; Kumarajiva writes 小劫 (xiǎo jié, "small eon"), a name from another way of dividing time, and accounts of its length differ.

verses.en: "Then, when sixty intermediate eons had passed, the Blessed One Chandrasuryapradipa, the Tathagata, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, having taught that Dharma discourse, the Lotus of the True Dharma, a very extensive sutra, an instruction for bodhisattvas, held dear by all buddhas, in that very instant announced his final nirvana before the world with its gods, its Maras and its Brahmas, before all creatures with their ascetics and brahmins, gods, humans and asuras: 'Monks, tonight, in the middle watch of the night, the Tathagata will pass into final nirvana, into the realm of nirvana where nothing of the conditions of existence is left.'

"Then, Ajita, the Blessed One Chandrasuryapradipa, the Tathagata, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, predicted that a bodhisattva, a great being named Shrigarbha, would reach unsurpassed, perfect awakening, and he said to that whole assembly: 'Monks, this bodhisattva Shrigarbha will awaken to unsurpassed, perfect awakening right after me. He will be a Tathagata named Vimalanetra (Spotless Eye), an arhat, a fully awakened buddha.'

cmp.note: 两个名字：Śrīgarbha「吉祥藏」，鸠摩罗什译「德藏」；Vimalanetra「无垢眼」，白话「净眼」，鸠摩罗什却译「净身」，眼变成了身，可能他的底本不同。
cmp.en: Two names: Śrīgarbha, "womb of glory," which Kumarajiva renders 德藏 (Dézàng, "store of virtue"); and Vimalanetra, "spotless eye," plain Chinese 净眼 (Jìngyǎn, "pure eye"), which Kumarajiva gives as 净身 (Jìngshēn, "pure body"), eye turned into body, perhaps from a different source text.

verses.en: "Then, Ajita, that same night, in the middle watch, the Blessed One Chandrasuryapradipa, the Tathagata, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, passed into final nirvana in the realm of nirvana where nothing is left. The bodhisattva, the great being Varaprabha, kept that Dharma discourse, the Lotus of the True Dharma; for eighty intermediate eons after that Blessed One's final nirvana, the bodhisattva Varaprabha kept his teaching and made it known. And there, Ajita, that Blessed One's eight sons, led by Mati, became pupils of that same bodhisattva Varaprabha. He ripened them for unsurpassed, perfect awakening. Afterward they saw and honored many hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas of buddhas, and all of them awakened to unsurpassed, perfect awakening.
"And the last of them was the Tathagata Dipamkara (Lamp Maker), the arhat, the fully awakened buddha.

cmp.note: 燃灯佛，传说中为释迦牟尼前世授记的那位佛。这里说他是妙光弟子之一，等于把燃灯也放进了文殊（妙光）的师承里。
cmp.en: Dipamkara is the buddha who, in legend, gave Shakyamuni his prediction in a former life. Making him one of Varaprabha's pupils here places Dipamkara himself in the lineage of Manjushri (Varaprabha).

verses.en: "Among those eight hundred pupils there was one bodhisattva who cared far too much for gain, for honor, for being known, who was greedy for fame. The words and phrases he was taught kept slipping away from him; they would not stay. So he got the name Yashaskama (Fame Seeker). Yet by that root of goodness he too came to please many hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas of buddhas, and having pleased them, he honored, respected, revered, worshipped, adored, and venerated them. Now, Ajita, you may have some doubt, uncertainty, or hesitation: was the bodhisattva, the great being named Varaprabha, the teacher of the Dharma at that time, someone else? Don't see it that way. Why? I was the bodhisattva, the great being named Varaprabha, the teacher of the Dharma, at that time.

"And the bodhisattva named Yashaskama, who had fallen into laziness: you yourself, Ajita, were the bodhisattva named Yashaskama, fallen into laziness, at that time. So, Ajita, having seen this earlier sign of the Blessed One, I reason in this way from seeing such a ray sent out: the Blessed One, too, wants to teach that Dharma discourse, the Lotus of the True Dharma, a very extensive sutra, an instruction for bodhisattvas, held dear by all buddhas."

cmp.note: 梵文明说求名菩萨「陷于懈怠」，而他就是弥勒。白话照译；鸠摩罗什只说「贪着利养」「多所忘失」，没有「懒惰」这个字眼，对弥勒的批评淡了一些。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says outright that Yashaskama had "fallen into laziness," and that he was Maitreya. The plain Chinese keeps this; Kumarajiva says only 贪着利养 ("attached to gain") and 多所忘失 ("forgot much"), without the word "lazy," softening the criticism of Maitreya.

verses.en: Then Manjushri the Prince, to show this same matter more fully, spoke these verses at that time:
I remember a time long past, in an inconceivable, measureless eon, when there was a Victor, highest of beings, named Lamp of Moon and Sun.
The Guide of beings taught the true Dharma; he trained endless kotis of beings, and he encouraged many bodhisattvas toward the inconceivable, unsurpassed knowledge of a buddha.
The eight sons that this Guide had back when he was a prince, seeing the great sage go forth, quickly gave up sense pleasures, and they all went forth too.
And the Lord of the World taught the Dharma, a sutra called the excellent Endless Teaching; this extensive text is what it is called, and he made it known to thousands of kotis of living beings.
As soon as he had spoken it, the Guide crossed his legs in that very instant; seated on the Dharma seat, the best of sages entered the excellent samadhi called Endless Teaching.
There was a heavenly rain of mandarava flowers, and drums sounded though no one struck them; gods and yakshas, standing in the air, worshipped the Best of the Two-footed.
And at that moment the whole field shook; it was astonishing, utterly marvelous there; and the Guide sent out a single ray from between his brows, a beautiful thing to see.
That ray went to the eastern direction and filled eighteen thousand fields; shining, it lit up the whole world and showed the deaths and rebirths of beings.
Some fields there are made of jewels, and some gleam like beryl; brightly colored and very beautiful, they are seen by the light of the Guide's ray.
Gods and humans, nagas and yakshas, gandharvas, apsarases (heavenly nymphs), and kinnaras there, and those devoted to worshipping the Sugata, are seen worshipping in those world systems.
And the buddhas are seen, self-arisen in their own right, lovely as golden pillars, like a golden image set in beryl, teaching the Dharma in the middle of their assemblies.

cmp.note: 「自己生起的、自成的」，指不依老师而觉悟。白话「自己觉悟的」、英文 self-arisen 都照字面；鸠摩罗什译「自然成佛道」，读者容易理解成「自然而然就成了佛」。
cmp.en: "Self-existent, self-become," meaning awakened without a teacher. The plain Chinese 自己觉悟的 ("self-awakened") and the English "self-arisen" are literal; Kumarajiva's 自然成佛道 (zìrán chéng fó dào, "naturally achieving the buddha way") can be read as "became buddhas just by nature."

verses.en: The disciples there cannot be counted; the Sugata's disciples are beyond measure. In each and every field of the Guides, the light of the ray shows them all.
Endowed with effort, with discipline unbroken, discipline without a crack, like precious jewels, the sons of the Guides of Men are seen, those who live in mountain caves.
Giving away all they own, strong in patience, delighting in meditation, steadfast: many bodhisattvas, as many as the sands of the Ganges, are all seen by that ray.
Unmoving, unshaken, standing firm in patience, delighting in meditation, collected: the Sugata's own true sons are seen; by meditation they have set out for the highest awakening.
Knowing the true state, peaceful and free of outflows, they make it known; they teach the Dharma in many world systems. Such work as this comes from the Sugata's power.
And the four assemblies, seeing this power of the Protector, Lamp of Moon and Sun, all became joyful at that moment and asked one another, "What is this?"
Before long the Guide of the World, worshipped by humans, gods, and yakshas, rose from his samadhi and spoke to his son Varaprabha, the wise bodhisattva and teacher of the Dharma:

"You are the eye of the world and its refuge, wise and trustworthy, the one who holds the Dharma for me. You are the witness here to my treasury of the Dharma, to how I shall speak for the good of living beings."
Having settled many bodhisattvas, gladdened them, praised and commended them, that Victor taught the highest truths for a full sixty intermediate eons.
And all the finest, highest Dharma that the Lord of the World taught, staying on one seat, was kept in memory by that son of the Victor, Varaprabha, who became the teacher of the Dharma.
And that Victor, having taught the highest Dharma and gladdened a great many people, on that same day the Guide spoke before the world with its gods:
"I have made known this way of the Dharma; I have explained what the true nature of things is like. Monks, the time of my nirvana is today, here in the middle watch of the night.

cmp.note: 「法的自性、事物的本性」。英文 the true nature of things、白话「法的本性」相当；鸠摩罗什译「诸法实相」，这是他最有名的译语之一，后来成了天台宗的核心概念。
cmp.en: "The own-nature of dharmas, the nature of things." The English "the true nature of things" and the plain Chinese 法的本性 ("the nature of the Dharma/things") match it; Kumarajiva writes 诸法实相 (zhū fǎ shíxiàng, "the true mark of all dharmas"), one of his most famous coinages, which later became a core idea of the Tiantai school.

verses.en: "Be heedful, make faith your core, and work hard in this teaching of mine. Victors, great seers, are very hard to find; they come only after kotis of nayutas of eons."
Many sons of the Buddha grew anxious and were seized by sharp pain, hearing the voice of the Best of the Two-footed, the word "nirvana" coming so very soon.
And the King of the Lords of Men comforted those many, inconceivable kotis of beings: "Do not be afraid, monks, when I have gone to nirvana; there will be a buddha after me.
"This wise bodhisattva Shrigarbha has reached the goal in knowledge free of outflows; he will touch the supreme, highest awakening and become the Victor named Vimalagranetra (Spotless Highest Eye)."
That same night, in the middle watch, he passed into final nirvana like a lamp when its fuel is spent. His relics were spread far and wide, and the stupas were endless kotis of nayutas.
And the monks and nuns there who had set out for the supreme, highest awakening, as many as the sands of the Ganges, worked hard in that Sugata's teaching.
And the monk who was then the teacher of the Dharma, Varaprabha, by whom that Dharma was kept, taught the highest truths in that teaching for a full eighty intermediate eons.
He had eight hundred pupils, all of whom he ripened at that time; they saw many kotis of buddhas and honored those great seers.

cmp.note: 梵文偈颂这里说被妙光调教成佛的是「八百弟子」；鸠摩罗什和前面的散文都说是「八王子」。英文照梵文译。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit verses here say it was the "eight hundred pupils" whom Varaprabha ripened into buddhas; Kumarajiva, and the prose earlier, say the "eight princes." The English follows the Sanskrit.

verses.en: Having followed the practice that goes along with the Dharma, they became buddhas in many world systems; and one after another, in turn, they gave each other predictions of the highest awakening.
And of those buddhas in succession, the last was Dipamkara, god above the gods, worshipped by hosts of seers, who trained thousands of kotis of living beings.
And when that son of the Sugata, Varaprabha, was teaching the Dharma, there was a pupil, lazy and greedy at heart, seeking gain and recognition.
He was hungry for fame beyond measure, and he went from family to family; all the reciting and studying he was taught would not stay with him at that time.
And this is what his name became: he was known in every direction by the name Yashaskama. And by that deed of his, a mixed and spotted one,

cmp.note: 这几个字可以拆成「那不善的」（tena akuśalena），也可以读成「那善的」（tena kuśalena），意思正好相反。前面散文说「凭着那份善根」，鸠摩罗什也说「亦行众善业」；白话作「夹杂着瑕疵的业」，英文也取「好坏夹杂」的折中读法。
cmp.en: These letters can be split as "by that unwholesome" (tena akuśalena) or read as "by that wholesome" (tena kuśalena), exactly opposite meanings. The prose earlier says "by that root of goodness," and Kumarajiva says 亦行众善业 ("he also did many good deeds"); the plain Chinese has "a deed mixed with flaws," and the English likewise takes the middle reading, "mixed and spotted."

verses.en: he came to please thousands of kotis of buddhas and made vast offerings to them; he practiced the excellent way that goes along with the Dharma, and he has seen this buddha, the Lion of the Shakyas.
And he will be the last; he will gain unsurpassed, highest awakening. He will be a blessed one of the Maitreya clan, and he will train thousands of kotis of living beings.

cmp.note: 梵文说他将成为「弥勒族姓的」世尊，Maitreya 在这里像是姓氏；鸠摩罗什直接写「号名曰弥勒」，当成了佛号。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says he will be a blessed one "of the Maitreya clan," treating Maitreya here like a family name; Kumarajiva writes 号名曰弥勒 (hào míng yuē Mílè, "his title will be Maitreya"), treating it as a buddha-name.

verses.en: The one who had fallen into laziness then, in the teaching of the Sugata who had passed into nirvana: you yourself were that person, and I was the teacher of the Dharma then.
For this reason and cause, seeing today a sign like this, I say: it is the well-known sign of that knowledge, the one I first saw there.
Surely the King of Victors too, the All-seeing One, the overlord of the Shakyas, who sees the ultimate truth, wishes to teach that very same highest discourse that I heard back then.
That same sign is complete today: it is the skillful means of the Guides. The Lion of the Shakyas is settling the assembly; he will teach the seal of the true nature of things.

cmp.note: 「法之自性的印」，像盖章一样确认事物本性的教法。白话照译；鸠摩罗什译「实相义」，把「印」省掉了。
cmp.en: "The seal of the own-nature of dharmas": a teaching that confirms the nature of things the way a seal stamps a document. The plain Chinese keeps this; Kumarajiva writes 实相义 (shíxiàng yì, "the meaning of the true mark") and drops the seal.

verses.en: Be attentive, keep your minds well, join your palms: the one who cares for the good of the world will speak. He will rain an endless rain of the Dharma and refresh those who stand firm for the sake of awakening.
Whoever here has any doubt at all, any uncertainty, any hesitation, the Wise One will take it away for his sons, the bodhisattvas here who have set out for awakening.

cmp.note: 梵文说佛要为「发心走向觉悟的菩萨」消除疑惑；鸠摩罗什改成「诸求三乘人」，把对象扩大到声闻、缘觉、菩萨三乘，为下一品「开三显一」埋伏笔。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says the Buddha will remove the doubts of "the bodhisattvas who have set out for awakening"; Kumarajiva writes 诸求三乘人 (zhū qiú sān shèng rén, "all who seek the three vehicles"), widening the audience to disciples, solitary buddhas, and bodhisattvas, setting up the next chapter's theme of the three vehicles being one.

verses.en: Here ends the first chapter, called Introduction, in the noble Dharma discourse, the Lotus of the True Dharma.

cmp.note: 「起因、缘起」，佛经开头交代因缘的部分。英文 Introduction 是意译；白话「因缘」照字面；鸠摩罗什称「序品」，同样是意译。
cmp.en: "Cause, occasion": the opening section of a sutra that sets out how it came about. The English "Introduction" translates the function; the plain Chinese 因缘 (yīnyuán, "causes and conditions") is literal; Kumarajiva's 序品 (xù pǐn, "preface chapter") is likewise a functional rendering.

verses.en: Then the Blessed One, mindful and fully aware, came out of that samadhi (deep meditative absorption). Having come out of it, he spoke to the venerable Shariputra: "Shariputra, the knowledge of a buddha is deep, hard to see, hard to understand. The Tathagatas, the arhats, the fully awakened buddhas have woken up to it, and all the disciples (shravakas) and solitary buddhas (pratyekabuddhas) find it hard to grasp. Why is that? Because, Shariputra, the Tathagatas, arhats, fully awakened buddhas have attended on many hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas (both huge numbers) of buddhas; they have practiced the practice under many hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas of buddhas; they have gone a long way toward unsurpassed, perfect awakening; they have made great effort; they possess wonderful, marvelous qualities, qualities that are hard to grasp, and they have come to know qualities that are hard to grasp."

cmp.note: 梵文这里说的是「佛的智慧」本身难懂。鸠摩罗什译另加了「其智慧门难解难入」，多出一个「门」的意象；英文和白话照梵文，没有「门」。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says the buddha's knowledge itself is hard to understand. Kumarajiva's version adds 其智慧门难解难入 (qí zhìhuì mén nán jiě nán rù, "the gate of that wisdom is hard to understand and hard to enter"), bringing in an image of a gate; the English and the plain Chinese follow the Sanskrit and have no gate.

verses.en: "Shariputra, what the Tathagatas, arhats, fully awakened buddhas say with a hidden intent is hard to understand. Why? They make known teachings that each person has to realize for themselves, using many kinds of skillful means, knowledge and insight, explanations of causes and reasons, objects of thought, word explanations, and conventional names; with these skillful means they free beings who are stuck here and there. Shariputra, the Tathagatas, arhats, fully awakened buddhas have reached the highest perfection of great skillful means, knowledge, and insight. They possess wonderful qualities: knowledge and insight that cling to nothing and are blocked by nothing, the powers, the fearlessnesses, the qualities found in no one else, the faculties, the strengths, the factors of awakening, the meditations, the liberations, the samadhis and the attainments; and they make known teachings of every kind. Shariputra, the Tathagatas, arhats, fully awakened buddhas have attained what is greatly wonderful and marvelous. Enough, Shariputra, let it be enough to say just this: Shariputra, the Tathagatas, arhats, fully awakened buddhas have attained what is supremely wonderful."

cmp.note: 「带着深意说的话」：表面一层，底下另有用意。英文 say with a hidden intent、白话「带着深意说的话」都译出来了；鸠摩罗什译改成「随宜所说意趣难解」，放在上一段末尾，强调「看情况而说」。
cmp.en: "Speech with an intention behind it": one layer on the surface, another purpose underneath. The English "say with a hidden intent" and the plain Chinese 带着深意说的话 ("words spoken with deep meaning") both carry it; Kumarajiva renders it 随宜所说意趣难解 (suí yí suǒ shuō yìqù nán jiě, "what is said to suit the occasion, its intent is hard to grasp") and moves it to the end of the previous passage, stressing "speaking as the situation requires."

verses.en: "Only a Tathagata, Shariputra, can teach a Tathagata's teachings, the things that a Tathagata knows. Shariputra, it is only a Tathagata who teaches all things, and only a Tathagata who knows all things: what those things are, how they are, what they are like, what marks they have, and what their nature is. What they are, how, what like, with what marks and what nature: in all these things, only the Tathagata sees them directly, with his own eyes, not at second hand."

cmp.w: ye ca yathā ca yādṛśāśca yallakṣaṇāśca yatsvabhāvāśca
cmp.note: 梵文列了五项：是什么、怎样、像什么、什么特征、什么本质。鸠摩罗什译扩成著名的「十如是」（如是相、性、体、力、作、因、缘、果、报、本末究竟等），后来成了天台宗的根本教义。英文和白话照梵文只有五项。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit lists five items: what, how, what like, with what marks, with what nature. Kumarajiva expands this into the famous 十如是 (shí rúshì, "ten suchnesses": such appearance, nature, substance, power, function, cause, condition, effect, result, and their consistency from beginning to end), which later became a core doctrine of the Tiantai school. The English and the plain Chinese follow the Sanskrit's five.

verses.en: Then the Blessed One, to show this same meaning more fully, spoke these verses at that time:
The great heroes are beyond measure in this world of gods and humans. No being at all can fully know these guides.
What their powers and liberations are like, what their fearlessnesses are like, and what the qualities of a buddha are like, no one is able to know.
The practice they followed in the past, in the presence of kotis of buddhas, is deep and subtle, hard to grasp, very hard to see.
Having carried out that practice for inconceivable kotis of eons, I have seen its fruit at the seat of awakening, just as it is.

cmp.note: 字面是「觉悟的圆场、精华之地」，指佛陀成道的那块地方。英文 seat of awakening、白话「菩提道场」都是通行译法；中文「道场」后来也指寺院、法会，意思变宽了。
cmp.en: Literally "the circle or essence-place of awakening," the spot where the Buddha woke up. The English "seat of awakening" and the plain Chinese 菩提道场 (pútí dàochǎng, "field of awakening") are standard renderings; the Chinese 道场 later also came to mean a temple or a ritual service, so its range widened.

verses.en: I know what it is, and so do the other guides of the world: how it is, what it is, what it is like, and what its marks are like.
It cannot be shown; there are no words for it. Nor is there any being in the world

cmp.note: 梵文是「没有能说它的话」。鸠摩罗什译「言辞相寂灭」，把它说成「言语的相状都止息了」，带上了寂灭的哲学色彩。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says "there is no speech for it." Kumarajiva's 言辞相寂灭 (yáncí xiàng jìmiè, "the marks of words are stilled") gives it the philosophical color of everything coming to rest.

verses.en: who, if this teaching were taught to him, could understand what was taught, except the bodhisattvas who stand firm in faith.

And those disciples of the Knower of the World who have done their earlier work, whom the Sugata (the Well-Gone One) has praised, whose outflows (defilements) are used up and who carry their last body: the knowledge of the Victors is not within their reach either.
Even if this whole world were filled with people like Shariputra, and they all became of one mind and thought it over, they still could not know the knowledge of the Sugata.
Even if all ten directions were filled with wise men like you, and filled in just the same way with these other disciples of mine,
and today they all became of one mind and thought over the knowledge of the Sugata, all of them together still could not know how immeasurable my buddha-knowledge is.
If all ten directions were filled with solitary buddhas, free of outflows, with sharp faculties, carrying their last body, as thick as reeds or as bamboo in a grove,
and they became one and thought for endless kotis of nayutas of eons about just a fraction of my highest teaching, they would not know its true meaning.

If these ten directions were filled with bodhisattvas newly set out on the vehicle, who have done their earlier work under many kotis of buddhas, who have settled the meaning well and often teach the Dharma,

cmp.note: 「刚踏上（大）乘的」。白话「新踏上菩萨之路」、鸠摩罗什「新发意菩萨」都对，英文照字面写 newly set out on the vehicle。
cmp.en: "Newly set out on the vehicle." The plain Chinese 新踏上菩萨之路 ("newly set out on the bodhisattva path") and Kumarajiva's 新发意菩萨 (xīn fāyì púsà, "bodhisattvas who have newly made the resolve") are both accurate; the English keeps the literal "vehicle."

verses.en: so that the whole world were always packed full of them, like reeds and bamboo, with no gap, and they became one and thought over the teaching that the Sugata has seen face to face,
thinking it through for many kotis of eons, as countless as the grains of sand in the Ganges, minds on nothing else, with subtle wisdom, even for them it is not within reach.
If bodhisattvas who can no longer turn back, as many as the sands of the Ganges, thought it over with minds on nothing else, even for them it is not within reach.
The teachings of the buddhas are deep and subtle, beyond reasoning, all free of outflows. I know here what they are like, and so do the Victors in the world in the ten directions.
Shariputra, have firm faith in what the Sugata says. The Victor, the great seer, never says one thing and means another; after a long time he speaks the highest meaning.
I address all these disciples, and those who have set out for the awakening of a solitary buddha: I established you in nirvana and set you free from the endless chain of suffering.

cmp.note: 梵文是「我把你们安顿在涅槃里」，这句话为后面的「那只是方便」埋下伏笔。鸠摩罗什译「逮得涅槃者」，像是在说他们自己已经得到涅槃，伏笔的意味淡了。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says "I settled you in nirvana," which sets up the later reveal that this was only a skillful means. Kumarajiva's 逮得涅槃者 (dǎi dé nièpán zhě, "those who have attained nirvana") reads as if they reached nirvana by themselves, so the setup is weaker.

verses.en: This is my highest skillful means: with it I teach the Dharma in many ways in the world. I free those who are stuck here and there, and I show them three vehicles.

cmp.note: 「三乘」：yāna 是「车、交通工具」，指声闻、独觉、菩萨三条路。英文 three vehicles 保留了「车」的画面，这个画面到下一品的火宅喻里会真的变成三种车。
cmp.en: "Three vehicles": yāna means "a cart, a means of travel," here the three paths of disciples, solitary buddhas, and bodhisattvas. The English "vehicles" keeps the picture of a cart, which in the next chapter's parable of the burning house turns into three actual carts.

verses.en: Then, in that gathered assembly, the great disciples headed by Ajnata Kaundinya, twelve hundred arhats whose outflows were used up and who had mastered themselves, along with the other monks, nuns, laymen and laywomen of the disciple vehicle, and those who had set out on the solitary-buddha vehicle, all had this thought: "What is the reason, what is the cause, that the Blessed One praises the Tathagatas' skillful means so highly? That he praises it, saying, 'This Dharma I have woken up to is deep'? That he praises it, saying, 'It is hard for all disciples and solitary buddhas to grasp'? Up to now the Blessed One has taught only one liberation, and we too have gained the Buddha's teachings and reached nirvana. Yet we do not know what the Blessed One means by this."

Then the venerable Shariputra, knowing the doubt and uncertainty of the four assemblies, reading the thoughts in their minds with his own mind, and having himself fallen into doubt about the teaching, said to the Blessed One at that time: "Blessed One, what is the reason, what is the cause, that the Blessed One praises so highly, again and again, the Tathagatas' skillful means, knowledge and insight, and teaching of the Dharma, saying, 'The Dharma I have woken up to is deep,' and praises again and again, saying, 'What is said with a hidden intent is hard to grasp'? I have never before heard such a discourse on the Dharma from the Blessed One. And Blessed One, these four assemblies have fallen into doubt and uncertainty. So please, Blessed One, explain why the Tathagata keeps praising the deep Dharma of the Tathagata again and again."

cmp.note: 抄本这里写成 saṃghā-（「僧团」），应是上文 saṃdhābhāṣya（带深意的话）的笔误。英文和白话都照 saṃdhā 理解。
cmp.en: The manuscript here reads saṃghā- ("community"), which is most likely a slip for saṃdhābhāṣya ("speech with a hidden intent") used earlier. The English and the plain Chinese both read it as saṃdhā.

verses.en: Then the venerable Shariputra spoke these verses at that time:
After a long time, sun among humans, today you speak like this: that you have touched powers, liberations and meditations beyond measure.
You speak of the seat of awakening, yet no one has asked you about it. You speak of what is said with a hidden intent, and no one asks you.
Unasked, you speak out; you praise your own practice, you speak of the knowledge you have reached, and you declare what is deep.
Today these masters of themselves, free of outflows, have fallen into doubt, and so have those who are making for nirvana: what is the Victor saying?
Nuns and monks seeking the awakening of a solitary buddha, and gods, nagas, yakshas, gandharvas and mahoragas (great serpent spirits),
talking with one another, gaze at the best of two-footed beings, wondering and full of questions: explain it, great sage!
Of all the disciples the Sugata has here, I am the one the supreme seer has named as having reached the far shore.

cmp.note: 字面是「到达彼岸、达到圆满的」，这里指舍利弗在声闻中智慧最高。鸠摩罗什译直接写「佛说我第一」，白话「达到圆满的那一位」，英文保留了「到彼岸」的字面画面。
cmp.en: Literally "one who has reached the far shore, reached perfection," here meaning Shariputra is foremost in wisdom among the disciples. Kumarajiva writes plainly 佛说我第一 (fó shuō wǒ dìyī, "the Buddha says I am the first"); the plain Chinese says "the one who has reached perfection"; the English keeps the literal picture of the far shore.

verses.en: Yet even I, best of humans, have doubts here about where I stand: is nirvana my final goal, or have you shown me a practice still to be walked?
Let your voice ring out, you whose voice is like a splendid drum; declare how this Dharma is. Here stand the true sons of the Victor, born of his breast, palms joined, looking up at the Victor.

cmp.note: 「从胸口生的、亲生的（儿子）」，指真正的嫡子。鸠摩罗什译「佛口所生子」改成「从口里生的」，意思是听佛说法而生的弟子，画面换了一个身体部位。
cmp.en: "Born from the breast," meaning a true, legitimate son. Kumarajiva's 佛口所生子 (fó kǒu suǒ shēng zǐ, "sons born from the Buddha's mouth") changes the body part: disciples born from hearing the Buddha speak.

verses.en: Gods and nagas with yakshas and rakshasas (man-eating demons), thousands of kotis of them, like the sands of the Ganges; and those who seek complete awakening, a full eighty thousand of them, are standing here;
kings, lords of the earth, wheel-turning monarchs who have come from thousands of kotis of lands, all stand with palms joined and full of reverence: how are we to bring the practice to completion?

cmp.note: 「转轮王」，以法统治天下的理想君主，转动统治的轮宝。英文 wheel-turning monarch 照字面，白话、古译都用「转轮王」。
cmp.en: A "wheel-turner," the ideal king who rules the world by right, rolling his sovereign wheel before him. The English "wheel-turning monarch" is literal; the plain Chinese and the old translation both use 转轮王 (zhuǎnlún wáng, "wheel-turning king").

verses.en: When this was said, the Blessed One told the venerable Shariputra: "Enough, Shariputra. What use is it to speak of this matter? Why? Shariputra, if this matter were explained, this world with its gods would be terrified." A second time the venerable Shariputra pressed the Blessed One: "Let the Blessed One speak, let the Sugata speak of this very matter. Why? Blessed One, in this assembly there are many hundreds of living beings, many thousands, many hundreds of thousands, many hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas of living beings who have seen buddhas in the past and who are wise. They will trust what the Blessed One says, believe it, and take it up."
Then the venerable Shariputra addressed the Blessed One with this verse:
Speak clearly, highest of Victors! There are thousands of living beings here in this assembly with faith, at peace, full of reverence for the Sugata. They will understand the Dharma you declare.

Then the Blessed One spoke a second time to the venerable Shariputra: "Enough, Shariputra, of making this matter plain. Shariputra, if this matter were explained, this world with its gods would be terrified, and monks full of arrogance would fall over a great cliff."

cmp.note: 「自以为已经得到、其实没得到」的骄慢。英文 arrogance、白话「傲慢自大」都偏向一般的傲慢；古译「增上慢」是专门术语，正好指「未得谓得」。
cmp.en: The pride of thinking you have attained what you have not. The English "arrogance" and the plain Chinese 傲慢自大 ("arrogant and conceited") lean toward ordinary pride; the old translation's 增上慢 (zēngshàng màn, "overreaching pride") is a technical term for exactly "claiming an attainment one has not reached."

verses.en: Then the Blessed One spoke this verse at that time:
Enough of speaking the Dharma here. This knowledge is subtle and beyond reasoning. There are many fools caught in arrogance; when the Dharma is taught, not understanding it, they would revile it.

A third time the venerable Shariputra pressed the Blessed One: "Let the Blessed One speak, let the Sugata speak of this very matter. Blessed One, there are many hundreds of beings like me in this assembly, and many other hundreds of beings, Blessed One, many thousands, many hundreds of thousands, many hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas, whom the Blessed One brought to ripeness in former lives. They will trust what the Blessed One says, believe it, and take it up, and it will be for their benefit, their good and their happiness for a long time."

cmp.note: 字面是「长夜」，习惯上只是「长久」的意思。白话「长久地」、英文 for a long time 取其意；古译「长夜安隐」保留了字面的「夜」。
cmp.en: Literally "for a long night," an idiom simply meaning "for a long time." The plain Chinese 长久地 and the English "for a long time" give the sense; the old translation's 长夜安隐 (cháng yè ān yǐn, "at peace through the long night") keeps the literal night.

verses.en: Then the venerable Shariputra spoke these verses at that time:
Teach the Dharma, highest of two-footed beings! I, your eldest son, ask you. There are thousands of kotis of beings here who will trust the Dharma you teach.
And the beings you have always brought to ripeness in former lives, through a very long night, all stand here too with palms joined; they will trust this Dharma of yours.
We twelve hundred, people like us, and those who have set out for the highest awakening: let the Sugata look at them and speak, and give rise to the greatest joy in them.

Then the Blessed One, knowing that the venerable Shariputra had asked him a third time, said to him: "Now, Shariputra, you have asked the Tathagata as many as three times. When you ask like this, Shariputra, what can I say? Listen then, Shariputra, and take it to heart well and thoroughly. I will tell you."

No sooner had the Blessed One said these words than some five thousand arrogant monks, nuns, laymen and laywomen in the assembly rose from their seats, bowed their heads at the Blessed One's feet, and left the assembly. This was because, through arrogance, an unwholesome root, they believed they had reached what they had not reached and realized what they had not realized. Knowing themselves to be wounded, they left the assembly. And the Blessed One let them go in silence.

cmp.note: 「带着伤口的」：这些人自知有毛病、心虚，所以离开。白话「带着伤（有毛病）」照字面加了解释；鸠摩罗什译「有如此失，是以不住」只说「有过失」，伤口的画面没有了。
cmp.en: "With a wound": these people knew they had a flaw and felt exposed, so they left. The plain Chinese 带着伤 ("carrying a wound") is literal with a gloss; Kumarajiva's 有如此失，是以不住 (yǒu rúcǐ shī, shì yǐ bú zhù, "they had such a fault, so they did not stay") says only "fault," and the image of a wound is gone.

cmp.note: 梵文是「以沉默表示同意」，印度礼节里沉默即认可。鸠摩罗什译「默然而不制止」，侧重「没有拦」；英文 let them go in silence 介于两者之间。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit is "consented by being silent"; in Indian etiquette silence means assent. Kumarajiva's 默然而不制止 (mòrán ér bú zhìzhǐ, "silent and did not stop them") stresses not holding them back; the English "let them go in silence" sits between the two.

verses.en: Then the Blessed One spoke to the venerable Shariputra: "Shariputra, my assembly is free of chaff; the empty husks are gone, and it stands firm in the solid grain of faith. It is good, Shariputra, that these arrogant ones have left. So now, Shariputra, I will speak of this matter." "Very good, Blessed One," the venerable Shariputra answered the Blessed One.

cmp.note: 两个农事比喻：没有糠秕、去掉了空心的废料，剩下实心的谷粒。白话照译；鸠摩罗什改成「无复枝叶，纯有贞实」，换成了树木的比喻。
cmp.en: Two farming images: no chaff, the hollow waste removed, only solid grain left. The plain Chinese follows them; Kumarajiva switches to a tree image, 无复枝叶，纯有贞实 (wú fù zhīyè, chún yǒu zhēn shí, "no more branches and leaves, only solid trunk").

verses.en: The Blessed One said: "Only now and then, Shariputra, does the Tathagata give a teaching like this. Just as an udumbara flower (a fig blossom that is almost never seen) is seen only now and then, in the same way, Shariputra, the Tathagata gives a teaching like this only now and then. Trust me, Shariputra: I speak what is real, I speak what is so, I do not speak otherwise. Shariputra, what the Tathagata says with a hidden intent is hard to understand. Why? Shariputra, I have made the Dharma known through all kinds of word explanations, teachings, expressions and instructions, through many hundreds of thousands of different skillful means. Shariputra, the true Dharma is beyond reasoning, outside the range of reasoning, to be understood by a Tathagata. Why is that?

cmp.note: 优昙钵是一种无花果树，花藏在果实里，平时看不见，所以成了「极难得一见」的比喻。英文加了括注；白话和古译都只音译。
cmp.en: The udumbara is a kind of fig tree whose flowers are hidden inside the fruit and so are never seen, which made it a figure for "something almost never seen." The English adds a gloss; the plain Chinese and the old translation only transliterate it as 优昙钵 (yōutánbō).

verses.en: Shariputra, a Tathagata, an arhat, a fully awakened buddha appears in the world for one task, one thing to be done, a great task, a great thing to be done. And what, Shariputra, is that one task, that one thing to be done, that great task, great thing to be done, for which a Tathagata, arhat, fully awakened buddha appears in the world? It is this: a Tathagata, arhat, fully awakened buddha appears in the world in order to lead beings to take up the Tathagata's knowledge and insight. He appears in the world in order to show beings the Tathagata's knowledge and insight. He appears in the world in order to bring beings into the Tathagata's knowledge and insight. He appears in the world in order to awaken beings to the Tathagata's knowledge.

cmp.note: 「一件要做的事」。鸠摩罗什译成「一大事因缘」，后来成了中国佛教的名句；梵文没有「因缘」二字，只是反复说「一件事、一件大事」。四个动作在古译里是「开、示、悟、入」，次序和梵文（引导接受、展示、进入、觉悟）不同。
cmp.en: "One task to be done." Kumarajiva renders it 一大事因缘 (yí dà shì yīnyuán, "the cause and condition of one great matter"), which became a famous phrase in Chinese Buddhism; the Sanskrit has no "cause and condition," only the repeated "one task, one great task." The four actions in the old translation are 开示悟入 (kāi shì wù rù, "open, show, awaken, enter"), in a different order from the Sanskrit (lead to take up, show, bring into, awaken).
