verses.en: He appears in the world in order to bring beings onto the path to the Tathagata's knowledge and insight. This, Shariputra, is the Tathagata's one task, one thing to be done, great task, great thing to be done, his single purpose for appearing in the world. So, Shariputra, whatever is the Tathagata's one task, one thing to be done, great task, great thing to be done, that the Tathagata does. Why? Shariputra, I am the one who leads beings to take up the Tathagata's knowledge and insight; Shariputra, I am the one who shows the Tathagata's knowledge and insight; Shariputra, I am the one who brings beings into the Tathagata's knowledge and insight; Shariputra, I am the one who awakens them to the Tathagata's knowledge and insight; Shariputra, I am the one who brings them onto the path to the Tathagata's knowledge and insight. Shariputra, I teach beings the Dharma on the basis of one vehicle only, that is, the buddha vehicle.

cmp.note: 「一乘」是本经的核心：只有一条车道，就是成佛之路。英文 one vehicle、白话「一乘」、古译「一佛乘」意思一致；古译此处还插入了「诸佛如来但教化菩萨」一句，梵文这段没有。
cmp.en: "One vehicle" is the heart of this sutra: there is only one road, the road to buddhahood. The English "one vehicle," the plain Chinese 一乘 (yī shèng), and the old 一佛乘 (yī fó shèng, "one buddha vehicle") agree; but the old translation also inserts 诸佛如来但教化菩萨 ("the buddhas teach only bodhisattvas"), which this Sanskrit passage does not have.

verses.en: Shariputra, there is no second vehicle at all, nor a third. Shariputra, this is the way things are everywhere, in the world of the ten directions. Why? Shariputra, the Tathagatas, arhats, fully awakened buddhas who were there in times past, in immeasurable, countless world systems in the ten directions, for the good of many, for the happiness of many, out of compassion for the world, for the benefit, good and happiness of a great body of people, of gods and humans: they taught the Dharma after knowing the inclinations of beings with all kinds of convictions and all kinds of dispositions and leanings, through skillful means of every kind, through various ways of guiding and explaining, various causes, reasons, examples, objects of thought and word explanations.

All of them too, Shariputra, those buddhas, those blessed ones, taught beings the Dharma on the basis of one vehicle only, that is, the buddha vehicle, which ends in all-knowing; that is, they taught beings the Dharma only to lead them to take up the Tathagata's knowledge and insight, only to show it, only to bring them into it, only to awaken them to it, only to bring them onto the path to the Tathagata's knowledge and insight. And Shariputra, the beings who heard the true Dharma from those past Tathagatas, arhats, fully awakened buddhas all came to gain unsurpassed, perfect awakening.

cmp.note: 梵文说听过法的众生都「得到了无上正等正觉」。鸠摩罗什译「究竟皆得一切种智」，换成了「一切种智」，意思相近，但用的是另一个术语。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says the beings who heard the teaching "gained unsurpassed, perfect awakening." Kumarajiva writes 究竟皆得一切种智 (jiūjìng jiē dé yíqiè zhǒng zhì, "in the end all attain knowledge of all modes"), close in meaning but a different technical term.

verses.en: Shariputra, the Tathagatas, arhats, fully awakened buddhas who will be in times to come, in immeasurable, countless world systems in the ten directions, for the good of many, for the happiness of many, out of compassion for the world, for the benefit, good and happiness of a great body of people, of gods and humans, and who will teach the Dharma after knowing the inclinations of beings with all kinds of convictions and all kinds of dispositions and leanings, through various ways of guiding and explaining, various causes, reasons, examples, objects of thought, word explanations and skillful means: all of them too, Shariputra, those buddhas, those blessed ones, will teach beings the Dharma on the basis of one vehicle only, that is, the buddha vehicle, which ends in all-knowing; that is, they will teach beings the Dharma only to lead them to take up the Tathagata's knowledge and insight, only to show it, only to bring them into it, only to awaken them to it, only to bring them onto the path to the Tathagata's knowledge and insight.
And Shariputra, the beings who will hear that Dharma from those future Tathagatas, arhats, fully awakened buddhas will all come to gain unsurpassed, perfect awakening.

Shariputra, the Tathagatas, arhats, fully awakened buddhas who right now, in the present time, in immeasurable, countless world systems in the ten directions, are standing, living, carrying on, and teaching the Dharma for the good of many, for the happiness of many, out of compassion for the world, for the benefit, good and happiness of a great body of people, of gods and humans, who teach the Dharma after knowing the inclinations of beings with all kinds of convictions and all kinds of dispositions and leanings, through various ways of guiding and explaining, various causes, reasons, examples, objects of thought, word explanations and skillful means: all of them too, Shariputra, those buddhas, those blessed ones, teach beings the Dharma on the basis of one vehicle only, that is, the buddha vehicle, which ends in all-knowing; that is, they teach beings the Dharma only to lead them to take up the Tathagata's knowledge and insight, only to show it, only to bring them into it, only to awaken them to it, only to bring them onto the path to the Tathagata's knowledge and insight.
And Shariputra, the beings who hear that Dharma from those present Tathagatas, arhats, fully awakened buddhas will all come to gain unsurpassed, perfect awakening.

I too, Shariputra, now a Tathagata, an arhat, a fully awakened buddha, for the good of many, for the happiness of many, out of compassion for the world, for the benefit, good and happiness of a great body of people, of gods and humans, teach the Dharma after knowing the inclinations of beings with all kinds of convictions and all kinds of dispositions and leanings, through various ways of guiding and explaining, various causes, reasons, examples, objects of thought, word explanations and skillful means. I too, Shariputra, teach beings the Dharma on the basis of one vehicle only, that is, the buddha vehicle, which ends in all-knowing; that is, I teach beings the Dharma only to lead them to take up the Tathagata's knowledge and insight, only to show it, only to bring them into it, only to awaken them to it, only to bring them onto the path to the Tathagata's knowledge and insight.

And Shariputra, the beings who now hear this Dharma of mine will all come to gain unsurpassed, perfect awakening. So, Shariputra, in this way too it should be understood that nowhere in the world of the ten directions is a second vehicle set up, let alone a third.

cmp.note: 「设立、施设」：没有第二乘被「设立」出来。英文 set up 照字面；古译「尚无二乘，何况有三」说成「没有」，少了「被人为设立」的意思。
cmp.en: "Setting up, designation": no second vehicle is "set up." The English "set up" is literal; the old translation's 尚无二乘，何况有三 (shàng wú èr shèng, hékuàng yǒu sān, "there is not even a second vehicle, let alone a third") just says "there is no," losing the sense of something put in place by convention.

verses.en: And yet, Shariputra, Tathagatas, arhats, fully awakened buddhas sometimes appear in a time when the age is turbid, or when beings are turbid, or afflictions are turbid, or views are turbid, or lifespans are turbid. Shariputra, in such turbid times, when the age is in turmoil and beings are mostly greedy, with few wholesome roots, then, Shariputra, the Tathagatas, arhats, fully awakened buddhas, by skillful means, teach that one buddha vehicle by teaching it as three vehicles. And here, Shariputra, those disciples, arhats or solitary buddhas who do not hear, do not enter into, and do not understand this work of the Tathagata, his leading beings to take up the buddha vehicle, should not be regarded as the Tathagata's disciples, Shariputra, nor as arhats, nor as solitary buddhas.

cmp.note: 本义是「浑浊的、有沉渣的」，像搅浑的水。英文 turbid、白话「污浊」都保留了这层意思；古译「五浊恶世」多加了一个「恶」字。
cmp.en: Originally "muddy, full of sediment," like stirred-up water. The English "turbid" and the plain Chinese 污浊 (wūzhuó, "murky") both keep this; the old translation's 五浊恶世 (wǔ zhuó è shì, "evil world of five turbidities") adds the word "evil."

verses.en: And further, Shariputra, if some monk or nun should claim to be an arhat, without taking up the vow for unsurpassed, perfect awakening, and should say, "I am cut off from the buddha vehicle," or should say, "This is the final nirvana of this body of mine, the last one," know that person to be arrogant, Shariputra. Why? Shariputra, it is impossible, there is no room for it, that a monk who is an arhat, his outflows used up, should hear this Dharma face to face with the Tathagata and not believe it, unless the Tathagata has already entered final nirvana. Why? Because, Shariputra, at that time, when the Tathagata has entered final nirvana, disciples will not be keepers or teachers of sutras like these. But in the presence of other Tathagatas, arhats, fully awakened buddhas, Shariputra, they will become free of doubt.

Trust me, Shariputra, in these teachings of the Buddha; believe them, accept them. Shariputra, Tathagatas do not speak falsely. Shariputra, there is only this one vehicle, that is, the buddha vehicle.
Then the Blessed One, to show this same meaning more fully, spoke these verses at that time:
Then the monks and nuns and laymen and laywomen who were caught in arrogance, without faith, nearly five thousand of them,

cmp.note: 梵文是「差一点到五千」，比散文部分的「大约五千」更具体。鸠摩罗什译「其数有五千」把零头去掉了。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says "five thousand less a few," a little more exact than the prose's "about five thousand." Kumarajiva's 其数有五千 (qí shù yǒu wǔqiān, "their number was five thousand") rounds it off.

verses.en: not seeing this fault in themselves, their training full of holes, guarding their wounds, left, those childish minds.
Knowing the dregs in the assembly, the Lord of the World let it be. They do not have the good roots to hear this Dharma.

cmp.note: 梵文是「默许、容忍」，佛只是让他们走。鸠摩罗什译「佛威德故去」，说他们是因佛的威德而离开，好像是佛的力量把他们送走的，和梵文语气不同。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit means "allowed it, put up with it": the Buddha simply let them go. Kumarajiva's 佛威德故去 (fó wēidé gù qù, "they left because of the Buddha's majestic power") makes it sound as if the Buddha's power sent them away, a different tone from the Sanskrit.

verses.en: My assembly is pure, free of chaff, standing firm; the husks are all gone, and what remains here is solid grain.
Listen to me, son of Shari, to how this Dharma was woken up to by the best of humans, and how the buddhas, the guides, teach it with many hundreds of skillful means.

cmp.note: 「舍利（Śārī）的儿子」，即舍利弗名字的意译：他母亲名叫舍利。英文照字面译出，白话直接写「舍利弗」。
cmp.en: "Son of Shari," a translation of Shariputra's name: his mother was called Shari. The English renders it literally; the plain Chinese simply writes 舍利弗 (Shèlìfú, "Shariputra").

verses.en: Knowing the inclinations and the conduct of kotis of living beings here, with all their different convictions, knowing their varied deeds and the good they did in the past,
I bring these beings to understanding with various word explanations and reasons; with causes and hundreds of illustrations I satisfy all beings, each in their own way.
I speak sutras and verses, stories of the past, birth stories and marvels; I speak with origin stories and hundreds of colorful parables, and I speak songs and instructions as well.

cmp.note: 这里列的是佛经的九种体裁（下文称「九部」）：契经、偈颂、本事、本生、希有法、因缘、譬喻、应颂、论议。英文用日常词意译；白话和古译用传统术语，古译多半是音译（修多罗、伽陀、祇夜、优波提舍）。
cmp.en: This lists the nine genres of the Buddha's teaching (called the "nine parts" below): sutras, verses, past stories, birth stories, marvels, origin stories, parables, songs, and instructions. The English uses everyday words; the plain Chinese and the old translation use the traditional terms, the old one mostly as transliterations such as 修多罗 (xiūduōluó, sūtra), 伽陀 (qiétuó, gāthā), 祇夜 (qíyè, geya), 优波提舍 (yōubōtíshè, upadeśa).

verses.en: For those who delight in what is lesser, who lack understanding, who have not practiced under many kotis of buddhas, who are stuck in samsara (the round of birth and death) and suffer greatly, I show nirvana.

cmp.note: 「喜好低劣的」：hīna 是「低、差、少」，后来「小乘」（hīnayāna）一词就由此而来。白话「喜好低劣之法」、英文 delight in what is lesser 照字面；鸠摩罗什译「钝根乐小法」多了「钝根」，并把「低劣」柔化成「小」。
cmp.en: "Delighting in what is low": hīna means "low, inferior, small," the source of the later term hīnayāna, "Lesser Vehicle." The plain Chinese 喜好低劣之法 ("fond of inferior teachings") and the English "delight in what is lesser" are literal; Kumarajiva's 钝根乐小法 (dùn gēn lè xiǎo fǎ, "dull-rooted, delighting in small teachings") adds "dull roots" and softens "low" to "small."

verses.en: The Self-Existent One uses this as a skillful means, to awaken them to a buddha's knowledge. But he never tells them, "You too will become buddhas here in the world."

cmp.note: 「自己生成的、自然而有的」，这里是佛的称号，指不靠老师自己觉悟。英文 Self-Existent One 照字面；白话「自然觉悟者」把意思解释了出来。
cmp.en: "Self-existent, self-become," here a title of the Buddha: one who awakened without a teacher. The English "Self-Existent One" is literal; the plain Chinese 自然觉悟者 ("one awakened of himself") spells out the meaning.

verses.en: Why? The Protector watches for the right time, and only when he sees the moment does he speak. That moment has somehow come today, and so I declare here what is truly certain.

cmp.note: 「确定的真实」。鸠摩罗什译「决定说大乘」，把它直接点名为「大乘」，梵文这一句并没有出现「大乘」一词。
cmp.en: "The settled truth." Kumarajiva's 决定说大乘 (juédìng shuō dàshèng, "I resolve to teach the Great Vehicle") names it outright as the Great Vehicle; that word does not appear in this Sanskrit line.

verses.en: This nine-part teaching of mine has been taught according to how strong or weak beings are. I have shown it as a skillful means, to bring them into the knowledge of the Giver of Gifts.
And for the children of the Buddha here who are always pure, clear-minded, clean and gentle, who have done their earlier work under many kotis of buddhas, I teach the extensive sutras.

cmp.note: 「方广经」，字面是「广大展开的经」，大乘经的一种自称。英文 extensive sutras 照字面；鸠摩罗什译直接写成「大乘经」。
cmp.en: "Vaipulya sutras," literally "broad, expanded sutras," a name Mahayana sutras gave themselves. The English "extensive sutras" is literal; Kumarajiva simply writes 大乘经 (dàshèng jīng, "Great Vehicle sutras").

verses.en: Because they are endowed with excellent intention and pure form, I tell them, kind and caring as they are: "You will become buddhas in the time to come."
Hearing this, they are all filled with joy: "We will become buddhas, foremost in the world!" And knowing their practice, I teach the extensive sutras again.
And these are the disciples of the Guide who have heard this supreme teaching: anyone who has heard or kept even a single verse is headed for awakening, there is no doubt.

cmp.note: 梵文这里只说「这些声闻弟子」。鸠摩罗什译「声闻若菩萨」，把菩萨也加了进去，范围更大。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit here says only "these disciples." Kumarajiva's 声闻若菩萨 (shēngwén ruò púsà, "disciples or bodhisattvas") adds bodhisattvas, making the circle wider.

verses.en: For there is only one vehicle; there is no second, and never anywhere in the world a third, except as the skillful means of the best of humans, when they show a variety of vehicles.

cmp.note: 梵文只说「世间只有一乘」。鸠摩罗什译「十方佛土中，唯有一乘法」，多了「十方佛土」，又加了「但以假名字，引导于众生」，说三乘只是借用的名字。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says only "there is one vehicle in the world." Kumarajiva writes 十方佛土中，唯有一乘法 ("in the buddha lands of the ten directions there is only the one-vehicle Dharma"), adding "ten directions," and also adds 但以假名字，引导于众生 ("only using provisional names to guide beings"), calling the three vehicles mere borrowed names.

verses.en: The Lord of the World appears in the world to make known a buddha's knowledge. There is one task only, no second; the buddhas do not lead beings by a lesser vehicle.
Where the Self-Existent One himself stands, that buddha-knowledge, however it is and whatever it is like, with its powers, meditations, liberations and faculties: right there he sets beings too.
It would be the fault of stinginess in me if, having touched awakening, spotless and supreme, I set even one being in a lesser vehicle. That would not be right for me.
There is no stinginess in me anywhere, no envy, no craving. All bad qualities in me are cut off; that is why I am a buddha, through awakening to the world.

cmp.note: 这句可以读成「我的一切法中，恶的都已断除」，也就是「我身上所有不好的品质都断了」。白话「我在一切法上的恶都已断除」照字面，略显生硬；英文取后一种读法。
cmp.en: This can be read as "among all my qualities, the bad ones are cut off," that is, "every bad quality in me is gone." The plain Chinese 我在一切法上的恶都已断除 ("my evil in all dharmas is cut off") is literal and a little stiff; the English takes the second reading.

verses.en: Since I, adorned with the marks, light up this whole world, and am honored by many hundreds of beings, I teach this seal of the true nature of things.

cmp.note: 「诸法自性之印」。鸠摩罗什译「实相印」，用了他偏爱的「实相」一词；英文 seal of the true nature of things 照梵文。
cmp.en: "The seal of the own-nature of dharmas." Kumarajiva writes 实相印 (shíxiàng yìn, "seal of the true mark"), using his favorite term 实相; the English "seal of the true nature of things" follows the Sanskrit.

verses.en: And this is what I thought, Shariputra: "How could all beings come to be like this, bearing a body with the thirty-two marks (of a great being), shining with their own light, knowers of the world, awakened by themselves?"

cmp.note: 梵文具体说出佛想让众生变成什么样：有三十二相、自身放光、了知世间、自然觉悟。英文、白话照译；鸠摩罗什只概括为「如我等无异」。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit spells out what the Buddha wants beings to become: bearing the thirty-two marks, shining with their own light, knowers of the world, self-awakened. The English and plain Chinese follow it; Kumarajiva sums it up as 如我等无异 (rú wǒ děng wú yì, "no different from me").

verses.en: "As I see, as I think, as I resolved long ago, so this vow of mine is now fulfilled: I make known the buddhas and awakening."
"If, son of Shari, I were to say to beings, 'Raise the wish for awakening,' they would all fail to understand and would wander about confused, and they would never take up my good words."
"I know them to be like this: they did not practice in former lives; they are sunk in sense pleasures and attached to them, stupefied by craving, their minds deluded."

"For the sake of desire they fall into bad destinies, worn out in the six realms of rebirth (gods, humans, asuras, animals, hungry ghosts, hells). Again and again they fill up the cemeteries, crushed by suffering, with little merit."

cmp.note: kaṭasī 是「坟场、尸骨场」，字面是「让坟场一再增多」，即一再死去。英文 fill up the cemeteries、白话「使坟场增多」照字面；鸠摩罗什译作「受胎之微形，世世常增长」，理解完全不同。
cmp.en: Kaṭasī means "cemetery, charnel ground"; literally "they swell the cemeteries again and again," that is, they keep dying. The English "fill up the cemeteries" and the plain Chinese 使坟场增多 ("make the cemeteries grow") are literal; Kumarajiva reads it quite differently: 受胎之微形，世世常增长 (shòu tāi zhī wēi xíng, shìshì cháng zēngzhǎng, "the tiny form conceived in the womb keeps growing life after life").

verses.en: "They are always caught in thickets of views: 'it is,' 'it is not,' 'it both is and is not.' Leaning on the sixty-two views, they hold on to what is not real and stay stuck there."

cmp.note: 「六十二种见解」，指佛经里列举的六十二种错误哲学观点。英文 sixty-two views、白话、鸠摩罗什都照数目译，三方一致。
cmp.en: "Sixty-two views," the list of sixty-two mistaken philosophical positions found in early Buddhist texts. The English "sixty-two views," the plain Chinese and Kumarajiva all keep the number.

verses.en: "They are hard to purify, proud and hypocritical, crooked, deceitful, of little learning and foolish. Not once in thousands of kotis of lives do they hear the Buddha's good voice."
"For them, son of Shari, I speak a skillful means: 'Put an end to suffering.' Seeing beings crushed by suffering, I show them nirvana there."
"And I say this: all these dharmas (things) are forever at rest, calm from the very beginning. A child of the Buddha who completes the practice will become a Victor in time to come."

cmp.note: 梵文只说一切法「永远寂灭、本来寂静」。鸠摩罗什在前面多加了一句「我虽说涅槃，是亦非真灭」，梵本没有。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit simply says all dharmas are "forever at rest, calm from the beginning." Kumarajiva adds a line in front of it that the Sanskrit lacks: 我虽说涅槃，是亦非真灭 (wǒ suī shuō nièpán, shì yì fēi zhēn miè, "though I speak of nirvana, it is not a true extinction").

verses.en: "This is my skill in means: I show three vehicles. But there is only one vehicle, one way, and the teaching of the Guides is one."

cmp.note: yāna 是「车、交通工具」，英文 vehicle、中文「乘」都保留了「载人上路」的画面。这一句是全经的核心：三乘只是展示出来的，实际只有一乘。
cmp.en: Yāna means "a carriage, a conveyance"; the English "vehicle" and the Chinese 乘 (shèng, "a carriage") both keep the image of something that carries people along a road. This line is the heart of the whole sutra: the three vehicles are only shown; in reality there is one.

verses.en: "Put away doubt and hesitation, whoever here has any doubt. The Leaders of the world never say one thing and mean another: this is the one vehicle; there is no second."
"And the Tathagatas who lived before, the many thousands of buddhas who have passed into final nirvana in the past, countless eons ago, there is never any measuring their number."
"All those highest of humans made known many pure teachings, with examples, with reasons and causes, with many hundreds of skillful means."
"And all of them showed the one vehicle; they bring beings into the one vehicle, and within the one vehicle they ripen countless thousands of kotis of living beings."
"The Victors have other skillful means of many kinds by which they make this highest Dharma known, knowing the inclinations and intentions of beings in the world with its gods."
"And the beings who heard the Dharma face to face from them back then, or who had heard it, who gave gifts, kept the precepts, and completed all their practice with patience,"
"who did the groundwork with effort and meditation, or reflected on these teachings with wisdom, who did good deeds of many kinds, all of them gained awakening."

cmp.note: 这一句反复出现。梵文是「他们全都得到了菩提」；鸠摩罗什译作「皆已成佛道」，说成已经成佛，语气更肯定。英文、白话照梵文。
cmp.en: This refrain recurs throughout the passage. The Sanskrit says "all of them gained awakening"; Kumarajiva writes 皆已成佛道 (jiē yǐ chéng fó dào, "all have already attained the buddha way"), which sounds more definite. The English and plain Chinese follow the Sanskrit.

verses.en: "And whatever beings there were in the teaching of those Victors after they had passed into final nirvana, who were patient, self-controlled and disciplined, all of them gained awakening."
"And those who honored the relics of those Victors after their final nirvana, who built many thousands of stupas made of jewels, of gold, silver and crystal,"
"who made stupas of emerald, some of cat's-eye and pearl, of the finest beryl and of sapphire, all of them gained awakening."

cmp.note: 宝石名在三种语言里很难一一对上。英文译作 emerald、cat's-eye；白话作「绿宝石」「猫睛石」；鸠摩罗什用的是汉地习用的「车𤦲」「马脑」等，并非逐一对应。
cmp.en: Gem names are hard to match across the three languages. The English gives "emerald" and "cat's-eye," the plain Chinese 绿宝石 ("green gem") and 猫睛石 ("cat's-eye stone"); Kumarajiva uses familiar Chinese treasure names such as 车𤦲 (chēqú, "giant clam shell") and 马脑 (mǎnǎo, "agate"), which do not correspond one to one.

verses.en: "Those who build stupas in the mountain rock, some of sandalwood and aloeswood, some of deodar (Himalayan cedar), some of joined timber,"
"who joyfully build stupas for the Victors of brick or of piled-up clay, who for their sake heap up mounds of dust in the wilds and wastelands,"
"or the little children who, playing here and there, pile up sand into heaps as stupas for the Victors, all of them gained awakening."
"Likewise, those who had images made of jewels for the buddhas, bearing a body with the thirty-two marks, all of them gained awakening."
"Those who had images of the Sugatas made of the seven precious things, or of copper, or of bronze, all of them gained awakening."
"Those who had figures of the Sugatas made of lead, of iron, or of clay, or lovely ones made of modeled plaster, all of them gained awakening."
"Those who make figures on painted walls, with full bodies and the marks of a hundred merits, whether they paint them themselves or have others paint them, all of them gained awakening."
"And those who back then, while learning, or just amusing themselves at play, scratched figures on walls with a fingernail or a stick, whether grown men or children,"
"all of them became compassionate, all of them carried kotis of living beings across, inspiring many bodhisattvas; all of them gained awakening."
"And those who offered flowers and incense to the relics of the Tathagatas, or to stupas, or to clay figures, or to painted walls, or to a stupa of dust,"
"those who had instruments played there, kettledrums and conch shells and sweet-sounding hand drums, who beat great drums to honor the highest, finest awakening,"
"those who played lutes, cymbals and small drums, clay drums, flutes and lovely reed pipes, whether in a single-minded celebration or as tender children, all of them gained awakening."

cmp.note: 这半句意思不太确定：ekotsava 可能是「一心欢庆」，sukumāraka 是「娇嫩的、小孩子」。英文、白话都按这个读法译；鸠摩罗什没有译这半句。
cmp.en: The sense of this half-line is not quite certain: ekotsava may mean "in a single-minded celebration," and sukumāraka means "tender, a small child." The English and plain Chinese both take it this way; Kumarajiva leaves the half-line out.

verses.en: "those who had small cymbals played, water drums or clapping drums, or who sang a song, well sung, sweet and lovely, to honor the Sugatas,"
"all of them became buddhas in the world, having made those many kinds of offerings to the relics. Even something small offered to the relics of the Sugatas, even having a single instrument played,"
"even honoring the images of the Sugatas on a painted wall with a single flower, even honoring them with a distracted mind, they will see kotis of buddhas in due course."
"And those who joined their palms before a stupa there, even once fully, or just touching palm to palm; who raised their head for a moment, or bowed their body once,"
"who said just once, 'Homage to the Buddha,' before those shrines holding relics, even once with a distracted mind, all of them reached this highest awakening."

cmp.note: 梵文「礼敬佛陀」，鸠摩罗什译作「南无佛」，这三个字后来成了汉地念佛的常用语。鸠摩罗什在这一段前面还多加了「自成无上道……如薪尽火灭」几句，梵本这里没有。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit "Homage to the Buddha" is Kumarajiva's 南无佛 (nāmó fó), which later became a standard Chinese devotional phrase. Before it, Kumarajiva also adds several lines the Sanskrit does not have here, ending with 如薪尽火灭 (rú xīn jìn huǒ miè, "like a fire going out when the firewood is used up").

verses.en: "Whatever beings, back in the time of those Sugatas, whether they had passed into final nirvana or were still alive, heard even the name of the Dharma, all of them gained awakening."

cmp.note: 梵文是「哪怕只听到法的名字」。英文 even the name of the Dharma、白话照译；鸠摩罗什作「若有闻是法」，没有「只是名字」这层意思。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says "even just the name of the Dharma." The English and plain Chinese follow it; Kumarajiva writes 若有闻是法 (ruò yǒu wén shì fǎ, "if anyone hears this Dharma"), dropping the "only the name."

verses.en: "In the future too there will be many kotis of buddhas, beyond thought, beyond measure; those Victors, highest Lords of the World, will also make this skillful means known."
"Those Guides of the world will have endless skill in means, with which they will lead kotis of living beings here into the buddha knowledge free of outflows (defilements)."

"Never will a single being who hears the Dharma from them fail to become a buddha. For this is the vow of the Tathagatas: 'Having practiced for awakening myself, I will lead others to practice for it.'"
"In time to come they will make known many thousands of kotis of doors to the Dharma, showing this one vehicle; they will teach the Dharma that leads to being a Tathagata."
"For this is the lasting rule, the constant way of the Dharma: the nature of all dharmas always shines. Knowing this, the buddhas, highest of two-footed beings, will make my one vehicle known."

cmp.note: 梵文是「诸法的本性永远光明」（原文末尾有残缺，按补读）。英文、白话照译；鸠摩罗什却译作「知法常无性，佛种从缘起」，说法没有固定的本性、佛种从因缘生起，跟梵本意思差得很远。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says "the nature of dharmas always shines" (the end of the line is damaged and restored). The English and plain Chinese follow it; Kumarajiva instead writes 知法常无性，佛种从缘起 (zhī fǎ cháng wú xìng, fó zhǒng cóng yuán qǐ, "knowing that dharmas have no fixed nature, and the seed of buddhahood arises from conditions"), which is far from the Sanskrit.

verses.en: "The standing of the Dharma, the fixed order of the Dharma, stays forever in the world, unshakable. And the buddhas, having awakened on the seat of awakening on the earth, will make this skill in means known."

cmp.note: 「法的安住」「法的定则」，说的是道理本来如此、恒常不变。鸠摩罗什译作「是法住法位，世间相常住」，这两句后来在汉传佛教里非常有名，但「世间相常住」比梵文走得更远。
cmp.en: "The standing of the Dharma" and "the fixed order of the Dharma" say that the way things are holds constant. Kumarajiva writes 是法住法位，世间相常住 (shì fǎ zhù fǎwèi, shìjiān xiàng cháng zhù, "these dharmas abide in their Dharma-position; the marks of the world abide forever"), lines that became famous in Chinese Buddhism, though "the marks of the world abide forever" goes further than the Sanskrit.

verses.en: "In the ten directions there are buddhas, as many as the grains of sand in the Ganges, honored by humans and gods. To bring happiness to all living beings here, they too teach this highest awakening."
"The buddhas make skill in means known; they show various vehicles, and they shed light on the one vehicle, this highest ground of peace."
"Knowing the conduct of all embodied beings, their intentions and what they have practiced before, knowing their effort and strength, and understanding their inclinations, they teach."
"By the power of their knowledge the Guides show many examples and causes, many reasons; knowing that beings have different inclinations, they show different ways of leading them."
"And I too, now, the king of Victors, the Guide, have appeared to bring happiness to beings; I show this buddha awakening in thousands of kotis of different ways."
"I teach the Dharma in many forms, knowing the inclinations and intentions of living beings; I delight them with various skillful means. This is my own power of knowledge, known within myself."
"I see beings who are poor, cut off from wisdom and merit, fallen into the round of rebirth, shut in among dangers, sunk again and again in an unbroken chain of suffering."
"Stuck in craving like a yak with its tail, foolish, blinded here by desires all the time, they do not seek the Buddha of great power, nor look for the Dharma that leads to the end of suffering."

cmp.note: camarī 是牦牛，传说牦牛爱惜自己的尾巴到不惜性命。英文 like a yak with its tail、白话、鸠摩罗什「如牦牛爱尾」都保留了这个比喻。
cmp.en: Camarī is the yak, said to love its own tail so much that it would risk its life for it. The English "like a yak with its tail," the plain Chinese and Kumarajiva's 如牦牛爱尾 (rú máoniú ài wěi, "like a yak loving its tail") all keep the image.

verses.en: "Their minds are hemmed in among the six realms; they stand unshakable in wrong views, running from suffering to suffering. My compassion for them is strong."
"Knowing this, I stayed at the seat of awakening for three full weeks, thinking over this matter, gazing up at the tree there."
"I watched that king of trees without blinking and walked back and forth beneath it: 'This knowledge is wondrous and outstanding, and these beings are blinded by delusion, without understanding.'"
"At that time Brahma begged me, and Shakra (Indra), and the four guardians of the world, Maheshvara and Ishvara too, and thousands of kotis of hosts of wind gods."

cmp.note: marut 是风神群。英文 hosts of wind gods、白话「风神」照字面；鸠摩罗什概括为「余诸天众」。
cmp.en: The maruts are the storm and wind gods. The English "hosts of wind gods" and the plain Chinese 风神 ("wind gods") are literal; Kumarajiva generalizes to 余诸天众 (yú zhū tiān zhòng, "the other hosts of gods").

verses.en: "All stood respectfully with joined palms, and I thought it over: 'What shall I do? I speak in praise of awakening, but these beings are overwhelmed by suffering.'"
"'They will throw out my Dharma as the talk of a fool, and having thrown it out they will go to the bad realms. It would be better for me never to speak at all. Let my peaceful nirvana come today.'"
"Then I remembered the buddhas of the past and how they used skill in means: 'What if I too divide this buddha awakening into three and make it known here?'"
"As I was thinking about this teaching, the other buddhas in the ten directions showed themselves to me and called out, 'Well done!'"
"'Well done, Sage, foremost Guide of the world! Having reached the unsurpassed knowledge here, and thinking about skill in means, you are following the training of the Guides of the world.'"

cmp.note: 梵文呼格「牟尼（圣者）啊」，英文 Sage、白话「牟尼」照译；鸠摩罗什写成「释迦文」，即释迦牟尼的另一种音译，直接点出名字。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit vocative is "O Sage (muni)," rendered by the English "Sage" and the plain Chinese 牟尼 (móuní); Kumarajiva writes 释迦文 (Shìjiāwén), an older transliteration of Shakyamuni, naming him outright.

verses.en: "'We too, back then, made known the highest state of a buddha by dividing it in three. For people of low inclinations and little understanding would not believe it if told, "You will become buddhas."'"
"'So we use a gathering of reasons and practice skill in means; by describing the fruits people long for, we inspire many bodhisattvas.'"

cmp.note: 梵文说用方便「引导许多菩萨」。鸠摩罗什译作「虽复说三乘，但为教菩萨」，把意思说得更直白：说三乘只是为了教化菩萨。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says that by skillful means "we inspire many bodhisattvas." Kumarajiva says it more bluntly: 虽复说三乘，但为教菩萨 (suī fù shuō sānshèng, dàn wèi jiào púsà, "though we speak of three vehicles, it is only to teach bodhisattvas").

verses.en: "Hearing the lovely voice of those bulls among men, I was elated then, and with a joyful heart I said to those protectors: 'The excellent great seers do not speak falsely.'"

cmp.note: 梵文是佛对诸佛说「大仙人们说的不是虚妄的话」。鸠摩罗什改成「喜称南无佛」，变成欢喜地念「南无佛」。
cmp.en: In the Sanskrit the Buddha tells the other buddhas, "the great seers do not speak falsely." Kumarajiva changes this to 喜称南无佛 (xǐ chēng nāmó fó, "joyfully I said, 'Homage to the Buddha'").

verses.en: "'I too will act this way, just as the wise Guides of the world say. I too have appeared in this cruel upheaval, in the midst of the corruption of beings.'"
"Then, son of Shari, knowing this, I set out at that time for Varanasi, and there I taught the five monks the Dharma, the ground of peace, by skillful means."

cmp.note: 「五位比丘」，即佛陀成道后最早度化的五个同修。鸠摩罗什在这里多加了「诸法寂灭相，不可以言宣」两句，梵本没有。
cmp.en: "The five monks," the Buddha's five former companions, the first he taught after his awakening. Kumarajiva adds two lines here that are not in the Sanskrit: 诸法寂灭相，不可以言宣 (zhū fǎ jìmiè xiàng, bù kěyǐ yán xuān, "the stillness of all dharmas cannot be put into words").

verses.en: "From that moment my wheel of the Dharma began to turn, and the word 'nirvana' came into the world, and there too the word 'arhat,' the word 'Dharma,' and the word 'Sangha' (the community)."
"For many years I taught and showed the ground of nirvana, and I always said: 'This is the end of the suffering of the round of rebirth.'"

cmp.note: 梵文是「许多年」。英文、白话照译；鸠摩罗什作「从久远劫来」，从「多年」放大成「无数劫」。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says "for many years." The English and plain Chinese follow it; Kumarajiva writes 从久远劫来 (cóng jiǔyuǎn jié lái, "since eons long ago"), stretching years into eons.

verses.en: "And when, Shariputra, I saw the sons of the highest of two-footed beings who had set out for the highest awakening, many thousands of kotis of them,"
"they all came up to me and stood respectfully with joined palms, those who had heard the Dharma from the Victors, skill in means of many kinds."
"Then at that very moment I thought: 'Now is my time to speak the highest Dharma, the reason I was born here in the world. Here I will make that highest awakening known.'"
"'Today this will be hard to believe for those of childish minds who hold on to signs and appearances, who are full of conceit and lack understanding. But these bodhisattvas will listen.'"
"Then, fearless and delighted, putting aside all hesitation, I spoke among the children of the Sugata and inspired them toward awakening."

cmp.note: 梵文是「抛开一切畏缩」。鸠摩罗什译作「正直舍方便，但说无上道」，说成「舍弃方便」，这是汉传佛教常引的一句，但梵本这里说的是舍弃退缩，不是舍弃方便。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says "putting aside all hesitation." Kumarajiva writes 正直舍方便，但说无上道 (zhèngzhí shě fāngbiàn, dàn shuō wúshàng dào, "honestly setting aside skillful means, I teach only the unsurpassed way"), a line much quoted in Chinese Buddhism; but what is set aside in the Sanskrit is timidity, not skillful means.

verses.en: "Seeing such children of the Buddha, your doubt too will be removed; and these twelve hundred, free of outflows, will all become buddhas in the world."
"Just as is the nature of the Dharma for those protectors of the past and the Victors of the future, so it is for me too, free of division; just so I teach you today."
"Rarely, somewhere, somehow, do bulls among men appear in the world; and once they have appeared in the world, those of endless vision only rarely teach a Dharma like this."
"A highest Dharma like this is very hard to come by, even in kotis of nayutas of eons; and very hard to find are beings who, hearing the highest Dharma, believe it."
"Just as the udumbara flower is hard to find, seen only rarely, somewhere, somehow, lovely to look at, a wonder to the world with its gods,"

cmp.note: udumbara 是一种无花果树，花藏在果里看不见，所以传说「极难得见」。英文保留原名，白话、鸠摩罗什用音译「优昙（钵）花」。
cmp.en: The udumbara is a kind of fig tree whose flowers are hidden inside the fruit, hence the legend that its flower is almost never seen. The English keeps the name, and the plain Chinese and Kumarajiva transliterate it as 优昙花 (yōután huā).

verses.en: "I say something even more wonderful than that: whoever hears this well-spoken Dharma, rejoices in it and says even one word has made an offering to all the buddhas."
"Put away doubt and hesitation here. I, the king of the Dharma, declare: I inspire beings toward the highest awakening; here I have no disciples (shravakas) at all."

cmp.note: 字面是「我这里没有任何声闻」。意思是：被叫作「声闻」的弟子，其实全是走向成佛的人。白话加了「（只当）」来补这层意思；英文照字面，靠上下文。
cmp.en: Literally "here I have no shravakas at all." The point is that the disciples called shravakas are in fact all on the way to buddhahood. The plain Chinese inserts （只当） ("merely") to bring this out; the English stays literal and relies on context.

verses.en: "Shariputra, let this be a secret for you, and for all my disciples; and let these foremost bodhisattvas keep this secret of mine."
"Why? Because in the time of the five corruptions beings are mean and wicked, blinded here by desires, childish in mind; they never turn their minds to awakening."

cmp.note: 「五浊」：劫浊、见浊、烦恼浊、众生浊、命浊，指末世的五种污浊。英文 five corruptions、白话、鸠摩罗什都照译。
cmp.en: "The five corruptions" (or five turbidities): of the age, of views, of afflictions, of beings, and of lifespan, the marks of a degenerate time. The English "five corruptions," the plain Chinese and Kumarajiva all translate it directly.

verses.en: "And in time to come, hearing that this one vehicle of mine was made known by that Victor, beings will be confused; they will throw out the sutra and go to hell."
"But to beings who have a sense of shame and are pure, who have set out for the highest awakening, I will fearlessly speak endless praise of the one vehicle."
"Such is the teaching of the Guides; this is the finest skill in means. It is spoken in many words with hidden meaning, and the untrained find it hard to understand."
"So understand the words with hidden meaning of the buddhas, teachers and protectors of the world; drop your doubt, cast off hesitation: you will become buddhas. Be glad!"
This is the second chapter, called Skillful Means, in the noble Dharma discourse of the Lotus of the True Dharma.

cmp.note: 梵本这一品是第二品，本站把开经题记算作第一章，所以排在第三章。英文、白话照梵文写「第二」。
cmp.en: In the Sanskrit this is the second chapter; the site counts the opening title and homage as chapter 1, so it appears as chapter 3 here. The English and plain Chinese keep the Sanskrit "second."

verses.en: Then at that moment the venerable Shariputra, pleased, uplifted, delighted, overjoyed, full of joy and gladness, joined his palms toward the Blessed One, faced him, and gazing at the Blessed One said to him: "Blessed One, I am filled with wonder and amazement, I am in rapture, having heard such words from the Blessed One. Why? Before I heard this kind of teaching from the Blessed One, Blessed One, I saw other bodhisattvas and heard the names they will have as buddhas in the future, and I grieved terribly and was tormented terribly: I had lost the Tathagata's range of knowledge, his knowing and seeing.

cmp.note: audbilya 是佛教梵文里「狂喜、雀跃」的意思。英文 in rapture、白话「心中涌起狂喜」照译；鸠摩罗什作「心怀勇跃」。
cmp.en: Audbilya is Buddhist Sanskrit for "elation, exultant joy." The English "in rapture" and the plain Chinese 心中涌起狂喜 ("rapture welled up in my heart") follow it; Kumarajiva says 心怀勇跃 (xīn huái yǒngyuè, "my heart leapt").

verses.en: "And Blessed One, whenever I went off to mountains, caves, thickets, parks, riverbanks and the roots of trees, lonely places, to spend the day, even then, Blessed One, I mostly spent my time thinking this: 'We have entered the same realm of the Dharma, yet the Blessed One has led us out by a lesser vehicle.' And Blessed One, then I would think: 'This is our own fault, not the Blessed One's fault. Why? If we had waited for the Blessed One while he gave the highest teaching of the Dharma, the one that has unsurpassed, perfect awakening as its aim, we would have gone forth in those teachings.'

cmp.note: 「低劣的乘」，英文 lesser vehicle、白话「低劣的乘」照字面。鸠摩罗什译「小乘法」，后来成了常用词，带贬义的意味比原文更固定。
cmp.en: "By an inferior vehicle." The English "lesser vehicle" and the plain Chinese 低劣的乘 ("an inferior vehicle") are literal. Kumarajiva's 小乘法 (xiǎoshèng fǎ, "the Dharma of the Small Vehicle") later became a stock term, fixing a put-down that is looser in the Sanskrit.

cmp.note: 英文 realm of the Dharma、白话「法界（真理的领域）」；鸠摩罗什作「法性」，指诸法的本性，意思相近但不是同一个词。
cmp.en: The English "realm of the Dharma" and the plain Chinese 法界 (fǎjiè, "Dharma realm") are close to the word; Kumarajiva writes 法性 (fǎxìng, "the nature of things"), similar in meaning but a different term.

verses.en: "But Blessed One, when the bodhisattvas were not present, we did not understand that the Blessed One was speaking with a hidden intent. In a hurry, as soon as we heard the Tathagata's first teaching of the Dharma, we took it up, kept it, practiced it, thought it over and fixed our minds on it. So, Blessed One, I have spent most of my days and nights just blaming myself. Today, Blessed One, I have reached nirvana. Today, Blessed One, I have fully passed into peace. Today, Blessed One, I have reached arhatship. Today, Blessed One, I am the Blessed One's son, his eldest, his own child, born from his mouth, born of the Dharma, made by the Dharma, heir to the Dharma, brought to completion by the Dharma. Today, Blessed One, my burning is gone, having heard from the Blessed One these words, this wonderful Dharma never heard before."

cmp.note: 梵文舍利弗说「今天我才得到涅槃、才证得阿罗汉果」，英文、白话照译；鸠摩罗什只写「快得安隐」「今日乃知真是佛子」，没有译「今天才证阿罗汉」这几句。
cmp.en: In the Sanskrit Shariputra says "today I have reached nirvana, today I have reached arhatship," and the English and plain Chinese follow it; Kumarajiva writes only 快得安隐 (kuài dé ānyǐn, "I have quickly found peace") and 今日乃知真是佛子 ("today I know I am truly the Buddha's son"), leaving out the lines about attaining arhatship today.

verses.en: Then at that moment the venerable Shariputra spoke to the Blessed One in these verses:
"Great Guide, I am filled with wonder and rapture on hearing these words. I have no doubt left at all; I have been ripened here in the highest vehicle."

"The voice of the Sugatas (the Well-Gone Ones) is wonderful; it takes away the doubt and grief of living beings. I had already ended the outflows (the defilements), yet whatever grief I had is all gone now that I have heard this voice."
"Spending the day walking up and down in thickets, parks and at the roots of trees, or staying in mountain caves, I kept turning over this one thought:"
"'Ah, I have been cheated by my own wrong thoughts! Though the teachings without outflows are the same, I will not teach the highest Dharma in the three worlds in the future.'"

cmp.note: 「被坏念头欺骗了」。英文、白话都译成被自己的错误念头所骗；鸠摩罗什作「云何而自欺」，变成反问自己。
cmp.en: "Cheated by wrong thoughts." The English and plain Chinese both say he was deceived by his own wrong thinking; Kumarajiva turns it into a rhetorical question, 云何而自欺 (yúnhé ér zì qī, "why did I deceive myself?").

verses.en: "'I have lost the thirty-two marks (the special features of a buddha's body), I have lost the golden sheen of the skin; the powers and the liberations have all slipped away from me. Though the teachings are the same, ah, how deluded I am!'"
"'The eighty minor marks of the great sages, perfect, excellent, distinguished, and the eighteen qualities found only in a buddha, these too I have lost. Ah, I have been cheated!'"
"Seeing you, who care for the world and feel for it, I would go off alone to spend the day and think: 'Alas, I have been cheated, shut out from that unobstructed, inconceivable knowledge.'"
"Protector, I spent my nights and days mostly thinking just this. I wanted to ask the Blessed One himself: 'Have I lost it, or not?'"
"Lord of Victors, thinking like this, my nights and days went by, all the time, as I saw many other bodhisattvas praised by the Guide of the World."

"And now that I have heard this teaching of the Buddha, I see that it was spoken with a hidden intent: the Victor at the seat of awakening points to a knowledge beyond reasoning, subtle and without outflows."

cmp.note: saṃdhāya 的变体，意为「带着深意、有所指地」。英文 with a hidden intent、白话「带着深意」照译；鸠摩罗什作「随宜而说法」，解释成因人说法。
cmp.en: A variant of saṃdhāya, "with an intended meaning." The English "with a hidden intent" and the plain Chinese 带着深意 ("with deep intent") follow it; Kumarajiva gives 随宜而说法 (suíyí ér shuōfǎ, "teaching as suits the occasion").

verses.en: "Before, I was caught up in views; I was a wandering ascetic, respected by the outsiders (followers of other sects). Then the Protector, knowing my disposition, spoke of nirvana to free me from views."

cmp.note: 梵文说舍利弗曾是游方修行人，「受外道敬重」；鸠摩罗什作「为诸梵志师」，说他是婆罗门修行者的老师，比原文更进一步。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says Shariputra had been a wandering ascetic "respected by the outsiders"; Kumarajiva writes 为诸梵志师 (wéi zhū fànzhì shī, "a teacher of the brahmin ascetics"), going a step further than the original.

verses.en: "Having freed myself completely from all those views and come in contact with the emptiness of things, I thought, 'I have reached peace.' But this is not what is called nirvana."

"When one becomes a buddha, the highest of beings, honored by humans, gods, yakshas (fierce spirits) and rakshasas (man-eating demons), bearing a body with the thirty-two marks, then one has reached peace without remainder."
"All my fancies are gone, and having heard your voice I am at peace today, now that you predict me to the highest awakening before the world with its gods."
"When I first heard the Guide's words, I was badly frightened: 'Could this be Mara (the tempter) come to torment me, having taken on the look of a buddha here on earth?'"

cmp.note: 「惊恐、发呆」。英文 badly frightened、白话「非常惊恐」照译；鸠摩罗什作「大惊疑」，多了一层怀疑。
cmp.en: "Being stunned with fright." The English "badly frightened" and the plain Chinese 非常惊恐 ("greatly terrified") follow it; Kumarajiva's 大惊疑 (dà jīngyí, "great alarm and doubt") adds a layer of suspicion.

verses.en: "But when the excellent awakening of the buddhas was shown with reasons and causes and kotis of nayutas (huge numbers) of illustrations, and was set firmly in place, then hearing the Dharma I was free of doubt."
"And when you tell of thousands of kotis of buddhas, Victors who have passed into final nirvana, and how they taught this Dharma, standing firm in skillful means,"
"and how the many buddhas of the future, and those now living in the world who see the highest truth, will show and do teach the Dharma with hundreds of skillful means,"

"and you have told of your own conduct, what it was like from the time you left home, and what kind of buddha you are, and what kind of Dharma wheel you turn, and how your teaching of the Dharma is arranged,"
"then I know this is not Mara: the Lord of the World is showing the true way of practice. Maras have no access here at all; it was my own mind that had fallen into doubt."

cmp.note: 英文 Mara、白话「魔」都用通称；鸠摩罗什在这里用了魔王的名字「波旬」（Pāpīyas）。
cmp.en: The English "Mara" and the plain Chinese 魔 (mó, "demon") use the general term; Kumarajiva here uses the demon king's personal name, 波旬 (Bōxún, Pāpīyas, "the Evil One").

verses.en: "And when I was made glad by the Buddha's voice, sweet, deep and lovely, all my uncertainties were crushed, doubt was gone, and I stood firm in knowledge."
"Without doubt I will become a Tathagata, honored in this world with its gods. With hidden intent I will speak of this awakening of the buddhas, encouraging many bodhisattvas."

cmp.note: 「我将带着深意宣说」，英文、白话照译；鸠摩罗什改成「转无上法轮」，没有「深意」这一层。
cmp.en: "I will speak with hidden intent"; the English and plain Chinese follow it. Kumarajiva changes it to 转无上法轮 (zhuǎn wúshàng fǎlún, "turn the unsurpassed Dharma wheel"), dropping the idea of hidden intent.

verses.en: When he had said this, the Blessed One said to the venerable Shariputra: "Shariputra, I tell you, I declare to you, before this world with its gods, its Maras and its Brahmas, before all people, with their ascetics and brahmins: Shariputra, in the presence of twenty hundred thousand kotis of nayutas (huge numbers) of buddhas, I ripened you for unsurpassed, perfect awakening. And for a long time, Shariputra, you trained under me. Shariputra, it was through the bodhisattvas' counsel, the bodhisattvas' secret, that you were born here into my teaching. Shariputra, because of the bodhisattvas' sustaining power, you do not remember your former practice and vow, that counsel and secret of the bodhisattvas, and you think, 'I have reached nirvana.'

cmp.note: 「菩萨的秘密」：梵文说舍利弗是因菩萨的秘密安排才生在佛的教法中，又因菩萨的加持而忘了本愿。英文、白话照译；鸠摩罗什概括成「我以方便引导汝故」，把秘密说成佛的方便。
cmp.en: "The bodhisattvas' secret": the Sanskrit says Shariputra was born into the Buddha's teaching through a secret arrangement of the bodhisattvas, and forgot his vow through their sustaining power. The English and plain Chinese follow it; Kumarajiva sums it up as 我以方便引导汝故 (wǒ yǐ fāngbiàn yǐndǎo rǔ gù, "because I guided you by skillful means"), turning the secret into the Buddha's skillful means.

cmp.note: 梵文是二十个百千俱胝那由他尊佛；鸠摩罗什作「二万亿佛」，数目不同。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit has twenty hundred-thousand kotis of nayutas of buddhas; Kumarajiva gives 二万亿佛 (èrwàn yì fó, "twenty thousand hundred-millions of buddhas"), a different figure.

verses.en: "Shariputra, because I want you to remember the understanding of your former practice and vow, I am making known to the disciples this Dharma discourse, the Lotus of the True Dharma, a sutra of great breadth, an instruction for bodhisattvas, embraced by all the buddhas."

cmp.note: 「极其广大的（经）」，英文 of great breadth、白话「极其广大的经」照字面；鸠摩罗什译成「大乘经」，换成了另一个概念。
cmp.en: "Of great breadth." The English "a sutra of great breadth" and the plain Chinese 极其广大的经 ("an extremely vast sutra") are literal; Kumarajiva renders it 大乘经 (dàshèng jīng, "a Great Vehicle sutra"), swapping in a different idea.

verses.en: "And further, Shariputra, in the future, after countless, inconceivable, immeasurable eons (kalpas), having kept the true Dharma of many hundred thousand kotis of nayutas of Tathagatas, having made many kinds of offerings and completed this very bodhisattva practice, you will become a Tathagata in the world named Padmaprabha (Lotus Light), an arhat, a fully awakened buddha, perfect in knowledge and conduct, the Sugata, knower of the world, unsurpassed, tamer of those who can be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a buddha, a Blessed One."

cmp.note: padma 是红莲，prabha 是光。英文 Lotus Light、白话「莲华光」照字面；鸠摩罗什简作「华光」，莲变成了泛称的花。
cmp.en: Padma is the lotus and prabha is light. The English "Lotus Light" and the plain Chinese 莲华光 (Liánhuá Guāng, "Lotus Light") are literal; Kumarajiva shortens it to 华光 (Huá Guāng, "Flower Light"), so the lotus becomes just a flower.

verses.en: "At that time, Shariputra, the buddha field of that Blessed One, the Tathagata Padmaprabha, will be called Viraja (Free of Dust). It will be level, lovely, pleasing, most beautiful to see, pure, flourishing, prosperous, safe, with plenty of food, crowded with many men and women, and full of gods. It will be made of beryl and marked off in a checkerboard by golden cords. On those squares there will be trees of jewels, always laden with flowers and fruits of the seven precious things."

cmp.note: aṣṭāpada 是一种棋盘，指大地用金绳划成方格。英文 checkerboard、白话「棋盘般的方格」照字面；鸠摩罗什作「八交道」，按字面「八」理解成八条交叉的道路。
cmp.en: Aṣṭāpada is a kind of game board, here meaning the ground is marked into squares by golden cords. The English "checkerboard" and the plain Chinese 棋盘般的方格 ("checkerboard squares") follow it; Kumarajiva writes 八交道 (bā jiāo dào, "eight crossing roads"), reading the "eight" in the word literally.

verses.en: "And Shariputra, that Tathagata Padmaprabha, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, will teach the Dharma in terms of the three vehicles. Shariputra, although that Tathagata will not appear in an eon of corruption, he will still teach the Dharma this way because of his vow. Shariputra, that eon will be called Maharatnapratimandita (Adorned with Great Jewels). What do you think, Shariputra, why is that eon called Adorned with Great Jewels? Shariputra, in a buddha field, bodhisattvas are called jewels. At that time in that world Viraja there will be many bodhisattvas, countless, innumerable, inconceivable, beyond comparison, beyond measure, beyond all counting except the counting of a Tathagata. For that reason the eon is called Adorned with Great Jewels."

"At that time, Shariputra, the bodhisattvas in that buddha field will mostly walk on jewel lotuses. And those bodhisattvas will not be beginners: they will have practiced the roots of goodness for a long time, led the pure life under many hundred thousands of buddhas, been praised by the Tathagatas, be devoted to the knowledge of the buddhas, be born of the practice of the great higher knowledges, skilled in the ways of all things, gentle and mindful. Shariputra, that buddha field will be full mostly of bodhisattvas like these."

"And Shariputra, the lifespan of the Tathagata Padmaprabha will be twelve intermediate eons, not counting his time as a prince. The lifespan of the beings there will be eight intermediate eons. And Shariputra, after twelve intermediate eons have passed, the Tathagata Padmaprabha will predict the bodhisattva, great being Dhritiparipurna (Full of Resolve) to unsurpassed, perfect awakening and then pass into final nirvana, saying: 'Monks, this bodhisattva, great being Dhritiparipurna will awaken to unsurpassed, perfect awakening right after me. He will become a Tathagata in the world named Padmavrishabhavikramin (Striding Like a Bull on Lotuses), an arhat, a fully awakened buddha, perfect in knowledge and conduct, the Sugata, knower of the world, unsurpassed, tamer of those who can be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a buddha, a Blessed One.'

cmp.note: 「中间劫」。英文 intermediate eons、白话「中劫」照字面；鸠摩罗什作「小劫」，名称不同。
cmp.en: "Intermediate eon." The English "intermediate eons" and the plain Chinese 中劫 (zhōngjié, "middle eon") are literal; Kumarajiva calls it 小劫 (xiǎojié, "small eon").

cmp.note: 「像公牛一样在莲花上迈步的人」。英文、白话保留了公牛的意象；鸠摩罗什作「华足安行」，公牛不见了。
cmp.en: "One who strides on lotuses like a bull." The English and plain Chinese keep the bull; Kumarajiva's 华足安行 (Huázú Ānxíng, "Flower-Footed Calm Walker") drops it.

verses.en: "Shariputra, the buddha field of that Tathagata Padmavrishabhavikramin will be just the same."

"And Shariputra, after the Tathagata Padmaprabha has passed into final nirvana, the true Dharma will last for thirty-two intermediate eons. Then, when the true Dharma has worn away, a likeness of the true Dharma will last for thirty-two intermediate eons."

cmp.note: 「正法的仿制品、相似的正法」。英文 a likeness of the true Dharma、白话「相似的正法」照字面；鸠摩罗什译成「像法」，后来成了「正法、像法、末法」三时说的专名。
cmp.en: "A counterfeit or likeness of the true Dharma." The English "a likeness of the true Dharma" and the plain Chinese 相似的正法 ("a resembling true Dharma") are literal; Kumarajiva's 像法 (xiàngfǎ, "semblance Dharma") later became a technical term in the Chinese scheme of three ages of the Dharma.

verses.en: Then at that moment the Blessed One spoke these verses: "Son of Shari, you too will be a Victor, a Tathagata, in the future, named Padmaprabha, the one whose eye sees everywhere, and you will guide thousands of kotis of living beings."

cmp.note: 「舍利（Śārī，他母亲的名字）之子」，就是舍利弗（Śāriputra）的另一种说法。英文 Son of Shari 照字面；白话加了括注。
cmp.en: "Son of Shari" (Shari was his mother's name), simply another form of Shariputra. The English "Son of Shari" is literal, and the plain Chinese adds a note.

verses.en: "Having honored many kotis of buddhas and gained there the strength of practice, and having brought forth the ten powers, you will touch the highest, supreme awakening."
"After an inconceivable, measureless eon, there will be an eon called Prabhutaratna (Abundant Jewels), and the world will be called Viraja, the pure field of the best of two-footed beings."

cmp.note: 偈颂里劫名是「多宝」（Prabhūtaratna），跟前面散文的「大宝庄严」不同。英文、白话照偈颂译；鸠摩罗什统一成「大宝严」。
cmp.en: In the verse the eon is called Prabhutaratna ("Abundant Jewels"), not the "Adorned with Great Jewels" of the prose. The English and plain Chinese follow the verse; Kumarajiva makes them match with 大宝严 (Dà Bǎo Yán, "Great Jewel Adornment").

verses.en: "The ground will be covered with beryl and adorned with golden cords, with hundreds of trees made of jewels, beautiful to see, adorned with fruits and flowers."
"Many mindful bodhisattvas will be there, well versed in bringing practice and vow to fulfillment. Those who have trained in practice under hundreds of buddhas will be born in that field."
"And that Victor, in his last body, having passed through the time of a prince, will give up pleasures, leave home, and touch the highest, supreme awakening."
"The lifespan of that Victor will be twelve intermediate eons in all, and the lifespan of the people there will be eight intermediate eons."
"After that Victor has passed into final nirvana, the true Dharma will remain at that time for a full thirty-two intermediate eons, for the good of the world with its gods."
"When the true Dharma has worn away, its likeness will remain for thirty-two intermediate eons. The relics of that protector will be spread far and wide, always honored by humans and gods."
"Such will that Blessed One be. Be glad, son of Shari: you yourself will be that one, unconquered, the highest of two-footed beings."

Then the four assemblies, monks, nuns, laymen and laywomen, along with gods, nagas, yakshas, gandharvas, asuras, garudas, kinnaras and mahoragas (eight kinds of spirit beings), humans and non-humans, having heard face to face from the Blessed One this prediction of the venerable Shariputra to unsurpassed, perfect awakening, were pleased, uplifted, delighted, overjoyed, full of joy and gladness, and covered the Blessed One with their own robes. Shakra, lord of the gods, and Brahma, Lord of the Saha world, and other hundreds of thousands of kotis of sons of the gods covered the Blessed One with heavenly garments and scattered heavenly mandarava flowers and great mandarava flowers over him. They whirled heavenly garments up in the sky, and up in the sky they played hundreds of thousands of heavenly instruments and drums.

cmp.note: 梵文是众人用自己的衣服「覆盖」世尊。英文、白话照译；鸠摩罗什作「脱身所着上衣，以供养佛」，变成脱衣供养。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says they "covered" the Blessed One with their own robes. The English and plain Chinese follow it; Kumarajiva writes 脱身所着上衣，以供养佛 (tuō shēn suǒ zhuó shàngyī, yǐ gòngyǎng fó, "took off their upper robes to offer to the Buddha").

verses.en: Having rained down a great rain of flowers, they said: "Long ago the Blessed One turned the wheel of the Dharma at Varanasi, in the Deer Park at Rishipatana. Today the Blessed One has turned the second, unsurpassed wheel of the Dharma." And at that moment those sons of the gods spoke these verses:
"Great hero beyond compare, you turned the wheel of the Dharma in the world at Varanasi: the arising and passing away of the heaps (skandhas, the parts that make up a person)."

cmp.note: 梵文这里只说讲了「诸蕴的生灭」。英文、白话照译；鸠摩罗什另加了「转四谛法轮」，点明是四谛。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says only that he taught "the arising and passing of the heaps." The English and plain Chinese follow it; Kumarajiva adds 转四谛法轮 (zhuǎn sìdì fǎlún, "turned the Dharma wheel of the four truths"), naming the four noble truths.

verses.en: "There you turned it the first time; here, Guide, the second. Today, Guide, you have taught what is hard for them to believe."
"We have heard much Dharma in the presence of the Lord of the World, but we have never before heard a Dharma like this."
"Great hero, we rejoice in the great seer's speech with hidden intent, for the fearless Shariputra has been given a true prediction."
"May we too become such unsurpassed buddhas in the world, teaching the unsurpassed awakening of the buddhas with hidden intent."
"Whatever we have heard and done, in this world or another, and whatever has pleased the Buddha, may it become our aspiration for awakening."

cmp.note: 「愿它成为求觉悟的心愿」。英文、白话照译；鸠摩罗什作「尽回向佛道」，用了「回向」这个专门词。
cmp.en: "May it become an aspiration for awakening." The English and plain Chinese follow it; Kumarajiva uses the technical term 回向 (huíxiàng, "dedicate merit toward"): 尽回向佛道 ("dedicate it all to the buddha way").

verses.en: Then the venerable Shariputra said to the Blessed One: "Blessed One, I have no doubt left, no uncertainty, now that I have heard face to face from the Blessed One my own prediction to unsurpassed, perfect awakening. But Blessed One, these twelve hundred who have mastered themselves were earlier placed by the Blessed One on the level of training, and were instructed and taught like this: 'Monks, my Dharma and discipline comes down to this: going beyond birth, old age, sickness, death and grief, and arriving at nirvana.' And Blessed One, these two thousand monks, the Blessed One's disciples in training and beyond training, are all free of the view of a self, the view of being, the view of non-being, and every other view, and they think of themselves, 'We stand on the level of nirvana.' Having heard from the Blessed One this kind of Dharma never heard before, they have fallen into doubt."
"So, Blessed One, please speak to these monks to dispel their regret, so that, Blessed One, these four assemblies may be free of doubt and uncertainty."

When he had said this, the Blessed One said to the venerable Shariputra: "Shariputra, did I not tell you before that the Tathagata, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, teaches the Dharma by knowing the disposition of beings, who have various inclinations and various natures and dispositions, and uses various accomplishments, explanations, many kinds of causes and reasons, examples, grounds, words and skillful means? With all his teaching of the Dharma he aims at this unsurpassed, perfect awakening, and leads them only into the bodhisattva vehicle. But Shariputra, I will give you a parable to show this same point even more fully. Why? Because here some intelligent people understand the meaning of what is said through a parable."

"Shariputra, suppose that in some village, town, market town, district, region, kingdom or royal capital there were a householder, old, aged, advanced in years, well past his prime, rich, very wealthy, with great possessions. He has a great house, high and wide, built long ago and run down, home to two, three, four or five hundred living beings. The house has a single door. It is roofed with thatch, its upper rooms have fallen in, the bases of its pillars are rotten, and the plaster of its walls and screens has crumbled. And suddenly the whole house is set ablaze on all sides by a great mass of fire. And the man has many little children, five or ten or twenty.

cmp.w: pañca vā daśa vā viṃśatir vā
cmp.note: 梵文说孩子有「五个、十个或二十个」，英文、白话照译；鸠摩罗什作「若十、二十，或至三十」，人数都往上加了。住在宅中的「两三四五百个生灵」，他也改成「一百、二百乃至五百人」。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says the children number "five or ten or twenty," and the English and plain Chinese follow it; Kumarajiva has 若十、二十，或至三十 ("ten, twenty, or even thirty"), raising every figure. The "two, three, four or five hundred living beings" in the house likewise become 一百、二百乃至五百人 ("one, two, up to five hundred people").

cmp.note: 梵文用 prāṇin「生灵、有生命的」，不只是人；英文 living beings、白话「生灵」照译；鸠摩罗什作「人众」。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit uses prāṇin, "living creatures," not only people; the English "living beings" and the plain Chinese 生灵 (shēnglíng, "living creatures") follow it, while Kumarajiva says 人众 (rénzhòng, "people").

verses.en: "And the man has gone out of the house and is outside."

cmp.note: 梵文明说父亲已经在宅子外面了。英文、白话照译；鸠摩罗什本没有这一句，后文只说他「能于此所烧之门安隐得出」，读起来像他还在屋里。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says plainly that the father is already outside the house; the English and plain Chinese follow it. Kumarajiva's version lacks this line, and later says only that he could 安隐得出 (ānyǐn dé chū, "get out safely") by the burning door, which reads as if he were still inside.

verses.en: "Then, Shariputra, seeing his own house blazing all around with a great mass of fire, the man is frightened, terrified, his mind shaken, and he thinks: 'I am able to get out of this burning house through the door and run out quickly and safely, untouched and unburned by this great mass of fire. But these boys, my own young children, are right here in this burning house, playing with this toy and that, enjoying themselves, having fun. They do not know, do not realize, do not notice, do not grasp that the house is on fire, and they are not alarmed. Even though they are being scorched by this great mass of fire and touched by a great mass of suffering, they pay no attention to the pain, and they do not even think of getting out.'

"And Shariputra, the man is strong, with powerful arms. He thinks: 'I am strong, with powerful arms. Why don't I gather all these children together, take them in my arms, and carry them out of this house?' But then he thinks: 'This house has only one entrance, and the door is shut. And the children are restless, fidgety, just little children. They might run around and come to grief in this great mass of fire. Better that I warn them.' Having thought this over, he calls to the children: 'Come here, children, come out! This house is burning with a great mass of fire. Don't all get burned up here by this great fire and come to grief!'

cmp.note: 梵文是「抱在怀里」带出去。英文 take them in my arms、白话「抱在怀里」照译；鸠摩罗什作「以衣裓、若以机案，从舍出之」，变成用衣襟或几案把孩子运出去。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says to carry them out "in my lap," in his arms. The English "take them in my arms" and the plain Chinese 抱在怀里 ("hold them in my arms") follow it; Kumarajiva writes 以衣裓、若以机案，从舍出之 ("carry them out of the house on a cloth or on a table").

cmp.note: 梵文说门「是关着的」；鸠摩罗什作「唯有一门，而复狭小」，说门很窄。英文、白话照梵文。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says the door is "shut"; Kumarajiva says 唯有一门，而复狭小 ("there is only one door, and it is narrow"). The English and plain Chinese follow the Sanskrit.

verses.en: "But the children do not understand what this man who wants their good is saying. They are not alarmed, not frightened, not scared, they feel no fear; they don't think about it, they don't run out. They don't even know or understand what this 'burning' is. Instead they just run this way and that, and look at their father again and again. Why? Because they are so childish."

"Then the man thinks: 'This house is ablaze, burning with a great mass of fire. I don't want me and these children to come to grief right here in this great fire. Why don't I get these children out of the house by skillful means?' The man knows the children's minds and understands what they like. And the children have many toys of many kinds, all sorts of lovely things that they want, love, like and enjoy, and these are hard to come by."

"Then the man, knowing the children's minds, says to them: 'Children, those toys of yours, lovely, wonderful, amazing, the ones you're upset not to have, of many colors and many kinds, like little ox carts, little goat carts and little deer carts, the ones you want, love, like and enjoy, I have put them all outside the door of the house for you to play with. Come on, run out of this house! I will give each one of you whatever you want and need. Come quickly for them, run out!'

cmp.note: 梵文的次序是牛车、羊车、鹿车，英文、白话照这个次序；鸠摩罗什作「羊车、鹿车、牛车」，后来汉传把三车分别配给声闻、缘觉、菩萨，就依他的次序。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit order is ox carts, goat carts, deer carts, and the English and plain Chinese keep it; Kumarajiva gives 羊车、鹿车、牛车 (yáng chē, lù chē, niú chē, "goat cart, deer cart, ox cart"), and later Chinese tradition matched the three carts to the three vehicles following his order.

verses.en: "Then, hearing the names of those toys, lovely, just what they wished and longed for, wanted, loved, liked and enjoyed, the children quickly set to it, and with all their strength and speed, not waiting for one another, shoving each other as they jostled, 'Who's first? Who's the very first?', they ran out of the burning house in no time."

"Then the man, seeing that the children have got out safe and sound and knowing that they are out of danger, sits down in the open at the village crossroads, full of joy and gladness, free of worry, free of obstacles, free of fear. Then the children come up to their father and say: 'Daddy, give us those lovely toys of all kinds, the little ox carts, goat carts and deer carts.'

cmp.note: 梵文里在十字路口露天坐下的是父亲；英文、白话照译。鸠摩罗什写成孩子们「皆于四衢道中露地而坐」。
cmp.en: In the Sanskrit it is the father who sits down in the open at the crossroads, and the English and plain Chinese follow it. Kumarajiva has the children do it: 皆于四衢道中露地而坐 (jiē yú sìqú dào zhōng lùdì ér zuò, "all sat in the open at the crossroads").

verses.en: "Then, Shariputra, the man gives his own sons ox carts, and only ox carts, as fast as the wind: made of the seven precious things, with railings, hung with nets of little bells, tall and roomy, decorated with wonderful, amazing jewels, made splendid with strings of jewels, adorned with garlands of flowers, spread with cotton mattresses and woolen rugs, covered with fine cloth, with red cushions at both ends, yoked to swift oxen white as can be, attended by many servants, and flying banners. To each child he gives an ox cart as fast and strong as the wind, all of one color and one kind. Why? Because, Shariputra, the man is rich, very wealthy, with storehouses full to overflowing. He thinks: 'Enough of giving these children other carts.' Why?

cmp.note: 梵文强调给的「只是牛车」，而且「同一颜色、同一样式」。英文 ox carts, and only ox carts、白话照译；鸠摩罗什作「各赐诸子等一大车」，没说是牛车，但下文「驾以白牛」，意思一样。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit stresses that he gives "only ox carts," "of one color and one kind." The English "ox carts, and only ox carts" and the plain Chinese follow it; Kumarajiva writes 各赐诸子等一大车 (gè cì zhūzǐ děng yí dà chē, "gave each child a great cart") without naming the ox, though his next line 驾以白牛 ("yoked to white oxen") comes to the same thing.

verses.en: "'These children are all my own sons, and I love and cherish every one of them. And I have great carts like these. I should think of all these children equally, not unequally. I have many treasuries and storehouses; I could give great carts like these to all beings, let alone to my own sons.' And at that time the children climb into those great carts, filled with wonder and amazement. What do you think, Shariputra? Was that man telling a lie, when he first showed the children three kinds of carts and afterward gave all of them great carts, the finest carts?"

cmp.note: 这里 mahāyāna 字面就是「大车」，英文 great carts、白话「大车」都按故事里的意思译；同一个词在别处就是「大乘」，梵文读者能同时听到两层意思，英文、中文都得二选一。
cmp.en: Here mahāyāna literally means "great cart," and the English "great carts" and the plain Chinese 大车 (dà chē, "great cart") translate it as the story requires; the same word elsewhere means "the Great Vehicle," so a Sanskrit reader hears both at once, while English and Chinese must choose one.

verses.en: Shariputra said: "No, Blessed One, no, Sugata. Blessed One, for this reason alone that man would not be a liar: by skillful means he got the children out of the burning house and gave them the gift of their lives. Why? Blessed One, by getting their very lives back, they have in effect received all the toys there are. Even if, Blessed One, that man had not given the children a single cart, still, Blessed One, he would not be a liar. Why? Because, Blessed One, that man had thought beforehand: 'By skillful means I will free these children from this great mass of suffering.' In this way too, Blessed One, that man would not be lying."

"How much less so when that man, considering that he has plenty of treasuries and storehouses, and out of love for his sons and wanting to please them, gave them carts all of one color and one kind, namely great carts. Blessed One, that man has told no lie."

When he had said this, the Blessed One said to the venerable Shariputra: "Good, good, Shariputra! That is so, Shariputra, it is just as you say. In just the same way, Shariputra, the Tathagata, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, has turned away from all fear, and is completely, entirely, in every way free from all disasters, troubles, misfortunes, suffering and sorrow, and from the coverings of the darkness, gloom and fog of ignorance. The Tathagata has knowledge, the powers, the forms of fearlessness, and the qualities found only in a buddha. By the power of his supernatural abilities he is extremely strong; he is the father of the world. He has reached the highest perfection of great skillful means and knowledge. He is greatly compassionate, never weary in mind, wishing the good of others, kind.

"He is born in the three worlds (the whole round of rebirth), which are like a run-down house with a rotting roof, burning with a great mass of suffering and sorrow. He is born to free beings from passion, hatred and delusion, beings who are caught in birth, old age, sickness, death, grief, lamenting, suffering, sorrow and distress, and wrapped in the coverings of the darkness, gloom and fog of ignorance, and to lead them to unsurpassed, perfect awakening. Once born, he sees beings burning, roasting, scorching and being tormented by birth, old age, sickness, death, grief, lamenting, suffering, sorrow and distress. For the sake of enjoyment and because of their desires, they go through many kinds of suffering. In this life, because of seeking and grasping, and in the next life in the hells, among animals and in the world of Yama (the realm of the dead), they will go through many kinds of suffering.

cmp.note: 「阎罗的世界」，即死者的国度。英文 world of Yama、白话「阎罗世界」照译；鸠摩罗什作「饿鬼」，换成了汉地熟悉的三恶道说法。
cmp.en: "The world of Yama," the realm of the dead. The English "world of Yama" and the plain Chinese 阎罗世界 (Yánluó shìjiè, "world of Yama") follow it; Kumarajiva writes 饿鬼 (èguǐ, "hungry ghosts"), fitting the familiar Chinese set of three bad rebirths.

verses.en: "They go through the sufferings of gods and humans: poverty, being stuck with what they hate, being parted from what they love. And turning round and round in that very mass of suffering, they play, enjoy themselves and have fun. They are not frightened, not scared, feel no fear; they do not understand, do not notice, are not alarmed, and do not look for a way out. They delight in the three worlds, which are like a burning house, and run this way and that. Struck by that great mass of suffering, they still do not form the thought, 'This is suffering.'"

"Then, Shariputra, the Tathagata sees it this way: 'I am the father of these beings. I must free these beings from such a great mass of suffering, and I must give them the measureless, inconceivable happiness of a buddha's knowledge, so that they can play in it, enjoy themselves, have fun and make merry.'"

"Then, Shariputra, the Tathagata sees it this way: 'If, thinking "I have the power of knowledge, I have supernatural power," I were to tell these beings, without skillful means, about the Tathagata's knowledge, powers and forms of fearlessness, these beings would not get out by means of those teachings. Why? These beings are attached to the five kinds of sense pleasure, to the delights of the three worlds. They are not free from birth, old age, sickness, death, grief, lamenting, suffering, sorrow and distress. They are burning, roasting, scorching, tormented. They have not run out of the three worlds, which are like a burning house with a rotting roof. How could they come to understand a buddha's knowledge?'"

"So, Shariputra, just as that man with strong arms set aside the strength of his arms and got the children out of the burning house by skillful means, and having got them out afterward gave them noble, great carts, in the same way, Shariputra, the Tathagata, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, who has the Tathagata's knowledge, powers and forms of fearlessness, sets them aside and, by his knowledge of skillful means, in order to get beings out of the three worlds, which are like a burning house with a rotting roof, shows them three vehicles: the disciple vehicle, the solitary-buddha vehicle and the bodhisattva vehicle. With the three vehicles he entices beings, and he says to them: 'Friends, do not delight in these three worlds, which are like a burning house, in base sights, sounds, smells, tastes and touches.

cmp.note: 梵文第三种是「菩萨乘」，英文、白话照译；鸠摩罗什这里作「佛乘」，直接把第三车和佛乘画上等号，这正是后来汉地「三车、四车」之争的起点之一。
cmp.en: The third in the Sanskrit is "the bodhisattva vehicle," and the English and plain Chinese follow it; Kumarajiva writes 佛乘 (fóshèng, "buddha vehicle") here, equating the third cart with the buddha vehicle, one of the starting points of the later Chinese debate over whether there are three carts or four.

verses.en: "'Delighting in these three worlds, you are burning, scorching and tormented by the craving that comes with the five kinds of sense pleasure. Run out of these three worlds! You will get three vehicles: the disciple vehicle, the solitary-buddha vehicle and the bodhisattva vehicle. I am your guarantor in this; I will give you these three vehicles. Strive to escape from the three worlds.' And I entice them like this: 'Friends, these vehicles are noble, praised by the noble ones, full of great delights. With them, friends, you will play, enjoy yourselves and have fun to your heart's content. Through the faculties, the powers, the factors of awakening, the meditations, the liberations, the concentrations and the attainments, you will feel great delight, and you will be filled with great happiness and gladness.'"

"Now, Shariputra, beings who are wise by nature put their trust in the Tathagata, the father of the world, and having trusted him, they apply themselves to the Tathagata's teaching and make an effort. Some beings, wanting to follow what they hear from the voice of another, apply themselves to the Tathagata's teaching for the sake of their own final nirvana, to understand the four noble truths. They are said to run out of the three worlds wanting the disciple vehicle, just as some of the children ran out of the burning house wanting the deer cart. Other beings, wanting knowledge without a teacher, self-control and calm, apply themselves to the Tathagata's teaching for the sake of their own final nirvana, to understand causes and conditions. They are said to run out of the three worlds wanting the solitary-buddha vehicle,
