"'The fierce hells grew, and the animal realm, and the asuras too, and kotis of living beings by the thousands were reborn among the hungry ghosts.
"The heavenly bodies dwindle, and when the gods fall from heaven they go to bad rebirths. Because they have not heard the Dharma of the buddhas, their destiny is a wretched one.
"The conduct, purity, destiny and wisdom of all living beings dwindle. Their happiness is destroyed, and even the idea of happiness disappears.

cmp.note: 梵文列的是「行为、清净、去处、智慧」四样。英文、白话照译；鸠摩罗什改成「色力及智慧」，变成容貌、体力和智慧。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit lists four things: conduct, purity, destiny and wisdom. The English and plain Chinese follow it; Kumarajiva changes it to 色力及智慧 (sè lì jí zhìhuì, "looks, strength and wisdom").

verses.en: "They behave badly and stand firm in what is not the true Dharma. Untamed by the Lord of the World, they fall into bad rebirths.
"Lamp of the world, we have seen you! After a very long time you have come. You have arisen for the sake of all beings, full of compassion.
"How fortunate that you have safely reached the unsurpassed knowledge of a buddha! We rejoice with you, and so does the world with its gods.
"Lord, these palaces have become so beautiful through your power. Great hero, we give them to you; great sage, please accept them.
"Out of compassion for us, Guide, make use of them. And may we and all beings touch the highest awakening."

"Then, monks, after those great Brahmas had praised the Blessed One, the Tathagata Mahabhijnajnanabhibhu, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, face to face with these fitting verses, they said to that Blessed One: 'May the Blessed One turn the wheel of the Dharma! May the Sugata turn the wheel of the Dharma! May the Blessed One teach the way to nirvana! May the Blessed One carry all beings across! May the Blessed One be kind to this world! May the Blessed One teach the Dharma to this world with its Maras and Brahmas, to all its people with their ascetics and brahmins, its gods, humans and asuras. It will be for the good of many, for the happiness of many, out of compassion for the world, for the benefit, good and happiness of the great mass of people, of gods and humans.'

cmp.note: nirvṛti 是「寂灭、安息」，涅槃的同义词。英文 the way to nirvana、白话「开示涅槃」都直说涅槃；鸠摩罗什此处整段压缩成「多所安隐，多所度脱」，没有逐句译。
cmp.en: Nirvṛti means "extinction, coming to rest," a synonym of nirvana. The English "the way to nirvana" and the plain Chinese both name nirvana outright; Kumarajiva compresses the whole request into 多所安隐，多所度脱 (duō suǒ ānyǐn, duō suǒ dùtuō, "bringing peace to many, freeing many") and does not translate it line by line.

verses.en: "Then, monks, those fifty hundred thousand kotis of nayutas of Brahmas, with one voice, singing together, spoke to that Blessed One in these two fitting verses:
"'Turn the excellent, unsurpassed wheel; beat the drum of the deathless. Free beings from hundreds of sufferings, and show them the path to nirvana.

cmp.note: 「不死之鼓」。amṛta 是「不死」，英文 drum of the deathless 保留这层；白话「不死的大鼓」也照字面；鸠摩罗什译「甘露法鼓」，用「甘露」，看不出「不死」。
cmp.en: "The drum of the deathless." Amṛta means "deathless," which the English keeps, and the plain Chinese 不死的大鼓 ("great drum of the deathless") is literal too; Kumarajiva's 甘露法鼓 (gānlù fǎgǔ, "Dharma drum of sweet dew") uses "sweet dew," so the sense of deathlessness disappears.

verses.en: "'Since we have asked you, speak the Dharma; be kind to us and to this world. Let out your lovely, sweet voice, perfected over thousands of kotis of eons.'"

"Then, monks, that Blessed One, the Tathagata Mahabhijnajnanabhibhu, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, knowing the request of those hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas of Brahmas and of his sixteen sons, the princes, at that moment turned the wheel of the Dharma, with its three turnings and twelve aspects, which no ascetic or brahmin, no god, Mara or Brahma, nor anyone else in the world had ever turned in accordance with the Dharma. That is: 'This is suffering; this is the arising of suffering; this is the ending of suffering; this is the path leading to the ending of suffering': the noble truths.

cmp.note: 「三转十二相」：四谛各讲三遍（这是什么、应当做、已经做到），共十二种。英文照字面，没有展开；白话和鸠摩罗什「三转十二行」也一样只给名目。
cmp.en: "Three turnings, twelve aspects": each of the four truths is stated three times (what it is, what is to be done about it, that it has been done), making twelve. The English is literal and does not spell this out; the plain Chinese and Kumarajiva's 三转十二行 (sān zhuǎn shí'èr xíng) likewise give only the label.

verses.en: "And he explained in detail how dependent arising unfolds: 'So, monks, with ignorance as condition come formations; with formations as condition, consciousness; with consciousness as condition, name-and-form (mind and body); with name-and-form as condition, the six sense bases; with the six sense bases as condition, contact; with contact as condition, feeling; with feeling as condition, craving; with craving as condition, grasping; with grasping as condition, becoming; with becoming as condition, birth; with birth as condition come old age and death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, distress and despair. This is how this whole great mass of suffering arises.

cmp.note: 「缘起」，字面是「依靠条件而一起生起」。英文 dependent arising 照字面；鸠摩罗什用「十二因缘」，强调的是这十二个环节，而不是「生起」这个动作。
cmp.en: "Dependent arising," literally "arising together in dependence on conditions." The English "dependent arising" is literal; Kumarajiva uses 十二因缘 (shí'èr yīnyuán, "the twelve causes and conditions"), which stresses the twelve links rather than the act of arising.

verses.en: "'With the ending of ignorance, formations end; with the ending of formations, consciousness ends; with the ending of consciousness, name-and-form ends; with the ending of name-and-form, the six sense bases end; with the ending of the six sense bases, contact ends; with the ending of contact, feeling ends; with the ending of feeling, craving ends; with the ending of craving, grasping ends; with the ending of grasping, becoming ends; with the ending of becoming, birth ends; with the ending of birth, old age and death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, distress and despair come to an end. This is how this whole great mass of suffering comes to an end.'

"And monks, as soon as that Blessed One, the Tathagata Mahabhijnajnanabhibhu, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, had turned this wheel of the Dharma before the assembly of the world with its gods, Maras and Brahmas, of all its people with ascetics and brahmins, gods, humans and asuras, in that very instant, that moment, that second, the minds of sixty hundred thousand kotis of nayutas of living beings were freed from the outflows (defilements) through not grasping. All of them came to have the three knowledges and the six higher knowledges, and to meditate on the eight liberations. Then, monks, that Blessed One gave a second teaching of the Dharma in turn, and a third, and a fourth.

cmp.note: 梵文是「六十个百千俱胝那由他」众生，英文、白话照译；鸠摩罗什作「六百万亿那由他人」，数目写法不同。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says "sixty hundred thousand kotis of nayutas" of beings, which the English and plain Chinese follow; Kumarajiva writes 六百万亿那由他人 (liùbǎi wàn yì nàyóutā rén), a differently stated figure.

verses.en: "Then, monks, at each teaching of the Dharma by that Blessed One, the Tathagata Mahabhijnajnanabhibhu, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, the minds of hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas of living beings, as many as the grains of sand in the Ganges, were freed from the outflows through not grasping. After that, monks, that Blessed One's community of disciples grew beyond counting.

"Now at that time, monks, those sixteen princes, while they were still only boys, went forth in faith from home into homelessness. They all became novices (shramaneras, young monks not yet fully ordained): learned, clear-minded, intelligent and skilled, having practiced under many hundreds of thousands of buddhas and seeking unsurpassed, perfect awakening. Then, monks, those sixteen novices said to that Blessed One, the Tathagata Mahabhijnajnanabhibhu, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha: 'Blessed One, these many hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas of the Tathagata's disciples, with great supernatural power, great might and great fame, have all been brought to completion by the Blessed One's teaching of the Dharma.

cmp.note: 「还只是孩子」。英文 still only boys、白话「还都是小孩子」照字面；鸠摩罗什「以童子出家」意思相同。
cmp.en: "Still being boys." The English "still only boys" and the plain Chinese are literal; Kumarajiva's 以童子出家 (yǐ tóngzǐ chūjiā, "left home as children") has the same sense.

verses.en: "'So it would be good, Blessed One, if the Tathagata, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, out of compassion for us, would teach the Dharma with unsurpassed, perfect awakening in view, so that we too may train after the Tathagata. Blessed One, we long for the Tathagata's knowledge and insight. The Blessed One himself is our witness in this. And Blessed One, you know the intentions of all beings; you know our deepest intention.'

"And at that time, monks, seeing those young boys, the princes, gone forth as novices, half of the following of that wheel-turning king went forth too: eighty hundred thousand kotis of nayutas of beings.

cmp.note: 梵文说转轮王的随从中「有一半」出家，人数是八十个百千俱胝那由他。英文、白话照译；鸠摩罗什作「八万亿人」，又加了「王即听许」，梵文没有。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says "half" of the wheel-turning king's following went forth, eighty hundred thousand kotis of nayutas of beings. The English and plain Chinese follow it; Kumarajiva has 八万亿人 (bāwàn yì rén, "eight trillion people") and adds 王即听许 (wáng jí tīngxǔ, "the king at once gave permission"), which is not in the Sanskrit.

verses.en: "Then, monks, that Blessed One, the Tathagata Mahabhijnajnanabhibhu, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, knowing the intention of those novices, after twenty thousand eons had passed, explained in full to all four assemblies (monks, nuns, laymen and laywomen) the Dharma discourse called the Lotus of the True Dharma, a vast and extensive sutra, an instruction for bodhisattvas, held dear by all the buddhas.

cmp.note: 「大方广」，指篇幅、内容广大的经。英文 vast and extensive、白话加括注照译；鸠摩罗什改称「大乘经」，用的是另一个概念。
cmp.en: "Vast and extensive," a label for long, wide-ranging sutras. The English "vast and extensive" and the plain Chinese (with a gloss) translate it; Kumarajiva calls it 大乘经 (dàshèng jīng, "a Great Vehicle sutra"), a different idea.

verses.en: "And at that time, monks, those sixteen princes, the novices, took up what that Blessed One had said, kept it in memory, mastered it and knew it thoroughly.

"Then, monks, that Blessed One, the Tathagata Mahabhijnajnanabhibhu, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, predicted those sixteen novices to unsurpassed, perfect awakening. And monks, while that Tathagata Mahabhijnajnanabhibhu, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, was teaching this Dharma discourse, the Lotus of the True Dharma, the disciples placed their faith in it, and so did those sixteen novices; but many hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas of living beings fell into doubt.

"Then, monks, that Blessed One, the Tathagata Mahabhijnajnanabhibhu, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, after teaching this Dharma discourse, the Lotus of the True Dharma, without rest for eight thousand eons, went into his dwelling to withdraw into meditation. And monks, withdrawn like that, the Tathagata stayed in his dwelling for eighty-four thousand eons.

cmp.note: 「独处、退居静修」。英文 withdraw into meditation、白话「静修」照译；鸠摩罗什「入静室，住于禅定」点明了是禅定。
cmp.en: "Seclusion, withdrawing in retreat." The English "withdraw into meditation" and the plain Chinese 静修 (jìngxiū, "quiet practice") follow it; Kumarajiva's 入静室，住于禅定 (rù jìngshì, zhù yú chándìng, "entered a quiet room and stayed in meditative absorption") names the absorption explicitly.

verses.en: "Then, monks, those sixteen novices, knowing that the Blessed One, the Tathagata Mahabhijnajnanabhibhu, had withdrawn into meditation, each set up a Dharma seat, a lion seat, of his own. Sitting on them, after paying homage to that Blessed One, the Tathagata Mahabhijnajnanabhibhu, they explained this Dharma discourse, the Lotus of the True Dharma, in full to the four assemblies for eighty-four thousand eons. There, monks, each novice bodhisattva brought to maturity for unsurpassed, perfect awakening hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas of living beings, as many as the grains of sand in sixty Ganges rivers: he inspired them, delighted them, fired them up, gladdened them and led them in.

cmp.note: 梵文是「六十条恒河的沙数」那么多。英文、白话照译；鸠摩罗什作「六百万亿那由他恒河沙等众生」，把数目放大了。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says "as many as the sands of sixty Ganges rivers." The English and plain Chinese follow it; Kumarajiva writes 六百万亿那由他恒河沙等众生 ("beings equal to six million hundred-million nayutas of Ganges sands"), inflating the figure.

verses.en: "Then, monks, when those eighty-four thousand eons had passed, that Blessed One, the Tathagata Mahabhijnajnanabhibhu, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, mindful and fully aware, rose from that concentration. Having risen, the Blessed One, the Tathagata Mahabhijnajnanabhibhu, went to the Dharma seat, and when he got there he sat down on the seat that had been prepared.

"And monks, as soon as that Blessed One, the Tathagata Mahabhijnajnanabhibhu, had sat down on that Dharma seat, he looked around the whole circle of the assembly and said to the community of monks: 'Monks, these sixteen novices are wonderful, amazing! They are wise; they have served many hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas of buddhas and have carried out the practice; they serve the buddha knowledge, take hold of the buddha knowledge, lead others into the buddha knowledge and show the buddha knowledge. Monks, serve these sixteen novices again and again. Monks, whoever, whether they follow the disciple vehicle, the solitary-buddha vehicle or the bodhisattva vehicle, does not reject the Dharma teaching of these sons of good family,
"'and does not oppose it, all of them will quickly gain unsurpassed, perfect awakening, and all of them will attain the Tathagata's knowledge.'

"And monks, those sixteen sons of good family made this Dharma discourse, the Lotus of the True Dharma, known again and again in that Blessed One's teaching. And monks, the hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas of beings, as many as the grains of sand in sixty Ganges rivers, whom each of those sixteen novices, bodhisattvas, great beings, had inspired toward awakening, all went forth along with them, life after life. Seeing only them, they heard the Dharma from them. They have pleased forty thousand kotis of buddhas, and some are pleasing buddhas even now.

cmp.note: 梵文是「四十个千俱胝」即四万俱胝尊佛，英文、白话照译；鸠摩罗什作「四百万亿诸佛世尊」，数目不同。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says "forty thousand kotis" of buddhas, which the English and plain Chinese follow; Kumarajiva has 四百万亿诸佛世尊 (sìbǎi wàn yì zhū fó shìzūn, "four million hundred-million buddhas, World-Honored Ones"), a different figure.

verses.en: "I tell you, monks, I announce to you: those sixteen princes, then still boys, who became novices and teachers of the Dharma in that Blessed One's teaching, have all woken up to unsurpassed, perfect awakening. And all of them are living now, staying and carrying on, teaching the Dharma to many hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas of disciples and bodhisattvas in various buddha-fields in the ten directions. That is to say, monks: in the east, in the world system Abhirati (Delight), are the Tathagata named Akshobhya (Unshakable), the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, and the Tathagata named Merukuta (Peak of Meru), the arhat, the fully awakened buddha. In the southeast, monks, are the Tathagata named Simhaghosha (Lion's Roar), the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, and the Tathagata named Simhadhvaja (Lion Banner), the arhat, the fully awakened buddha.

"In the south, monks, are the Tathagata named Akashapratishthita (Standing in Space), the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, and the Tathagata named Nityaparinirvrita (Always at Final Rest), the arhat, the fully awakened buddha. In the southwest, monks, are the Tathagata named Indradhvaja (Indra's Banner), the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, and the Tathagata named Brahmadhvaja (Brahma's Banner), the arhat, the fully awakened buddha. In the west, monks, are the Tathagata named Amitayus (Boundless Life), the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, and the Tathagata named Sarvalokadhatupadravodvegapratyuttirna (One Who Has Crossed Beyond the Troubles and Fears of All Worlds), the arhat, the fully awakened buddha. In the northwest, monks, are the Tathagata named Tamalapatrachandanagandhabhijna (Higher Knowledge Fragrant as Tamala Leaf and Sandalwood), the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, and the Tathagata named Merukalpa (Like Meru), the arhat, the fully awakened buddha.

cmp.note: 西方这位佛是 Amitāyus「无量寿」，就是后来净土信仰中的阿弥陀佛。英文给出意思；白话和鸠摩罗什都用音译「阿弥陀」，中文读者一眼认得，英文读者要靠括注。
cmp.en: The buddha in the west is Amitāyus, "Boundless Life," the same buddha later worshipped in Pure Land devotion as Amitabha. The English gives the meaning; the plain Chinese and Kumarajiva both use the transliteration 阿弥陀 (Ēmítuó), which every Chinese reader recognizes at once, while the English reader needs the gloss.

verses.en: "In the north, monks, are the Tathagata named Meghasvaradipa (Lamp of the Cloud Voice), the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, and the Tathagata named Meghasvararaja (King of the Cloud Voice), the arhat, the fully awakened buddha. In the northeast, monks, is the Tathagata named Sarvalokabhayachambhitatvavidhvamsanakara (Destroyer of All the World's Fear and Paralysis), the arhat, the fully awakened buddha. And I, monks, the Tathagata named Shakyamuni, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, am the sixteenth: I woke up to unsurpassed, perfect awakening in the middle of this Saha world (our world of endurance).

"And monks, those beings who back then heard the Dharma from us while we were novices in that Blessed One's teaching, the many hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas of beings, as many as the grains of sand in the Ganges, whom each of us bodhisattvas, great beings, inspired toward unsurpassed, perfect awakening: those beings, monks, are still standing on the level of disciples even today. They are still being brought to maturity for unsurpassed, perfect awakening. This is the very order by which they will wake up to unsurpassed, perfect awakening. Why? Because, monks, the Tathagata's knowledge is so hard to believe in. And who, monks, are those beings, the immeasurable, countless hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas of beings, as many as the grains of sand in the Ganges, to whom I, as a bodhisattva in that Blessed One's teaching, made the Dharma of all-knowing knowledge heard?
"You, monks, were those beings at that time and on that occasion."

cmp.note: 梵文这一句只说「那时的众生就是你们」。鸠摩罗什多加了「及我灭度后未来世中声闻弟子是也」，把下一段的意思提前并进来了。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says only, "you were those beings at that time." Kumarajiva adds 及我灭度后未来世中声闻弟子是也 ("and also the disciples of the future, after my passing"), pulling in the idea of the next passage.

verses.en: "And there will be those who become disciples in the future, after my final nirvana, who will hear of the bodhisattva's practice and yet not understand that they are bodhisattvas. Monks, even though all of them, thinking they have reached final nirvana, will pass into final nirvana, still, monks, wherever I stay in other world systems under other names, they will be born again there, seeking the Tathagata's knowledge. And there they will hear this matter again: the Tathagatas have only one final nirvana; there is no other, second nirvana apart from it. Monks, understand this as the Tathagatas' skillful means and their way of setting out the teaching of the Dharma.

cmp.note: 梵文说这些声闻「会听到菩萨的修行」，只是不明白自己就是菩萨。白话照译；鸠摩罗什反过来写「不闻是经，不知不觉菩萨所行」，变成没听过这部经。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says these disciples "will hear of the bodhisattva's practice" but not realize they themselves are bodhisattvas; the plain Chinese follows it. Kumarajiva turns it around: 不闻是经，不知不觉菩萨所行 (bù wén shì jīng, bù zhī bù jué púsà suǒ xíng, "do not hear this sutra and do not know or realize what bodhisattvas practice").

verses.en: "Monks, when the Tathagata sees that the time for his own final nirvana has come, and sees that the assembly is pure, strong in faith, has penetrated the teaching of emptiness, and is practiced in meditation and great meditation, then, monks, knowing 'This is the time,' the Tathagata gathers all the bodhisattvas and all the disciples and then lets them hear this truth: 'Monks, there is nothing in the world called a second vehicle or a second final nirvana, let alone a third.' Monks, this is the skillful means of the Tathagatas, the arhats: knowing that the realm of beings is long lost, delighting in what is low, sunk in the mud of desire, the Tathagata, monks, speaks to them of the nirvana they are able to believe in.

cmp.note: 「沉在欲望的泥里」。英文 sunk in the mud of desire、白话「陷在欲望的泥沼里」照字面；鸠摩罗什「深着五欲」只说贪着，没有泥沼的画面。
cmp.en: "Sunk in the mud of desire." The English and the plain Chinese 陷在欲望的泥沼里 ("stuck in the swamp of desire") are literal; Kumarajiva's 深着五欲 (shēn zhuó wǔ yù, "deeply attached to the five desires") states the attachment without the image of mud.

verses.en: "Suppose, monks, there were a wilderness here, a stretch of wild country five hundred yojanas (a yojana is roughly a day's march) across, and a great crowd of people set out through it to reach the Isle of Jewels. And suppose they had one guide, clear-headed, learned, sharp, intelligent, and skilled in the dangers of the wilderness, and he led that caravan into the wilderness. Then that great crowd, tired, worn out, frightened and scared, said: 'Noble guide, leader, please understand: we are tired, worn out, frightened, scared and uneasy. We are going to turn back. This wilderness goes on too far from here.' Then, monks, that guide, skilled in means, knowing those people wanted to turn back, thought: 'These poor people must not miss reaching such a great Isle of Jewels.' Out of compassion for them, he put his skill in means to work.

cmp.note: dvīpa 是「岛、洲」，ratnadvīpa 是「宝岛」，商人航海求宝的目的地。英文 Isle of Jewels、白话「宝洲」保留了「岛」；鸠摩罗什译「珍宝处」「宝所」，只说是有宝的地方。
cmp.en: Dvīpa means "island," and ratnadvīpa is "the jewel island," the goal of merchants sailing in search of treasure. The English "Isle of Jewels" and the plain Chinese 宝洲 (bǎozhōu, "jewel isle") keep the island; Kumarajiva's 珍宝处 (zhēnbǎo chù) and 宝所 (bǎosuǒ) just say "the place of treasure."

verses.en: "In the middle of the wilderness, after they had gone a hundred, two hundred or three hundred yojanas, he would conjure up a city by supernatural power. Then he would say to those people: 'Don't be afraid, sirs, don't turn back. Here is that great town. Rest here. Do whatever you need to do here. Stay here, having reached rest, at ease. Whoever still has business to do will go on to the great Isle of Jewels.'

cmp.note: 向导说「在这里得到 nirvāṇa」，字面就是「涅槃」，在故事里是「歇息、安乐」的日常用法，同时影射后文的涅槃。英文 having reached rest、白话「得到安乐」都只译出日常义，双关在译文里看不出来。
cmp.en: The guide says "having reached nirvāṇa here," the very word for nirvana, used in the story in its everyday sense of "rest, relief," while pointing ahead to the nirvana of the teaching. The English "having reached rest" and the plain Chinese 得到安乐 ("found ease") give only the everyday sense, so the pun is lost in translation.

verses.en: "Then, monks, the beings in that wilderness would be filled with wonder and amazement: 'We are free of the wilderness! We will stay here, having reached rest.' And monks, those people would enter the city made by supernatural power, thinking they had arrived, thinking they had crossed over, and they would feel, 'We are at rest, we have cooled down.' Then the guide, knowing they were rested, would make that city made by supernatural power vanish. Having made it vanish, he would say to those people: 'Come on, good people! The great Isle of Jewels is close by. This city I conjured up for you so that you could rest.'

cmp.note: 「由神通造成的城」。英文 city made by supernatural power、白话「神通变出的城」照字面；鸠摩罗什译「化城」，后来成了这一品的名字「化城喻品」，英文常说 phantom city。
cmp.en: "A city made of supernatural power." The English and the plain Chinese 神通变出的城 ("a city conjured by supernatural power") are literal; Kumarajiva's 化城 (huàchéng, "conjured city") later gave this chapter its Chinese name, and in English it is often called the "phantom city."

verses.en: "In just the same way, monks, the Tathagata, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, is the guide for you and for all beings. And monks, the Tathagata, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, sees it like this: 'This great wilderness of afflictions has to be crossed, gone through and left behind. These people must not hear of the one buddha knowledge only to turn straight back and never come near it, thinking, "This buddha knowledge takes so much hardship to achieve."'

"So the Tathagata, knowing that beings are weak of will, does as the guide did when he conjured up the city by supernatural power so that those beings could rest, and then, once they were rested, told them, 'This is a city made by supernatural power.' In the same way, monks, the Tathagata, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, with great skill in means, teaches and explains two stages of nirvana along the way so that beings can rest: the stage of the disciple and the stage of the solitary buddha. And monks, when those beings are standing there, the Tathagata lets them hear this: 'Monks, you have not done what had to be done, you have not finished your work. But monks, you are near. From here, monks, look at the Tathagata's knowledge, think it over.

cmp.note: 「近处」：如来说「你们已经接近了」。英文 you are near、白话「你们只是离得近了」照字面；鸠摩罗什作「汝所住地，近于佛慧」，意思相同，把「接近」说成接近佛的智慧。
cmp.en: "Nearness": the Tathagata says, "you are close." The English "you are near" and the plain Chinese are literal; Kumarajiva's 汝所住地，近于佛慧 (rǔ suǒ zhù dì, jìn yú fó huì, "the stage you stand on is near the Buddha's wisdom") says the same and spells out what they are near.

verses.en: "'Your nirvana is not nirvana at all. Rather, monks, it is the skillful means of the Tathagatas, the arhats, the fully awakened buddhas, that they explain three vehicles.'"
Then the Blessed One, to show this meaning still more fully, spoke these verses at that time:
"Abhijnajnanabhibhu, the guide of the world, sat at the seat of awakening for ten full intermediate eons, and though he saw the highest truth, he did not gain awakening.

cmp.note: 「中劫」，劫与劫之间的一段时期。白话译「中劫」；鸠摩罗什译「十劫」，后文又说「十小劫」，名称前后不一。英文用 intermediate eons。
cmp.en: "Intermediate eon," a period within a full eon. The plain Chinese says 中劫 (zhōngjié, "middle eon"); Kumarajiva says 十劫 (shí jié, "ten eons") here and 十小劫 ("ten small eons") a few lines later, not consistently. The English uses "intermediate eons."

verses.en: "Gods, nagas, asuras and guhyakas (hidden ones, spirits of the yaksha kind) set about worshipping that Victor; they let a rain of flowers fall there, for the awakening of this guide of humans."
"And above in the sky drums sounded, to honor and worship that Victor; and they were deeply troubled that the Victor there was so long in waking up to the unsurpassed state.
"After ten intermediate eons had passed, that Blessed One, Anabhibhu, touched awakening. Then gods, humans, nagas and asuras were all delighted and elated.

cmp.note: 偈颂为了凑音节，把佛名缩成 Anābhibhū（字面「不可胜」）。英文照原文写 Anabhibhu；白话、鸠摩罗什直接用全名「大通智胜」。
cmp.en: To fit the meter, the verse shortens the buddha's name to Anābhibhū (literally "unsurpassable"). The English keeps "Anabhibhu" as in the text; the plain Chinese and Kumarajiva simply use the full name 大通智胜 (Dàtōng Zhìshèng).

verses.en: "Then the sixteen sons of that guide of humans, heroic princes rich in good qualities, surrounded by thousands of kotis of living beings, came to that foremost lord of two-footed beings.
"They bowed at the Guide's feet and asked him: 'Make the Dharma known! Lion among humans, satisfy us and this world here with your good words.'
"'After a long time in the world you have appeared, great Guide, and become known in these ten directions. To rouse living beings with signs, the palaces of Brahma were made to shake.
"'In the eastern direction fifty thousand kotis of lands were shaken, and the finest palaces of Brahma there shone beyond measure.

cmp.note: 梵文是「五十个千俱胝」国土，英文、白话照译；鸠摩罗什偈颂作「五百万亿国」，和散文部分的说法一致，但和梵文偈颂不同。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says "fifty thousand kotis" of lands, which the English and plain Chinese follow; Kumarajiva's verse has 五百万亿国 (wǔbǎi wàn yì guó, "five million hundred-million lands"), matching his prose but not the Sanskrit verse.

verses.en: "'Knowing this sign that came first, they went to the lord of the world's guides. Scattering flowers over the Guide here, they offered him all their palaces.
"'They asked him to turn the wheel and praised him with sung verses. But that king of humans stayed silent: "It is not yet time for me to speak the Dharma."'

cmp.w: na tāva kālo mama dharma bhāṣitum
cmp.note: 梵文用佛自己的话：「我说法的时候还没到。」英文、白话照译；鸠摩罗什改成叙述句「佛知时未至，受请默然坐」。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit puts it in the Buddha's own words: "It is not yet time for me to speak the Dharma." The English and plain Chinese keep this; Kumarajiva turns it into narration: 佛知时未至，受请默然坐 (fó zhī shí wèi zhì, shòu qǐng mòrán zuò, "the Buddha knew the time had not come; he accepted the request and sat in silence").

verses.en: "'In the same way, in the south and then in the west, below, in the north, above, and in the in-between directions too, thousands of kotis of Brahmas came.
"'They scattered flowers over the Guide, bowed at the Guide's feet, handed over all their palaces, praised him, and asked him again:
"'"Turn the wheel, you of endless vision! You are so very hard to meet, even in many kotis of eons. Show the power of loving-kindness you practiced in the past; open the door of the deathless."'
"Knowing their request, the one of endless vision made the Dharma known in many ways: the four truths in full, and how all these things have arisen in dependence.

cmp.note: 梵文偈颂说「这一切存在都是依缘生起的」，是缘起的一般说法。英文、白话照译；鸠摩罗什直接写成「十二缘」这个名目。
cmp.en: The verse says "all these things have arisen in dependence," the general statement of dependent arising. The English and plain Chinese follow it; Kumarajiva writes the label 十二缘 (shí'èr yuán, "the twelve links") instead.

verses.en: "Beginning with ignorance, the one with vision spoke of suffering that ends in death: 'All these faults come from being born. Know that this is just what human death is.'
"As soon as he had spoken the Dharma, in many kinds, varied and endless, eighty kotis of nayutas of beings heard it and quickly came to stand on the ground of the disciples.

cmp.note: 梵文是「八十俱胝那由他」众生，安住在「声闻地」上。白话照译；鸠摩罗什作「六百万亿姟，得尽诸苦际，皆成阿罗汉」，数目不同，也把「声闻地」说成了「成阿罗汉」。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says "eighty kotis of nayutas" of beings came to stand "on the ground of the disciples"; the plain Chinese follows it. Kumarajiva has 六百万亿姟，得尽诸苦际，皆成阿罗汉 ("six million hundred-million gai reached the end of suffering and all became arhats"), with a different number and "became arhats" in place of "the disciples' ground."

verses.en: "There was a second occasion, another one, when that Victor spoke much Dharma, and pure-hearted beings like the grains of sand in the Ganges became disciples in an instant.
"After that, the community of that guide of the world was beyond counting. Even counting them one by one for kotis of nayutas of eons, you would never reach the end of them.
"And those sixteen princes, his own sons, all took the robe of renunciants. As novices they said to that Victor: 'Guide, make the highest Dharma known,
"'so that we may become knowers of the world just like you, highest of all Victors; and may all these beings too become just like you, hero with pure eyes.'
"And that Victor, knowing the intentions of his own sons, who were still boys, made known the highest, supreme awakening with many kotis of nayutas of illustrations.
"Showing it with thousands of reasons and setting in motion higher knowledge and wisdom, the Lord of the World showed the true practice, how wise bodhisattvas practice.

cmp.note: 梵文只说「真实的修行」。白话照译；鸠摩罗什补出了「六波罗蜜」，梵本这里没有。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says only "the true practice"; the plain Chinese follows it. Kumarajiva adds 六波罗蜜 (liù bōluómì, "the six perfections"), which is not in the Sanskrit here.

verses.en: "This very Lotus of the True Dharma, the extensive sutra, is what the Blessed One spoke, in many thousands of verses, as many as the grains of sand in the Ganges.
"Having spoken this sutra, that Victor went into his dwelling and withdrew into reflection. For a full eighty-four eons the Lord of the World sat absorbed on a single seat.

cmp.note: 偈颂这里是「整整八十四劫」，散文部分是「八万四千劫」，梵本前后不一。英文、白话照偈颂原文；鸠摩罗什偈颂仍作「八万四千劫」，与散文统一了。
cmp.en: The verse says "a full eighty-four eons," while the prose said "eighty-four thousand eons"; the Sanskrit is inconsistent. The English and plain Chinese follow the verse as written; Kumarajiva's verse keeps 八万四千劫 (bāwàn sìqiān jié, "eighty-four thousand eons"), bringing it into line with the prose.

verses.en: "Those novices, knowing the Guide was sitting in his dwelling and would not come out, made many kotis of beings hear this buddha knowledge, free of outflows and blessed.
"Each setting out his own seat, they spoke this very sutra to them. In that Sugata's teaching they did the same kind of work I do.
"They made it heard to sixty thousand, beyond measure like the grains of sand in the Ganges. Each one of that Sugata's sons trained beings in great numbers.

cmp.note: 「六万」后面没有名词，可以理解为六万（个恒河沙数的众生），也可以是六万人。英文照原文写得含糊；白话补了「众生」；鸠摩罗什作「六百万亿恒河沙等众」。这句拿不准。
cmp.en: "Sixty thousand" has no noun after it: it may mean sixty thousand Ganges-sands of beings, or simply sixty thousand. The English keeps the ambiguity; the plain Chinese supplies 众生 ("beings"); Kumarajiva has 六百万亿恒河沙等众 ("a multitude equal to six million hundred-million Ganges sands"). The line is uncertain.

verses.en: "After that Victor's final nirvana, they went on practicing and saw kotis of buddhas. Together with those who had heard them back then, they made offerings to the highest of two-footed beings.
"Having carried out a vast and outstanding practice, they woke up and became buddhas in the ten directions. Those sixteen sons of that Victor became Victors, two by two, in every direction.
"And those who had heard the Dharma from them back then all became disciples of those Victors. Step by step, with many kinds of means, the Victors lead them toward this very awakening.
"I too was among them, and I made all of you hear the Dharma. That is why you are my disciples today, and here, with skillful means, I lead you all to awakening.
"This was the cause back then, this the condition for my speaking the Dharma like this: I am leading you to my highest awakening. Monks, do not be alarmed at this.
"Suppose there were a fierce and terrible wilderness, empty, with nothing to hold on to and nowhere to shelter, full of wild beasts and without water, a frightening place for the ignorant.
"And suppose many thousands of people had set out into that wilderness, and the wilderness was empty and long, a full fifty yojanas.

cmp.note: 偈颂说荒野「五十由旬」，散文部分是「五百由旬」，梵本前后不一。英文、白话照偈颂原文；鸠摩罗什偈颂作「五百由旬」，和散文统一。
cmp.en: The verse says the wilderness is "fifty yojanas," while the prose said "five hundred"; the Sanskrit is inconsistent. The English and plain Chinese follow the verse as written; Kumarajiva's verse says 五百由旬 (wǔbǎi yóuxún, "five hundred yojanas"), matching the prose.

verses.en: "And there would be a man to guide them there through that hard and dreadful wilderness: well-off, mindful, clear-headed, steady, well trained and fearless.

cmp.note: āḍhya 是「富有的」。英文 well-off、白话「富有」照字面；鸠摩罗什没有译这个词，只说向导「强识有智慧」。
cmp.en: Āḍhya means "wealthy." The English "well-off" and the plain Chinese 富有 (fùyǒu, "rich") are literal; Kumarajiva leaves the word out and says only that the guide was 强识有智慧 (qiáng shí yǒu zhìhuì, "of strong memory and wise").

verses.en: "Those many kotis of people, worn out, said to the guide at that time: 'Sir, we are worn out and cannot go on. Today we would rather turn back.'
"Then that skilled and wise leader would think of a means: 'Alas, what a pity! These fools will all lose the jewels by turning themselves back.'
"'What if I now conjure up a great city by supernatural power, adorned with thousands of kotis of houses and made beautiful with dwellings and parks?
"'I will conjure up ponds and rivers, and adorn it with the flowers of gardens, make it beautiful with walls and gates, and fill it with men and women beyond compare.'
"Having made this conjured city, he would say to them: 'Don't be afraid, be glad! You have reached the finest city. Go in and see to your business quickly.'
"'Be uplifted, and say here: "We are at rest; we have crossed the whole wilderness, every bit of it."' He would say these words to comfort them, so that none of them would turn back.
"And seeing that they all looked rested, he would gather them together and speak again: 'Come here, listen to what I say: this city is conjured, made by supernatural power.
"'I saw how tired you were and thought, "They must not turn back." This was my skill in means. Now summon up your energy to go on to the Isle.'
"In just the same way, monks, I am the guide and leader of thousands of kotis of living beings. In the same way I see living beings worn out, unable to break the eggshell of the afflictions.

cmp.note: 「烦恼的蛋壳」，众生像还没破壳的雏鸟。英文 eggshell of the afflictions、白话「烦恼的蛋壳」照字面；鸠摩罗什改成「烦恼诸险道」，又回到险道的比喻，蛋壳的画面没有了。
cmp.en: "The eggshell of the afflictions": beings are like chicks not yet hatched. The English and the plain Chinese 烦恼的蛋壳 ("eggshell of afflictions") are literal; Kumarajiva changes it to 烦恼诸险道 (fánnǎo zhū xiǎndào, "the dangerous roads of affliction"), returning to the road image and losing the eggshell.

verses.en: "So I thought of this: these places of rest are what I call nirvana. 'This is the ending of all suffering; on the stage of the arhat you have done what had to be done.'
"But when I see that you are standing in that place, that all of you there are arhats, then I gather you all here and tell you the real truth of what this Dharma is.
"It is the skillful means of the Guides, the great seers, that they teach three vehicles. For there is only one vehicle, there is no second; two vehicles are taught only to give rest.

cmp.note: 「只有一乘，没有第二乘」。英文 one vehicle、白话「一乘」照字面；鸠摩罗什译「唯有一佛乘」，把「一乘」直接点明为「佛乘」。
cmp.en: "There is only one vehicle, there is no second." The English "one vehicle" and the plain Chinese 一乘 (yī shèng) are literal; Kumarajiva writes 唯有一佛乘 (wéi yǒu yī fó shèng, "there is only the one buddha vehicle"), naming the one vehicle outright as the buddha vehicle.

verses.en: "So I tell you today, monks: summon up the highest, greatest energy. You are to work for all-knowing knowledge; with only this much, there is no nirvana at all.
"When you touch all-knowing knowledge, the ten powers and the qualities of the Victors, and bear a body with the thirty-two marks, when you have become buddhas, then you will be at rest in nirvana.
"This is how the Guides teach: they speak of nirvana as a place of rest. And knowing that beings have rested in that nirvana, they lead them all to all-knowing knowledge."
This is the seventh chapter, called Former Ties, in the noble Dharma discourse of the Lotus of the True Dharma.

cmp.note: 梵文品名是「往昔的因缘」，讲的是大通智胜佛时代结下的缘。英文 Former Ties、白话「往昔因缘」照字面；鸠摩罗什以其中的譬喻命名为「化城喻品」。梵本这是第七品，本站排第八。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit chapter title means "former connections," the ties formed in the time of the buddha Mahabhijnajnanabhibhu. The English "Former Ties" and the plain Chinese 往昔因缘 (wǎngxī yīnyuán) are literal; Kumarajiva names the chapter after its parable, 化城喻品 (Huàchéng Yù Pǐn, "The Parable of the Conjured City"). In the Sanskrit this is the seventh chapter; the site places it eighth.

chapters.title: Chapter 9 · Predictions for the Five Hundred Monks

verses.en: Then the venerable Purna Maitrayaniputra heard from the Blessed One this teaching given with hidden meaning, this knowing and seeing of skillful means; he heard the predictions of these great disciples, heard this story connected with former lives, and heard of the Blessed One's bull-like strength. He was filled with wonder and amazement, and his mind, free of any craving, was flooded with joy and delight. With great joy and delight and great reverence for the Dharma he rose from his seat, bowed down at the Blessed One's feet, and thought: "It is wonderful, Blessed One! It is wonderful, Sugata (the Well-Gone One)!

cmp.note: 字面是「公牛的气概」，梵文常用公牛比喻领袖的威严。英文 bull-like strength、白话「如雄牛般的威严气概」保留了这个比喻；鸠摩罗什改成「诸佛有大自在神通之力」，公牛不见了。
cmp.en: Literally "bull-ness": Sanskrit often uses the bull as an image of a leader's commanding strength. The English "bull-like strength" and the plain Chinese keep the image; Kumarajiva writes 诸佛有大自在神通之力 (zhū fó yǒu dà zìzài shéntōng zhī lì, "the buddhas have great, sovereign supernatural power"), and the bull is gone.

verses.en: "The Tathagatas, the arhats, the fully awakened buddhas do something supremely hard: they go along with this world of so many different natures, teach the Dharma to beings with many displays of knowledge and skillful means, and with skillful means free beings who are stuck here and there. What can we do about this, Blessed One? Only the Tathagata knows our deep intentions and our practice in former lives." He touched the Blessed One's feet with his head and stood to one side, paying homage to the Blessed One and gazing at him without blinking.

Then the Blessed One saw what was in the venerable Purna Maitrayaniputra's mind and said to the whole community of monks: "Monks, do you see this disciple, Purna Maitrayaniputra? I have named him the foremost of the Dharma speakers in this community of monks, and I have praised him for many real good qualities. In many ways he has worked to take hold of the true Dharma in this teaching of mine. He gladdens the four assemblies (monks, nuns, laymen and laywomen), encourages them, inspires them and delights them; he never tires of teaching the Dharma; he is fully able to explain this Dharma and fully able to help his fellow practitioners. Monks, apart from the Tathagata, no one can outdo Purna Maitrayaniputra in either meaning or wording. Now what do you think, monks: is it only my true Dharma that he takes hold of?"

"But, monks, you should not see it that way. Why? Monks, I remember that in the past, under ninety-nine kotis (a koti is ten million) of buddhas, he took hold of the true Dharma in the teaching of those buddhas, the Blessed Ones. Just as he is with me now, everywhere he was the foremost of the Dharma speakers, everywhere he had mastered emptiness, everywhere he had gained the four kinds of analytical knowledge, and everywhere he had mastered the bodhisattva's higher knowledges. He taught the Dharma with full certainty, without doubt, and with perfect purity. In the teaching of those buddhas, the Blessed Ones, he lived the holy life for as long as his life lasted, and everywhere people knew him simply as a disciple."

cmp.note: 梵文是「九十九俱胝」佛，英文、白话照译；鸠摩罗什作「九十亿诸佛」，少了九。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says "ninety-nine kotis" of buddhas, which the English and plain Chinese follow; Kumarajiva has 九十亿诸佛 (jiǔshí yì zhū fó, "nine billion buddhas"), dropping the nine.

cmp.note: 「人们把他当作声闻」：他其实是菩萨，只是外表像声闻。这是本品的关键。英文 people knew him simply as a disciple 用 simply 点出「只是外表」；鸠摩罗什「咸皆谓之实是声闻」加了「实是」，更强调别人被瞒过。
cmp.en: "He was known as a disciple": in fact he was a bodhisattva who only looked like a disciple, which is the key to this chapter. The English "simply as a disciple" hints that this was only the surface; Kumarajiva's 咸皆谓之实是声闻 (xián jiē wèi zhī shí shì shēngwén, "all said he truly was a shravaka") adds "truly," stressing that others were taken in.

verses.en: "By this means he did good to countless, measureless hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas (huge numbers) of beings, and brought countless, measureless beings to maturity for unsurpassed, perfect awakening. Everywhere he served beings by doing a buddha's work, everywhere he purified his own buddha-field, and he worked hard to bring beings to maturity. Monks, among the seven Tathagatas headed by Vipashyin, of whom I am the seventh, he was likewise the foremost of the Dharma speakers."

"And, monks, in the future, in this Good Eon (bhadrakalpa, the eon we live in, in which a thousand buddhas appear), there will be a thousand buddhas less four, and in their teaching too this same Purna Maitrayaniputra will be the foremost of the Dharma speakers and a keeper of the true Dharma. In this way, in the future he will keep the true Dharma of countless, measureless buddhas, the Blessed Ones; he will do good to countless, measureless beings and bring countless, measureless beings to maturity for unsurpassed, perfect awakening. He will always work hard to purify his own buddha-field and to bring beings to maturity. Having completed a bodhisattva's practice like this, after countless, measureless eons he will wake up to unsurpassed, perfect awakening."

cmp.note: 「一千尊佛减去四尊」：贤劫千佛中已有四尊出世（释迦是第四），所以说将来还有九百九十六尊。英文照字面；白话把算式算了出来；鸠摩罗什只说「贤劫中当来诸佛」。
cmp.en: "A thousand buddhas less four": four of the Good Eon's thousand buddhas have already appeared (Shakyamuni is the fourth), so 996 are still to come. The English is literal; the plain Chinese works out the sum; Kumarajiva just says 贤劫中当来诸佛 (xiánjié zhōng dānglái zhū fó, "the buddhas to come in the Good Eon").

verses.en: "He will appear in the world as a Tathagata named Dharmaprabhasa (Radiance of the Dharma), an arhat, a fully awakened buddha, perfect in knowledge and conduct, the Sugata, knower of the world, unsurpassed, tamer of those who can be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a buddha, a Blessed One. He will arise in this very buddha-field."

"At that time, monks, great trichiliocosms (each a billion-world universe), as many as the grains of sand in the Ganges, will form a single buddha-field. It will be level like the palm of a hand, made of the seven jewels, without mountains, and full of towers made of the seven jewels. The palaces of the gods will stand in the sky; the gods will see humans and humans will see the gods. At that time, monks, this buddha-field will be free of evil and free of women. All the beings there will be born spontaneously; they will live the holy life, with bodies made of mind, shining with their own light, with supernatural powers, moving through the air, energetic, mindful and wise, with golden bodies adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great man."

cmp.note: 「没有女人」：所有众生都是化生、过梵行，所以没有性别与生育。英文 free of women、白话「没有女人」都照字面，没有加解释；鸠摩罗什同样写「亦无女人」，并补了一句「无有婬欲」。
cmp.en: "Free of women": all beings there are born spontaneously and live the holy life, so there is no sex and no childbirth. The English "free of women" and the plain Chinese are both literal, with no softening; Kumarajiva likewise writes 亦无女人 (yì wú nǚrén, "also no women") and adds 无有婬欲 (wú yǒu yínyù, "there is no sexual desire").

verses.en: "At that time, monks, the beings in that buddha-field will have two kinds of food. Which two? The food of joy in the Dharma and the food of joy in meditation. There will be countless, measureless hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas of bodhisattvas, all with great higher knowledges, masters of analytical knowledge, skilled at instructing beings. His disciples will be beyond counting, with great supernatural power and great might, practicing the meditation of the eight liberations. That buddha-field will have countless good qualities like these. That eon will be called Ratnavabhasa (Jewel Radiance), and that world system will be called Suvishuddha (Thoroughly Pure). His lifespan will be countless, measureless eons."

"And after the final nirvana of that Blessed One, the Tathagata Dharmaprabhasa, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, his true Dharma will last a long time, and that world system will be filled with stupas made of jewels. Such, monks, are the inconceivable good qualities that the buddha-field of that Blessed One will have."
So spoke the Blessed One. Having said this, the Sugata, the Teacher, said something more:
"Monks, listen to me about this: how this son of mine carried out his practice, how well he learned skillful means, and how he carried out this practice of awakening.
"Knowing that these beings have low aspirations and are frightened of the great vehicle, the bodhisattvas become disciples and show the awakening of a solitary buddha (pratyekabuddha).

cmp.note: 「志向低下」，即只想求小解脱。英文 low aspirations、白话照译；鸠摩罗什作「乐小法」，从「志向」变成「喜好小法」。
cmp.en: "Of low aspiration," wanting only a small liberation. The English "low aspirations" and the plain Chinese follow it; Kumarajiva writes 乐小法 (lè xiǎo fǎ, "delighting in the small Dharma"), turning aspiration into taste.

verses.en: "With many hundreds of skillful means they bring many bodhisattvas to maturity, and they say: 'We are only disciples; we are far from the highest, supreme awakening.'
"Learning this practice from them, kotis of beings come to maturity; and those of low aspirations, the lazy ones, will all become buddhas step by step.
"They go about as if they knew nothing, saying: 'We are disciples with little left to do.' Weary of all dying and being reborn, they purify their own fields."

cmp.note: 字面是「无知的修行」，指装作不知道自己是菩萨。英文 as if they knew nothing、白话「装作无知的样子」都把「装」补了出来；鸠摩罗什改写成有名的「内秘菩萨行，外现是声闻」。
cmp.en: Literally "a practice of not-knowing," meaning they act as if unaware they are bodhisattvas. The English "as if they knew nothing" and the plain Chinese 装作无知的样子 ("pretending to know nothing") both add the pretending; Kumarajiva rewrites it as the famous line 内秘菩萨行，外现是声闻 (nèi mì púsà xíng, wài xiàn shì shēngwén, "inwardly hiding the bodhisattva practice, outwardly appearing as shravakas").

verses.en: "They show themselves as having desire, anger and delusion; and knowing that beings are stuck in their views, they take up those views too."
"Practicing like this, many of my disciples set beings free by skillful means. If one were to reveal everything they do, ignorant people would go mad."

cmp.note: 梵文说得很重：「会发狂」。英文 would go mad、白话「会吓得发狂」照译；鸠摩罗什缓和成「心则怀疑惑」。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit is strong: "they would go mad." The English "would go mad" and the plain Chinese follow it; Kumarajiva softens it to 心则怀疑惑 (xīn zé huái yíhuò, "their minds would be full of doubt").

verses.en: "Monks, this disciple of mine, Purna, practiced in the past under thousands of kotis of buddhas, and he took hold of their true Dharma, seeking this buddha knowledge.
"Everywhere he was the chief disciple, learned, a brilliant and fearless speaker, one who gladdened people, never weary, always serving by doing a buddha's work.
"He always mastered the great higher knowledges and gained the analytical knowledges. He knew the faculties of beings and the range they move in, and he always taught a pure Dharma.
"Making the excellent true Dharma known, he brought thousands of kotis of beings to maturity in this unsurpassed, supreme vehicle, while purifying his own excellent field.
"In the future too, in the same way, he will make offerings to thousands of kotis of buddhas, take hold of the excellent true Dharma, and purify his own field.
"Always fearless, he will teach the Dharma with thousands of kotis of skillful means, and he will bring many beings to maturity in the all-knowing knowledge that is free of outflows (defilements).
"Having made offerings to the guides of humankind and always kept the excellent true Dharma, he will become a self-born buddha in the world, Dharmaprabhasa, famous in all directions.
"His field will be thoroughly pure, always outstanding with the seven jewels. That eon will be Ratnavabhasa, and that world system will be Suvishuddha.
"Thousands of kotis of bodhisattvas, highly skilled in the great higher knowledges, pure, clean and with great supernatural power, will fill that world system.

"Then that Guide's community of disciples too will be thousands of kotis strong, with great supernatural power, practicing the meditation of the eight liberations, and masters of analytical knowledge.

cmp.note: 梵文这里只说「八解脱」，英文、白话照译；鸠摩罗什的散文和偈颂都多了「六通、三明」。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit mentions only the "eight liberations," and the English and plain Chinese follow it; Kumarajiva adds 六通、三明 (liù tōng, sān míng, "the six powers and the three knowledges") both in prose and in verse.

verses.en: "All the beings in that buddha-field will be pure and live the holy life, all born spontaneously, golden in color, bearing the thirty-two marks.
"There will be no thought of food there, except delight in the Dharma and joy in meditation. Nor will there be women there, nor any fear of the lower realms or bad destinies.
"Such will be the excellent field of Purna, who is full of every good quality, crowded with beings of real goodness. What I have described is only a small part of it."

Then the twelve hundred who had gained mastery thought: "How wonderful, how amazing! If only the Tathagata would predict us too, each one separately, just as the Blessed One has predicted these other great disciples!" The Blessed One knew with his own mind what was going on in the minds of those great disciples, and said to the venerable Mahakashyapa: "Kashyapa, here are these twelve hundred who have gained mastery, and I am now face to face with them. Kashyapa, I will now, one after another, predict all these twelve hundred who have gained mastery."

cmp.note: 「得自在者」，指心已得自在的阿罗汉。英文 those who had gained mastery 照字面；白话补了「阿罗汉」；鸠摩罗什直接写「千二百阿罗汉」。
cmp.en: "Those who have gained mastery," meaning arhats whose minds are fully under their control. The English "who had gained mastery" is literal; the plain Chinese adds 阿罗汉 (āluóhàn, "arhats"), and Kumarajiva simply writes 千二百阿罗汉 (qiān èrbǎi āluóhàn, "twelve hundred arhats").

verses.en: "Kashyapa, among them the monk Kaundinya, a great disciple, after sixty-two hundred thousand kotis of nayutas of buddhas, further on still, will appear in the world as a Tathagata named Samantaprabhasa (Light Shining Everywhere), an arhat, a fully awakened buddha, perfect in knowledge and conduct, the Sugata, knower of the world, unsurpassed, tamer of those who can be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a buddha, a Blessed One. Kashyapa, there will be five hundred Tathagatas with this one name. So these five hundred great disciples will all, one after another, wake up to unsurpassed, perfect awakening, and all of them will be named Samantaprabhasa: the five hundred who have gained mastery, headed by Gayakashyapa, Nadikashyapa, Urubilvakashyapa, Kala, Kalodayin, Aniruddha, Revata, Kapphina, Bakkula, Chunda and Svagata."

cmp.note: 梵文是「六十二个百千俱胝那由他」尊佛，英文、白话照译；鸠摩罗什作「六万二千亿佛」，数目算法不同。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says "sixty-two hundred thousand kotis of nayutas" of buddhas, which the English and plain Chinese follow; Kumarajiva gives 六万二千亿佛 (liùwàn èrqiān yì fó, "sixty-two thousand hundred-millions of buddhas"), counting differently.

verses.en: Then at that moment the Blessed One spoke these verses:
"This disciple of mine of the Kaundinya clan will become a Tathagata, a Lord of the World, in the future, in endless eons, and he will guide thousands of kotis of living beings.
"He will become a Victor named Samantaprabha (Light Everywhere), and his field will be pure, in endless eons in the future, after he has seen many buddhas without end.
"Radiant, endowed with a buddha's powers, his fame ringing out in the ten directions, honored by thousands of kotis of living beings, he will teach the highest, supreme awakening.
"There the bodhisattvas, full of effort, will climb into the finest palaces and live there in reflection, pure in conduct, always behaving well.
"Having heard the Dharma of the best of two-footed beings, they will keep traveling to other fields too, bowing to thousands of buddhas and making vast offerings to them.
"And in an instant they will come back again to the field of this Guide, the best of humans, named Prabhasa. Such will be the power of his practice.
"The lifespan of that Sugata will be sixty thousand full eons, and after the protector's final nirvana his Dharma will last here twice as long again.
"And then the semblance of it will last three times as long again. When the true Dharma of that protector is lost, humans and gods will grieve.

cmp.note: 梵文偈颂说相似正法住「三倍」，英文、白话照译；鸠摩罗什作「像法复倍是」，只说两倍，和前文格式一致。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit verse says the semblance of the Dharma lasts "three times" as long, which the English and plain Chinese follow; Kumarajiva writes 像法复倍是 (xiàngfǎ fù bèi shì, "the semblance Dharma doubles it again"), only twice, matching the pattern used elsewhere.

verses.en: "Victors with the same name, Samantaprabha, best of men, a full five hundred guides, will come one after another.
"All of them will have the same kind of splendor, the same power of supernatural ability and buddha-field; the same community and the same true Dharma; and their true Dharma will last the same time.
"All of them will then have this same name in the world with its gods, just as I proclaimed it before for Samantaprabhasa, the best of humans.
"In succession, one to the next, they will make predictions, kind and caring for others' good: 'Right after me, today, this one will come,' just as I now teach the whole world.
"So, Kashyapa, remember them here today, these full five hundred who have gained mastery, and my other disciples too, and tell it to the other disciples as well."

Then those five hundred arhats, having heard their own predictions face to face with the Blessed One, were pleased, elated, delighted and overjoyed, full of happiness and gladness. They went up to the Blessed One, fell with their heads at his feet, and said: "Blessed One, we confess our fault. Blessed One, we kept thinking, over and over: 'This is our final nirvana; we have reached final nirvana.' Blessed One, we were like people who are inexperienced, unskilled and do not know the right way. Why? Because, Blessed One, when we should have woken up to the Tathagata's knowledge, we were content with a little knowledge like this.

"Blessed One, it is as if a man went into a friend's house and got drunk or fell asleep, and the friend tied a priceless jewel into the hem of his clothes, thinking, 'Let this jewel be his.' Then, Blessed One, the man got up from his seat and went off to another region. There he fell on hard times and struggled to find food and clothing; with great effort he somehow got a little food, and with that he was pleased, content and happy. Then, Blessed One, his old friend, the one who had tied that priceless jewel into the hem of his clothes, saw him again

cmp.note: 梵文说那人「喝醉了或睡着了」，英文、白话照译；鸠摩罗什写「醉酒而卧」，又加了朋友「官事当行」先走一步的情节，梵本没有。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says the man was "drunk or asleep," and the English and plain Chinese follow it; Kumarajiva writes 醉酒而卧 (zuì jiǔ ér wò, "lay down drunk") and adds that the friend had to leave on official business, a detail not in the Sanskrit.

verses.en: and said to him: "Hey, man, why are you struggling to find food and clothing, when long ago, for your comfort, I tied a priceless jewel into the hem of your clothes, one that grants every wish? I gave you this jewel of mine, man, and it is still tied into the hem of your clothes. Yet you never looked to see: what has been tied onto me, who tied it, for what reason, for what cause was it tied? You are a fool, man, to be content with struggling for food and clothing. Go, take this jewel to the big city and exchange it, and with that money do everything that money can do."

cmp.note: 「能成办一切欲求的」宝珠。英文 grants every wish、白话「能满足一切欲望」照译；鸠摩罗什写成朋友要让他「五欲自恣」，把重点从宝珠转到享乐上。
cmp.en: A jewel "that brings about every wish." The English "grants every wish" and the plain Chinese follow it; Kumarajiva has the friend say he wanted the man to 五欲自恣 (wǔ yù zì zì, "freely enjoy the five sense pleasures"), shifting the stress from the jewel to enjoyment.

verses.en: "In just the same way, Blessed One, when the Tathagata was long ago carrying out the bodhisattva's practice, he stirred up in us the thought of all-knowing. But, Blessed One, we did not know it or understand it. Blessed One, we believed that we had reached nirvana at the stage of the arhat. We lived a hard life, Blessed One, being content with such a little knowledge, while our vow for all-knowing knowledge was never lost. And the Tathagata woke us up, Blessed One: 'Monks, do not think this is nirvana. Monks, in your mind-stream there are roots of goodness that I brought to maturity long ago. And now, that you think this is nirvana is my own skillful means, in the words I use to teach the Dharma.'"
"So the Blessed One woke us up, and today he has predicted us to unsurpassed, perfect awakening."

cmp.note: 梵文只说「今天为我们授了记」。鸠摩罗什多了一句「我今乃知实是菩萨」，点出这群阿罗汉原来是菩萨，梵本这里没有。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says only "today he has predicted us." Kumarajiva adds 我今乃知实是菩萨 (wǒ jīn nǎi zhī shí shì púsà, "now at last I know that I am truly a bodhisattva"), spelling out that these arhats were bodhisattvas all along; the Sanskrit does not say this here.

verses.en: Then at that moment the five hundred who had gained mastery, headed by Ajnata Kaundinya, spoke these verses:
"We are glad, overjoyed, to hear this comfort, so unsurpassed: that we have been predicted to the highest, supreme awakening. Homage to you, Guide of endless vision!
"We confess our fault before you: like children, unknowing and ignorant, we were content in the Sugata's teaching with a mere scrap of nirvana.
"It is as if some man went into a friend's house here, and his friend, rich and wealthy, gave him plenty to eat and drink.
"Having fed him well, he gave him a jewel worth a great deal, tying it with a knot into the hem of his inner garment; and having given it, he was pleased.
"The fool got up and left, and went to another city. There he fell on hard times, a poor wretch searching, worn out with looking for food.
"He was satisfied with the food he scraped together, never thinking of a fine meal; and he forgot that jewel, with no memory of it tied into his inner garment.
"Then the old friend who had given him the jewel in his own house saw him, scolded him soundly, and showed him the jewel in his garment.
"Seeing it, he was filled with the greatest happiness, such was the power of that jewel: he became a man of great wealth with a full treasury, enjoying the five kinds of sense pleasure.
"Just so, Blessed One, we did not know of our earlier vow like this; for the Tathagata himself gave it to us in former lives, here, through the long night.
"And here, Blessed One, we were childish in mind, knowing nothing in the Sugata's teaching. We were content with mere nirvana; we neither sought nor even thought of anything higher.
"But the Kinsman of the World woke us up: 'This is no nirvana of that kind at all. The excellent knowledge of the best of humans, that is nirvana, that is the highest happiness.'
"Having heard this grand, vast, many-sided, unsurpassed prediction, and of predicting one another in turn, Protector, we are filled with joy and delight beyond measure."
This is the eighth chapter, called Prediction for the Five Hundred Monks, in the noble Dharma discourse of the Lotus of the True Dharma.

cmp.note: 梵本这一品是第八品，本站排在第九，鸠摩罗什本也是第八品。英文、白话照梵文写「第八」。
cmp.en: In the Sanskrit this is the eighth chapter; the site places it ninth, while in Kumarajiva's version it is also the eighth. The English and plain Chinese keep the Sanskrit "eighth."

chapters.title: Chapter 10 · Predictions for Ananda, Rahula and Two Thousand Others

verses.en: Then at that moment the venerable Ananda thought: "If only we too could receive a prediction like this!" Having thought this, turned it over and longed for it, he rose from his seat and fell at the Blessed One's feet. And the venerable Rahula, having thought the same, turned it over and longed for it, also fell at the Blessed One's feet, and they said: "Blessed One, let our turn come too! Sugata, let our turn come too! For the Blessed One is our father, the one who brought us into being, our shelter and our protection. Blessed One, in this world with its gods, humans and asuras we are especially looked at; people say, 'These are the Blessed One's son and the Blessed One's attendant, and they keep the Blessed One's treasury of the Dharma.' So, Blessed One, it would be fitting if the Blessed One were to predict us quickly to unsurpassed, perfect awakening."

cmp.note: 梵文「父亲、生养者」对罗睺罗是字面意思（他真是佛的儿子），对阿难是比喻。英文、白话都照译；鸠摩罗什改成「唯有如来，我等所归」，没有「父亲」这层。
cmp.en: "Father, the one who begot us" is literal for Rahula, who really is the Buddha's son, and figurative for Ananda. The English and plain Chinese keep it; Kumarajiva writes 唯有如来，我等所归 (wéi yǒu rúlái, wǒděng suǒ guī, "only the Tathagata is our refuge"), dropping the word "father."

verses.en: Two thousand monks and more, disciples in training and beyond training, also rose from their seats, put their upper robes over one shoulder, joined their palms and stood facing the Blessed One, gazing up at him, turning over this same thought, this very buddha knowledge: "If only we too could receive a prediction to unsurpassed, perfect awakening!"

Then the Blessed One said to the venerable Ananda: "Ananda, in the future you will become a Tathagata named Sagaravaradharabuddhivikriditabhijna (One Whose Higher Knowledge Plays with an Awakened Mind Vast as the Ocean), an arhat, a fully awakened buddha, perfect in knowledge and conduct, the Sugata, knower of the world, unsurpassed, tamer of those who can be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a buddha, a Blessed One. After honoring, respecting, revering and making offerings to sixty-two kotis (a koti is ten million) of buddhas, keeping the true Dharma of those buddhas, Blessed Ones, and taking charge of their teaching, you will wake up to unsurpassed, perfect awakening. And once you have woken up to unsurpassed, perfect awakening, Ananda, you will bring to maturity for unsurpassed, perfect awakening hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas of bodhisattvas, as many as the grains of sand in twenty Ganges rivers.

cmp.note: 这个佛名字面是「以持海般殊胜的觉智游戏的神通者」。英文只给大意；白话译「海持觉游戏神通」；鸠摩罗什译「山海慧自在通王」，多了「山」和「王」。
cmp.en: The name literally means "one whose higher knowledge plays with an awakened mind that holds the excellent ocean." The English gives only the gist; the plain Chinese renders it 海持觉游戏神通 (hǎi chí jué yóuxì shéntōng); Kumarajiva's 山海慧自在通王 (shān hǎi huì zìzài tōng wáng, "Mountain-Sea Wisdom, Sovereign King of Powers") adds "mountain" and "king."

verses.en: "Your buddha-field will be rich and made of beryl. The world system will be called Anavanamitavaijayanti (Victory Banner Never Lowered), and the eon will be called Manojnashabdabhigarjita (Thundering with Lovely Sound). The lifespan of that Blessed One, the Tathagata Sagaravaradharabuddhivikriditabhijna, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, will be beyond measure, so many eons that no counting can reach their end; that is how countless the hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas of eons of that Blessed One's lifespan will be. And Ananda, after his final nirvana his true Dharma will last twice as long as that Blessed One's lifespan."

"And the semblance of the true Dharma will last twice as long as his true Dharma lasts. And Ananda, many hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas of buddhas in the ten directions, as many as the grains of sand in the Ganges, will speak in praise of that Tathagata Sagaravaradharabuddhivikriditabhijna."

cmp.note: 「正法的相似物」，即正法衰退后只剩外形的时期。英文 semblance of the true Dharma、白话「相似正法」照字面；鸠摩罗什译「像法」，后来成了正法、像法、末法三时说的专名。
cmp.en: "A likeness of the true Dharma," the period after the true Dharma declines when only its outward form remains. The English "semblance of the true Dharma" and the plain Chinese 相似正法 (xiāngsì zhèngfǎ, "resembling true Dharma") are literal; Kumarajiva's 像法 (xiàngfǎ, "image Dharma") later became a fixed term in the Chinese scheme of three ages: true Dharma, semblance Dharma, and final Dharma.

verses.en: Then at that moment the Blessed One spoke these verses:
"I announce to the community of monks: the good Ananda, who keeps my Dharma, will become a Victor in the future, after making offerings to sixty kotis of Sugatas.

cmp.note: 偈颂里是「六十俱胝」，散文里是「六十二俱胝」，梵本前后不一致，英文、白话都照各自原文译。鸠摩罗什偈颂里只写「当供养诸佛」，没有数目。
cmp.en: The verse says "sixty kotis," while the prose said "sixty-two kotis"; the Sanskrit is not consistent, and the English and plain Chinese follow each passage as it stands. Kumarajiva's verse just says 当供养诸佛 (dāng gòngyǎng zhū fó, "will make offerings to the buddhas"), with no number.

verses.en: "His name will be Sagarabuddhidharin (Holder of an Ocean-Wide Awakened Mind), and there he will be known as one who has gained the higher knowledges, in a pure and lovely field called Anonata Dhvajavaijayanti (Banner of Victory Never Lowered).

"There the bodhisattvas will be like the sands of the Ganges, and he will bring still more to maturity. That Victor will have great supernatural power, and his fame will ring out in the world of the ten directions.
"His life then will be beyond measure, and he will remain out of compassion, for the good of the world. And after the protecting Victor's final nirvana, his true Dharma will last twice as long.
"The semblance of it will last twice as long again in that Victor's teaching. Even then, beings like the sands of the Ganges will plant here the cause of a buddha's awakening."

Then eight thousand bodhisattvas in that assembly who had newly set out in the vehicle thought: "We have never before heard such a grand prediction even for bodhisattvas, let alone for disciples. What could be the cause of this, what the reason?" The Blessed One knew with his own mind what was going on in the minds of those bodhisattvas, and said to them: "Sons of good family, Ananda and I set our minds on unsurpassed, perfect awakening together, in the same instant, the same moment, in the presence of the Tathagata Dharmagaganabhyudgataraja (King Risen High in the Sky of the Dharma), the arhat, the fully awakened buddha. Back then, sons of good family, he devoted himself constantly to hearing much, and I devoted myself to effort. So I woke up to unsurpassed, perfect awakening sooner.

cmp.note: 佛名字面是「在法的虚空中升起的王」。白话译「法云涌起王」，把「虚空」换成了「云」；鸠摩罗什只取后半，译「空王佛」。
cmp.en: The name literally means "king risen up in the sky of the Dharma." The plain Chinese 法云涌起王 (fǎ yún yǒngqǐ wáng) turns "sky" into "cloud"; Kumarajiva keeps only part of it: 空王佛 (Kōngwáng Fó, "Buddha King of Space").

verses.en: "But the good Ananda has always been the keeper of the treasury of the true Dharma of the buddhas, the Blessed Ones. That, sons of good family, was this son of good family's vow, for the sake of bringing bodhisattvas to completion."

Then the venerable Ananda, having heard from the Blessed One his own prediction to unsurpassed, perfect awakening, having heard of the splendid qualities of his own buddha-field, and having heard of the practice of his past vow, was pleased, elated, delighted and overjoyed, full of happiness and gladness. And at that moment he remembered the true Dharma of many hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas of buddhas, and his own past vow.
Then at that moment the venerable Ananda spoke these verses:
"How wonderful are the immeasurable Victors, who remind me of the Dharma teaching I heard! The protecting Victors who have passed into final nirvana, I remember them as if it were today or tomorrow.
"I have no doubts left; I stand firm on the way to awakening. This is my skillful means: I am the Sugata's attendant, and I keep the true Dharma for the sake of awakening."

cmp.note: 阿难说做侍者、守法藏本身就是他的「善巧方便」。英文 skillful means、白话「善巧方便」照译；鸠摩罗什「方便为侍者」压缩成一句，意思相同。
cmp.en: Ananda says that serving as attendant and guarding the teaching is itself his "skill in means." The English "skillful means" and the plain Chinese 善巧方便 (shànqiǎo fāngbiàn) translate it directly; Kumarajiva compresses it to 方便为侍者 (fāngbiàn wéi shìzhě, "as a means, he is the attendant"), with the same sense.

verses.en: Then the Blessed One said to the venerable, good Rahula: "Good Rahula, in the future you will become a Tathagata named Saptaratnapadmavikrantagamin (One Who Walks Striding on Lotuses of the Seven Jewels), an arhat, a fully awakened buddha, perfect in knowledge and conduct, the Sugata, knower of the world, unsurpassed, tamer of those who can be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a buddha, a Blessed One, after you have honored, respected, revered, made offerings to and worshipped Tathagatas, arhats, fully awakened buddhas as many as the atoms of dust in ten world systems. You will always be the eldest son of those buddhas, the Blessed Ones, just as you are mine now.

"And good Rahula, the lifespan of that Blessed One, the Tathagata Saptaratnapadmavikrantagamin, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, will be just the same, and his wealth of good qualities of every kind will be just the same, as the splendid qualities of every kind in the buddha-field of that Blessed One, the Tathagata Sagaravaradharabuddhivikriditabhijna, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha. And Rahula, you will be the eldest son of that Tathagata Sagaravaradharabuddhivikriditabhijna too. After that, further on, you will wake up to unsurpassed, perfect awakening."
Then at that moment the Blessed One spoke these verses:
"This Rahula is my eldest son, my own son, born to me when I was a prince. Now that I have reached awakening, he is still my son, an heir of the Dharma, a great seer."

cmp.note: aurasa 是「亲生的、从胸口生的」，dāyāda 是「继承人」。梵文用血缘的儿子过渡到继承法的儿子。英文 own son / heir of the Dharma、白话「亲生儿子 / 继承教法」都保留了两层；鸠摩罗什「受法为法子」只留了后一层的说法。
cmp.en: Aurasa means "one's own, born of one's breast," and dāyāda means "heir": the Sanskrit moves from a son by blood to a son who inherits the Dharma. The English "my own son... an heir of the Dharma" and the plain Chinese keep both; Kumarajiva's 受法为法子 (shòu fǎ wéi fǎzǐ, "receiving the Dharma, he is a Dharma son") keeps the second idea in his own phrasing.

verses.en: "In the future you will see many kotis of buddhas, beyond all measure. He will be the son of all those Victors, seeking awakening."
"Rahula's practice goes unseen, and I know this vow of his. Among his relatives in the world he declares, 'I am the Tathagata's son.'

cmp.note: 「不为人所知的修行」。英文 practice goes unseen、白话照译；鸠摩罗什译「密行」，后来成了罗睺罗「密行第一」这个称号的出处。
cmp.en: "Practice that is not known to others." The English "practice goes unseen" and the plain Chinese translate it directly; Kumarajiva's 密行 (mìxíng, "hidden practice") later became the basis of Rahula's traditional title, "foremost in hidden practice."

verses.en: "The good qualities of my own son Rahula here are kotis of nayutas beyond measure; there is never any counting them. For this is how he stands firm, for the sake of awakening."

The Blessed One also saw those two thousand disciples, in training and beyond training, looking toward the Blessed One, facing him, with clear, soft and gentle minds. Then at that moment the Blessed One said to the venerable Ananda: "Ananda, do you see these two thousand disciples, in training and beyond training?" He said: "I see them, Blessed One; I see them, Sugata."

The Blessed One said: "Ananda, all these two thousand monks will carry out the bodhisattva's practice together. They will honor, respect, revere, make offerings to, worship and serve buddhas, Blessed Ones, as many as the atoms of dust in fifty world systems, and keep the true Dharma. Then in their last body, in one instant, one moment, one second, at one and the same time, they will wake up to unsurpassed, perfect awakening in the ten directions, in different world systems, each in his own buddha-field. They will become Tathagatas, arhats, fully awakened buddhas, all named Ratnaketuraja (King of the Jewel Banner). Their lifespan will be a full eon. The splendid qualities of their buddha-fields will be the same; their communities of disciples and bodhisattvas will be the same; their final nirvana will be the same; and their true Dharma will last the same length of time."

cmp.note: 佛名是「宝幢王」，英文、白话照译；鸠摩罗什作「宝相如来」，把「幢（旗）」换成了「相」，也没有「王」。
cmp.en: The name is "King of the Jewel Banner," which the English and plain Chinese follow; Kumarajiva has 宝相如来 (Bǎoxiàng Rúlái, "Jewel-Mark Tathagata"), replacing "banner" with "mark" and dropping "king."

verses.en: Then at that moment the Blessed One spoke these verses:
"Ananda, these two thousand disciples standing before me are wise, and today I predict them: in the future they will become Tathagatas.
"Making the highest offerings to buddhas beyond count, as the comparisons have shown, they will win my supreme awakening, standing in their very last body.

cmp.note: 字面是「以无尽的譬喻和例证」，可以读成在形容所供养的佛多到要用譬喻来说（如前文的「微尘」），也可以读成「以无穷的譬喻和示现」去供养。白话取后一种；英文取前一种，与鸠摩罗什「如上说尘数」一致。这半句拿不准。
cmp.en: Literally "with endless comparisons and illustrations." It can mean the buddhas are so many that they can only be described by comparison (like the "atoms of dust" above), or that the offerings are made "with endless parables and displays." The plain Chinese takes the second reading; the English takes the first, which matches Kumarajiva's 如上说尘数 (rú shàng shuō chénshù, "as many as the dust grains said above"). The phrase is uncertain.

verses.en: "With one name, in the ten directions, in one instant and one moment, seated at the foot of the finest of trees, they will touch knowledge and become buddhas.
"They will all have one name, Jewel Banner, famous here in the world. Their fields will be equally fine, and their communities of disciples and bodhisattvas the same.
"Rich in supernatural power, they will make the Dharma known everywhere in all this world, in the ten directions; and when they reach nirvana, their true Dharma will last just the same."

Then those disciples in training and beyond training, having heard their own predictions face to face from the Blessed One, were pleased, elated, delighted and overjoyed, full of happiness and gladness, and spoke to the Blessed One in two verses:
"Lamp of the world, we are satisfied, having heard this prediction. Tathagata, we are as happy as if we had been sprinkled with the nectar of immortality."

cmp.note: amṛta 字面是「不死」，指神话里的不死甘露。英文 nectar of immortality 把「不死」译出；白话和鸠摩罗什的「甘露」只剩「甜美的露水」。
cmp.en: Amṛta literally means "deathless," the mythical drink of immortality. The English "nectar of immortality" keeps the "deathless"; the plain Chinese and Kumarajiva's 甘露 (gānlù, "sweet dew") keep only the sweetness.

verses.en: "Best of humans, we will have no doubt and no hesitation. Today we have found happiness, having heard this prediction."
This is the ninth chapter, called Prediction for Ananda, Rahula and Two Thousand Other Monks, in the noble Dharma discourse of the Lotus of the True Dharma.

Then the Blessed One, addressing himself through the bodhisattva, great being Bhaishajyaraja (the Medicine King), spoke to those eighty thousand bodhisattvas: "Bhaishajyaraja, do you see in this assembly the many gods, nagas, yakshas, gandharvas, asuras, garudas, kinnaras and mahoragas (spirit beings of many kinds), humans and non-humans, monks, nuns, laymen and laywomen, those set out in the disciple vehicle, the solitary-buddha vehicle and the bodhisattva vehicle, who have heard this Dharma discourse face to face with the Tathagata?" He said: "I see them, Blessed One; I see them, Sugata." The Blessed One said: "Bhaishajyaraja, all of these are bodhisattvas, great beings: everyone in this assembly who has heard even a single verse, even a single line, or who has rejoiced in this sutra with even a single moment of thought. Bhaishajyaraja, I predict all these four assemblies to unsurpassed, perfect awakening."

cmp.note: 梵文先宣布「这些人全都是菩萨大士」，再授记。英文、白话照译；鸠摩罗什省去了这句宣告，直接说「我皆与授记」。
