cmp.en: The Sanskrit first declares "all of these are bodhisattvas, great beings," and then gives the prediction. The English and plain Chinese keep it; Kumarajiva leaves out the declaration and goes straight to 我皆与授记 (wǒ jiē yǔ shòujì, "I give them all the prediction").

verses.en: "And Bhaishajyaraja, whoever hears this Dharma discourse after the Tathagata's final nirvana, even hearing a single verse, even rejoicing in it with a single moment of thought, these sons and daughters of good family too, Bhaishajyaraja, I predict to unsurpassed, perfect awakening. Bhaishajyaraja, these sons and daughters of good family will be people who have served a full hundred thousand kotis of nayutas (huge numbers) of buddhas; Bhaishajyaraja, these sons and daughters of good family will be people who have made vows before hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas of buddhas."

"You should know that they have been reborn here among humans in Jambudvipa (our continent) out of compassion for beings: those who keep even a single verse of this Dharma discourse, recite it, make it known, help others take it in, copy it out and, having copied it, keep it in mind and look at it from time to time. They will feel for that book the reverence due to the Tathagata; with the reverence due to the Teacher they will honor, respect, revere and make offerings to it; and they will worship that book with flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, flags, music and so on, with bows and joined palms. Bhaishajyaraja, whatever sons or daughters of good family keep even a single verse of this Dharma discourse, or rejoice in it, I predict all of them, Bhaishajyaraja, to unsurpassed, perfect awakening."

cmp.note: pustaka 是写成的「书、经卷」。梵本这里一再强调对书本本身的供养，反映出写本崇拜。英文 book、白话「经卷」照译；鸠摩罗什也写「于此经卷敬视如佛」。
cmp.en: Pustaka is a written "book, manuscript." The Sanskrit keeps stressing worship of the physical book itself, which reflects a cult of the written text. The English "book" and the plain Chinese 经卷 (jīngjuàn, "sutra scroll") follow it; Kumarajiva likewise says 于此经卷敬视如佛 (yú cǐ jīngjuàn jìng shì rú fó, "regard this scroll with reverence as if it were the Buddha").

verses.en: "And Bhaishajyaraja, if any man or woman should ask, 'What sort of beings will become Tathagatas, arhats, fully awakened buddhas in the future?', then Bhaishajyaraja, that man or woman should be shown a son or daughter of good family who keeps even a four-line verse of this Dharma discourse, or has it heard, or teaches it, or holds this Dharma discourse in reverence: 'This is the son or daughter of good family who will become a Tathagata, an arhat, a fully awakened buddha in the future. See it this way.' Why? Because, Bhaishajyaraja, that son or daughter of good family should be recognized by the world with its gods as a Tathagata."

"Anyone who keeps even a single verse of this Dharma discourse should be honored like a Tathagata, to say nothing of someone who takes up this whole Dharma discourse from beginning to end, keeps it, recites it, masters it, makes it known, copies it or has it copied, and having copied it keeps it in mind; who honors that book, respects it, reveres, worships, venerates and serves it with flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, flags, music, joined palms, bows and prostrations. Bhaishajyaraja, that son or daughter of good family should be known as one who has already accomplished unsurpassed, perfect awakening, and as one who has seen the Tathagata. Out of kindness and compassion for the world, by the power of a vow, that person has been reborn here among humans in Jambudvipa to make this Dharma discourse known."

"You should know that such a person has set aside his own grand store of merit and a grand rebirth in a buddha-field, and has been born here after my final nirvana for the good of beings and out of compassion, in order to make this Dharma discourse known. Bhaishajyaraja, that son or daughter of good family should be known as a messenger of the Tathagata. Bhaishajyaraja, that son or daughter of good family should be recognized as one who does the Tathagata's work, sent by the Tathagata: anyone who makes this Dharma discourse known after the Tathagata's final nirvana, even if in private, in secret, to just one single being, makes it known or tells it."

cmp.note: 字面是「在暗处、像偷东西一样」。英文 in private, in secret、白话「私下里、悄悄地」都淡化成「秘密」；鸠摩罗什的「窃为一人说」保留了「窃」字。
cmp.en: Literally "in a hidden place, as if by theft." The English "in private, in secret" and the plain Chinese 私下里、悄悄地 ("privately, quietly") soften it to secrecy; Kumarajiva's 窃为一人说 (qiè wèi yì rén shuō, "stealthily tell one person") keeps the word 窃 (qiè, "steal").

verses.en: "And Bhaishajyaraja, suppose some being, with a wicked, sinful, violent mind, were to speak ill of the Tathagata to his face for an entire eon; and suppose someone else were to say even one unpleasant word, true or false, to Dharma teachers who keep this sutra, whether householders or monastics. I say the second is the far heavier bad deed. Why? Because, Bhaishajyaraja, that son or daughter of good family should be known as adorned with the Tathagata's own ornaments. Bhaishajyaraja, whoever copies out this Dharma discourse, makes it into a book and carries it on the shoulder, carries the Tathagata on the shoulder."

cmp.note: 梵文是很具体的画面：把写成书的经扛在肩上，就是扛着如来。英文、白话照译；鸠摩罗什写成「则为如来肩所荷担」，变成被如来用肩扛着，主客正好颠倒。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit is concrete: carrying the sutra as a book on your shoulder is carrying the Tathagata. The English and plain Chinese follow it; Kumarajiva writes 则为如来肩所荷担 (zé wéi rúlái jiān suǒ hèdān, "is carried on the Tathagata's shoulder"), reversing who carries whom.

verses.en: "Wherever such a person goes, beings should greet him with joined palms; they should honor, respect, revere, make offerings to, worship and serve him with divine and human flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, flags, music, food, drink and vehicles, and with heaps of the finest divine jewels. That Dharma teacher should be honored, respected, revered and given offerings, and heaps of divine jewels should be presented to that Dharma teacher. Why? Because if he were to let this Dharma discourse be heard even once, countless, measureless beings who hear it would quickly accomplish unsurpassed, perfect awakening."
Then at that moment the Blessed One spoke these verses:
"Whoever wants to stand in buddhahood and seeks the self-born knowledge should honor the beings who keep this way of teaching.

cmp.note: 「自生者的智慧」，即不靠老师、自己生起的佛智。英文 self-born knowledge 照字面；白话加了括注；鸠摩罗什译「自然智」。
cmp.en: "The knowledge of the Self-Born," the buddha knowledge that arises without a teacher. The English "self-born knowledge" is literal and the plain Chinese adds a gloss; Kumarajiva renders it 自然智 (zìrán zhì, "natural knowledge").

verses.en: "Whoever wants all-knowing and wonders how it might come quickly should keep this sutra, or honor the one who keeps it.
"Whoever recites this sutra out of compassion for beings has been sent by the Lord of the World to train beings.
"Whoever keeps this sutra out of compassion for beings is a steadfast one who has given up a lovely rebirth and come here.
"His rebirth is at his own command; that is why he is seen there, speaking this unsurpassed sutra in the last age.
"Honor the Dharma teacher with divine flowers and with every human perfume; cover him with divine clothes and shower him with jewels.
"Always join your palms to him, as to the self-born king of Victors, whoever keeps this sutra in this terrible last age after the final nirvana.
"Give food to eat and food to enjoy, drink and nourishment, dwellings, beds, seats and kotis of garments as offerings to the Victor's son, even if he speaks the sutra only once.
"He does what the Tathagatas must do, and I have sent him into human life: whoever in the final age copies out this sutra, keeps it, or even listens to it.
"If a man were to stand here face to face with the Victor and speak ill of him for a full eon, with a wicked mind and a frown, that man would bring about a great deal of evil.
"But if someone speaks abuse and insult against those who keep this sutra and make it known here, I say his evil is greater still.
"If a man, seeking this supreme awakening, were to praise me face to face with joined palms for a full eon, with many kotis of nayutas of verses,
"he would gain much merit there, praising me with delight; but the person who speaks in praise of those who keep the sutra gains far more than that.
"If someone for eighteen thousand kotis of eons makes offerings to these books with sounds, sights and tastes, with divine perfumes and divine things to touch,

cmp.note: 梵文是「一万八千俱胝劫」，供养的对象是「这些经卷」。英文、白话照译；鸠摩罗什作「八十亿劫」，供养对象换成「持经者」。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says "eighteen thousand kotis of eons," and the offerings are made to "these books." The English and plain Chinese follow it; Kumarajiva has 八十亿劫 (bāshí yì jié, "eight billion eons") and makes the offerings go to 持经者 (chí jīng zhě, "those who keep the sutra").

verses.en: "having made offerings to the books like this for eighteen thousand kotis of eons, if he hears this sutra just once, he gains a great and wonderful gain."

"I tell you, Bhaishajyaraja, I announce it to you: I have spoken many Dharma discourses, Bhaishajyaraja, I speak them now and I will speak more. And of all those Dharma discourses, Bhaishajyaraja, this Dharma discourse is the one that goes against the whole world, the one the whole world finds hard to believe. Bhaishajyaraja, it is the Tathagata's own inner secret of the Dharma, guarded by the Tathagata's power, never before opened up, never before told, never before declared. Bhaishajyaraja, this Dharma discourse is rejected by many people even while the Tathagata is still living, to say nothing of after his final nirvana."

cmp.note: 「与整个世间相违」，即违背世人的常识与期待。英文 goes against the whole world、白话照译；鸠摩罗什把这一段改写成「此法华经最为难信难解」，又在偈颂里加了「法华最第一」，梵本这里没有「第一」。
cmp.en: "Opposed to the whole world," running against what people commonly believe and expect. The English "goes against the whole world" and the plain Chinese follow it; Kumarajiva rewrites this as 此法华经最为难信难解 (cǐ Fǎhuá jīng zuì wéi nán xìn nán jiě, "this Lotus Sutra is the hardest to believe and understand") and adds, in verse, 法华最第一 (Fǎhuá zuì dì-yī, "the Lotus is foremost"), a ranking the Sanskrit does not make here.

verses.en: "Yet, Bhaishajyaraja, those sons and daughters of good family should be known as covered by the Tathagata's robe. The Tathagatas living in other world systems watch over them and empower them. They will have their own strength of faith, strength of roots of goodness and strength of vows. Bhaishajyaraja, those sons and daughters of good family will live in the same dwelling as the Tathagata, and the Tathagata will stroke their heads with his hand: whoever, after the Tathagata's final nirvana, trusts this Dharma discourse, recites it, copies it, honors it, respects it, and lets others hear it."

"And Bhaishajyaraja, in whatever spot on earth this Dharma discourse is spoken, taught, copied, studied or chanted together, in that spot, Bhaishajyaraja, a shrine to the Tathagata should be built, large, made of jewels, tall and imposing. And there is no need to place relics of the Tathagata in it. Why? Because the Tathagata's body, whole and undivided, has been placed in any spot on earth where this Dharma discourse is spoken, taught, read, chanted together or copied, or where it stands written down as a book. And that stupa should be honored, respected, revered, worshipped and venerated with every kind of flower, incense, perfume, garland, ointment, powder, robe, parasol, banner, flag and victory pennant,

cmp.note: 梵文 śarīra 既指「身体」也指「舍利（遗骨）」，这里说经所在之处已经有了如来「整块的身体」，所以不必再放舍利。英文 body, whole and undivided、鸠摩罗什「如来全身」都把这层双关译成「全身」。
cmp.en: Sanskrit śarīra means both "body" and "relics (bodily remains)." The text says that where the sutra is, the Tathagata's "solid, single body" is already present, so no relics are needed. The English "body, whole and undivided" and Kumarajiva's 如来全身 (rúlái quánshēn, "the Tathagata's whole body") both render the pun as "whole body."

verses.en: "and worship should be made with every kind of song, music, dance, drums, cymbals and ensemble playing. And Bhaishajyaraja, whatever beings get to bow to that shrine of the Tathagata, worship it or even see it, all of them, Bhaishajyaraja, should be known as having come near to unsurpassed, perfect awakening. Why? Because, Bhaishajyaraja, many householders and monastics follow the bodhisattva's practice and yet do not get to see, hear, copy or worship this Dharma discourse. Bhaishajyaraja, as long as they do not hear this Dharma discourse, they are not yet skilled in the bodhisattva's practice.

"But those who hear this Dharma discourse, and having heard it, trust it, enter into it, understand it and take hold of it, at that time will stand close to unsurpassed, perfect awakening; they will be very near it."

"Bhaishajyaraja, it is like a man who needs water and is looking for water. For the sake of water he has a well dug in a dry, high piece of land. As long as he sees dry, pale dirt being carried out, he knows: 'Water is still far from here.' Then later the man sees damp earth being carried out, mixed with water, turned into mud and slime, with drops of water dripping from it, and sees the well-diggers smeared with mud. Then, Bhaishajyaraja, having seen these early signs, the man has no more doubt or hesitation: 'Water is close now.'

"In just the same way, Bhaishajyaraja, bodhisattvas, great beings, are far from unsurpassed, perfect awakening as long as they do not hear this Dharma discourse, do not take it up, do not enter it, do not plunge into it, and do not reflect on it. But Bhaishajyaraja, when bodhisattvas, great beings, hear this Dharma discourse, take it up, keep it, recite it, enter it, study it, reflect on it and cultivate it, then they will be close to unsurpassed, perfect awakening. Bhaishajyaraja, beings' unsurpassed, perfect awakening is born from this Dharma discourse. Why? Because this Dharma discourse is the Tathagatas', the arhats', the fully awakened buddhas' uncovering of what they have said with the deepest hidden meaning. It tells the hidden place of the Dharma, so that bodhisattvas, great beings, may reach completion."

cmp.note: 「对最深的密意之言的揭开」。英文、白话照译；鸠摩罗什改写成有名的「开方便门，示真实相」，把「密意」解释成「方便」与「真实」的对照。
cmp.en: "The uncovering of what was said with the deepest hidden intent." The English and plain Chinese follow it; Kumarajiva recasts it in the famous phrase 开方便门，示真实相 (kāi fāngbiàn mén, shì zhēnshí xiàng, "opening the gate of skillful means to show the mark of the real"), reading "hidden intent" as a contrast between skillful means and truth.

verses.en: "Bhaishajyaraja, any bodhisattva who is alarmed, frightened or terrified by this Dharma discourse should be known, Bhaishajyaraja, as a bodhisattva, a great being, who has only newly set out in the vehicle. And if someone of the disciple vehicle is alarmed, frightened or terrified by this Dharma discourse, Bhaishajyaraja, that person of the disciple vehicle should be known as conceited, one who thinks he has reached what he has not."

"Bhaishajyaraja, any bodhisattva, great being, who makes this Dharma discourse known to the four assemblies in the last age, the last time after the Tathagata's final nirvana, should do so, Bhaishajyaraja, by entering the Tathagata's dwelling, putting on the Tathagata's robe, and sitting on the Tathagata's seat; that is how this Dharma discourse should be made known to the four assemblies. And what, Bhaishajyaraja, is the Tathagata's dwelling? Living in loving-kindness toward all beings, Bhaishajyaraja, is the Tathagata's dwelling; that son of good family should enter it. And what, Bhaishajyaraja, is the Tathagata's robe? Great patience and gentleness, Bhaishajyaraja, is the Tathagata's robe; that son or daughter of good family should put it on. And what, Bhaishajyaraja, is the Tathagata's Dharma seat?

cmp.note: 梵文只说「对一切众生的慈爱（maitrī）」。英文 loving-kindness、白话「慈爱」照译；鸠摩罗什作「大慈悲心」，多了「悲」。layana 原是「庇护所、居处」，英文 dwelling、白话「居室」，鸠摩罗什「如来室」。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says only "loving-kindness (maitrī) toward all beings." The English "loving-kindness" and the plain Chinese 慈爱 (cí'ài) follow it; Kumarajiva writes 大慈悲心 (dà cíbēi xīn, "a mind of great kindness and compassion"), adding compassion. Layana means "shelter, dwelling": the English "dwelling," the plain Chinese 居室 (jūshì), and Kumarajiva's 如来室 (rúlái shì, "the Tathagata's room").

verses.en: "Entering into the emptiness of all things, Bhaishajyaraja, is the Tathagata's Dharma seat. That son of good family should sit there, and having sat down, should make this Dharma discourse known to the four assemblies. With a mind that does not shrink back, the bodhisattva should make it known in front of the company of bodhisattvas, to the four assemblies set out in the bodhisattva vehicle. And Bhaishajyaraja, though I am living in another world system, I will gather assemblies for that son of good family by means of magically created beings, and I will send magically created monks, nuns, laymen and laywomen to hear the Dharma. They will not contradict what that Dharma teacher says, nor reject it."

"And if he goes off into the forest, there too I will send him many gods, nagas, yakshas, gandharvas, asuras, garudas, kinnaras and mahoragas to hear the Dharma. Bhaishajyaraja, though I am living in another world system, I will show my face to that son of good family; and whatever words and syllables of this Dharma discourse he has lost, I will say them back to him as he studies."
Then at that moment the Blessed One spoke these verses:
"Put away all shrinking back and listen to a sutra like this. Getting to hear it is rare, and trusting it is rare too.

cmp.note: līyanā 是「退缩、畏缩」。英文 shrinking back、白话「退缩」照译；鸠摩罗什译「懈怠」，从害怕退缩变成了懒惰。
cmp.en: Līyanā means "shrinking, holding back." The English "shrinking back" and the plain Chinese 退缩 (tuìsuō) follow it; Kumarajiva renders it 懈怠 (xièdài, "laziness"), turning timidity into sloth.

verses.en: "It is like someone who needs water and has a well dug in dry land; as it is dug, again and again he sees dry dirt.
"Seeing this, he thinks: 'Water must be far from here. This sign shows it is far: only dry dirt is coming up.'
"But when he sees, again and again, wet and moist earth, he becomes certain: 'Water is not far from here.'
"In the same way, people like that are far from a buddha's knowledge, as long as they have not heard this sutra and have not cultivated it again and again.
"But when they hear this profound king of sutras, which settles the question for the disciples, and reflect on it even once,

cmp.note: 「为声闻作出的决断」，指这部经最终说清楚了声闻的归宿（也能成佛）。英文 settles the question for the disciples、白话照译；鸠摩罗什「决了声闻法」意思相近。
cmp.en: "The decision about the disciples," meaning the sutra finally settles where disciples end up (they too will become buddhas). The English "settles the question for the disciples" and the plain Chinese follow it; Kumarajiva's 决了声闻法 (jué liǎo shēngwén fǎ, "resolving the shravaka teaching") is close.

verses.en: "those wise ones are close to a buddha's knowledge, just as when the earth is wet, water is said to be near.
"Entering the Victor's dwelling, putting on my robe, and sitting on my seat, the wise one should speak without fear.
"The strength of loving-kindness is the dwelling, patience and gentleness the robe, and emptiness my seat; standing in these, one should teach.
"If clods of earth, sticks, spears, insults or threats come to him while he speaks there, he should bear them, remembering me.
"In thousands of kotis of fields I have a firm body, and I teach the Dharma to beings for inconceivable kotis of eons.
"For that hero who makes this sutra known after my final nirvana, I too will send many magically created beings:
"monks and nuns, laymen and laywomen, who will make offerings to him and gather assemblies too.
"And those who would give him clods, sticks, insults, threats and abuse, the magically created beings will hold them back.
"And when he is living alone, studying in a place without people, in the forest or in the mountains,
"then I will show him my shining body, and when he slips in his study, I will say it back to him again and again.
"And while he lives there alone, wandering in the forest, I will send him gods and yakshas as companions, many times over.
"Such are the good qualities of one who makes this known to the four assemblies: living alone in forest caves, studying, he will see me.
"His eloquence will be unhindered, and he will know many ways of explaining the Dharma; he will delight thousands of kotis of living beings, because the Buddha empowers him.
"And the beings who rely on him will all quickly become bodhisattvas; and those who keep company with him will see buddhas as many as the sands of the Ganges."
This is the tenth chapter, called The Dharma Teacher, in the noble Dharma discourse of the Lotus of the True Dharma.

cmp.note: 梵本这一品是第十品，本站排在第十一，鸠摩罗什本也是第十品。英文、白话照梵文写「第十」。
cmp.en: In the Sanskrit this is the tenth chapter; the site places it eleventh, and Kumarajiva's version also has it tenth. The English and plain Chinese keep the Sanskrit "tenth."

chapters.title: Chapter 12 · The Stupa Appears (with the Story of Devadatta)

verses.en: Then, in front of the Blessed One, from that spot of ground in the middle of the assembly, a stupa (a monument holding a buddha's remains) made of the seven precious things rose up, five hundred yojanas (a yojana is a day's journey, roughly ten-odd kilometers) high and broad in proportion. Having risen, it stood still in the open sky, many-colored and lovely to see. It was beautifully adorned with five thousand railings for holding flowers, decked with many thousands of arched gateways, hung with thousands of flags and victory banners, hung with thousands of jewel garlands, hung with thousands of silk ribbons and bells, and it gave off the scent of tamala leaves and sandalwood. That scent filled this entire world system.

cmp.note: 梵文只说宽度「与高度相称」。英文、白话照译；鸠摩罗什写成「纵广二百五十由旬」，给了一个具体数字。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit only says the width was "in proportion" to the height. The English and plain Chinese follow it; Kumarajiva gives a precise figure: 纵广二百五十由旬 (zòngguǎng èrbǎi wǔshí yóuxún, "two hundred and fifty yojanas long and wide").

verses.en: Its tiers of parasols rose all the way up to the palaces of the gods of the Four Great Kings, made of the seven precious things: gold, silver, beryl, musaragalva, ashmagarbha, red pearl and karketana. The young gods of the Thirty-Three (the heaven where Shakra rules) scattered, strewed and showered that jewel stupa with heavenly mandarava and great mandarava flowers. And from that jewel stupa came a voice like this: "Well done, well done, Blessed Shakyamuni! You have spoken this Dharma discourse, the Lotus of the True Dharma, well. That is how it is, Blessed One; that is how it is, Sugata (the Well-Gone One)."

cmp.note: 梵文多宝佛只说「你讲得好，正是这样」。英文、白话照译；鸠摩罗什加了「能以平等大慧，教菩萨法，佛所护念」等赞语，还插入了天龙八部供养一段，梵本这里没有。
cmp.en: In the Sanskrit, Prabhutaratna only says "you have spoken it well; that is how it is." The English and plain Chinese follow it; Kumarajiva adds praises such as 能以平等大慧，教菩萨法，佛所护念 (néng yǐ píngděng dà huì, jiào púsà fǎ, fó suǒ hùniàn, "with great impartial wisdom you teach the bodhisattva Dharma, guarded by the buddhas"), and also inserts a passage on gods, nagas and others making offerings, which is not here in the Sanskrit.

verses.en: Then the four assemblies (monks, nuns, laymen and laywomen), seeing that great jewel stupa standing in the open sky, were delighted and filled with joy, gladness and clear faith. At that moment they rose from their seats and stood with joined palms.

Then at that moment the bodhisattva, great being named Mahapratibhana (Great Eloquence), knowing that the world with its gods, humans and asuras was full of curiosity, said to the Blessed One: "Blessed One, what is the cause, what is the condition, for such a great jewel stupa to appear in the world? And Blessed One, who is it that sends out such a voice from this great jewel stupa?" When he had said this, the Blessed One said to the bodhisattva, great being Mahapratibhana: "Mahapratibhana, in this great jewel stupa the body of a Tathagata stays, whole and solid. This is his stupa; it is he who sends out the voice. Mahapratibhana, in the lower direction, beyond countless hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas (both huge numbers) of world systems, there is a world system called Ratnavishuddha (Jewel-Pure). In it there was a Tathagata, an arhat, a fully awakened buddha named Prabhutaratna (Many Jewels).

cmp.note: 梵文说宝净世界在「下方」。英文、白话照译；鸠摩罗什作「东方」。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit places the world Ratnavishuddha "in the lower direction." The English and plain Chinese follow it; Kumarajiva has 东方 (dōngfāng, "in the east").

cmp.note: 「凝成一整块」，指身体完整未散。英文 whole and solid、白话「完整凝成一体」照译；鸠摩罗什译「全身」，后来成为「多宝全身舍利」的说法。
cmp.en: "Formed into one solid mass," meaning the body is whole and undispersed. The English "whole and solid" and the plain Chinese 完整凝成一体 ("whole, solidified into one") follow it; Kumarajiva writes 全身 (quánshēn, "the whole body"), the source of the later phrase "Prabhutaratna's whole-body relic."

verses.en: "That Blessed One had made this vow long ago: 'When I was practicing the bodhisattva's practice in the past, I did not reach unsurpassed, perfect awakening until I had heard this Dharma discourse, the Lotus of the True Dharma, this instruction for bodhisattvas. It was only after I heard this Dharma discourse, the Lotus of the True Dharma, that I was made complete in unsurpassed, perfect awakening.' And Mahapratibhana, when the time came for his final nirvana, that Blessed One, the Tathagata Prabhutaratna, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, announced before the world with its gods, Maras and Brahmas, before all people with their ascetics and brahmins: 'Monks, after my final nirvana, one great jewel stupa should be built for this body of the Tathagata. Other stupas should be built in my name.'

cmp.note: 梵文的「本愿」是：他自己是听了《法华》才成佛的。鸠摩罗什本把誓愿写成「灭度后，有说法华经处，我之塔庙踊现其前」，把下一段的内容提到这里，缺了「听经才成佛」这层。英文、白话照梵文。
cmp.en: In the Sanskrit his "former vow" is about his own awakening: he only became a buddha after hearing the Lotus. Kumarajiva's version makes the vow 灭度后，有说法华经处，我之塔庙踊现其前 (mièdù hòu, yǒu shuō Fǎhuá jīng chù, wǒ zhī tǎmiào yǒngxiàn qí qián, "after my nirvana, wherever the Lotus Sutra is taught, my stupa will spring up before it"), pulling in the content of the next passage and dropping the point that hearing the sutra made him a buddha. The English and plain Chinese follow the Sanskrit.

verses.en: "And Mahapratibhana, that Blessed One, the Tathagata Prabhutaratna, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, made this lasting resolve: 'In whatever buddha-fields in all the world systems of the ten directions this Dharma discourse, the Lotus of the True Dharma, is made known, in each of them this stupa holding my body shall rise up. While those buddhas, Blessed Ones, are speaking this Dharma discourse, the Lotus of the True Dharma, it shall stand in the open sky above the assembly. And this stupa holding my body shall call out "Well done!" to those buddhas, Blessed Ones, as they speak this Dharma discourse, the Lotus of the True Dharma.' And this, Mahapratibhana, is the relic stupa of that Blessed One, the Tathagata Prabhutaratna, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha.

cmp.note: 指以愿力立下、一直生效的安排，没有贴切的英文词。英文 lasting resolve、白话「加持」加括注；鸠摩罗什作「神通愿力」。
cmp.en: Adhiṣṭhāna is an arrangement set up by the power of a vow that keeps working, and English has no exact word for it. The English says "lasting resolve"; the plain Chinese uses 加持 (jiāchí, "empowerment") with a gloss; Kumarajiva writes 神通愿力 (shéntōng yuànlì, "supernatural power and the force of his vow").

verses.en: "Here in this Saha world (our world of endurance), while I was speaking this Dharma discourse, the Lotus of the True Dharma, it rose up from the middle of the assembly, stood in the open sky above, and called out 'Well done!'"

Then the bodhisattva, great being Mahapratibhana said to the Blessed One: "Blessed One, by the Blessed One's power, let us see this body of the Tathagata." When he had said this, the Blessed One said to the bodhisattva, great being Mahapratibhana: "Mahapratibhana, the vow of that Blessed One, the Tathagata Prabhutaratna, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, was a weighty one. This was his vow: 'Whenever buddhas, Blessed Ones, in other buddha-fields speak this Dharma discourse, the Lotus of the True Dharma, this stupa holding my body shall go into the presence of those Tathagatas to hear this Dharma discourse, the Lotus of the True Dharma.'

"'And when those buddhas, Blessed Ones, wish to open up my body and show it to the four assemblies, then those Tathagatas must first gather together all the Tathagata-forms they have conjured from their own bodies in the various buddha-fields of the ten directions, bearing different names and teaching the Dharma to beings in those buddha-fields. Only after that, together with those Tathagata-forms conjured from their own bodies, is this stupa holding my body to be opened and shown to the four assemblies.' So, Mahapratibhana, I too have conjured many Tathagata-forms, who teach the Dharma to beings in the various buddha-fields of the ten directions, in thousands of world systems. All of them will have to be brought here."

cmp.note: 「从自身化现出来的如来身形」。英文 Tathagata-forms conjured from their own bodies 照字面；白话和鸠摩罗什都用「分身」，这个词已成了专名，字面看不出是「化出来的」。
cmp.en: "Tathagata forms conjured from one's own body." The English is literal; the plain Chinese and Kumarajiva both use 分身 (fēnshēn, "split-off bodies"), which has become a fixed term and no longer shows that they are magically produced.

verses.en: Then the bodhisattva, great being Mahapratibhana said to the Blessed One: "Blessed One, then let us pay homage to all those Tathagata bodies conjured by the Tathagata as well."

Then at that moment the Blessed One sent out a ray of light from the tuft of hair between his eyebrows (one of a buddha's marks). As soon as that ray was sent out, all the buddhas, Blessed Ones, living in the eastern direction in hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas of world systems as many as the grains of sand in fifty Ganges rivers became visible. Those buddha-fields were seen to be made of crystal and bright with jewel trees, adorned with cloth, ribbons and garlands, full of many hundreds of thousands of bodhisattvas, spread with canopies and covered with golden nets of the seven precious things. In each of them buddhas, Blessed Ones, were seen teaching the Dharma to beings in sweet, lovely voices, and those buddha-fields were seen to be full of hundreds of thousands of bodhisattvas. So it was in the southeast; so it was in the south.

cmp.note: 梵文是「五十条恒河沙数」的世界。英文、白话照译；鸠摩罗什作「五百万亿那由他恒河沙等国土」，数目不同。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit has world systems "as many as the sands of fifty Ganges rivers." The English and plain Chinese follow it; Kumarajiva has 五百万亿那由他恒河沙等国土 (wǔbǎi wànyì nàyóutā Hénghé shā děng guótǔ, "lands as many as the sands of five hundred myriad hundred-million nayutas of Ganges rivers"), a different number.

verses.en: So it was in the southwest, in the west, in the northwest, in the north, in the northeast, below and above. So in each of all ten directions all the buddhas, Blessed Ones, who live in many hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas of buddha-fields like the sands of many Ganges rivers, in many hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas of world systems like the sands of many Ganges rivers, became visible.

Then those Tathagatas, arhats, fully awakened buddhas in the ten directions said to their own hosts of bodhisattvas: "Sons of good family, we must go to the Saha world, into the presence of the Blessed One, the Tathagata Shakyamuni, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, to pay homage to the relic stupa of the Tathagata Prabhutaratna, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha." Then those buddhas, Blessed Ones, each with an attendant or two, came to this Saha world.

cmp.note: 字面是「自己算第二个、自己算第三个」，即带着一两位侍者。英文、白话照意思译；鸠摩罗什这句没有译。
cmp.en: Literally "themselves the second, themselves the third," that is, with one or two attendants. The English and plain Chinese render the sense; Kumarajiva leaves it out here.

verses.en: At that time this entire world system became adorned with jewel trees, made of beryl, covered with golden nets of the seven precious things, fragrant with the incense of great jewels, strewn with mandarava and great mandarava flowers, decorated with nets of little bells, and marked off like a checkerboard with golden cords. Villages, towns, market towns, countryside, kingdoms and royal capitals were gone; the Black Mountains were gone; the Muchilinda and Great Muchilinda mountains were gone; the Chakravala and Great Chakravala mountains (the iron ring mountains at the world's edge) were gone; Mount Sumeru was gone, and the other great mountains were gone; the great oceans were gone; the rivers and great rivers were gone. The bodies of gods, humans and asuras were gone, and the hells, the animal realm and the world of Yama (lord of the dead) were gone.

cmp.note: aṣṭāpada 是八格棋盘，意思是用金绳把地面界成棋盘格。英文 marked off like a checkerboard 照这个画面；白话和鸠摩罗什「以界八道」把「八」理解成八条道路。
cmp.en: Aṣṭāpada is an eight-square game board, so the ground is laid out in a checkerboard with golden cords. The English "like a checkerboard" keeps that picture; the plain Chinese and Kumarajiva's 以界八道 (yǐ jiè bā dào, "marking off eight roads") take the "eight" as eight roads.

cmp.note: 梵本这里说天、人、阿修罗之类也没有了，与上下文（会众仍在）不太合，可能有抄误。英文、白话照字面；鸠摩罗什此处没有这一句。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says even the bodies of gods, humans and asuras were gone, which sits oddly with the assembly still being present; the text may be corrupt. The English and plain Chinese translate it as it stands; Kumarajiva has no such line here.

verses.en: At that time all the beings born in the six realms of rebirth in this Saha world were moved away to other world systems, except those gathered in that assembly. Then those buddhas, Blessed Ones, each with an attendant or two, came to this Saha world. As each Tathagata arrived, he settled at the foot of a jewel tree, by a lion throne. Each jewel tree was five hundred yojanas high, with branches, leaves and shoots in good order and in proportion, and adorned with flowers and fruit. At the foot of each jewel tree a lion throne (a buddha's seat) had been set up, five hundred yojanas high and adorned with great jewels. On it each Tathagata sat down cross-legged.

cmp.note: 梵文的狮子座高「五百由旬」，与树一样高。英文、白话照译；鸠摩罗什作「高五由旬」，小了一百倍。
cmp.en: In the Sanskrit the lion throne is "five hundred yojanas" high, as tall as the tree. The English and plain Chinese follow it; Kumarajiva has 高五由旬 (gāo wǔ yóuxún, "five yojanas high"), a hundred times smaller.

verses.en: In this way Tathagatas were seated cross-legged at the foot of all the jewel trees throughout the whole great trichiliocosm (a billion-world universe).

At that time this great trichiliocosm was full of Tathagatas, and yet the forms conjured from the body of the Blessed One, the Tathagata Shakyamuni, had not all arrived even from a single direction. So the Blessed One, the Tathagata Shakyamuni, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, conjured up room for those Tathagata-forms as they kept arriving. All around, in the eight directions, twenty hundred thousand kotis of nayutas of buddha-fields became made of beryl, covered with golden nets of the seven precious things, decorated with nets of little bells, strewn with mandarava and great mandarava flowers, spread with heavenly canopies, hung with garlands of heavenly flowers, and fragrant with heavenly incense.

cmp.note: 梵文是每方「二十个百千俱胝那由他」佛土；鸠摩罗什作「二百万亿那由他国」，数目不同。英文、白话照梵文。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit has "twenty hundred thousand kotis of nayutas" of buddha-fields in each direction; Kumarajiva has 二百万亿那由他国 (èrbǎi wànyì nàyóutā guó, "two hundred myriad hundred-million nayutas of lands"), a different figure. The English and plain Chinese follow the Sanskrit.

verses.en: And he made all those twenty hundred thousand kotis of nayutas of buddha-fields free of villages, towns, market towns, countryside, kingdoms and royal capitals; free of the Black Mountains, the Muchilinda and Great Muchilinda mountains, the Chakravala and Great Chakravala mountains, Mount Sumeru and the other great mountains; free of great oceans, rivers and great rivers; free of the bodies of gods, humans and asuras; and free of the hells, the animal realm and the world of Yama. And he made all those many buddha-fields into one single buddha-field, one single stretch of ground, level and delightful, bright with trees made of the seven precious things. Those jewel trees were five hundred yojanas in height and girth, with branches, leaves, flowers and fruit in good order.

At the foot of every jewel tree a lion throne had been set up, five hundred yojanas in height and breadth, made of heavenly jewels, many-colored and lovely to see. As the Tathagatas kept arriving, they sat down cross-legged on the lion thrones at the foot of those jewel trees. In the same way, the Tathagata Shakyamuni cleared another twenty hundred thousand kotis of nayutas of world systems in each direction, to make room for the Tathagatas who had come.

Those twenty hundred thousand kotis of nayutas of world systems in each direction he also made free of villages, towns, market towns, countryside, kingdoms and royal capitals; free of the Black Mountains, the Muchilinda and Great Muchilinda mountains, the Chakravala and Great Chakravala mountains, Mount Sumeru and the other great mountains; free of great oceans, rivers and great rivers; free of the bodies of gods, humans and asuras; and free of the hells, the animal realm and the world of Yama. All the beings there were moved away to other world systems. Those buddha-fields too were made of beryl, covered with golden nets of the seven precious things, decorated with nets of little bells, strewn with mandarava and great mandarava flowers, spread with heavenly canopies, hung with garlands of heavenly flowers, fragrant with heavenly incense, and beautified with jewel trees.

All those jewel trees were five hundred yojanas high, and lion thrones five yojanas high were conjured up. Then those Tathagatas sat down cross-legged, each on his own lion throne at the foot of a jewel tree.

cmp.note: 这里梵文说狮子座高「五由旬」，与前文的「五百由旬」不一致；鸠摩罗什一律作五由旬。英文、白话照这一段原文。
cmp.en: Here the Sanskrit says the lion thrones were "five yojanas" high, which does not match the "five hundred yojanas" earlier; Kumarajiva uses five yojanas throughout. The English and plain Chinese follow this passage as it stands.

verses.en: At that time all the Tathagatas conjured by the Blessed One Shakyamuni, who had been teaching the Dharma to beings in the east in hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas of buddha-fields like the sands of the Ganges, had gathered from the ten directions, and having come, they sat down in the eight directions. At that time thirty hundred thousand kotis of world systems in each of the eight directions all around were filled by those Tathagatas. Then those Tathagatas, seated on their own lion thrones, each sent his own attendant into the presence of the Blessed One Shakyamuni. Giving them double handfuls of jewel flowers, they said: "Go to Vulture Peak (the mountain outside Rajagriha where the Buddha often taught).

cmp.note: 梵文是每方「三十个百千俱胝」世界；鸠摩罗什作「四百万亿那由他国土」。英文、白话照梵文。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit has "thirty hundred thousand kotis" of world systems in each direction; Kumarajiva has 四百万亿那由他国土 (sìbǎi wànyì nàyóutā guótǔ, "four hundred myriad hundred-million nayutas of lands"). The English and plain Chinese follow the Sanskrit.

verses.en: "When you get there, pay homage to the Blessed One, the Tathagata Shakyamuni, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, and in our name ask whether he and his hosts of bodhisattvas and disciples are free of illness and discomfort, strong, and living at ease. Shower him with this heap of jewels and say: 'The Blessed One, the Tathagata, gives his consent to the opening of this great jewel stupa.'" In this way all those Tathagatas sent out their own attendants.

cmp.note: chanda 在这里是僧团议事用语「同意、授权」。英文 consent、白话「同意」照译；鸠摩罗什「与欲」是照僧团术语直译，现代读者不易看懂。
cmp.en: Chanda here is a term from monastic procedure, "consent, proxy approval." The English "consent" and the plain Chinese 同意 (tóngyì, "agree") give the sense; Kumarajiva's 与欲 (yǔ yù, "give one's wish") is a literal rendering of the monastic term that modern readers find hard to follow.

verses.en: Then at that moment the Blessed One, the Tathagata Shakyamuni, knowing that the forms he had conjured had all arrived without exception and were seated each on his own lion throne, knowing that the attendants of those Tathagatas, arhats, fully awakened buddhas had come, and knowing that those Tathagatas, arhats, fully awakened buddhas had given their consent, rose from his own Dharma seat and stood in the open sky. And all the four assemblies rose from their seats, joined their palms and stood gazing up at the Blessed One's face. Then the Blessed One, with a finger of his right hand, opened up the middle of that great jewel stupa standing in the sky, and having opened it, he drew its two walls apart.

Just as the great double doors of a great city gate swing apart when the bolt is drawn, so the Blessed One, with a finger of his right hand, opened up the middle of that great jewel stupa standing in the sky and laid it open. The moment that great jewel stupa was opened, the Blessed One, the Tathagata Prabhutaratna, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, was seen sitting on the lion throne with legs crossed, his limbs dried out but his body held together, as if he were in meditative absorption. And he said: "Well done, well done, Blessed Shakyamuni! You have spoken this Dharma discourse, the Lotus of the True Dharma, well. It is good indeed, Blessed Shakyamuni, that you speak this Dharma discourse, the Lotus of the True Dharma, in the middle of the assembly.

cmp.note: 梵文说多宝佛「肢体干枯，身躯连成一体」，像一具完整的干尸。英文、白话照字面；鸠摩罗什只写「全身不散」，没有「干枯」的形象。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says Prabhutaratna's "limbs were dried out, his body held together," like an intact mummified body. The English and plain Chinese are literal; Kumarajiva writes only 全身不散 (quánshēn bú sàn, "his whole body had not come apart"), without the image of drying.

verses.en: "Blessed One, I have come here to hear this very Dharma discourse, the Lotus of the True Dharma."

Then the four assemblies, seeing the Blessed One, the Tathagata Prabhutaratna, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, who had passed into final nirvana many hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas of eons (kalpas, vast ages) ago, speaking like this, were filled with wonder and amazement. At that moment they showered that Blessed One, the Tathagata Prabhutaratna, and the Blessed One, the Tathagata Shakyamuni, with heaps of heavenly and human jewels. Then the Blessed One, the Tathagata Prabhutaratna, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, gave half of that very lion throne to the Blessed One, the Tathagata Shakyamuni, there inside the great jewel stupa, and said: "Let the Blessed One, the Tathagata Shakyamuni, sit right here."

Then the Blessed One, the Tathagata Shakyamuni, sat down on that half-seat together with that Tathagata. And both Tathagatas were seen sitting on the lion throne in the middle of that great jewel stupa, standing in the open sky.

Then the four assemblies thought: "We are far away from these two Tathagatas. What if we too rose into the sky by the Tathagata's power?" The Blessed One, the Tathagata Shakyamuni, knew with his own mind what was going on in the minds of the four assemblies, and at that moment, by his supernatural power, set the four assemblies in the open sky above. Then at that moment the Blessed One, the Tathagata Shakyamuni, said to the four assemblies: "Monks, which of you has the courage to make this Dharma discourse, the Lotus of the True Dharma, known in that Saha world? This is the time, this is the moment. The Tathagata is here before you."
"Monks, the Tathagata wishes to entrust this Dharma discourse, the Lotus of the True Dharma, and then pass into final nirvana."
Then at that moment the Blessed One spoke these verses:
"Monks, this great seer, the Guide who has passed into nirvana, has come here inside a stupa made of jewels in order to hear this Dharma. Who would not rouse his effort for the sake of the Dharma?
"Though he passed into final nirvana many kotis of eons ago, he still listens to the Dharma today. He goes here and there for the sake of the Dharma; a Dharma like this is very hard to come by.
"This was the vow of that Guide, which he made and kept in a former life: even after final nirvana he seeks out this Dharma throughout the whole world, in all ten directions.
"And all these are my own bodies, thousands of kotis of them, like the sands of the Ganges. They have come to do the work of the Dharma and to see this Protector who has passed into final nirvana.
"Leaving their own fields, and all their many disciples and gods, they have all come to guard the true Dharma: how can the Dharma's guidance last a long time?

cmp.note: netrī 是「引导者、缰绳」，dharmanetrī 指法作为引路的线索、教法的传承。英文 the Dharma's guidance、白话「法的引导」照字面；鸠摩罗什意译成「令法久住」。
cmp.en: Netrī means "that which leads, a guiding line," so dharmanetrī is the Dharma as a guide, the line of the teaching. The English "the Dharma's guidance" and the plain Chinese 法的引导 (fǎ de yǐndǎo, "the guidance of the Dharma") are literal; Kumarajiva gives the gist as 令法久住 (lìng fǎ jiǔ zhù, "so that the Dharma may long endure").

verses.en: "To give these buddhas a place to sit, I moved all the beings of many thousands of kotis of world systems elsewhere, and by supernatural power made those worlds pure.
"This is how eager I am: how can I make the Dharma's guidance known? And these countless buddhas sit at the foot of the trees like heaps of lotuses.
"At the foot of kotis of trees, the Guides on their lion thrones, with their great bodies, shine and stay shining all the time, like fire in the darkness.
"The lovely scent of the Guides of the world drifts through the ten directions, and as the wind keeps blowing here, all beings are made giddy with it.

cmp.note: 梵文只说香气随风吹来。鸠摩罗什多了「譬如大风，吹小树枝。以是方便，令法久住」几句，梵本没有。英文、白话照梵文。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit only says the scent comes on the wind. Kumarajiva adds lines not in the Sanskrit: 譬如大风，吹小树枝。以是方便，令法久住 (pìrú dàfēng, chuī xiǎo shùzhī. yǐ shì fāngbiàn, lìng fǎ jiǔ zhù, "like a great wind blowing small branches; by this means the Dharma will long endure"). The English and plain Chinese follow the Sanskrit.

verses.en: "Whoever will keep this Dharma discourse after my nirvana, let him speak up quickly, here before the Lords of the World.
"For the fully awakened one who has passed into final nirvana, the sage Prabhutaratna, will hear the lion's roar of whoever makes that resolve.
"I am the second, and these many kotis of Guides who have come here are more: we will hear the resolve of the Victor's son who has the courage to make this Dharma known.
"By him I will always be honored, and so will the Victor Prabhutaratna, the self-existent one, who always travels to the directions and in-between directions to hear a Dharma like this.

"And these Lords of the World who have come here, who have made this ground so many-colored and splendid, they too will have received a vast and abundant offering through the making known of this sutra.
"It will be as if he had seen me here on this seat, and the Blessed One who stays in the middle of the stupa, and these many other Lords of the World who have come from many hundreds of fields.
"Think about it, sons of good family, out of compassion for all beings: this is a very hard place to stand, and only Guides take it on.
"There are many thousands of sutras, as many as the sands of the Ganges. If someone were to make all of them known, that would not be hard.
"If someone took hold of Mount Sumeru with one hand, gripped it in his fist and threw it across kotis of fields, that would not be hard.
"If someone shook this whole trichiliocosm with his big toe and threw it across kotis of fields, that would not be hard.
"If a man stood at the peak of existence (the highest heaven of all the realms) and taught people here thousands of other sutras, that would not be hard.
"But when the Lord of the World has passed into nirvana, in the terrible time after, whoever keeps or speaks this sutra, that is very hard.
"If someone put the whole of space into one fist and walked about holding it, that would not be hard.
"But whoever, after I have passed into nirvana, in the time after, even copies out a sutra like this, that is hard.
"If someone put the whole earth on the tip of his fingernail, walked about with it and even climbed up to the world of Brahma,
"he would not be doing anything hard, nor would it take much effort, even if he did that 'hard' thing in front of the whole world.
"Harder than that is this: when I have passed into nirvana, in the time after, for someone to speak this sutra even for a moment.
"It is not hard in this world for a man to walk through the fire that burns up the world at the end of an eon, carrying a load of grass, without being burned.
"Harder than that is this: when I have passed into nirvana, for someone to keep this sutra and let even one being hear it.
"If someone kept the eighty-four thousand sections of the Dharma and taught them, with their explanations, just as they were spoken, to kotis of living beings,

cmp.note: 梵文只说「八万四千法蕴」。鸠摩罗什加了「十二部经」，梵本没有。英文 sections of the Dharma 照字面。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit only says "eighty-four thousand sections (heaps) of the Dharma." Kumarajiva adds 十二部经 (shí'èr bù jīng, "the twelve divisions of scripture"), which is not in the Sanskrit. The English "sections of the Dharma" is literal.

verses.en: "that would not be hard for monks in that time; nor to train my disciples and set them in the five higher knowledges.

cmp.note: 梵文是「五种神通」。英文、白话照译；鸠摩罗什作「六神通」。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says "the five higher knowledges." The English and plain Chinese follow it; Kumarajiva has 六神通 (liù shéntōng, "six supernatural powers").

verses.en: "Harder for him than that is to keep this sutra, to trust it, to have faith in it, or to speak it again and again.
"If someone set many thousands of kotis of beings, like the sands of the Ganges, in arhatship, with the six higher knowledges and great good fortune,
"that best of humans who keeps this excellent sutra after my nirvana does a greater work than that.
"I have taught many teachings in thousands of world systems, and I still teach today, for the sake of the buddha knowledge.
"But this one is called the highest sutra among all sutras. Whoever keeps this sutra keeps the Victor's body."
"Speak up, sons of good family! The Tathagata is here before you. Which of you has the courage to keep it in the time after?
"Whoever keeps this sutra, so hard to keep, even for a moment, does something that greatly pleases all the Lords of the World.
"He will always be praised by the Lords of the World. He is a hero, a brave one, and will quickly gain the higher knowledges for awakening.

cmp.note: 梵文是「勇士、英雄」。鸠摩罗什译「是则勇猛，是则精进，是名持戒，行头陀者」，多了「持戒」「头陀行」，梵本没有。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says "a hero, a brave one." Kumarajiva writes 是则勇猛，是则精进，是名持戒，行头陀者 (shì zé yǒngměng, shì zé jīngjìn, shì míng chíjiè, xíng tóutuó zhě, "this is courage, this is effort, this is keeping the precepts, practicing austerities"), adding precepts and ascetic practice, which the Sanskrit does not mention.

verses.en: "Whoever keeps this sutra carries the load; he is the own son of the Lords of the World, and he has reached the stage of the tamed.
"Whoever makes this sutra known after the Guide of humans has passed into nirvana becomes an eye for the world with its gods and humans.
"Whoever speaks this sutra even for a moment in the last age is a wise person worthy of homage from all beings."

Then the Blessed One addressed the whole host of bodhisattvas and the world with its gods and asuras, and said: "Monks, once upon a time, in the past, for immeasurable, countless eons I sought the sutra of the Lotus of the True Dharma, without tiring and without rest. In the past, for many eons, many hundreds of thousands of eons, I was a king who had made the vow to reach unsurpassed, perfect awakening, and my mind never turned back. Working to complete the six perfections, I gave away gifts beyond measure: gold, gems, pearls, beryl, conch, crystal, coral, raw gold, silver, ashmagarbha, musaragalva and red pearls; villages, towns, market towns, countryside, kingdoms and royal capitals; wives, sons and daughters, female and male slaves, workers and servants, elephants, horses and chariots; up to giving up my own body, giving away hands, feet, head, limbs and life itself.

cmp.note: 字面是「到彼岸」或「圆满」。英文 perfections 取「圆满」义；白话、鸠摩罗什用音译「波罗蜜」，白话另加括注。
cmp.en: Literally "gone to the far shore" or "perfection." The English "perfections" takes the second sense; the plain Chinese and Kumarajiva transliterate it as 波罗蜜 (bōluómì), and the plain Chinese adds a gloss.

verses.en: "And never did a grasping thought arise in me. At that time people in this world lived long, and for a life of many hundreds of thousands of years I ruled the kingdom for the sake of the Dharma, not for the sake of pleasures. Then I anointed my eldest son as king and set out in the four directions to seek the highest Dharma. I had it proclaimed with a bell: 'Whoever will give me the highest Dharma and explain its meaning, I will be his slave.' At that time there was a seer, and he said to me: 'Great king, there is a sutra called the Lotus of the True Dharma that sets out the highest Dharma. If you agree to be my slave, I will let you hear that Dharma.' Hearing the seer's words, I was glad, pleased, elated and delighted, full of joy and happiness, and I went to where the seer was.

cmp.note: 「最上的法、最高的法」。英文 highest Dharma、白话「最上的法」照译；鸠摩罗什译成「大乘」，把它直接点明为大乘教法。
cmp.en: "The highest, foremost Dharma." The English "highest Dharma" and the plain Chinese 最上的法 (zuìshàng de fǎ) follow it; Kumarajiva renders it 大乘 (dàshèng, "the Great Vehicle"), naming it outright as the Mahayana teaching.

verses.en: "When I got there I said: 'Whatever work a slave of yours should do, I will do.' So, having become that seer's slave, I did a servant's work: fetching grass, firewood and water, digging roots and gathering fruit and the like, and I was even his doorkeeper. After doing such work all day, at night, as he lay on his couch, I held his feet. Neither my body nor my mind grew tired. A full thousand years passed while I did this.

cmp.note: 梵文是夜里仙人躺在床上，「我捧着他的脚」。英文、白话照译；鸠摩罗什写成「以身而为床座」，变成拿自己的身体当床座。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says that at night, while the seer lay on his couch, "I held his feet." The English and plain Chinese follow it; Kumarajiva writes 以身而为床座 (yǐ shēn ér wéi chuángzuò, "made my own body his couch").

verses.en: Then at that moment the Blessed One, to make this point clear, spoke these verses:
"I remember eons long past, when I was a king of the Dharma who lived by the Dharma. I ruled for the sake of the Dharma, not for pleasure, but for the sake of the highest Dharma.
"I proclaimed in the four directions: 'Whoever will speak the Dharma, I will become his slave.' At that time there was a wise seer, a teacher of the sutra called the True Dharma.

cmp.note: 梵文只说「一位聪慧的仙人」，没有名字。鸠摩罗什作「阿私仙」，给了名字（阿私陀）。英文、白话照梵文。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit only says "a wise seer," with no name. Kumarajiva calls him 阿私仙 (Āsī xiān, "the seer Asita"), giving him a name. The English and plain Chinese follow the Sanskrit.

verses.en: "He said to me: 'If you long for the Dharma, come and be my slave, and then I will teach you the Dharma.' Pleased to hear those words, I did then the work fit for a slave.
"No weariness of body or mind touched me, who had become a slave for the sake of the true Dharma. My vow then was for the sake of beings, not aimed at myself, and not for the sake of pleasure.
"That king was tireless in effort then, doing nothing else in the ten directions, unwearied for a full thousand eons, until he found the sutra called the Dharma."

cmp.note: 梵文偈颂说是「整整一千劫」，散文里是「一千年」，梵本前后不一。英文、白话照偈颂原文。鸠摩罗什此偈改成「遂致得成佛，今故为汝说」，没有数字。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit verse says "a full thousand eons," while the prose said "a thousand years"; the text is not consistent. The English and plain Chinese follow the verse as it stands. Kumarajiva's verse becomes 遂致得成佛，今故为汝说 (suì zhì dé chéng fó, jīn gù wèi rǔ shuō, "and so I became a buddha, and now I teach it to you"), with no number.

verses.en: "What do you think, monks: was that king at that time, on that occasion, someone else? You should not see it that way. Why? At that time, on that occasion, I was that king. And monks, could that seer at that time, on that occasion, have been someone else? You should not see it that way either. At that time, on that occasion, the monk Devadatta here was that seer. For, monks, Devadatta is my good friend. It is thanks to Devadatta that I completed the six perfections, great kindness, great compassion, great joy and great equanimity.

cmp.note: 「善友」，指带人走向善的朋友、良师。提婆达多在传统里是想害佛的人，这里佛却称他为善友。英文 good friend、白话「善友」照译；鸠摩罗什「善知识」是同一个词的常见古译。
cmp.en: Kalyāṇamitra, "good friend," a friend or mentor who leads one toward the good. In tradition Devadatta is the man who tried to kill the Buddha, yet here the Buddha calls him his good friend. The English "good friend" and the plain Chinese 善友 (shànyǒu) translate it directly; Kumarajiva's 善知识 (shàn zhīshì) is the usual classical rendering of the same word.

verses.en: "The thirty-two marks of a great man, the eighty minor marks, the golden color of my skin, the ten powers, the four kinds of fearlessness, the four ways of drawing people in, the eighteen qualities found only in a buddha, great supernatural power, the power to carry beings of the ten directions across: all of this came thanks to Devadatta. I tell you, monks, I announce to you: in the future, after immeasurable, countless eons, this monk Devadatta will become a Tathagata named Devaraja (King of the Gods), an arhat, a fully awakened buddha, perfect in knowledge and conduct, the Sugata, knower of the world, unsurpassed, tamer of those who can be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a Blessed One, in the world system called Devasopana (Stairway of the Gods). Monks, the lifespan of the Tathagata Devaraja will be twenty intermediate eons, and he will teach the Dharma at length.

"Beings as many as the grains of sand in the Ganges will abandon all afflictions and realize arhatship. Many beings will set their minds on a solitary buddha's awakening. Beings as many as the grains of sand in the Ganges will set their minds on unsurpassed, perfect awakening and gain the patience that never turns back. Monks, after the Tathagata Devaraja has passed into final nirvana, his true Dharma will last for twenty intermediate eons. His body will not break up into relics; his body will stay whole and solid and be placed in a stupa of the seven precious things. That stupa will be six thousand yojanas high and forty yojanas long. All the gods and humans there will honor it with flowers, incense, scents, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, flags and verses, and in this way they will praise it.

cmp.note: 梵文是「六十个百由旬」，即高六千由旬，英文、白话照译；鸠摩罗什作「高六十由旬」。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says "sixty hundred yojanas," six thousand yojanas high, which the English and plain Chinese follow; Kumarajiva has 高六十由旬 (gāo liùshí yóuxún, "sixty yojanas high").

verses.en: "Of those who walk around that stupa keeping it on their right, or bow to it, some will realize the highest fruit, arhatship, some will reach a solitary buddha's awakening, and gods and humans beyond count and beyond imagining will set their minds on unsurpassed, perfect awakening and never turn back."

Then the Blessed One spoke again to the community of monks: "Monks, any son or daughter of good family in the future who hears this chapter of the sutra of the Lotus of the True Dharma, and having heard it does not doubt or waver but trusts it with a pure mind, will find the door to the three bad destinies shut: he will not fall into rebirth in the hells, among animals, or in the world of Yama. If he is born in the buddha-fields of the ten directions, he will hear this very sutra in life after life. If he is born among gods or humans, he will reach a distinguished place. And in whatever buddha-field he is born, he will be born spontaneously in a lotus made of the seven precious things, in the presence of the Tathagata."

cmp.note: 梵文只说「《妙法莲华经》的这一品」。鸠摩罗什写明是「提婆达多品」——他的译本原无此品，后人补入后单独成品，梵本则是宝塔品的一部分。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit only says "this chapter of the Lotus sutra." Kumarajiva's text names it 提婆达多品 (Típódáduō pǐn, "the Devadatta chapter"): this part was missing from his original translation, was added later and made a chapter of its own, whereas in the Sanskrit it is part of the stupa chapter.

cmp.note: 梵文的三恶道是地狱、畜生、阎摩世界。鸠摩罗什作「地狱、饿鬼、畜生」，用了汉地常见的说法。
cmp.en: In the Sanskrit the three bad destinies are the hells, animals, and the world of Yama. Kumarajiva gives 地狱、饿鬼、畜生 (dìyù, èguǐ, chùshēng, "hells, hungry ghosts, animals"), the formula familiar in Chinese.

verses.en: Then at that moment a bodhisattva named Prajnakuta (Peak of Wisdom), who had come from the Tathagata Prabhutaratna's buddha-field in the lower direction, said to the Tathagata Prabhutaratna: "Blessed One, let us go back to our own buddha-field." Then the Blessed One, the Tathagata Shakyamuni, said to the bodhisattva Prajnakuta: "Wait a moment, son of good family, until you have settled some point of the Dharma with my bodhisattva Manjushri the Prince; then you can go back to your own buddha-field."

Then at that moment Manjushri the Prince, seated on a thousand-petaled lotus as big as a cart wheel, surrounded and attended by many bodhisattvas, rose up out of the middle of the ocean from the palace of Sagara, the naga king (nagas are serpent beings of the waters), and came up through the sky by the path of the birds to Vulture Peak, into the presence of the Blessed One. Manjushri the Prince stepped down from the lotus, bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One Shakyamuni and of the Tathagata Prabhutaratna, and went up to the bodhisattva Prajnakuta. Having come up to him, he exchanged friendly and pleasant greetings of many kinds with the bodhisattva Prajnakuta face to face, and sat down to one side. Then the bodhisattva Prajnakuta said to Manjushri the Prince: "Manjushri, while you were in the middle of the ocean, how many beings did you train?"

cmp.note: 字面是「童子、王子的身份」，指文殊以少年王子的样子出现。英文 the Prince、白话「法王子」；「法王子」是古译，意思是「法王（佛）的儿子」，比梵文多了一层。
cmp.en: Literally "in the state of a youth, a prince," Manjushri appearing as a young prince. The English says "the Prince"; the plain Chinese uses the classical 法王子 (fǎ wángzǐ, "prince of the Dharma King"), which adds the idea of being the Buddha's son.

verses.en: Manjushri said: "I have trained many beings, immeasurable and countless, so immeasurable and countless that words cannot express it or the mind conceive it. Wait a moment, son of good family, and you will see a sign of it." No sooner had Manjushri the Prince spoken these words than many thousands of lotuses rose out of the middle of the ocean into the sky above, and on those lotuses sat many thousands of bodhisattvas. Those bodhisattvas came by that same path of the birds to Vulture Peak, and having arrived, they were seen standing in the sky above. All of them had been trained by Manjushri the Prince for unsurpassed, perfect awakening.

Among them, the bodhisattvas who had set out in the Great Vehicle from the start were praising the good qualities of the Great Vehicle, the six perfections. The bodhisattvas who had once been disciples were praising only the disciple vehicle. But all of them understood that all things are empty, and understood the good qualities of the Great Vehicle. Then Manjushri the Prince said to the bodhisattva Prajnakuta: "Son of good family, all this training of beings was done by me in the middle of the ocean, and here you can see it." Then the bodhisattva Prajnakuta questioned Manjushri the Prince in verse:

cmp.note: 梵文说原本是声闻的菩萨「仍只称赞声闻乘」。英文、白话照译；鸠摩罗什写成他们「今皆修行大乘空义」，把这层张力抹平了。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says the bodhisattvas who used to be disciples "were praising only the disciple vehicle." The English and plain Chinese keep this; Kumarajiva writes that they 今皆修行大乘空义 (jīn jiē xiūxíng dàshèng kōng yì, "now all practice the Great Vehicle's meaning of emptiness"), smoothing over the tension.

verses.en: "Greatly good one, hero named for your wisdom, these countless beings you have trained today: whose power is this? Tell me, god among humans, since I ask you.
"What Dharma did you teach, or what sutra that points out the path to awakening, so that on hearing it these set their minds on awakening and found a firm footing in all-knowing?"

cmp.note: 梵文这两首偈是问句：「是谁的威力？你讲了什么法？」鸠摩罗什译成赞叹，「演畅实相义，开阐一乘法」，问句变成了答案。
cmp.en: In the Sanskrit these two verses are questions: "Whose power is this? What Dharma did you teach?" Kumarajiva turns them into praise, 演畅实相义，开阐一乘法 (yǎnchàng shíxiàng yì, kāichǎn yìshèng fǎ, "you expounded the meaning of true reality and opened up the One Vehicle Dharma"), so the question becomes the answer.

verses.en: Manjushri said: "In the middle of the ocean I taught the sutra of the Lotus of the True Dharma, and nothing else." Prajnakuta said: "This sutra is deep, subtle and hard to see into; there is no other sutra equal to this one. Is there any being who could honor this jewel of a sutra, understand it, and wake up to unsurpassed, perfect awakening?" Manjushri said: "There is, son of good family. Sagara the naga king has a daughter, eight years old by birth, of great wisdom and sharp faculties, whose actions of body, speech and mind are all led by knowledge. She has gained the dharani (power of holding in memory) for grasping the words and meanings of everything the Tathagatas have taught, and in a single instant she gained a thousand concentrations that hold together all things and all beings. She never turns back from the mind of awakening, her vows are vast, she loves all beings as herself, she is able to bring good qualities into being, and she never falls away from them.

"With a smiling face, endowed with supreme beauty and fullness of form, with a loving mind, she speaks compassionate words. She is able to wake up to perfect awakening." The bodhisattva Prajnakuta said: "I have seen the Blessed One, the Tathagata Shakyamuni, when he was a bodhisattva striving for awakening, doing countless meritorious deeds, and for many thousands of eons he never once let his effort slacken. In this great trichiliocosm there is not one spot of ground, not even the size of a mustard seed, where he did not lay down his body for the good of beings. Only after that did he wake up to awakening. Who could believe that she could wake up to unsurpassed, perfect awakening in a moment?"
Then at that moment the daughter of Sagara the naga king was seen standing in front of them. She bowed her head at the Blessed One's feet, stood to one side, and at that moment spoke these verses:
"Merit upon merit, deep, spreading through all directions; a subtle body adorned with the thirty-two marks,

cmp.note: 梵文是「福德、福德、深广」。鸠摩罗什译「深达罪福相」，加了「罪」，变成「通达罪与福的实相」。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit reads "merit, merit, deep." Kumarajiva renders it 深达罪福相 (shēn dá zuì fú xiàng, "deeply penetrating the marks of sin and merit"), adding "sin" and turning it into insight into both.

verses.en: "with the minor marks, honored by all beings, approachable by all beings, like a marketplace in town.

cmp.note: 「像城里的集市」：人人都能进去。这个朴素的比喻英文、白话都保留了；鸠摩罗什没有译，改成「天人所戴仰，龙神咸恭敬」。
cmp.en: "Like a marketplace in town": anyone can walk in. The English and plain Chinese keep this homely image; Kumarajiva leaves it out and writes 天人所戴仰，龙神咸恭敬 (tiānrén suǒ dàiyǎng, lóngshén xián gōngjìng, "looked up to by gods and humans, revered by dragons and spirits").

verses.en: "I have reached awakening as I wished; the Tathagata here is my witness. I will teach at length the Dharma that frees from suffering."

Then at that moment the venerable Shariputra said to the daughter of Sagara the naga king: "Daughter of good family, you have only set your mind on awakening. You will not turn back, and your wisdom is beyond measure, but perfect buddhahood is hard to win. There may be a woman who does not slacken in effort, who does meritorious deeds for many hundreds and thousands of eons and completes the six perfections, and still does not reach buddhahood even now. Why? There are five positions a woman does not reach even now. Which five? First, the position of Brahma; second, the position of Shakra; third, the position of a great king; fourth, the position of a wheel-turning king; fifth, the position of a bodhisattva who never turns back."

cmp.note: 梵文舍利弗只说女人有五种地位达不到。鸠摩罗什多了「女身垢秽，非是法器」一句，梵本没有这样贬低女身的话。英文、白话照梵文。
cmp.en: In the Sanskrit Shariputra only says there are five positions a woman does not reach. Kumarajiva adds 女身垢秽，非是法器 (nǚ shēn gòuhuì, fēi shì fǎqì, "a woman's body is filthy and is not a vessel for the Dharma"), a disparagement of the female body that the Sanskrit does not contain. The English and plain Chinese follow the Sanskrit.

verses.en: Then at that moment the daughter of Sagara the naga king had a jewel worth as much as the whole great trichiliocosm. The daughter of Sagara the naga king gave that jewel to the Blessed One, and the Blessed One accepted it out of compassion. Then the daughter of Sagara the naga king said to the bodhisattva Prajnakuta and the elder Shariputra: "This jewel I gave the Blessed One: did the Blessed One accept it quickly or not?" The elder said: "You gave it quickly, and the Blessed One accepted it quickly." The daughter of Sagara the naga king said: "Venerable Shariputra, if I had great supernatural power, I would wake up to perfect awakening even faster, and there would be no one there yet to accept this jewel."

cmp.note: 梵文龙女说「如果我有大神通，我成佛会更快」。鸠摩罗什改成「以汝神力，观我成佛」，变成请对方用神通来看她成佛。最后半句「连接珠的人都还没有」意思有点难懂，英文、白话都照字面。
cmp.en: In the Sanskrit the naga girl says "if I had great supernatural power, I would become a buddha even faster." Kumarajiva changes it to 以汝神力，观我成佛 (yǐ rǔ shénlì, guān wǒ chéng fó, "use your supernatural power to watch me become a buddha"), so she is asking them to watch. The last clause, "there would be no one yet to accept this jewel," is a little obscure; the English and plain Chinese render it literally.

verses.en: Then at that moment, before the eyes of the whole world and before the eyes of the elder Shariputra, the female organ of the daughter of Sagara the naga king disappeared, a male organ appeared, and she showed herself as a bodhisattva. At that moment he went off to the south. In the south there is a world system called Vimala (Stainless). There he showed himself seated at the foot of a bodhi tree made of the seven precious things, fully awakened, bearing the thirty-two marks and the form of all the minor marks, filling the ten directions with light and teaching the Dharma. And all the beings in the Saha world saw that Tathagata, honored by all the gods, nagas, yakshas, gandharvas, asuras, garudas, kinnaras, humans and non-humans, and teaching the Dharma.

cmp.note: 梵文明说是女性器官消失、男性器官出现，英文、白话照字面；鸠摩罗什只写「变成男子」。梵文随后改用阳性代词，英文也跟着从 she 换成 he。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says plainly that her female organ disappeared and a male organ appeared; the English and plain Chinese are literal, while Kumarajiva writes only 变成男子 (biànchéng nánzǐ, "turned into a man"). The Sanskrit then switches to masculine forms, and the English follows, moving from "she" to "he."

cmp.note: 梵文是坐在七宝「菩提树」下成佛；鸠摩罗什作「坐宝莲华」。
cmp.en: In the Sanskrit he awakens seated at the foot of a seven-jeweled "bodhi tree"; Kumarajiva has 坐宝莲华 (zuò bǎo liánhuá, "seated on a jeweled lotus").

verses.en: And all the beings who heard that Tathagata's teaching of the Dharma came to never turn back from unsurpassed, perfect awakening. That world system Vimala and this Saha world shook in six ways. Three thousand living beings in the Blessed One Shakyamuni's assembly gained patience with the truth that things do not arise, and three hundred thousand living beings received predictions to unsurpassed, perfect awakening. Then the bodhisattva, great being Prajnakuta and the elder Shariputra fell silent.

cmp.note: 梵文以智积和舍利弗「沉默了」作结，很有戏剧性。英文、白话照译；鸠摩罗什作「默然信受」，加了「信受」。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit ends dramatically with Prajnakuta and Shariputra simply "falling silent." The English and plain Chinese follow it; Kumarajiva has 默然信受 (mòrán xìnshòu, "silently believed and accepted"), adding the acceptance.

verses.en: This is the eleventh chapter, called The Stupa Appears, in the noble Dharma discourse of the Lotus of the True Dharma.

cmp.note: 梵本这一品是第十一品，包括提婆达多的故事；本站排第十二，鸠摩罗什本则分成第十一宝塔品和第十二提婆达多品。英文、白话照梵文写「第十一」。
cmp.en: In the Sanskrit this is the eleventh chapter, and it includes the Devadatta story; the site numbers it twelfth, and Kumarajiva's version splits it into chapter 11 (the stupa) and chapter 12 (Devadatta). The English and plain Chinese keep the Sanskrit "eleventh."

chapters.title: Chapter 13 · Taking Up the Sutra with Courage

verses.en: Then the bodhisattva, great being Bhaishajyaraja (the Medicine King) and the bodhisattva, great being Mahapratibhana (Great Eloquence), with a following of two hundred thousand bodhisattvas, said this in the presence of the Blessed One: "Blessed One, please do not worry about this. After the Tathagata has passed into final nirvana, we will teach this Dharma discourse to beings and make it widely known. Blessed One, it is true that the beings of that time will be deceitful, with few roots of goodness, full of conceit, intent on gain and honor, set on unwholesome ways, hard to tame, lacking faith and mostly without trust. Even so, Blessed One, we will show the strength of patience at that time, and we will recite this sutra, keep it, teach it, copy it out, and honor, respect, revere and make offerings to it."

cmp.note: 梵文是「二十个十万」，即二十万菩萨，英文、白话都照译；鸠摩罗什译作「二万」，数目少了十倍。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says "twenty hundred-thousands," that is, two hundred thousand bodhisattvas, and the English and plain Chinese follow it; Kumarajiva's version has 二万 (èr wàn, "twenty thousand"), a tenth of the number.

verses.en: "Blessed One, we will give up even body and life to make this sutra known. Please do not worry, Blessed One."

Then in that assembly about five hundred monks, some still in training and some beyond training, said to the Blessed One: "Blessed One, we too have the courage to make this Dharma discourse known, but in other world systems." Then all the Blessed One's disciples, in training and beyond training, whom he had predicted to unsurpassed, perfect awakening, eight thousand monks in all, joined their palms toward the Blessed One and said: "Please do not worry, Blessed One. We too will make this Dharma discourse known in the last age, the last time after the Tathagata's final nirvana, but in other world systems. Why? Because in this Saha world (our world of endurance), Blessed One, beings are conceited, have few roots of goodness, always carry ill will, and are deceitful and crooked by nature."

cmp.note: 「有学」是还在修学的人，「无学」是已学完的阿罗汉。英文 in training / beyond training 是意译；白话加了括注；鸠摩罗什把前一批五百人直接写成「五百阿罗汉」。
cmp.en: Śaikṣa are those still in training; aśaikṣa are arhats with nothing left to learn. The English "in training / beyond training" renders the sense, and the plain Chinese adds a gloss; Kumarajiva simply calls the first group of five hundred 五百阿罗汉 (wǔbǎi āluóhàn, "five hundred arhats").

verses.en: Then Mahaprajapati Gautami, the Blessed One's mother's sister, together with six thousand nuns in training and beyond training, rose from her seat, joined her palms toward the Blessed One and stood gazing up at him. At that moment the Blessed One said to Mahaprajapati Gautami: "Gautami, why do you stand here looking at the Tathagata with a downcast heart, thinking, 'I have not been named or predicted to unsurpassed, perfect awakening'? But Gautami, you have already been predicted in the prediction given to the whole assembly. And further, Gautami, from now on you will honor, respect, revere, make offerings to, worship and pay homage to thirty-eight hundred thousand kotis of nayutas (huge numbers) of buddhas, and you will become a bodhisattva, a great being, a teacher of the Dharma."

cmp.note: 梵文是「三十八个百千俱胝那由他」尊佛，英文、白话照译；鸠摩罗什译作「六万八千亿诸佛」，数目不同。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit has "thirty-eight hundred thousand kotis of nayutas" of buddhas, which the English and plain Chinese follow; Kumarajiva gives 六万八千亿诸佛 (liùwàn bāqiān yì zhū fó, "sixty-eight thousand hundred-millions of buddhas"), a different figure.

verses.en: "These six thousand nuns, in training and beyond training, will also become bodhisattvas and teachers of the Dharma together with you in the presence of those Tathagatas, arhats, fully awakened buddhas. After that, further on still, having completed the bodhisattva's practice, you will become a Tathagata in the world named Sarvasattvapriyadarshana (Delight of All Beings to See), an arhat, a fully awakened buddha, perfect in knowledge and conduct, the Sugata, knower of the world, unsurpassed, tamer of those who can be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a buddha, a Blessed One. And Gautami, that Tathagata Sarvasattvapriyadarshana will predict those six thousand bodhisattvas, one after another, to unsurpassed, perfect awakening."

Then the nun Yashodhara, Rahula's mother, thought: "The Blessed One has not mentioned my name." The Blessed One knew with his own mind what was going on in the mind of the nun Yashodhara, and said to her: "I tell you, Yashodhara, I announce it to you: you too will honor, respect, revere, make offerings to, worship and pay homage to ten thousand kotis of buddhas and become a bodhisattva, a teacher of the Dharma. Completing the bodhisattva's practice step by step, you will become a Tathagata in the world named Rashmishatasahasraparipurnadhvaja (Banner Full of a Hundred Thousand Rays), an arhat, a fully awakened buddha, perfect in knowledge and conduct, the Sugata, knower of the world, unsurpassed, tamer of those who can be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a buddha, a Blessed One, in the world system called Bhadra (Good)."

cmp.note: 梵文是「十个千俱胝」，即一万俱胝尊佛，英文照译；白话写「一万俱胝」意思相同；鸠摩罗什作「百千万亿诸佛」。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit is "ten thousand kotis" of buddhas, which the English follows and the plain Chinese renders the same way; Kumarajiva has 百千万亿诸佛 (bǎiqiān wànyì zhū fó, "hundreds of thousands of myriads of hundred-millions of buddhas").

verses.en: "And the lifespan of that Blessed One, the Tathagata Rashmishatasahasraparipurnadhvaja, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, will be beyond measure."

Then the nun Mahaprajapati Gautami with her following of six thousand nuns, and the nun Yashodhara with her following of four thousand nuns, having heard from the Blessed One their own predictions to unsurpassed, perfect awakening, were filled with wonder and amazement, and at that moment spoke this verse:
"Blessed One, you are the trainer, you are the guide, you are the teacher of the world with its gods. You give comfort, and humans and gods worship you. Today, Protector, we too are content."
