Having spoken this verse, the nuns said to the Blessed One: "Blessed One, we too have the courage to make this Dharma discourse known in the last age, the last time, but in other world systems."

Then the Blessed One looked toward those eighty hundred thousand kotis of nayutas of bodhisattvas, who had gained the dharanis (powers of holding the teaching in memory) and who turn the wheel of the Dharma that never turns back. As soon as the Blessed One looked at them, those bodhisattvas, great beings, rose from their seats, joined their palms toward the Blessed One, and thought: "The Blessed One is asking us to make this Dharma discourse known." Thinking this, they were shaken and said to one another: "Sons of good family, what shall we do, now that the Blessed One is asking us to make this Dharma discourse known in the future?"

cmp.note: 梵文说菩萨们「被震动了」，互相商量怎么办。白话照译；鸠摩罗什改写成「佛今默然，不见告勅，我当云何」，变成在猜佛没有开口的意思。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says the bodhisattvas were "shaken" and asked one another what to do; the plain Chinese follows it. Kumarajiva rewrites it as 佛今默然，不见告勅，我当云何 (fó jīn mòrán, bú jiàn gàochì, wǒ dāng yúnhé, "the Buddha is silent and gives no order; what should I do?"), so they are guessing at what an unspoken silence means.

verses.en: Then those sons of good family, out of reverence for the Blessed One and because of the vows of their own past practice, roared a lion's roar before the Blessed One: "Blessed One, in the future, after the Tathagata has passed into final nirvana, we will go into the ten directions and lead all beings to copy out this Dharma discourse, recite it, reflect on it and make it known, by the Blessed One's own power. And the Blessed One, staying in another world system, will guard, shield and protect us."
Then those bodhisattvas, great beings, spoke to the Blessed One together in one voice with these verses:
"Blessed One, do not worry. After your final nirvana, in that last age, so very frightening, we will make this supreme sutra known.
"Guide, we will put up with the insults, the threats and the raised sticks of fools; we will bear them.
"In that terrible last age people will be dull-witted, crooked and deceitful, conceited fools who think they have reached what they have not reached.
"'We live in the forest, we wear a patched robe, we live a life of strict austerity,' these wrong-minded people will say.

cmp.note: kanthā 是用破布拼缝成的衣服，英文 patched robe、白话「破布衣」都照字面；鸠摩罗什「纳衣」是同一个意思，指僧人的粪扫衣。
cmp.en: Kanthā is a garment stitched together from rags; the English "patched robe" and the plain Chinese 破布衣 (pòbù yī, "rag clothing") are literal, and Kumarajiva's 纳衣 (nàyī, "patched robe") means the same thing, the rag robe worn by ascetic monks.

verses.en: "Greedy for tasty food and attached to it, they will teach the Dharma to householders, and they will be honored as if they had the six higher knowledges."

cmp.note: 「六种神通」，指具足六通的阿罗汉。英文 six higher knowledges 照字面，没有点出「阿罗汉」；白话和鸠摩罗什「如六通罗汉」都补了出来。
cmp.en: "The six higher knowledges," meaning arhats who have all six. The English "six higher knowledges" is literal and does not name the arhat; the plain Chinese and Kumarajiva's 如六通罗汉 (rú liù tōng luóhàn, "like arhats with the six powers") both spell it out.

verses.en: "Fierce-minded and malicious, always thinking about house and property, they will take cover in the forest and slander us."
"And these men, intent on gain and honor, will say of us: 'Alas, these monks are outsiders (followers of other sects), teaching poems of their own.'"

cmp.note: tīrthika 指佛教以外的宗教修行者，英文 outsiders 加括注，白话、鸠摩罗什都译「外道」。kāvya 是「诗作、文学作品」，英文 poems、白话「诗文」照字面；鸠摩罗什改成「外道论议」。
cmp.en: Tīrthika means a religious practitioner outside the Buddhist fold; the English says "outsiders" with a gloss, and the plain Chinese and Kumarajiva both use 外道 (wàidào, "outside paths"). Kāvya means "poems, literary compositions"; the English "poems" and the plain Chinese 诗文 (shīwén, "poems and prose") are literal, while Kumarajiva changes it to 外道论议 (wàidào lùnyì, "outsiders' doctrines").

verses.en: "'For the sake of gain and honor they have strung together sutras of their own and recite them in the middle of the assembly,' so they will run us down."
"Before kings and princes and royal ministers, before brahmins and householders, and before other monks too,"
"they will speak ill of us and say we spread the doctrines of outsiders. Out of reverence for the great seers, we will bear it all."
"And when in that age the wrong-minded mock us, saying, 'So these are going to be buddhas!', we will bear that too, in every way."

cmp.note: 梵文是嘲讽「这些人要成佛了」。英文、白话照译；鸠摩罗什作「汝等皆是佛」，像是当面说「你们都是佛」，把将来时变成了现在。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit is a sneer: "these are going to be buddhas." The English and plain Chinese follow it; Kumarajiva writes 汝等皆是佛 (rǔděng jiē shì fó, "you are all buddhas"), turning the future into the present.

verses.en: "In that cruel age of great fear, terrifying with the upheaval of the eon, many monks who look like yakshas (fierce spirits) will revile us."

cmp.note: 梵文是「许多长得像夜叉的比丘」辱骂我们。英文、白话照译；鸠摩罗什译成「恶鬼入其身」，变成被恶鬼附身。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says "many monks with the look of yakshas" will revile us; the English and plain Chinese follow it. Kumarajiva renders it 恶鬼入其身 (èguǐ rù qí shēn, "evil ghosts enter their bodies"), turning it into possession.

verses.en: "Out of reverence for the Lord of the World, we take on this very hard task here: tying on the belt of patience, I will make this sutra known."

cmp.note: 「系紧忍耐的腰带」，是准备上阵的比喻。英文、白话照字面；鸠摩罗什改成「着忍辱铠」，从腰带变成铠甲。
cmp.en: "Tying on the belt of patience," an image of girding up for battle. The English and plain Chinese are literal; Kumarajiva makes it 着忍辱铠 (zhuó rěnrǔ kǎi, "put on the armor of patience"), turning the belt into armor.

verses.en: "Guide, we care nothing for body or life. What we want is awakening, keeping safe what you have entrusted to us."
"The Blessed One himself knows what kind of bad monks there will be in the last age, who do not understand teaching with hidden meaning."

cmp.note: 「带着深意、意在言外的说法」。英文 teaching with hidden meaning、白话「带深意的说法」照译；鸠摩罗什译成「佛方便，随宜所说法」，把它解释成方便说法。
cmp.en: "Speech with an intended, deeper meaning." The English "teaching with hidden meaning" and the plain Chinese 带深意的说法 ("teaching with deep intent") follow it; Kumarajiva explains it as 佛方便，随宜所说法 (fó fāngbiàn, suíyí suǒ shuō fǎ, "the Buddha's skillful means, the Dharma taught as suits the occasion").

verses.en: "We must put up with every frown, with being ignored again and again, with being thrown out of the monasteries, and with being tied up and beaten in many ways."
"Remembering the command of the Lord of the World in the last age, we will speak this sutra fearlessly in the middle of the assembly."
"In towns and villages, wherever there are people who want it, we will go from place to place and hand over to them, Guide, what you have entrusted."
"Lord of the World, great sage, we will be your messengers. Do not worry, for you have reached peace, you are fully at rest."
"And all you lamps of the world who have come here from the ten directions: we speak the truth. You know our faith."
This is the twelfth chapter, called Courage, in the noble Dharma discourse of the Lotus of the True Dharma.

cmp.note: 梵本这一品是第十二品，本站和鸠摩罗什本把它排在第十三。英文、白话都照梵文写「第十二」。
cmp.en: In the Sanskrit this is the twelfth chapter; the site and Kumarajiva's version place it thirteenth. The English and plain Chinese both keep the Sanskrit "twelfth."

verses.en: Then Manjushri the Prince said to the Blessed One: "Blessed One, these bodhisattvas, great beings, have taken on something hard, something extremely hard, out of reverence for the Blessed One. Blessed One, how should these bodhisattvas, great beings, make this Dharma discourse known in the last age, the last time?" When he had said this, the Blessed One said to Manjushri the Prince: "Manjushri, a bodhisattva, a great being, should make this Dharma discourse known in the last age, the last time, standing firm in four things. Which four? Here, Manjushri, a bodhisattva, a great being, should make this Dharma discourse known in the last age, the last time, standing firm in proper conduct and a proper range. And how, Manjushri, does a bodhisattva, a great being, stand firm in proper conduct and a proper range?

cmp.note: ācāra 是「行为、举止」，gocara 本义是「牛吃草的地方」，引申为「出入的范围、活动的领域」。英文 conduct / range、白话「行为 / 活动范围」照字面；鸠摩罗什译「行处、亲近处」，把 gocara 理解成「该亲近什么」。
cmp.en: Ācāra means "conduct, behavior"; gocara originally means "a pasture where cattle graze," hence "the range one moves in." The English "conduct" and "range" and the plain Chinese 行为 / 活动范围 ("conduct" / "range of activity") are literal; Kumarajiva renders them 行处 (xíngchù, "place of practice") and 亲近处 (qīnjìn chù, "places to draw near"), reading gocara as "what one should associate with."

verses.en: "Manjushri, when a bodhisattva, a great being, is patient and self-controlled, has reached the stage of the tamed, has a mind that is not frightened or alarmed, and is not envious; and when, Manjushri, a bodhisattva, a great being, does not move in any dharma at all, but sees the own-character of dharmas as it really is, and does not examine or make distinctions about these dharmas: this, Manjushri, is called the conduct of a bodhisattva, a great being. And what, Manjushri, is the range of a bodhisattva, a great being?"

"It is this, Manjushri: a bodhisattva, a great being, does not wait on the king; he does not wait on, keep company with, attend or visit princes, royal ministers or royal officers. He does not wait on, keep company with or attend followers of other sects, such as charakas, wandering ascetics, Ajivikas and Nirgranthas (naked Jain ascetics), or people absorbed in poetry and secular learning. He does not wait on, keep company with or attend those who keep the spells of the Lokayata (the materialists) or the Lokayatikas themselves, and he does not become intimate with them. Nor does he go near chandalas (outcastes), boxers, pig-keepers, poultry-keepers, deer-hunters, butchers, actors and dancers, tumblers or wrestlers; he does not go to the other places where people amuse and enjoy themselves, and he does not become intimate with such people. Only when they come to him of their own accord does he teach them the Dharma from time to time, and he teaches it without depending on them.

cmp.note: 顺世派，古印度只承认物质、否认来世的学派。英文 Lokayata 加括注 materialists，白话也加了解释；鸠摩罗什只音译「路伽耶陀、逆路伽耶陀」，读者看不出是什么人。
cmp.en: The Lokayata were the ancient Indian school that accepted only matter and denied any afterlife. The English keeps the name with the gloss "materialists," and the plain Chinese also explains it; Kumarajiva only transliterates, 路伽耶陀、逆路伽耶陀 (lùjiāyētuó, nì lùjiāyētuó), so readers cannot tell who these people are.

verses.en: "He does not wait on, keep company with or attend monks, nuns, laymen or laywomen who follow the disciple vehicle, and he does not become intimate with them. He does not share a range with them, whether on the walking path or in the monastery. Only when they come to him of their own accord does he teach them the Dharma from time to time, and he teaches it without depending on them. This, Manjushri, is the range of a bodhisattva, a great being."

"Further, Manjushri, a bodhisattva, a great being, does not take up some sign of attraction toward one woman or another and teach her the Dharma again and again, nor is he always wanting to see women. He does not go visiting families, and he does not think he ought to keep chatting with girls, young unmarried women or young wives, or exchange pleasantries with them. He does not teach the Dharma to a eunuch, does not become intimate with one, and does not exchange pleasantries with one. He does not go alone into a house for alms, unless he goes keeping the Tathagata in mind. And if he teaches the Dharma to women, he does not teach it even with passion for the Dharma, let alone with passion for a woman. He does not so much as show a row of teeth, let alone pull broad faces.

cmp.note: 「一排牙齿」，即不露齿而笑。英文、白话照字面；鸠摩罗什写「不露齿笑，不现胸臆」，多了「不露胸口」一项，梵文没有。
cmp.en: "A row of teeth," that is, not even smiling with the teeth showing. The English and plain Chinese are literal; Kumarajiva writes 不露齿笑，不现胸臆 (bú lù chǐ xiào, bú xiàn xiōngyì, "no toothy smile, no showing the chest"), adding the chest, which the Sanskrit does not have.

verses.en: "He takes no pleasure in having a novice monk or novice nun, a monk or nun, a boy or girl around him; he does not become intimate with them or chat with them. He values solitary retreat and often goes into retreat. This, Manjushri, is called the first range of a bodhisattva, a great being."

"Further, Manjushri, a bodhisattva, a great being, sees all dharmas as empty: dharmas standing as they are, standing without distortion, standing as they really are, unmoving, unshakable, not turning back, not turning round, always standing as they really are; with the nature of space; beyond words and ordinary speech; unborn, not come into being, not produced, unconditioned, without continuity; not to be spoken of as existing; standing in a state of non-attachment; appearing only through the distortion of perception. Living in this way, Manjushri, a bodhisattva, a great being, constantly looking at all dharmas, stands within his range. This, Manjushri, is the second range of a bodhisattva."

cmp.note: 「从想（认知）的颠倒中显现」。英文、白话照译；鸠摩罗什写「但以因缘有，从颠倒生故说」，多了「因缘」，也多了「无名、无相、无量、无边」等梵文这里没有的词。
cmp.en: "Appearing out of a distortion of perception." The English and plain Chinese follow it; Kumarajiva writes 但以因缘有，从颠倒生故说 (dàn yǐ yīnyuán yǒu, cóng diāndǎo shēng gù shuō, "they exist only through causes and conditions, and are spoken of because they arise from distortion"), adding "causes and conditions" and further terms not in this Sanskrit passage.

verses.en: Then the Blessed One, to show this same meaning more fully, spoke these verses at that moment:
"A bodhisattva who wishes, in the very cruel time to come, to make this sutra known without shrinking back and without fear
"should guard his conduct and his range, stay unmixed and pure, and always avoid intimacy with princes and kings.
"Nor should he be intimate with the king's officers, nor at all with chandalas, boxers, drunkards or outsiders.
"He should not wait on the conceited, or on those stuck in the monastic rules and the scriptural collections; and he should avoid monks who are taken for arhats, and those who break the precepts.

cmp.note: 字面是「住于律和阿含（经文集）的人」。白话理解为「死守戒律和经文条文」；英文 stuck in the monastic rules and the scriptural collections 同样带贬义；鸠摩罗什直接译成「贪着小乘、三藏学者」，点明了指的是小乘。
cmp.en: Literally "those who stand in the Vinaya and the Agamas (the scriptural collections)." The plain Chinese reads it as clinging rigidly to rules and texts, and the English "stuck in" carries the same disapproval; Kumarajiva says it outright: 贪着小乘、三藏学者 (tānzhuó xiǎochéng, sānzàng xuézhě, "scholars of the Tripitaka attached to the Small Vehicle").

verses.en: "He should always avoid nuns whose range is joking and chatter, and avoid laywomen who carry on openly.
"Laywomen who seek peace in this very life: he should avoid intimacy with them. This is called his conduct.
"But if someone comes up to him and asks about the Dharma for the sake of the highest awakening, the wise one should always speak to him, without shrinking back and without depending on him.
"Women and eunuchs: he should avoid intimacy with them. And in households he should keep away from young wives and girls.
"He should never exchange pleasantries with them or ask how they are with a laugh. He should avoid intimacy with pig-keepers and shepherds,
"and with those who harm all kinds of living things for profit, and sell meat at the slaughterhouse; he should avoid intimacy with them.
"People who live off women, he should avoid intimacy with them; and with actors, tumblers and wrestlers, and other people like them.
"He should not wait on courtesans, or others who make a living from pleasure; he should avoid all friendly dealings with them.
"And when the wise one teaches the Dharma to women, he should not go in there alone, nor should he joke around.
"And when he goes into a village again and again looking for food, he should look for a second monk to go with him, or else keep the Buddha in mind.
"This is the first conduct and range I have pointed out, by which the wise live as they keep a sutra like this.
"When he does not move in any dharma, whether low, high or middling, conditioned or unconditioned, real or unreal, in any way at all;
"when the steady one does not treat anyone as 'a woman' or imagine anyone as 'a man'; when, because all dharmas are unborn, he looks for them and does not see them:
"this is what is called the conduct of all bodhisattvas. Now listen to me as I explain what their range is like.
"These dharmas are taught to be nonexistent; they have not appeared, they are all unborn. They are empty, without activity, standing so for all time. This is called the range of the wise.

"They are imagined by people whose perceptions are upside down: the nonexistent taken as existent, the unreal as real. Things that have not arisen, unborn dharmas, are imagined the wrong way round as born and real.

"With his mind on one point, always collected, standing firm like the peak of Mount Sumeru (the great mountain at the center of the world), standing like this he should look on all these dharmas as being like space.
"Always like space, without a solid core, unmoving and free of conceit: 'this is how dharmas stand, for all time.' This is called the range of the wise.

cmp.note: manyana 指「妄自思量、我执式的揣度」，也可理解为「自负」。英文 conceit、白话「妄自揣度」各取一边；鸠摩罗什这一句没有对应的词。
cmp.en: Manyana means "self-centered conceiving," the mind's assumption of "I" and "mine"; it can also mean "conceit." The English "conceit" and the plain Chinese 妄自揣度 (wàngzì chuǎiduó, "presumptuous speculation") each take one side of it; Kumarajiva's line has no corresponding word.

verses.en: "A monk who, after my nirvana, guards the deportment I have taught can make this sutra known in the world, and there will be no timidity in him at all.

cmp.note: īryāpatha 本指行、住、坐、卧四种威仪举止。白话「威仪举止」照译，英文 deportment 同；鸠摩罗什把这句改写成「入是行处、及亲近处」，接回前面的术语。
cmp.en: Īryāpatha originally means the four postures of deportment: walking, standing, sitting and lying down. The plain Chinese 威仪举止 (wēiyí jǔzhǐ, "dignified deportment") and the English "deportment" match it; Kumarajiva rewrites the line as 入是行处、及亲近处 (rù shì xíngchù, jí qīnjìn chù, "enters this place of practice and these places to draw near"), tying it back to the earlier terms.

verses.en: "At the right time the wise one, reflecting, goes into his cell and shuts the door. He looks into all these dharmas properly, then gets up and teaches with a mind that does not shrink back.
"Here kings will protect him, and princes will listen to the Dharma; and other householders and brahmins (the priestly class) will all gather around him.

"Further, Manjushri, a bodhisattva, a great being, who wants to make this Dharma discourse known after the Tathagata's final nirvana, in the last age, the last time, when the true Dharma is being destroyed, lives at ease. Living at ease, he teaches the Dharma, whether he carries it in his body (by memory) or in a book. When he teaches others he is not overly given to finding fault. He does not slander other monks who teach the Dharma, does not speak ill of them, and does not spread ill reports of them. He does not name other monks who follow the disciple vehicle and speak ill of them or spread ill reports of them, and he does not think of them as enemies. Why? Because he stands in a state of ease. He teaches the Dharma to all who come to hear it, welcoming them and without envy.

cmp.note: 「安乐地安住」，这一品的品名「安乐行」就来自这个词。英文 lives at ease、白话「安乐地安住」照字面；鸠摩罗什译「住安乐行」。
cmp.en: "Living at ease": the chapter's name comes from this word. The English "lives at ease" and the plain Chinese 安乐地安住 (ānlè de ānzhù, "dwelling in ease") are literal; Kumarajiva writes 住安乐行 (zhù ānlè xíng, "abide in the practice of ease").

cmp.note: 「在身中的或在书中的」，指背诵记住的或写成经卷的。英文加了括注 by memory；鸠摩罗什作「若口宣说、若读经时」。
cmp.en: "Carried in the body or carried in a book," meaning memorized or written down. The English adds the gloss "by memory"; Kumarajiva has 若口宣说、若读经时 (ruò kǒu xuānshuō, ruò dú jīng shí, "whether speaking it aloud or reading the sutra").

verses.en: "He does not quarrel, and when he is asked a question he does not answer it by way of the disciple vehicle; rather he answers it in such a way that the questioner wakes up to the buddha knowledge."
Then at that moment the Blessed One spoke these verses:
"The wise one always lives at ease, and sits at ease to teach the Dharma, having set out a broad seat in a clean and pleasant spot.
"Putting on a clean robe, well dyed in approved colors, wearing a black overgarment and a large lower robe,

cmp.note: 「黑色的 āsevaka」，具体是什么衣物不清楚，白话译「黑色的外衣」，英文 black overgarment 也是推测。鸠摩罗什只写「着新净衣，内外俱净」，没有这些细节。
cmp.en: "A black āsevaka": exactly what garment this is is unclear. The plain Chinese 黑色的外衣 ("black outer garment") and the English "black overgarment" are both guesses. Kumarajiva writes only 着新净衣，内外俱净 (zhuó xīn jìng yī, nèiwài jù jìng, "wearing new clean clothes, pure inside and out"), without these details.

verses.en: "he sits on a seat with a footstool, well covered with colorful cloths, climbing onto it with well-washed feet, his head and face glossy with oil.
"Seated here on the Dharma seat, with beings gathered with their minds on one point, he should offer many fine talks to monks and nuns,
"to laymen and laywomen, to kings and princes too. The wise one should always tell sweet stories rich in meaning, without envy.
"Even when they ask him questions, he should explain the meaning again in a fitting way, and teach those matters so that, having heard them, they will gain awakening.
"Throwing off laziness, never letting the thought of weariness arise, the wise one should drop all discontent and cultivate the power of kindness toward the assembly.
"Day and night the wise one should speak the highest Dharma with kotis of nayutas (huge numbers) of examples. He should delight the assembly and satisfy them, and never ask anything of them.
"Hard food and soft food, food and drink, clothes, bed and seat, robes, medicine for the sick: he should not think of these, nor ask the assembly for anything.
"Instead, the wise one should always think: 'May I become a buddha, and these beings too.' That I teach the Dharma for the good of the world: this is my whole support for happiness.
"And a monk who, after my nirvana, makes this known without envy will have no suffering and no obstacles; grief and distress will never come to him.
"No one will frighten him, beat him or speak ill of him, and he will never be driven out, because he stands firm in the strength of patience.
"The wise one who lives at ease, standing as I have described, has many hundreds of kotis of good qualities, which could not be told even in a hundred eons.

"Further, Manjushri, a bodhisattva, a great being, who keeps this sutra after the Tathagata's final nirvana, when the time of the true Dharma's end has come, is without envy, without deceit and without guile. He does not speak ill of other people who follow the bodhisattva vehicle; he does not run them down or belittle them. He does not stir up regret in other monks, nuns, laymen or laywomen, whether they follow the disciple vehicle, the solitary-buddha vehicle or the bodhisattva vehicle, by saying: 'Sons of good family, you are far from unsurpassed, perfect awakening; you are not fit for it. You live in utter carelessness; you are not able to wake up to that knowledge.' He does not stir up regret like this in anyone who follows the bodhisattva vehicle.

cmp.note: kaukṛtya 是「悔恨、内疚、不安」。英文 regret、白话「悔恨疑虑」照译；鸠摩罗什「令其疑悔」意思相同。
cmp.en: Kaukṛtya means "remorse, guilty unease." The English "regret" and the plain Chinese 悔恨疑虑 (huǐhèn yílǜ, "regret and doubt") follow it, and Kumarajiva's 令其疑悔 (lìng qí yí huǐ, "make them doubt and regret") means the same.

verses.en: "He takes no delight in disputes about the Dharma and does not dispute about it, and he does not let go of the strength of kindness toward any being. Toward all Tathagatas he thinks of them as his father; toward all bodhisattvas he thinks of them as his teacher. To the bodhisattvas, great beings, in the world in the ten directions he often bows with sincere intent and reverence. When he teaches the Dharma, he teaches it with nothing lacking and nothing extra, with an equal love for the Dharma; while making this Dharma discourse known, he shows no one extra favor, not even out of love for the Dharma.

cmp.note: 梵文是「慈（maitrī）的力量」。英文 strength of kindness、白话「慈心的力量」照译；鸠摩罗什改成「于一切众生起大悲想」，把「慈」换成了「悲」。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit is "the strength of kindness (maitrī)." The English and plain Chinese 慈心的力量 (cíxīn de lìliang) follow it; Kumarajiva writes 于一切众生起大悲想 (yú yíqiè zhòngshēng qǐ dàbēi xiǎng, "toward all beings, give rise to great compassion"), swapping kindness for compassion.

verses.en: "Manjushri, a bodhisattva, a great being, who has this third quality and makes this Dharma discourse known after the Tathagata's final nirvana, when the time of the true Dharma's end has come, lives in comfort and makes this Dharma discourse known without being harassed. He will have companions in reciting the Dharma, and listeners will appear for him who will hear this Dharma discourse from him, believe it, trust it, keep it, master it, copy it, have it copied, and, once it is in a book, honor, respect, revere and make offerings to it."
So spoke the Blessed One. Having said this, the Sugata, the Teacher, went on to say this:
"The Dharma teacher should throw away deceit, pride and trickery entirely. The wise one who wants to make this sutra known should never be envious.
"He should never speak ill of anyone, never quarrel over views, and never give cause for regret by saying, 'You will not gain the unsurpassed knowledge.'
"That son of the Sugata is always honest, gentle and patient. Again and again he makes this Dharma known, and never grows weary.
"The bodhisattvas who move through the world in the ten directions out of compassion for beings are all my teachers: the wise one should feel the reverence due to a teacher toward them.
"Remembering the buddhas, the best of two-footed beings, he should always think of the Victors as his father. Giving up every thought of conceit, he will then meet no obstacle.
"Having heard a Dharma like this, the wise one should guard it. Collected, so as to live at ease, he is himself well guarded by kotis of living beings.

cmp.note: 梵文是「被千万众生好好守护」。英文、白话照译；鸠摩罗什作「无量众所敬」，从「守护」变成「恭敬」。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says "he is well guarded by kotis of living beings." The English and plain Chinese follow it; Kumarajiva has 无量众所敬 (wúliàng zhòng suǒ jìng, "revered by countless beings"), turning "guarded" into "revered."

verses.en: "Further, Manjushri, a bodhisattva, a great being, who wants to keep this Dharma discourse after the Tathagata's final nirvana, when the time of the true Dharma's end has come, that monk should live far away, very far away, from householders and renunciants, and live in kindness. Toward all beings who have set out for awakening he should feel longing and admiration. And he should think this: 'Alas, these beings are terribly lacking in wisdom. They do not hear, do not know, do not understand, do not ask about, do not believe and do not trust the Tathagata's skillful means, his teaching with hidden meaning.'

cmp.note: 梵文要这位比丘「远远地离开在家人和出家人而住」。英文、白话照译；鸠摩罗什却作「于在家、出家人中生大慈心」，意思几乎相反。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says this monk "should live very far away" from householders and renunciants; the English and plain Chinese follow it. Kumarajiva instead has 于在家、出家人中生大慈心 (yú zàijiā, chūjiā rén zhōng shēng dà cíxīn, "toward householders and renunciants, give rise to great kindness"), almost the opposite.

cmp.note: spṛhā 是「渴慕、向往」。白话译「向往敬慕之心」，英文 longing and admiration；鸠摩罗什此处另作「于非菩萨人中生大悲心」，与梵文对不上。
cmp.en: Spṛhā means "longing, eager desire." The plain Chinese 向往敬慕之心 ("a heart of longing and admiration") and the English "longing and admiration" follow it; Kumarajiva has instead 于非菩萨人中生大悲心 (yú fēi púsà rén zhōng shēng dàbēi xīn, "toward those who are not bodhisattvas, give rise to great compassion"), which does not match the Sanskrit.

verses.en: "'Even though these beings do not enter into this Dharma discourse or understand it, once I have woken up to unsurpassed, perfect awakening, whatever state each one is in, right there I will win him over by the power of my supernatural powers, bring him to trust it, lead him into it and bring him to maturity.'"

"Manjushri, a bodhisattva, a great being, who has this fourth quality and makes this Dharma discourse known after the Tathagata's final nirvana, will not be harmed. He will be honored, respected, revered and given offerings by monks, nuns, laymen and laywomen, by kings, princes, royal ministers and high officials, by townsfolk and country people, by brahmins and householders. Faithful gods who move through the sky will follow close behind him to hear the Dharma. Sons of the gods will always follow him to guard him, whether he is in a village or a monastery. They will come day and night to ask about the Dharma, and his answers will leave them pleased, elated and delighted. Why? Manjushri, this Dharma discourse is empowered by all the buddhas.

cmp.note: 梵本「为什么？这部法门受一切佛加持」在这一段末尾；白话把它移到了下一段开头。英文照梵文分段。
cmp.en: In the Sanskrit, "Why? This Dharma discourse is empowered by all the buddhas" ends this passage; the plain Chinese moves it to the start of the next one. The English follows the Sanskrit division.

verses.en: "Manjushri, this Dharma discourse is constantly empowered by the Tathagatas, arhats, fully awakened buddhas of the past, future and present. Manjushri, in many world systems even the sound, the echo, the mere name of this Dharma discourse is hard to come by.

"Manjushri, it is like this. There is a king, a wheel-turning monarch by force of arms (an ideal ruler of the whole world), who has conquered his own kingdom by force. Then his rivals, enemies and hostile kings make war on him. That wheel-turning king has all kinds of warriors, and they fight those enemies. When the king sees his warriors fighting, he is pleased with them and delighted, and being pleased and delighted he gives those warriors all kinds of gifts.

cmp.note: 「以武力转轮的王」，佛典里转轮王有以金、银、铜、铁轮或以力服人等不同等级，这里指靠武力征服的一种。英文加括注说明转轮王；鸠摩罗什作「强力转轮圣王」，意思一致。
cmp.en: "A wheel-turning king by force": Buddhist texts rank wheel-turning kings by the wheel they hold or how they rule, and this is the kind who conquers by arms. The English adds a gloss for "wheel-turning monarch"; Kumarajiva's 强力转轮圣王 (qiánglì zhuǎnlún shèngwáng, "powerful wheel-turning sage king") has the same sense.

verses.en: "He gives them villages or village lands, towns or town lands; he gives clothes, turbans, bracelets, anklets, necklaces, earrings, gold threads, long and short strings of pearls; he gives gold coins, gold, gems, pearls, beryl, conch shell, crystal and coral; he gives elephants, horses, chariots and foot soldiers, slave women and slave men; he gives carriages and palanquins. But he does not give anyone the jewel in his crown. Why? Because that crown jewel is the only one, and it sits on the king's head. Manjushri, if the king were to give away even that crown jewel, the king's whole fourfold army would be amazed and astonished.

cmp.note: cūḍā 是「头顶的发髻」，cūḍāmaṇi 是戴在发髻上的宝珠。英文 crown jewel、白话「顶上宝珠」都译出了「头顶」；鸠摩罗什「髻中明珠」更贴近原词的「发髻」。
cmp.en: Cūḍā is "the topknot," and cūḍāmaṇi is the jewel worn in it. The English "crown jewel" and the plain Chinese 顶上宝珠 (dǐngshàng bǎozhū, "jewel on the top of the head") convey "on the head"; Kumarajiva's 髻中明珠 (jì zhōng míngzhū, "bright pearl in the topknot") is closer to the original "topknot."

verses.en: "In just the same way, Manjushri, the Tathagata, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, the lord of the Dharma, the king of the Dharma, rules a kingdom of the Dharma by the Dharma in the triple world (the whole world of rebirth), won by the strength of his own arm and the strength of his merit. Mara the Evil One (the tempter, lord of death and desire) invades his triple world. Then the Tathagata's noble warriors fight with Mara. Then, Manjushri, the Tathagata, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, the lord of the Dharma, the king of the Dharma, seeing those noble warriors fighting, speaks many hundreds of thousands of different sutras to delight the four assemblies. He gives them the city of nirvana, the great city of the Dharma, and he entices them with peace. But he does not speak a Dharma discourse like this one.

cmp.note: 梵文说如来的法国是「凭自己臂力、福德之力赢来的」，沿用武王的比喻。英文、白话照译；鸠摩罗什改成「以禅定智慧力得法国土」，把臂力和福德换成了禅定和智慧。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says the Tathagata's kingdom was "won by the strength of his own arm and the strength of his merit," keeping the warrior-king image. The English and plain Chinese follow it; Kumarajiva writes 以禅定智慧力得法国土 (yǐ chándìng zhìhuì lì dé fǎ guótǔ, "won the Dharma land by the power of meditation and wisdom"), replacing arm and merit with meditation and wisdom.

verses.en: "Now Manjushri, just as that wheel-turning king by force, amazed at the great courage of his warriors in battle, finally gives them that crown jewel, the last thing, worth all he owns, which the whole world would find hard to believe, a thing of wonder,

"and just as, Manjushri, that king's crown jewel has long been guarded and sits on his head, in just the same way, Manjushri, the Tathagata, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, the king of the Dharma in the triple world, ruling his kingdom by the Dharma, sees disciples and bodhisattvas fighting with the Mara of the aggregates or the Mara of the afflictions. When, fighting with them, they have done the great heroic deed of destroying greed, hatred and delusion, escaping the whole triple world and defeating every Mara, then the Tathagata, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, pleased in turn, speaks to those noble warriors this Dharma discourse, which goes against the whole world, which the whole world finds hard to believe, never spoken before, never taught before. The Tathagata hands to all the disciples this discourse that brings all-knowing knowledge, like the great crown jewel.

cmp.note: 「蕴魔」「烦恼魔」：把五蕴和烦恼当作魔。英文直译 the Mara of the aggregates / of the afflictions；鸠摩罗什多列了一个「死魔」，梵文这里只有两种。
cmp.en: "The Mara of the aggregates" and "the Mara of the afflictions" treat the five aggregates and the afflictions as tempters. The English renders them literally; Kumarajiva adds a third, 死魔 (sǐ mó, "the Mara of death"), while the Sanskrit here has only two.

verses.en: "For this, Manjushri, is the highest Dharma teaching of the Tathagatas; this is the last Dharma discourse of the Tathagatas. Of all Dharma discourses this is the deepest of all, the one that goes against the whole world. Just as that wheel-turning king by force today took off the crown jewel he had long guarded and gave it to his warriors, in the same way, Manjushri, the Tathagata too has today made known this secret of the Dharma, long guarded, that sits at the head of all Dharma discourses, to be understood only by Tathagatas."

cmp.note: 「最后的」法门，既可以理解为时间上最后说的，也可以理解为至高无上的。英文 last、白话「最后的」照字面；鸠摩罗什译「末后赐与」，取时间义。
cmp.en: "The last" Dharma discourse can mean the one taught last in time or the ultimate one. The English "last" and the plain Chinese 最后的 ("last") are literal; Kumarajiva's 末后赐与 (mòhòu cìyǔ, "given at the very end") takes the time sense.

verses.en: Then the Blessed One, to show this same meaning more fully, spoke these verses at that moment:
"Always showing the strength of kindness, always feeling compassion for all beings, one should make known a Dharma like this, this outstanding sutra praised by the Sugatas.

cmp.note: 梵文是「展现慈心的力量」。英文、白话照译；鸠摩罗什作「常行忍辱」，换成了「忍辱」。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says "showing the strength of kindness." The English and plain Chinese follow it; Kumarajiva has 常行忍辱 (cháng xíng rěnrǔ, "always practice patience"), substituting patience.

verses.en: "Toward householders and renunciants, and toward bodhisattvas, in that last age, he should show the strength of kindness to all, so that they do not reject the Dharma when they hear it.
"But once I have reached awakening and stand as a Tathagata, then, standing in skillful means, I will lead them in and let them hear this highest awakening.
"It is like a wheel-turning king by force who gives his warriors all kinds of gold; pleased, he gives elephants, horses, chariots and foot soldiers, towns and villages.
"Delighted, to some he gives bracelets, silver and gold thread, pearls and gems, conch shell, crystal and coral, and all kinds of slaves.
"But when he is amazed there by someone's supreme daring, and sees, 'This is a wonderful thing that has been done,' he takes off his crown and gives him the jewel.

"In just the same way I, the Buddha, am a king of the Dharma, with the strength of patience and a rich treasury of wisdom. I rule this whole world by the Dharma, caring for its good, full of compassion.
"Seeing beings being struck down, I speak thousands of kotis of sutras, knowing the courage of those living beings, pure beings who here destroy their afflictions.

"Then the king of the Dharma, the great physician, having spoken hundreds of kotis of discourses, knowing that beings have grown strong, the wise one teaches this sutra, as if it were the crown jewel.

cmp.note: 「大医生」，佛常被比作治众生病的医生。英文 great physician 照字面；白话译成「大医王般的」，加了「王」；鸠摩罗什这一句没有这个称呼。
cmp.en: "The great physician": the Buddha is often likened to a doctor curing beings' illness. The English "great physician" is literal; the plain Chinese 大医王般的 (dà yīwáng bān de, "like a great physician-king") adds "king"; Kumarajiva's line has no such title.

verses.en: "In this last age of the world I speak this sutra, foremost of all my sutras. I have guarded it and never spoken it before; today I let you hear it. Listen, all of you!
"These are the four qualities to be practiced after my nirvana by those who long for the highest, supreme awakening, and who do my work.
"Such a person has no grief and no obstacles, no ugliness and no illness. His skin does not turn dark, and he does not live in a mean town.

cmp.note: 「皮肤不会发黑」，反映古印度以肤色深为不吉的观念。英文、白话照字面；鸠摩罗什作「颜色鲜白」，从否定说法变成正面描写。
cmp.en: "His skin will not be dark" reflects the ancient Indian view of dark skin as unlucky. The English and plain Chinese are literal; Kumarajiva has 颜色鲜白 (yánsè xiān bái, "complexion fresh and fair"), turning the negative into a positive description.

verses.en: "That great seer is always a delight to see, honored like a Tathagata, and young sons of the gods always wait on him.
"No sword or poison will ever touch his body, nor stick or clod of earth. And whoever insults him will find his own mouth shut.
"Whoever keeps this sutra after my nirvana becomes a kinsman to living beings here. Wandering the earth, he becomes a light, taking away the darkness of many kotis of beings.

cmp.note: 梵文说他成了众生的「亲人」、成了「光」。英文、白话照译；鸠摩罗什改写成「游行无畏，如师子王，智慧光明，如日之照」，多了狮子王的比喻。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says he becomes a "kinsman" to beings and becomes "a light." The English and plain Chinese follow it; Kumarajiva rewrites it as 游行无畏，如师子王，智慧光明，如日之照 (yóuxíng wúwèi, rú shīzǐ wáng, zhìhuì guāngmíng, rú rì zhī zhào, "wandering fearless like the lion king, his wisdom shining like the sun"), adding the lion image.

verses.en: "In his dreams he sees auspicious things: he sees monks and nuns, and sees himself seated on a lion throne, making the Dharma known in many ways.
"Gods and yakshas (a class of nature spirits) like the sands of the Ganges, asuras and nagas of many kinds: in his dream he speaks the highest Dharma to all of them as they stand with joined palms.
"In his dream he sees the Tathagata teaching the Dharma to many kotis of beings, sending out thousands of rays, the gold-colored Lord with the lovely voice.
"And there he stands with joined palms, praising the sage, the best of two-footed beings; and the Victor, the great physician, speaks the highest Dharma to the four assemblies.

"Hearing it, he is overjoyed, and full of delight he makes offerings. In the dream he gains the dharanis (powers of holding the teaching in memory), quickly touching the knowledge that does not turn back.
"Knowing his intent, the Lord of the World predicts him to the state of a bull among men: 'Son of good family, in the future you too will touch here the unsurpassed, blessed knowledge.
"'Your field too will be vast, and you will have four assemblies just as I do. With reverence and joined palms they will hear the vast Dharma free of outflows.'
"Again, he sees himself practicing the Dharma in mountain caves. Having practiced the Dharma and touched the true nature of things, he gains concentration and sees the Victor.
"In his dream he sees the gold-colored one with the marks of a hundred merits, and hears the Dharma; having heard it, he makes it known in the assembly. This is the kind of dream he has.
"In a dream, too, he gives up his whole kingdom, his women's quarters and his family; leaving all pleasures behind, he goes forth and makes his way to the seat of awakening.
"Sitting on the lion throne there at the foot of the tree, seeking awakening, after seven days have passed he will reach the knowledge of the Tathagatas.
"Having reached awakening, he rises and turns the wheel free of outflows; he teaches the Dharma to the four assemblies for inconceivable thousands of kotis of eons.
"Having made known there the Dharma free of outflows and brought many kotis of beings to nirvana, he goes out like a lamp when its fuel is spent. Such is the dream he has.

cmp.note: 「像因（燃料）耗尽的灯一样熄灭」，nirvāti 本义就是「吹灭、熄灭」。英文、白话都译出了「燃料用尽」；鸠摩罗什作「如烟尽灯灭」，换成了「烟尽」。
cmp.en: "Like a lamp when its cause (fuel) is used up"; nirvāti itself means "to blow out, go out." The English and plain Chinese both convey "fuel spent"; Kumarajiva has 如烟尽灯灭 (rú yān jìn dēng miè, "like a lamp going out when the smoke is gone"), substituting smoke.

verses.en: "Manjughosha, many endless blessings will always come to the one who, in the last age, makes known this sutra, the highest Dharma, that I have taught so well."

cmp.note: 「妙音」，文殊师利的另一个名字，这里是呼格。英文保留 Manjughosha；白话写「文殊师利（妙音）」把两名对上；鸠摩罗什此句不出名字。
cmp.en: "Gentle Voice," another name of Manjushri, here used in address. The English keeps "Manjughosha"; the plain Chinese writes 文殊师利（妙音） (Wénshūshīlì, Miàoyīn) to link the two names; Kumarajiva's line names no one.

verses.en: This is the thirteenth chapter, called Living at Ease, in the noble Dharma discourse of the Lotus of the True Dharma.

cmp.note: 梵本这一品是第十三品，本站和鸠摩罗什本排在第十四。英文、白话照梵文写「第十三」。
cmp.en: In the Sanskrit this is the thirteenth chapter; the site and Kumarajiva's version place it fourteenth. The English and plain Chinese keep the Sanskrit "thirteenth."

chapters.title: Chapter 15 · Bodhisattvas Rising Up Out of the Earth

verses.en: Then, from among the bodhisattvas, great beings, who had come from other world systems, bodhisattvas as many as the grains of sand in eight Ganges rivers rose up out of the assembly. They pressed their palms together, faced the Blessed One, bowed to him, and said: “Blessed One, if you would allow us, we too would like to make this Dharma discourse known in this Saha world (our world of endurance) after the Tathagata has passed into final nirvana; we would recite it, have it written out, honor it, and devote ourselves to practicing it. Blessed One, please give us permission for this discourse too.” Then the Blessed One said to those bodhisattvas: “Enough, sons of good family. Why should you take on this task?

cmp.note: 梵文 alam 是很干脆的「够了、不必了」。英文 Enough、白话「够了」都照译；鸠摩罗什用「止」，再补一句「不须汝等护持此经」，意思一样，只是把拒绝说得更明白。
cmp.en: Sanskrit alam is a blunt “enough, no need.” The English “Enough” and the plain Chinese 够了 (gòu le, “enough”) both follow it; Kumarajiva uses 止 (zhǐ, “stop”) and adds 不须汝等护持此经 (“there is no need for you to protect this sutra”), the same meaning with the refusal spelled out.

verses.en: Here in this Saha world of mine, sons of good family, there are bodhisattvas, thousands as many as the grains of sand in sixty Ganges rivers, who make up the following of just one bodhisattva. And there are bodhisattvas like that, thousands as many as the sands of sixty Ganges rivers, each of whom has a following just as large. They are the ones who, after my final nirvana, in the last age, the last period, will hold this Dharma discourse, recite it, and make it known.

cmp.note: 梵文是说：六十恒河沙数千位菩萨，只是「一位菩萨」的随从；而像这样带随从的菩萨又有六十恒河沙数千位。白话第一句写成「每一位菩萨都有这样多的随从」，把「一位菩萨的随从」和后文「每一位」混在一起了。英文照梵文分成两层。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says that thousands of bodhisattvas as many as sixty Ganges' sands are the following of just one bodhisattva, and that there are again that many such leaders, each with a following that size. The plain Chinese first sentence says 每一位菩萨都有这样多的随从 (“each bodhisattva has this many followers”), merging the two layers; the English keeps them apart as the Sanskrit does.

verses.en: The moment the Blessed One said this, this Saha world cracked and split open on every side. And out of those cracks rose many hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas (kotis and nayutas are both enormous numbers) of bodhisattvas, with golden bodies and the thirty-two marks of a great man. They had been living below, in the space beneath this great earth, depending on this very Saha world. When they heard these words of the Blessed One, they rose up from under the earth. Each one of these bodhisattvas had a following of bodhisattvas as many as the sands of sixty Ganges rivers; each was a leader of a group, a leader of a great group, a teacher of a group.

cmp.note: 梵文是「裂开、崩开」，只说大地裂出缝来，菩萨从缝里出来。鸠摩罗什写「三千大千国土地皆震裂」，把范围扩大到整个三千大千世界，又加上「震」。品名「从地踊出」的「踊」也是汉译的生动说法，梵文是 samunmajjante「冒出来、浮上来」，像从水里冒出头。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says “cracked, split open”: the earth opens and the bodhisattvas come out of the cracks. Kumarajiva writes 三千大千国土地皆震裂 (“the ground of the whole trichiliocosm shook and split”), widening the scope and adding the shaking. The verb in the Chinese chapter title, 踊出 (yǒngchū, “leap/surge out”), is a vivid Chinese rendering; the Sanskrit samunmajjante means “surface, come up,” like rising out of water.

verses.en: Of such bodhisattvas, great beings, leaders of groups, leaders of great groups, teachers of groups, there were hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas as many as the sands of sixty Ganges rivers, surfacing out of the openings in the ground of this Saha world. What need is there to speak of the bodhisattvas, great beings, with followings of bodhisattvas as many as the sands of fifty Ganges rivers? Or forty Ganges rivers? Or thirty? Or twenty? Or ten Ganges rivers?

What need to speak of those with followings as many as the sands of five, four, three, or two Ganges rivers? Of those with followings as many as the sands of one Ganges? Of half a Ganges? Of those whose followings were a quarter, a sixth, an eighth, a tenth, a twentieth, a thirtieth, a fortieth, a fiftieth, a hundredth, a thousandth, a hundred-thousandth, a koti-th, a hundred-koti-th, a thousand-koti-th, a hundred-thousand-koti-th, a hundred-thousand-koti-nayuta-th of the sands of the Ganges? What need to speak of the bodhisattvas, great beings, whose followings were many hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas of bodhisattvas?

cmp.note: koṭi 一般作「千万」解，白话这里把「koṭi 分之一」写成「一亿分之一」，「百 koṭi」写成「百亿」，是把 koṭi 当成亿。梵文数目本来就是夸张的修辞，但单位换算前后不一；英文保留 koti 不折算。
cmp.en: Koti is usually taken as ten million; here the plain Chinese renders “a koti-th” as 一亿分之一 (“one hundred-millionth”) and “a hundred kotis” as 百亿 (“ten billion”), treating koti as 亿 (yì, a hundred million). The numbers are rhetorical anyway, but the conversion isn't consistent; the English keeps “koti” untranslated.

verses.en: What need to speak of the bodhisattvas, great beings, with a following of a koti? Of a hundred thousand? Of a thousand? Of five hundred? Of four hundred, three hundred, two hundred? Of a hundred? Of fifty bodhisattvas? And so on. What need to speak of those with followings of forty, thirty, twenty, ten, five, four, three, or two bodhisattvas? Or of bodhisattvas, great beings, with just one companion?

cmp.note: peyālam 是抄经人的省略记号，意思是「依此类推，中间省略」。白话写成「（以下同样省略）」，英文写 And so on。
cmp.en: Peyālam is a scribe's abbreviation mark meaning “and so on, the rest is left out.” The plain Chinese writes （以下同样省略） (“the rest omitted likewise”); the English writes “And so on.”

cmp.note: 字面是「自己算第二个」，也就是「自己加一个同伴，两个人」。白话「只带一位同伴」正确；鸠摩罗什写「将……一弟子者」。
cmp.en: Literally “those with themselves as the second,” that is, a bodhisattva plus one companion, two in all. The plain Chinese 只带一位同伴 (“with only one companion”) is right; Kumarajiva writes 一弟子 (“one disciple”).

verses.en: What need to speak of the bodhisattvas, great beings, who had no following and lived alone? No number, no count, no comparison, no likeness can be found for the bodhisattvas, great beings, who surfaced out of the openings in the ground here in the Saha world. As each surfaced, they went up to the great jeweled stupa standing in the air, in the sky, where the Blessed One Prabhutaratna (“Many Jewels,” a buddha of the past whose stupa had appeared to bear witness to this sutra), the Tathagata, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, who had long since passed into final nirvana, sat on the lion throne together with the Blessed One Shakyamuni, the Tathagata, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha.

cmp.note: 「独自居住的」，指没有随从、一个人修行的菩萨。白话照译；鸠摩罗什译「况复单己，乐远离行」，补出「喜欢远离人群」的意思。
cmp.en: “Living alone,” bodhisattvas who practice by themselves without followers. The plain Chinese follows it; Kumarajiva renders it 况复单己，乐远离行 (“let alone those on their own, who delight in a life apart”), adding the sense of liking solitude.

verses.en: When they arrived, they bowed their heads to the feet of both Tathagatas, arhats, fully awakened buddhas. Then they paid homage to all the Tathagata-forms that the Blessed One Shakyamuni had emanated from himself, who had gathered from the many world systems of the ten directions all around and sat on lion thrones at the foot of various jewel trees. They bowed to them all, walked around those Tathagatas, arhats, fully awakened buddhas, keeping them on their right, many hundreds of thousands of times, praised them with all kinds of bodhisattva hymns, and stood to one side. Pressing their palms together, they bowed facing the Blessed One Shakyamuni, the Tathagata, arhat, fully awakened buddha, and the Blessed One Prabhutaratna, the Tathagata, arhat, fully awakened buddha.

cmp.note: 梵文是右绕「许多百千次」。英文、白话照译（白话作「千百次」）；鸠摩罗什改成汉译常见的「右绕三匝」。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit has them circle “many hundreds of thousands of times.” The English and plain Chinese follow it; Kumarajiva changes it to the stock Chinese phrase 右绕三匝 (“circled three times to the right”).

verses.en: All the while those bodhisattvas, great beings, were surfacing from the openings in the earth, bowing to the Tathagatas and praising them with all kinds of bodhisattva hymns, fifty full intermediate eons (kalpas) went by. Through those fifty intermediate eons the Blessed One Shakyamuni, the Tathagata, arhat, fully awakened buddha, stayed silent, and the four assemblies also remained silent for those same fifty intermediate eons. Then the Blessed One worked such a feat of supernatural power that the four assemblies felt it had been only a single afternoon. And they saw this Saha world held in hundreds of thousands of skies, entirely filled with bodhisattvas.

cmp.note: 字面是「饭后（的时段）」，也就是一个下午。白话「一个下午」、英文 a single afternoon 照译；鸠摩罗什写「谓如半日」。
cmp.en: Literally “the after-meal (period),” that is, one afternoon. The plain Chinese 一个下午 and the English “a single afternoon” follow it; Kumarajiva writes 谓如半日 (“thought it was half a day”).

cmp.note: 这个复合词字面是「被百千虚空所占据/包住」，确切意思不太清楚。白话作「被千百万重虚空所包围」；鸠摩罗什作「见诸菩萨遍满无量百千万亿国土虚空」，理解成菩萨布满了无数国土的虚空。英文照字面译。
cmp.en: This compound literally means “taken up by / held in hundreds of thousands of skies,” and its exact sense is not clear. The plain Chinese reads 被千百万重虚空所包围 (“surrounded by millions of layers of space”); Kumarajiva has the bodhisattvas filling the sky over countless lands. The English stays literal.

verses.en: Now this great host, this great multitude of bodhisattvas, had four bodhisattvas, great beings, at its head: the bodhisattva, great being, named Vishishtacharitra (Distinguished Conduct); the bodhisattva, great being, named Anantacharitra (Boundless Conduct); the bodhisattva, great being, named Vishuddhacharitra (Pure Conduct); and the bodhisattva, great being, named Supratishthitacharitra (Firmly Established Conduct). These four bodhisattvas, great beings, were at the head of that great host, that great multitude of bodhisattvas. Then the four bodhisattvas, great beings, standing in front of that great host of bodhisattvas, pressed their palms together facing the Blessed One and said to him: “Blessed One, are you well, free from illness and discomfort, living at ease?

cmp.note: viśiṣṭa 是「殊胜、卓越」，白话译「殊胜行」；鸠摩罗什译「上行」，取「最上」之意。日本日莲宗特别看重「上行菩萨」，所以这个名字在东亚很有名。英文译 Distinguished Conduct。
cmp.en: Viśiṣṭa means “distinguished, excellent”; the plain Chinese has 殊胜行 (shūshèng xíng, “excellent conduct”), Kumarajiva 上行 (Shàngxíng, “superior conduct”). Japan's Nichiren tradition gives this bodhisattva special weight, so the name is well known in East Asia. The English gives “Distinguished Conduct.”

verses.en: Blessed One, are beings easy to deal with, easy to teach, easy to train, easy to purify? We hope they don't wear the Blessed One out.
Then those four bodhisattvas, great beings, spoke to the Blessed One in these two verses:
“Are you living at ease, Protector of the world, Maker of light? Are you free of illness? Is your body comfortable, sinless one?
Are those beings easy to deal with, easy to train, easy to purify? We hope they don't tire the Protector of the world as he teaches.”

Then the Blessed One said to the four bodhisattvas, great beings, at the head of that great host, that great multitude of bodhisattvas: “It is so, sons of good family, it is so. I live at ease, with little illness and little discomfort. These beings of mine are easy to deal with, easy to teach, easy to train, easy to purify, and purifying them doesn't wear me out. Why? Because these beings, sons of good family, have already done their groundwork under earlier fully awakened buddhas. Just by seeing me and hearing me, sons of good family, they trust me, and they enter and plunge into the knowledge of a buddha. Even those who had served on the level of the disciples (shravakas) or on the level of the solitary buddhas (pratyekabuddhas), I myself have now led into the knowledge of the Buddha's teaching, and had them hear the highest truth.”

cmp.note: 梵文说：就连修过声闻、独觉道的人，现在也都被我引入了佛智。鸠摩罗什写「除先修习学小乘者。如是之人，我今亦令得闻是经，入于佛慧」，先说「除了」再说「也」，语气先抑后扬。英文、白话照梵文。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says that even those who trained on the disciple or solitary-buddha paths have now been led into buddha-knowledge. Kumarajiva writes 除先修习学小乘者 (“except those who formerly trained in the Lesser Vehicle”) and then says that he lets them too hear this sutra; he first sets them apart, then brings them in. The English and plain Chinese follow the Sanskrit.

verses.en: Then at that time those bodhisattvas, great beings, spoke these two verses:
“Wonderful, wonderful, great hero! We rejoice that those beings of yours are easy to deal with, easy to train, easy to purify,
and that they hear this deep knowledge of yours, Leader, and having heard it, trust it and pass across, Leader.”

cmp.note: uttaranti 字面是「渡过、上升」，白话译「领悟」是意译。英文保留 pass across（渡过）的意象。鸠摩罗什这一句作「能问诸佛，甚深智慧」，和梵文出入较大。
cmp.en: Uttaranti literally means “cross over, go up”; the plain Chinese 领悟 (lǐngwù, “grasp it”) is a free rendering. The English keeps the image of “passing across.” Kumarajiva's line, 能问诸佛，甚深智慧 (“they can ask the buddhas about their deepest wisdom”), differs considerably from the Sanskrit.

verses.en: When they had said this, the Blessed One praised the four bodhisattvas, great beings, at the head of that great host of bodhisattvas: “Wonderful, wonderful, sons of good family, that you rejoice in the Tathagata.”

At that time this thought came to the bodhisattva, great being, Maitreya (the bodhisattva who will be the next buddha after Shakyamuni) and to the other hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas of bodhisattvas, as many as the sands of eight Ganges rivers: “We have never before seen this great host, this great multitude of great bodhisattvas, nor ever heard of it, surfacing out of the openings in the earth, standing before the Blessed One, honoring, revering, respecting, and worshipping him, and exchanging greetings with him. Where in the world have these bodhisattvas, great beings, come from?”

cmp.note: 梵文是「八恒河沙数」的菩萨，和本品开头请命的他方菩萨人数一致。鸠摩罗什写「八千恒河沙」，多了一个「千」。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says bodhisattvas as many as the sands of eight Ganges rivers, matching the visiting bodhisattvas at the start of the chapter. Kumarajiva writes 八千恒河沙 (“eight thousand Ganges' sands”), adding a “thousand.”

verses.en: Then the bodhisattva, great being, Maitreya, aware of his own doubt and uncertainty, and knowing with his own mind the thoughts in the minds of those hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas of bodhisattvas, as many as the sands of the Ganges, pressed his palms together then and there and asked the Blessed One about this very matter in verse:
“Many thousands, nayutas, countless kotis of bodhisattvas never seen before: tell us about them, best of two-footed beings.
Where have they come from, and how, these beings of great supernatural power? They are huge in body. Where have they come from?
All of these great seers are steadfast, all are mindful, and lovely to look at. Where have they come from?

cmp.note: maharṣi「大仙人」本是印度对古代圣贤的称呼，这里用来称菩萨。英文 great seers、白话「大仙人」都照字面；鸠摩罗什这一颂改写成「智慧叵思议，其志念坚固，有大忍辱力」，没有「仙人」。
cmp.en: Maharṣi, “great seer,” is the Indian title for the sages of old, used here for the bodhisattvas. The English “great seers” and the plain Chinese 大仙人 (dà xiānrén, “great immortals/seers”) are literal; Kumarajiva rewrites the verse as “wisdom beyond thought, firm in will and mindfulness, with great power of patience,” with no “seers” in it.

verses.en: Lord of the world, each of these wise bodhisattvas has a following beyond measure, like the grains of sand in the Ganges.
The following of one glorious bodhisattva is a full sixty Ganges' worth of sand, and all of them have set out for awakening.
Of heroes like these, protectors with assemblies of their own, there are as many as the sands of sixty Ganges rivers.
And there are others, even more, with endless followings: fifty Ganges' worth, forty, thirty,
a following all around equal to twenty Ganges' worth of sand; and others, even more, whose followings are ten or five,
for each single son of the Buddha, each protector. Where has such an assembly come from today, Guide?

cmp.note: 「佛之子」，经中常用来称菩萨。英文直译 son of the Buddha，白话「佛子」。
cmp.en: “Son of the Buddha,” a common name for bodhisattvas in the sutra. The English translates it directly; the plain Chinese has 佛子 (fózǐ, “Buddha's child”).

verses.en: Each one has a following, companions who train under him, equal to four, three, or two Ganges' worth of sand.
And there are others, even more, whose number has no end; even in thousands of kotis of eons one could not find a comparison for them.
Then there are the followings of heroic bodhisattvas, protectors, of half a Ganges, a third, a tenth, a twentieth part.
And there are others, even more, whose number cannot be known, even if one counted them one by one for hundreds of kotis of eons.
And there are others, even more, with endless followings: a koti, and a koti, and a koti, and half a koti as well.
And further there are others, beyond all counting, of these great seers: bodhisattvas of great wisdom, all standing here in reverence.
Followings of a thousand, a hundred, fifty: there is no counting them, even in hundreds of kotis of eons.
Twenty, ten, five, then four, three, two: such are the followings of these heroes, and their number cannot be known.
And those who wander by themselves alone, who find peace on their own, who have gathered here today: there is no counting them either.
If a person took counting sticks in hand and counted for as many eons as there are grains of sand in the Ganges, he would never reach the end.

cmp.note: śalākā 是用来计数的小木签。白话「竹签」、鸠摩罗什「行筹」都是这个东西；英文 counting sticks。
cmp.en: A śalākā is a small stick used for counting. The plain Chinese 竹签 (zhúqiān, “bamboo slips”) and Kumarajiva's 行筹 (xíng chóu, “handle tallies”) both mean this; the English says “counting sticks.”

verses.en: All these great-souled, energetic protectors, these heroic bodhisattvas: where have they come from?
Who taught them the Dharma? Who set them on the way to awakening? Whose teaching do they delight in? Whose teaching do they uphold?
Splitting the whole earth open on every side, in all four directions, they surface, beings of great wisdom, of supernatural power, clear-sighted.
Sage, this world has been riddled with holes on every side by these fearless bodhisattvas as they surfaced.
We have never, ever seen them before. Tell us the name of their world, Guide.
Again and again we have traveled the ten directions, yet we have never seen these bodhisattvas.
Not a single one of these sons of yours have we ever seen, and today we suddenly see them. Tell us their story, Sage.
Thousands, hundreds, nayutas of bodhisattvas, all filled with curiosity, are looking at the best of two-footed beings.
Explain it, great hero, immeasurable one, free of all clinging: where do these brave, fearless bodhisattvas come from?”

cmp.note: nirupadhi「无所依、无执取」，指已没有任何把人绑在轮回里的「依」。白话作「离一切执着的人」，英文 free of all clinging。鸠摩罗什改作「无量德世尊」。
cmp.en: Nirupadhi, “without substrate, without clinging,” describes one who no longer has anything binding him to rebirth. The plain Chinese has 离一切执着的人 (“one free of all attachment”), the English “free of all clinging”; Kumarajiva changes it to 无量德世尊 (“World-Honored One of boundless virtue”).

verses.en: At that time there were Tathagatas, arhats, fully awakened buddhas, who had come from hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas of other world systems: emanations of the Blessed One Shakyamuni, the Tathagata, who taught the Dharma to beings in other world systems, and who now sat cross-legged on great jeweled lion thrones at the foot of jewel trees in the eight directions all around the Blessed One Shakyamuni, the Tathagata, arhat, fully awakened buddha. Each of those Tathagatas had his own attendant. These attendants, too, saw that great host, that great multitude of bodhisattvas surfacing out of the openings in the earth on every side and standing in the sky, and they too were amazed and said to their own Tathagatas: “Blessed One, where are all these bodhisattvas, great beings, coming from, immeasurable and countless?”

When they said this, those Tathagatas, arhats, fully awakened buddhas, said to their own attendants: “Wait a moment, sons of good family. This bodhisattva, great being, named Maitreya, whom the Blessed One Shakyamuni has foretold as the very next to reach unsurpassed, perfect awakening, is asking the Blessed One Shakyamuni, the Tathagata, arhat, fully awakened buddha, about this. The Blessed One Shakyamuni, the Tathagata, arhat, fully awakened buddha, will explain it, and then you will hear.”

Then the Blessed One addressed the bodhisattva, great being, Maitreya: “Wonderful, wonderful, Ajita (“Unconquered,” another name of Maitreya)! It is a noble question, Ajita, that you ask me.” Then the Blessed One addressed the whole host of bodhisattvas: “Then, sons of good family, all of you, be attentive. Put on your armor and stand firm in your strength, this whole host of bodhisattvas. Sons of good family, the Tathagata, arhat, fully awakened buddha, is now about to reveal the Tathagata's knowledge and vision, the Tathagata's bull-like might, the Tathagata's work, the Tathagata's play, the Tathagata's lion-like stretch, the Tathagata's bold advance.”

cmp.note: vṛṣabhita 是「像公牛一样昂首」，vijṛmbhita 是「像狮子一样伸展身体（准备跃起）」，都是表示威力的动物比喻。白话译成「雄健」「奋迅」，比喻淡了；鸠摩罗什用「师子奋迅之力」保住了狮子。英文把公牛和狮子都写出来。
cmp.en: Vṛṣabhita is “bearing oneself like a bull,” vijṛmbhita “stretching like a lion (before it springs)”: both animal images of power. The plain Chinese gives 雄健 (“vigor”) and 奋迅 (“swift energy”), and the images fade; Kumarajiva keeps the lion in 师子奋迅之力 (“the power of the lion's spring”). The English spells out both the bull and the lion.

verses.en: Then at that time the Blessed One spoke these verses:
“Be attentive, all you sons of good family. I am about to speak words that are never otherwise. Don't be downcast here, wise ones: the knowledge of the Tathagatas is beyond thought.
Be steadfast, all of you, be mindful, all of you, stand composed. Today you are to hear a Dharma never heard before, the marvel of the Tathagatas.
Never doubt, any of you, for I will steady you. I am a guide whose word is never otherwise, and my knowledge is beyond counting.
The things the Well-Gone One (Sugata) has awakened to are deep, beyond reasoning, without measure. Today I will make those things known. Listen to me: what they are, and how they are.

When the Blessed One had spoken these verses, he then addressed the bodhisattva, great being, Maitreya: “I declare it to you, Ajita, I make it known. These bodhisattvas, Ajita, immeasurable, countless, inconceivable, incomparable, beyond reckoning, whom none of you have seen before, who have just now come out of the openings in the earth: all these bodhisattvas, great beings, Ajita, are ones I myself, after reaching unsurpassed, perfect awakening in this Saha world, encouraged, roused, and gladdened, and turned toward unsurpassed, perfect awakening. These sons of good family I ripened in this bodhisattva way; I established them in it, brought them into it, steadied them, led them in, awakened them, and purified them.

And these bodhisattvas, great beings, Ajita, live in the space below this Saha world. These sons of good family are devoted to recitation, teaching, reflection, and careful attention. They don't enjoy crowds or mixing with people; they never put down their burden and keep their energy going. These sons of good family, Ajita, delight in solitude and love it. They don't live depending on gods and humans; they love a life apart. These sons of good family delight in the Dharma and are intent on the knowledge of a buddha.”

cmp.note: 「不放下轭的」，dhura 是牛车的车轭，比喻承担的重任。白话「从不放下担子」照译；鸠摩罗什译「未曾休息」，比喻没了。
cmp.en: “Not laying down the yoke”: dhura is the yoke of an ox cart, an image for the burden one has taken on. The plain Chinese 从不放下担子 (“never putting down the load”) follows it; Kumarajiva's 未曾休息 (“never resting”) drops the image.

verses.en: Then at that time the Blessed One spoke these verses:
“These bodhisattvas, immeasurable, inconceivable, without limit, endowed with supernatural power, wisdom, and learning, have practiced in knowledge for many kotis of eons.
I ripened them all for awakening, and they live in my own field. I alone ripened them all; these bodhisattvas are my own sons.

cmp.note: kṣetra 字面是「田地」，佛典里指一位佛教化的世界，即「佛土」。白话译「国土」，英文保留 field 的字面。
cmp.en: Kṣetra literally means “field”; in Buddhist texts it is the world a buddha teaches in, a “buddha-field.” The plain Chinese renders it 国土 (guótǔ, “land, realm”); the English keeps the literal “field.”

verses.en: All of them are devoted to forest life and the ascetic practices, and always avoid places where people mix. These sons of mine move about without attachment, training in my supreme way of conduct.

cmp.note: āraṇya 是林居，dhuta 是一套简朴苦行（只穿粪扫衣、只乞食等），汉译作「头陀」。白话「林居和头陀苦行」照译；英文用 ascetic practices 意译。
cmp.en: Āraṇya is forest dwelling; dhuta is a set of austere practices (wearing only rag robes, living only on alms, and so on), rendered 头陀 (tóutuó) in Chinese. The plain Chinese 林居和头陀苦行 follows it; the English paraphrases as “ascetic practices.”

verses.en: These heroes live in the space below this field, bringing about this highest awakening, striving day and night, never careless.
All of them are energetic and mindful, standing firm in boundless strength of wisdom. They teach the Dharma fearlessly, and all of them, these sons of mine, are shining.
When I had reached this highest awakening at the foot of the tree there, at the town of Gaya, and turned the unsurpassed wheel of the Dharma, I ripened all of them here for the highest awakening.

cmp.note: 梵文是「在伽耶城」，佛成道的地方其实在伽耶城外不远（今菩提伽耶）。散文部分弥勒说的是「离伽耶城不远」，偈颂就简称「在伽耶城」。鸠摩罗什这一颂还多出「令初发道心，今皆住不退，悉当得成佛」，梵文这一颂没有。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says “at the town of Gaya”; the place of awakening was actually a short way outside Gaya (today's Bodh Gaya). In the prose Maitreya says “not far from Gaya,” and the verse shortens it to “at Gaya.” Kumarajiva's version of this verse adds 令初发道心，今皆住不退，悉当得成佛 (“I led them to first set their minds on the path; now all stand without falling back and will all become buddhas”), which this Sanskrit verse lacks.

verses.en: These words of mine are pure and true. Having heard them, all of you, trust me: it was long, long ago that I reached the highest awakening, and it was I alone who ripened all of these.”

cmp.note: 「我这样久以前就证得了最高的觉悟」——这是全经的转折点：下一品《如来寿量品》就要说明佛成道其实在无量劫前。白话「我早就证得了」和英文 long, long ago 都照译；鸠摩罗什写「我从久远来，教化是等众」，把「久远」挂在「教化」上，不是挂在「成道」上。
cmp.en: “So long ago did I reach the highest awakening”: this is the turning point of the whole sutra, and the next chapter will explain that the Buddha's awakening actually lies countless eons back. The plain Chinese 我早就证得了 and the English “long, long ago” follow it; Kumarajiva writes 我从久远来，教化是等众 (“from the distant past I have been teaching these beings”), attaching “long ago” to the teaching rather than to the awakening.

verses.en: Then the bodhisattva, great being, Maitreya, and all those many hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas of bodhisattvas were amazed, astonished, filled with wonder: “How could the Blessed One, in such a short stay, such a brief stretch of time, have encouraged so many countless bodhisattvas, great beings, and ripened them for unsurpassed, perfect awakening?” Then the bodhisattva, great being, Maitreya, said to the Blessed One: “Blessed One, how is it now? When the Tathagata was a young prince, he left Kapilavastu, the town of the Shakyas, reached the excellent seat of awakening not far from the town of Gaya, and there awakened to unsurpassed, perfect awakening. Blessed One, from then until today it has been a little over forty years.

cmp.note: 梵文是「惊奇、稀有、诧异」，三个词都是赞叹的口气。白话照译；鸠摩罗什写「心生疑惑，怪未曾有」，先说「疑惑」，把这一段读成弥勒起疑，下文请佛断疑也就顺理成章。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit has three words of wonder: amazed, astonished, filled with wonder. The plain Chinese follows them; Kumarajiva writes 心生疑惑，怪未曾有 (“doubt arose in their minds, they found it unheard of”), putting doubt first and reading the scene as Maitreya beginning to doubt, which fits his request below to settle the doubts.

verses.en: So how, Blessed One, in such a stretch of time, has the Tathagata done this immeasurable work of a Tathagata, shown a Tathagata's bull-like might and a Tathagata's bold advance, so that this great host, this great multitude of bodhisattvas, has in such a stretch of time been encouraged and ripened for unsurpassed, perfect awakening? Blessed One, if one counted this host, this multitude of bodhisattvas, even for hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas of eons, no end could be found. So immeasurable are these bodhisattvas, great beings, Blessed One, so countless; they have lived the holy life for a long time, planted roots of goodness under many hundreds of thousands of buddhas, and been perfected over many hundreds of thousands of eons.

Blessed One, suppose there were a man, young, a youth, a mere boy, his hair still black, in the first flush of life, twenty-five years old by birth. He points to some men a hundred years old and says, ‘Sirs, these are my sons.’ And those hundred-year-old men say, ‘This is our father, the one who begot us.’ Blessed One, people would not believe that man's words; the world would find it very hard to believe.

It is just like that with the Blessed One, who awakened to unsurpassed, perfect awakening not long ago, while these bodhisattvas, great beings, are many beyond measure, and have practiced the holy life for many hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas of eons. They made up their minds long ago. In the knowledge of a buddha they are skilled at entering and leaving hundreds of thousands of gateways of meditative concentration (samadhi). They have finished their training in the great higher knowledges and done the groundwork for them. They are learned in the level of a buddha, skilled at reciting together the teachings of the Tathagatas, a marvel and a wonder to the world, and have attained great energy, strength, and power. And yet the Blessed One says of them: ‘I encouraged them from the very start, roused them, ripened them, and turned them toward this bodhisattva level.’ And: ‘After I awakened to unsurpassed, perfect awakening, I made all this energetic effort.’

cmp.note: saṃgīti 是「合诵、结集」，佛灭后弟子们聚在一起合诵经典叫做结集。白话「善于结集如来的教法」照译；鸠摩罗什译「巧于问答」，意思不同。
cmp.en: Saṃgīti is “reciting together, a council”: after the Buddha's death his disciples gathered to recite the teachings together. The plain Chinese 善于结集如来的教法 (“skilled at compiling the Tathagata's teachings”) follows it; Kumarajiva has 巧于问答 (“skilled in question and answer”), a different sense.

verses.en: Blessed One, we ourselves will take the Tathagata's word on faith: the Tathagata never says anything that is not so, and only the Tathagata can know this matter. But bodhisattvas, great beings, who have newly set out on the vehicle, Blessed One, will fall into doubt. After the Tathagata's final nirvana, when they hear this Dharma discourse on this point, they will not accept it, will not believe it, will not trust it. And then, Blessed One, they will have done deeds that lead to the ruin of the Dharma. So please, Blessed One, explain this very matter, so that we may be free of doubt about this teaching, and so that in time to come sons or daughters of good family on the bodhisattva vehicle will hear it and not fall into doubt.”

cmp.note: 「会导致法的毁坏的业」。这里 dharmavyasana 可以理解为「毁坏佛法」，也可以理解为「（他们自己）失去法」。白话取「毁坏正法」，鸠摩罗什「破法罪业」也一样；英文 the ruin of the Dharma 保留同样的含糊。
cmp.en: “Deeds leading to the ruin of the Dharma.” Dharmavyasana can mean “destroying the Dharma” or “(their own) loss of the Dharma.” The plain Chinese takes 毁坏正法 (“destroying the true Dharma”), as does Kumarajiva's 破法罪业 (“the offense of breaking the Dharma”); the English “the ruin of the Dharma” keeps the same ambiguity.

verses.en: Then at that time the bodhisattva, great being, Maitreya, spoke to the Blessed One in these verses:
“You were born in the Shakya settlement called Kapila, left home, and reached awakening at the town called Gaya. That is a short time, Protector of the world.

Yet these fearless noble ones of yours are many, great leaders who have practiced for kotis of eons, standing unshaken in the strength of supernatural power, well trained, who have gone all the way in the strength of wisdom.

cmp.note: ārya 在这里可以读作呼格「圣者啊」（称佛），也可以读作形容这些菩萨「圣洁的」。白话读成「您这些圣者」，英文读成 these noble ones of yours，两边一致。
cmp.en: Ārya here could be a vocative, “noble one!” (addressing the Buddha), or describe the bodhisattvas as “noble.” The plain Chinese reads 您这些圣者 (“these noble ones of yours”), and the English agrees.

verses.en: Untouched like a lotus by water, they split the earth and have come here today. All stand with palms pressed together in reverence, the mindful sons of the world's sovereign.
How will these bodhisattvas believe this wonder of yours? To strike down the doubt, speak, and teach it just as the matter really is.
It is as if a man here were young, a mere boy with black hair, twenty years old or a little more, and pointed to sons a hundred years old,

cmp.note: 偈颂里说「二十岁或稍多」，散文里说二十五岁。白话「二十来岁」照偈颂；鸠摩罗什偈颂仍写「年始二十五」，跟散文对齐了。
cmp.en: The verse says “twenty or a little more,” while the prose says twenty-five. The plain Chinese 二十来岁 (“twenty-odd”) follows the verse; Kumarajiva's verse still says 年始二十五 (“just twenty-five”), matching the prose.

verses.en: wrinkled and gray-haired, and they said, ‘This is the one who made our bodies.’ That would be hard to believe, Protector of the world: that a young man has sons like these.
Just so, the Blessed One is new, still young, while these many wise bodhisattvas are mindful, fearless in wisdom, well trained over thousands of kotis of eons;

cmp.note: 「新、年轻」。偈颂直接说世尊「年轻」，意思是成佛的时间短，不是说佛的年龄小；白话「正值年轻」照字面。鸠摩罗什写「得道来甚近」，把意思说明白了。英文 new, still young 照字面。
cmp.en: “New, young.” The verse calls the Blessed One young, meaning that he became a buddha only recently, not that he is young in years; the plain Chinese 正值年轻 (“in his youth”) is literal. Kumarajiva writes 得道来甚近 (“it is very recent since he attained the Way”), making the sense clear. The English “new, still young” is literal.

verses.en: steadfast, discerning in wisdom, pleasing and lovely to look at, every one of them, fearless in settling questions of Dharma, praised by the guides of the world;
moving without attachment like the wind, they live always in space, depending on nothing. These sons of the Well-Gone One know effort, seeking this level of a buddha.
How will this be believed after the Guide of the world has passed into final nirvana? We ourselves have no doubt at all, for we hear it face to face from the Protector of the world,
but let no bodhisattvas fall into doubt on this point and go to a bad rebirth. Explain it as it is, Blessed One: how were these bodhisattvas ripened?”
Here ends the fourteenth chapter, called “Bodhisattvas Rising Up Out of the Earth,” in the glorious Dharma discourse of the Lotus of the True Dharma.

cmp.note: 梵本这一品是第十四品；鸠摩罗什本把提婆达多品单独列为一品，所以这一品在他的本子里是第十五品（本站的章次与之相同）。
cmp.en: In the Sanskrit this is the fourteenth chapter. Kumarajiva's version has a separate Devadatta chapter, so there this is the fifteenth (the same number as the site's chapter).

chapters.title: Chapter 16 · How Long the Tathagata Lives

verses.en: Then the Blessed One addressed the whole host of bodhisattvas: “Trust me, sons of good family. Believe the Tathagata when he speaks words that are true.” A second time the Blessed One said to those bodhisattvas: “Trust me, sons of good family. Believe the Tathagata when he speaks words that are true.” A third time the Blessed One said to those bodhisattvas: “Trust me, sons of good family. Believe the Tathagata when he speaks words that are true.” Then that whole host of bodhisattvas, with the bodhisattva, great being, Maitreya (the bodhisattva who will be the next buddha) standing at their head, pressed their palms together and said to the Blessed One: “Let the Blessed One speak about this very matter, let the Well-Gone One (Sugata, a title of the Buddha) speak. We will believe what the Tathagata says.”

A second time that whole host of bodhisattvas said to the Blessed One: “Let the Blessed One speak about this very matter, let the Well-Gone One speak. We will believe what the Tathagata says.” A third time that whole host of bodhisattvas said to the Blessed One: “Let the Blessed One speak about this very matter, let the Well-Gone One speak. We will believe what the Tathagata says.”

Then the Blessed One, knowing that the bodhisattvas had asked him a full three times, said to them: “Then listen, sons of good family, to how the power of my sustaining strength works.
