“In the same way he knows the smells of beings, of men and women, even from far away; by their smell he knows where boys and girls are.
“He knows kings too, wheel-turning kings (world-ruling monarchs), mighty wheel-turners and regional rulers, and their princes and ministers; by smell he knows their whole inner palace.
“The many kinds of precious things for use, the treasures buried in the ground, and the women who are counted among a king's jewels: the bodhisattva knows them all by smell.

cmp.note: strīratna「女宝」是转轮王七宝之一：一位完美的王后。英文直译为 counted among a king's jewels，并保留原文把女子当作「宝物」来列举的说法，不替原文修饰。
cmp.en: Strīratna, “woman-jewel,” is one of the seven treasures of a wheel-turning king: a perfect queen. The English keeps the original's way of listing a woman among a king's “jewels” rather than softening it.

verses.en: “Their ornaments of many shapes fastened on their bodies, their clothes, garlands, and scented ointments: the bodhisattva knows them by smell.
“Whether they are standing, sitting, or lying down, their play and pleasure and all their powers: the wise one who keeps this supreme sutra knows them by the power of smell.
“The scents of fragrant oils and of many kinds of flowers and fruits: staying in one place he knows and smells them, 'These scents are in such-and-such a place.'
“In the clefts between mountains there are many sandalwood trees in bloom, and beings who live there: the wise one knows them all by smell.
“Those who live along the Chakravala mountains, those who live in the middle of the ocean, the beings who live within the earth: the wise one knows them all by smell.
“He knows the gods and the asuras, and he knows the daughters of the asuras; he knows the asuras' play and pleasures. Such is the power of his sense of smell.
“Whatever four-footed creatures are in the forests, lions, tigers, and elephants, buffaloes, cattle, and wild oxen: by smell he knows where they live.
“Women who are pregnant, carrying a boy or a girl in the womb, their bodies weary: by smell he knows which one is there.
“He knows who has conceived, and he knows whose pregnancy is bound to fail: 'This woman too will be free of pain and give birth to a son full of merit.'
“He knows the many intentions of people and smells the scent of their intentions; he smells the scent of the lustful, the hostile, the hypocritical, and those whose minds are at peace.

cmp.note: 梵文 puruṣa 本义是「男人」，在这里泛指「人」。白话译「人们」；古译写「男女所念」。英文用 people。
cmp.en: Sanskrit puruṣa literally means “man” but here means people in general. The plain Chinese says 人们 (rénmen, “people”); the classical translation has 男女所念 (nánnǚ suǒ niàn, “what men and women think”). The English uses “people.”

verses.en: “Treasures hidden in the earth, wealth, gold coin, gold and silver, chests and copper pots filled to the brim: the bodhisattva smells them by their scent.
“Necklaces and half-necklaces, jewels and pearls, priceless gems of many kinds: by smell he knows them all, their names, their value, and their radiance.

cmp.note: 这半句字面是「无价之名、光辉之形」，意思不太确定，大概是说连宝物的名称、价值和光泽都知道。英文、白话都作这样的推测。
cmp.en: This half-line literally reads “priceless-name, radiance-form,” and its exact sense is uncertain; it probably means he knows the gems' names, worth, and luster. The English and the plain Chinese both take it this way.

verses.en: “And up among the gods, the flowers, mandarava and manjushaka, and the flowers of the parijata tree: the wise one smells them while staying here.
“Whatever the celestial palaces are like, and whose they are, whether grand, humble, or in between, wherever there are such splendid ones, staying here he smells them by the power of smell.
“He knows the pleasure gardens too, Sudharma, the gods' assembly hall, and Vaijayanta, the finest of palaces, and he knows the sons of the gods who enjoy themselves there.
“Staying here, he smells their scent; by scent he knows the sons of the gods, what each one is doing and where, whether standing, lying down, or going somewhere.
“The daughters of the gods, adorned with many flowers, decked with garlands and ornaments, wherever they enjoy themselves and wherever they go: the bodhisattva knows by smell.

“The gods above, up to the summit of existence, Brahma and the Great Brahmas who travel in their celestial palaces: he knows them there by scent, whether they are absorbed in meditation or have come out of it.

“He knows the sons of the gods in the Abhasvara heaven, those who are passing away, those being born there, and those newly arrived. Such is the sense of smell of the bodhisattva who keeps this sutra.
“The monks in the Sugata's teaching who stay on their walking paths, devoted to practice, monks who love reciting and studying the texts: the bodhisattva knows them all.
“The disciples, sons of the Victor (the Buddha), some of whom always live at the foot of a tree: the wise one knows them all by smell: 'That monk is staying over there.'
“The bodhisattvas who are mindful and meditate, who always love reciting and studying the texts, and who explain the Dharma in assemblies: the bodhisattva knows them by smell.

“In whatever direction the Sugata, the great sage, out of kindness and care for others' good, is explaining the Dharma, honored in the midst of the community of disciples: the bodhisattva knows that protector of the world by smell.
“The beings who hear the Dharma from him, and who are filled with joy once they have heard it: staying here, the bodhisattva knows them, and the Victor's whole assembly there.
“Such is the power of his sense of smell, though his nose is not yet divine. This comes first, as the forerunner of a divine sense of smell free of the taints.”

cmp.note: anāsrava 字面是「没有漏出」，āsrava 指不断从心里漏出、把人拖回轮回的烦恼。白话「无漏（没有烦恼）」、英文 free of the taints 都是意译，原词「漏」的比喻在英文里看不出来。
cmp.en: Anāsrava literally means “without outflow”; āsrava are the defilements that keep leaking out of the mind and drag a person back into rebirth. The plain Chinese 无漏 (wúlòu, “without leaking”) keeps the image, while the English “free of the taints” gives only the sense.

verses.en: “Further, Satatasamitabhiyukta, the son or daughter of good family who keeps this discourse on the Dharma, teaches it, explains it, and writes it out will gain a faculty of taste endowed with those twelve hundred qualities of the tongue. With such a tongue, whatever flavors he tastes, whatever flavors he puts on his tongue, all of them will release a great divine flavor. He will taste in such a way that he never tastes anything unpleasant; even unpleasant flavors, once placed on his tongue, will release a divine flavor. And whatever Dharma he speaks in the midst of an assembly, the beings there will have their senses delighted by it; they will be pleased, deeply pleased, and filled with joy.

“A sweet voice will come from him, lovely and pleasing, deep, touching the heart, endearing. With it those beings will be pleased and uplifted. And those to whom he teaches the Dharma, hearing his sweet, lovely voice, will think it worth going to him: even the gods will think they should go to see him, pay homage, attend on him, and hear the Dharma. Sons of the gods and daughters of the gods will think they should go to see him, pay homage, attend on him, and hear the Dharma. Shakras, Brahmas, and the gods of Brahma's retinue will think they should go to see him, pay homage, attend on him, and hear the Dharma. Nagas and naga maidens will think they should go to see him, pay homage, attend on him, and hear the Dharma.

“Asuras and asura maidens will think they should go to see him, pay homage, attend on him, and hear the Dharma. Garudas and garuda maidens will think they should go to see him, pay homage, attend on him, and hear the Dharma. Kinnaras and kinnara maidens, mahoragas and mahoraga maidens, yakshas and yaksha maidens, pishachas (flesh-eating demons) and pishacha maidens will think they should go to see him, pay homage, attend on him, and hear the Dharma. They will honor him, revere him, respect him, make offerings to him, worship him, and bow to him. Monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen will want to see him too. Kings, princes, royal ministers, and high officials will want to see him too.

“Mighty wheel-turning kings, and wheel-turning kings possessing the seven treasures, with their princes, ministers, inner palace, and retinue, will want to see him and to honor him. So sweetly will that Dharma teacher speak the Dharma, just as it truly is, just as the Tathagata taught it. Other brahmins and householders, townsfolk and country people, will follow that Dharma teacher constantly to the end of their lives. The Tathagata's disciples will want to see him, solitary buddhas will want to see him, and the buddhas, the blessed ones, will want to see him too. And in whatever direction that son or daughter of good family lives, in that direction he will teach the Dharma face to face with the Tathagatas, and he will become a vessel for the qualities of a buddha.

cmp.note: 梵文是「他会面对着如来说法」，主语是这位说法师。鸠摩罗什译成「诸佛皆向其处说法」，变成诸佛面向他所在的方向说法，主客颠倒了。英文、白话都照梵文。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says “he will teach the Dharma facing the Tathagatas,” with the Dharma teacher as subject. Kumarajiva renders it 诸佛皆向其处说法 (zhū fó jiē xiàng qí chù shuōfǎ, “all the buddhas teach the Dharma facing the place where he is”), reversing who faces whom. The English and the plain Chinese follow the Sanskrit.

verses.en: “Such is the lovely, deep sound of the Dharma that will come from him.”
Then, at that time, the Blessed One spoke these verses:
“His sense of taste becomes excellent; he never tastes a poor flavor. As soon as things are placed on his tongue they become divine, full of divine flavor.
“He speaks in a lovely voice, sweet words, worth hearing, welcome, delightful. In the midst of the assembly he always speaks with an endearing, deep voice.
“Whoever hears the Dharma as he speaks it, with many kotis of nayutas of illustrations (both are huge numbers), feels the highest joy and makes him boundless offerings.
“Gods, nagas, asuras, and guhyakas (hidden spirits attending the god of wealth) always want to see him and listen respectfully to the Dharma. All these are his good qualities.
“If he wishes, he could make his voice heard throughout this entire world system. His voice is smooth and sweet, deep, lovely, and most endearing.
“Kings, lords of the earth, wheel-turning kings, come to him wanting to make offerings; with their sons and wives they join their palms and listen to the Dharma all the time.
“He is always honored by yakshas, by nagas and hosts of gandharvas, by pishachas male and female; he is well respected, esteemed, and worshipped.
“Brahma and Vashavartin, Maheshvara and Ishvara, sons of the gods, Shakra and other sons of the gods, and many daughters of the gods come to him.

cmp.note: vaśavartin 可以读成「受他支配的」（白话取这一读：「梵天也会听他的话」），也可以读成天神的名字「自在天」（他化自在天之主，汉传常说成魔王）。鸠摩罗什译「梵天王魔王，自在大自在」，是把它当成名字。英文跟随这一读法，把它列为一位天神；两种读法梵文都说得通。
cmp.en: Vaśavartin can be read as “under his sway” (the plain Chinese takes this reading: 梵天也会听他的话, “even Brahma will heed him”) or as the name of a god, Vashavartin, lord of the highest sense-sphere heaven, whom Chinese tradition often identifies with Mara. Kumarajiva writes 梵天王魔王，自在大自在 (“Brahma king, Mara king, Ishvara, Maheshvara”), treating it as a name. The English follows that reading and lists him as a god; the Sanskrit allows both.

verses.en: “The buddhas who care for the good of the world, with their disciples, hearing his voice, protect him and let him see their faces, and they are pleased as he speaks the Dharma.”

“Further, Satatasamitabhiyukta, the bodhisattva, great being, who keeps this discourse on the Dharma, recites it, explains it, teaches it, or writes it out will gain eight hundred good qualities of the body. His body will become clean, thoroughly pure, its skin as clear as beryl, a joy for beings to see. In that purified body of his he will see the whole great trichiliocosm. The beings who pass away and are born in the great trichiliocosm, low and high, fair and ugly, in good destinies and bad; the beings who live among the Chakravala and Great Chakravala mountains and on Meru and Sumeru, the kings of mountains; the beings who live from Avichi below up to the summit of existence: he will see them all in his own body.

cmp.note: 梵文说他会「在自己的身体里看见」这一切，身体像一面清澈的琉璃镜子。古译「于身中现」也是同一个意思。英文照直译 see in his own body，读者可能一时不解，要结合前面「琉璃般清净」的比喻来读。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says he will “see in his own body” all of this: the body is like a clear beryl mirror. Kumarajiva's 于身中现 (yú shēn zhōng xiàn, “appear within the body”) means the same. The English translates directly; it makes sense when read with the earlier image of a body as clear as beryl.

verses.en: “And whatever disciples, solitary buddhas, bodhisattvas, or Tathagatas live in this great trichiliocosm, the Dharma those Tathagatas teach, and the beings who attend on those Tathagatas: he will see the bodily forms of all those beings in his own body. Why is that? Because his body is so thoroughly pure.”
Then, at that time, the Blessed One spoke these verses:
“The body of one who keeps this noble sutra becomes thoroughly pure, as clear as if it were made of beryl, and always a joy for beings to see.
“As one sees an image on the back of a mirror, so the world is seen in his body. He sees it himself; other beings do not. Such is a purified body.

cmp.note: 这句最自然的读法是「他自己看得见，别的众生看不见」，svayaṃ 是「自己」。白话把 svayaṃbhu 当成名词「自证者」，意思还在，但多了一层原文未必有的称号。鸠摩罗什「唯独自明了，余人所不见」和英文的读法一致。「镜子背面」是古印度的金属镜：磨亮的那一面叫作背。
cmp.en: The most natural reading is “he sees it himself; other beings do not,” with svayaṃ meaning “himself.” The plain Chinese takes svayaṃbhu as a noun, 自证者 (zìzhèngzhě, “the self-realized one”), which keeps the meaning but adds a title the text may not intend. Kumarajiva's 唯独自明了，余人所不见 (“only he himself sees clearly; others do not see”) agrees with the English. “The back of a mirror”: ancient Indian mirrors were polished metal, and the polished face was called its back.

verses.en: “All the beings here in the world system, humans, gods, asuras, or guhyakas, those in the hells, among the hungry ghosts, or born as animals: their reflections appear there in his body.
“The palaces of the gods up to the summit of existence, the rocky Chakravala mountains, the Himalaya, Sumeru, and great Meru: all of these are seen in his body.
“In his body he also sees the buddhas, with their disciples and the other children of the Buddha, the bodhisattvas who live alone and those who explain the Dharma in groups.
“Such is the purity of his body, in which the whole world system is seen. He has not yet attained the divine body; this is what his natural body becomes.”

“Further, Satatasamitabhiyukta, when the Tathagata has entered final nirvana, the faculty of mind of this bodhisattva, great being, who keeps this discourse on the Dharma, teaches it, explains it, writes it out, and recites it will become pure, endowed with those twelve hundred qualities of the mind. With that purified mind, if he hears even a single verse, he will understand its many meanings. Having understood it, he will teach the Dharma on that basis for a month, for four months, even for a year. Whatever Dharma he speaks, he will remember it and not lose it. All worldly customs and dealings, all treatises and spells, he will bring into harmony with the way of the Dharma.

cmp.note: 这几个字在梵文底本里有讹误，大意是「他领会之后」。英文、白话都按这个意思译。
cmp.en: These words are corrupt in the Sanskrit edition; the sense seems to be “having understood it.” The English and the plain Chinese both translate it that way.

cmp.note: saṃsyand 字面是「使流到一起、使相合」：世俗的学问、咒语，他都能让它们和佛法相通。鸠摩罗什「皆顺正法」意思相同。英文 bring into harmony with 取其意。
cmp.en: Saṃsyand literally means “to make flow together, to make agree”: he can make worldly learning and spells flow into accord with the Dharma. Kumarajiva's 皆顺正法 (jiē shùn zhèngfǎ, “all accord with the true Dharma”) means the same. The English “bring into harmony with” gives the sense.

verses.en: “He will know the stirrings of thought and conduct of all the beings who are wandering through the six destinies (gods, humans, asuras, animals, hungry ghosts, and hell-beings) in the great trichiliocosm. He will know and examine their agitations, their conceits, and their mental proliferations. Even before he has gained the wisdom of the noble ones, his faculty of mind will be purified like this. Whatever explanation of the Dharma he reflects on and teaches, all of it he will teach truly. All of it is what the Tathagata has spoken; all of it is what was taught in the sutras of the victors of the past.”
Then, at that time, the Blessed One spoke these verses:
“His faculty of mind becomes pure, radiant, clean, and clear. With it he understands teachings of every kind, low, high, and in between.
“Hearing even a single verse, the wise one understands the many meanings in it. He always speaks what is consistent and true, for four months, even for a year.
“The beings here in this world system, living within it and outside it, gods, humans, asuras, guhyakas, nagas, and those born as animals,
“the beings living in the six destinies, whatever they are thinking: the wise one knows it all in a single moment. These are the blessings of keeping this sutra.
“And the Dharma that the Buddha, with the marks of a hundred merits, explains to the whole world: he hears its pure sound, and whatever the Buddha says, he takes it in.
“He reflects on many supreme teachings and speaks many of them all the time, and he is never confused. These are the blessings of keeping this sutra.
“He knows what connects and what does not, the distinctive marks of all things; he understands meanings and the explanations of words, and as he knows them, so he speaks.

cmp.note: saṃdhi / visaṃdhi 字面是「接合与分开」，可能指经文前后的衔接与断开，也可能指诸法之间的相合与相离。白话取前一种（「经文之间的连贯与不连贯」），英文译得较宽（what connects and what does not）。鸠摩罗什作「随义识次第」，偏向前一种。
cmp.en: Saṃdhi / visaṃdhi literally means “joining and separating”; it may refer to how passages of a text connect and break off, or to how things combine and come apart. The plain Chinese takes the first sense (经文之间的连贯与不连贯, “where the text connects and where it doesn't”); the English stays broader. Kumarajiva's 随义识次第 (“follows the meaning and recognizes the order”) leans to the first.

verses.en: “The sutra that was spoken here over long ages by the world's teachers of the past: that Dharma he speaks all the time, fearless in the midst of the assembly.
“Such becomes the faculty of mind of one who keeps this sutra and recites it. He has not yet gained unobstructed knowledge, but this comes first, as its forerunner.

cmp.note: 梵文是「无碍（无所执着）的智慧」。白话照译；鸠摩罗什写「虽未得无漏」，换成了「无漏」，和前面鼻根那一段的说法统一了。英文照梵文。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says “unobstructed (unattached) knowledge.” The plain Chinese translates this directly; Kumarajiva writes 虽未得无漏 (“though not yet free of the outflows”), swapping in the term used earlier for the nose. The English follows the Sanskrit.

verses.en: “He stands on the ground of a teacher and can tell the Dharma to all beings; he becomes skilled in kotis of explanations, as he keeps this sutra of the Sugata.”
Here ends the eighteenth chapter, called “The Blessings of a Dharma Teacher,” in the glorious Dharma discourse of the Lotus of the True Dharma.

cmp.note: 梵本说这是「第十八品」，本站按鸠摩罗什的品次排在第十九章（本站把开经单独算一章、提婆达多品并入见宝塔品）。英文照原文写 eighteenth。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit calls this the “eighteenth chapter”; the site places it as chapter 19, following Kumarajiva's order (the site counts the opening as a chapter of its own and folds the Devadatta chapter into the Stupa chapter). The English follows the original's “eighteenth.”

verses.en: Then the Blessed One spoke to the bodhisattva, great being, Mahasthamaprapta (“one who has gained great strength”): “Mahasthamaprapta, here is another way to understand this. Those who reject a discourse on the Dharma like this one, and who abuse and revile the monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen who keep sutras like this, treating them with false and harsh words, will meet an unwelcome result so bad it cannot be put into words. And those who keep a sutra like this, recite it, teach it, master it, and explain it to others in detail will meet a welcome result such as I described before. They will attain that kind of purity of eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.

cmp.note: 梵文名字是「得到大力量的」。鸠摩罗什在这一品译作「得大势」，汉传更熟悉的名字是「大势至」，也就是西方三圣里站在阿弥陀佛另一侧的那位。英文保留梵文名字并附上意思。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit name means “one who has gained great strength.” In this chapter Kumarajiva renders it 得大势 (Dé Dàshì, “gained great power”); the name better known in China is 大势至 (Dàshìzhì), the bodhisattva who stands on Amitabha's other side, opposite Avalokiteshvara. The English keeps the Sanskrit name with a gloss.

verses.en: “Long ago, Mahasthamaprapta, in the past, countless eons ago, and further back than that, more countless, vast, immeasurable, inconceivable eons (kalpas) ago, at that time there appeared in the world a Tathagata named Bhishmagarjitasvararaja (“King of the Fearsome Thundering Voice”), an arhat, a fully awakened buddha, perfect in knowledge and conduct, the Sugata, knower of the world, unsurpassed trainer of people to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a buddha, a blessed one, in the eon called Vinirbhoga (“free of possessions”), in the world system Mahasambhava (“great becoming”). And, Mahasthamaprapta, that Blessed One, the Tathagata Bhishmagarjitasvararaja, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, taught the Dharma in that world system Mahasambhava before the world with its gods, humans, and asuras.

cmp.note: 梵文名字是「可畏的雷鸣之声的王」。鸠摩罗什简化为「威音王」（威严之声的王），白话沿用。英文保留梵文名字并附上意思。劫名 vinirbhoga「离受用」、世界名 mahāsaṃbhava「大成」，古译作「离衰」、「大成」。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit name means “King of the Fearsome Thundering Voice.” Kumarajiva shortens it to 威音王 (Wēiyīn Wáng, “King of the Awesome Voice”), and the plain Chinese follows him. The English keeps the Sanskrit name with a gloss. The eon is Vinirbhoga, “free of possessions,” and the world is Mahāsaṃbhava, “great becoming”; Kumarajiva gives 离衰 (“free of decline”) and 大成 (“great completion”).

verses.en: “To the disciples he taught the Dharma connected with the four noble truths, for going beyond birth, old age, sickness, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, distress, and despair: the unfolding of dependent arising, ending in nirvana. To the bodhisattvas, great beings, he taught the Dharma connected with the six perfections, starting from unsurpassed, perfect awakening and ending in the knowledge and vision of a Tathagata. Mahasthamaprapta, the life span of that Blessed One, the Tathagata Bhishmagarjitasvararaja, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, was hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas of eons (kotis and nayutas are huge numbers), as many as the grains of sand in forty Ganges rivers. After his final nirvana, the True Dharma lasted for hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas of eons, as many as the atoms of dust in Jambudvipa (the continent we live on).

“The semblance of the True Dharma lasted for thousands of kotis of nayutas of eons, as many as the atoms of dust in the four continents. Then, Mahasthamaprapta, in that world system Mahasambhava, after the Blessed One, the Tathagata Bhishmagarjitasvararaja, had entered final nirvana and the semblance of the True Dharma had also disappeared, another Tathagata, also named Bhishmagarjitasvararaja, appeared in the world, an arhat, a fully awakened buddha, perfect in knowledge and conduct, the Sugata, knower of the world, unsurpassed trainer of people to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a buddha, a blessed one. In this succession, Mahasthamaprapta, there were in that world system Mahasambhava twenty hundred thousand kotis of nayutas of Tathagatas, arhats, fully awakened buddhas, all named Bhishmagarjitasvararaja.

cmp.note: 「正法的相似品」：佛灭后先有正法时期，接着是表面相似、实质已衰的时期。鸠摩罗什译「像法」，白话作「相似正法」，英文 semblance of the True Dharma 是直译。
cmp.en: “The likeness of the True Dharma”: after a buddha's passing comes first the period of the True Dharma, then a period when the teaching still looks the same but has declined inside. Kumarajiva renders it 像法 (xiàngfǎ, “image Dharma”), the plain Chinese 相似正法 (“resembling true Dharma”); the English “semblance of the True Dharma” is literal.

verses.en: “Now, Mahasthamaprapta, after the very first of those Tathagatas, the Tathagata named Bhishmagarjitasvararaja, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, perfect in knowledge and conduct, the Sugata, knower of the world, unsurpassed trainer of people to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a buddha, a blessed one, had entered final nirvana, when the True Dharma had disappeared and the semblance of the True Dharma was disappearing, and his teaching had been overrun by arrogant monks, there was a bodhisattva monk named Sadaparibhuta. Why, Mahasthamaprapta, was that bodhisattva, great being, called Sadaparibhuta?

cmp.note: 这个名字有两种读法：sadā-paribhūta「常被轻视的人」，或 sadā-aparibhūta「常不被轻视的」。下文说名字是那些傲慢的人给他起的，因为他逢人就说「我不轻视你们，你们是不被轻视的」，所以带一点讥讽：前一种读法正合「被众人轻贱」的处境。鸠摩罗什译「常不轻」（常常不轻视别人），把它变成了这位菩萨自己的德行，汉传读者都是这样记住他的。英文保留梵文名字不译，以免替原文选定一种读法。
cmp.en: The name can be read two ways: sadā-paribhūta, “always despised,” or sadā-aparibhūta, “never despised.” The text goes on to say the name was given him by the arrogant people he kept telling, “I do not look down on you; you are not looked down on,” so it carries some mockery, and the first reading fits his situation of being scorned by everyone. Kumarajiva translates it 常不轻 (Cháng Bùqīng, “never disparaging”), turning it into the bodhisattva's own virtue of never looking down on others, and that is how Chinese readers remember him. The English keeps the Sanskrit name untranslated so as not to choose a reading for the text.

verses.en: “Mahasthamaprapta, whenever that bodhisattva, great being, saw any monk, nun, layman, or laywoman, he would go up to them and say: 'Venerable ones, I do not look down on you. You are not to be looked down on. Why? Because all of you should practice the conduct of a bodhisattva; you will become Tathagatas, arhats, fully awakened buddhas.' In this way, Mahasthamaprapta, that bodhisattva, great being, though he had become a monk, did not teach the texts or recite them. Instead, whoever he saw, even far away, he would go up to every one of them and announce this, to monk, nun, layman, or laywoman; going up to each he would say: 'Sisters, I do not look down on you. You are not to be looked down on. Why?

cmp.note: 梵文这句很短：「我不轻视你们。」鸠摩罗什扩成「我深敬汝等，不敢轻慢……汝等皆行菩萨道，当得作佛」，后来成了著名的「二十四字」，还加上「礼拜赞叹」的动作，梵文没有礼拜。英文、白话照梵文。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit is short: “I do not look down on you.” Kumarajiva expands it to 我深敬汝等，不敢轻慢 (“I deeply respect you all and dare not slight you”), which, with “you all practice the bodhisattva way and will become buddhas,” became the famous “twenty-four characters”; he also adds that the monk bowed and praised them, which the Sanskrit doesn't mention. The English and the plain Chinese follow the Sanskrit.

verses.en: 'All of you should practice the conduct of a bodhisattva. You will become Tathagatas, arhats, fully awakened buddhas.' Mahasthamaprapta, whatever monk, nun, layman, or laywoman that bodhisattva, great being, said this to at that time, most of them became angry, hostile, and displeased, and they abused and reviled him: 'Where does this monk come from, who shows us this attitude of not looking down on us when nobody asked him? He makes himself contemptible by predicting for us unsurpassed, perfect awakening, which is unreal and which we don't want.' And so, Mahasthamaprapta, many years passed for that bodhisattva, great being, while he was abused and reviled in this way. Yet he never got angry with anyone, and no hostile thought arose in him.

“When he said this, some would throw clods of earth or sticks at him. From a distance he would still call out loudly to them, 'I do not look down on you!' Because those arrogant monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen heard this from him constantly, they gave him the name Sadaparibhuta.

cmp.note: 梵文只说他「从远处」高声喊话；白话译成「远远地避开，仍然高声说道」，是照鸠摩罗什「避走远住，犹高声唱言」补出了「避开」的动作。英文照梵文。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit just says he called out loudly “from a distance”; the plain Chinese's 远远地避开 (“moved well out of the way”) supplies the act of retreating from Kumarajiva's 避走远住 (“ran off and stood far away”). The English follows the Sanskrit.

verses.en: “Mahasthamaprapta, when the time of death drew near for the bodhisattva, great being, Sadaparibhuta, when the moment of his dying came, he heard this discourse on the Dharma, the Lotus of the True Dharma. The Blessed One, the Tathagata Bhishmagarjitasvararaja, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, had spoken this discourse in verses numbering twenty times twenty hundred thousand kotis of nayutas. When the moment of his dying came, the bodhisattva, great being, Sadaparibhuta heard this discourse as a voice from the sky. Hearing the voice from the sky, spoken by someone or other, he took up this discourse on the Dharma, and he gained this kind of purity of eye, purity of ear, of nose, of tongue, of body, and of mind.

“As soon as he had gained these purities, he sustained his own life force for another twenty hundred thousand kotis of nayutas of years and explained this discourse on the Dharma, the Lotus of the True Dharma. And those arrogant beings, the monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen who had earlier been told 'I do not look down on you' and who had given him the name Sadaparibhuta, seeing the strength of his great supernatural power, the strength of his resolve and eloquence, and the strength of his wisdom, all became his followers in order to hear the Dharma. He led all of them, and many other hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas of living beings, to take up unsurpassed, perfect awakening.

“Mahasthamaprapta, after passing away from there, that bodhisattva, great being, served twenty hundred kotis of Tathagatas, arhats, fully awakened buddhas, all bearing the same name, Chandrasvararaja (“King of the Moon's Voice”), and under all of them he explained this discourse on the Dharma. In due course, by that same earlier root of goodness, he went on to serve twenty hundred thousand kotis of nayutas of Tathagatas, arhats, fully awakened buddhas, all bearing the same name, Dundubhisvararaja (“King of the Drum's Voice”). Under all of them he honored this same discourse on the Dharma, the Lotus of the True Dharma, and explained it to the four assemblies (monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen).

“By that same earlier root of goodness he went on to serve twenty hundred thousand kotis of Tathagatas, arhats, fully awakened buddhas, all bearing the same name, Meghasvararaja (“King of the Cloud's Voice”). Under all of them he honored this same discourse on the Dharma, the Lotus of the True Dharma, and explained it to the four assemblies. And under all of them he had that kind of purity of eye, and purity of ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.

“Mahasthamaprapta, after the bodhisattva, great being, Sadaparibhuta had honored, revered, respected, made offerings to, worshipped, and bowed to so many hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas of Tathagatas, and had honored, revered, respected, made offerings to, worshipped, and bowed to many other hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas of buddhas, and under all of them had honored this same discourse on the Dharma, the Lotus of the True Dharma, then, by that same earlier root of goodness, now ripened, he awoke to unsurpassed, perfect awakening.

“Now, Mahasthamaprapta, you might have some doubt, uncertainty, or hesitation: that the bodhisattva, great being, named Sadaparibhuta at that time, who was regarded by the four assemblies in the teaching of the Blessed One, the Tathagata Bhishmagarjitasvararaja, as Sadaparibhuta, and who served so many Tathagatas, arhats, fully awakened buddhas, was someone else. But, Mahasthamaprapta, you should not see it that way. Why? I myself, Mahasthamaprapta, was the bodhisattva, great being, named Sadaparibhuta at that time. If I had not taken up and kept this discourse on the Dharma in the past, Mahasthamaprapta, I would not have awakened so quickly to unsurpassed, perfect awakening.

“Because, Mahasthamaprapta, I kept, recited, and taught this discourse on the Dharma in the presence of the Tathagatas, arhats, fully awakened buddhas of the past, I awoke so quickly to unsurpassed, perfect awakening. And, Mahasthamaprapta, those hundreds of monks, hundreds of nuns, hundreds of laymen and laywomen in that Blessed One's teaching to whom the bodhisattva, great being, Sadaparibhuta announced this discourse: 'I do not look down on you. All of you should practice the conduct of a bodhisattva. You will become Tathagatas, arhats, fully awakened buddhas,'

“those who had felt hostility toward that bodhisattva did not once see a Tathagata for twenty hundred thousand kotis of nayutas of eons, nor did they hear the word Dharma or the word Sangha (the community). And for ten thousand eons they suffered terrible pain in the great Avichi hell. Then all of them were freed from that obstruction of their deeds, and that same bodhisattva, great being, ripened them toward unsurpassed, perfect awakening. Now, Mahasthamaprapta, you might have some doubt, uncertainty, or hesitation: who were those beings at that time who mocked and jeered at that bodhisattva, great being?

“Mahasthamaprapta, they are right here in this assembly: the five hundred bodhisattvas led by Bhadrapala, the five hundred nuns led by Simhachandra, and the five hundred laywomen led by Sugatachetana, all of whom have now been made irreversible on the way to unsurpassed, perfect awakening. So, Mahasthamaprapta, keeping, reciting, and teaching this discourse on the Dharma, so rich in meaning, leads bodhisattvas, great beings, to unsurpassed, perfect awakening. Therefore, Mahasthamaprapta, after the Tathagata has entered final nirvana, bodhisattvas, great beings, should keep, recite, teach, and explain this discourse on the Dharma again and again.”

cmp.note: 梵文是「五百位女居士」。鸠摩罗什作「思佛等五百优婆塞」，优婆塞是男居士，与梵文不同。英文照梵文。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says “five hundred laywomen.” Kumarajiva has 思佛等五百优婆塞 (“five hundred laymen led by Sifo”), and 优婆塞 (yōupósài) means laymen, not laywomen. The English follows the Sanskrit.

verses.en: Then, at that time, the Blessed One spoke these verses:
“I remember a past age, when the Victor Bhishmasvararaja lived, mighty, honored by humans and gods, a guide of humans, gods, yakshas, and rakshasas.
“After that Victor had entered final nirvana, in the last period, when the True Dharma was falling into turmoil, there was a monk, a bodhisattva, who was called by the name Sadaparibhuta.
“He would go up to other monks, and nuns as well, who held to views of grasping, and say: 'I never look down on you, for you are practicing the conduct that leads to the highest awakening.'

cmp.note: upalambha 是「抓取、认定有实在之物可得」，这里指执着于「有所得」的见解的出家人。鸠摩罗什「计著于法」、白话「执着于有所得见解」都译出了意思；英文 views of grasping 较简略。
cmp.en: Upalambha means “grasping, taking things as really there to be gotten”; here it describes monastics attached to views that something is truly gained or held. Kumarajiva's 计著于法 (jì zhuó yú fǎ, “fixated on dharmas”) and the plain Chinese 执着于有所得见解 (“attached to views of something to be gained”) both bring this out; the English “views of grasping” is briefer.

verses.en: “He kept announcing this all the time and bore their abuse and insults. When the time of his death drew near, he heard this sutra.
“The wise one did not die then; he sustained himself for a very long life, and he explained this sutra in that leader's teaching.
“And all those many who were attached to grasping, he ripened them for awakening. After passing away from there, that bodhisattva served thousands of kotis of buddhas.
“Step by step, through the merit he had made, always explaining this sutra, that son of the Victor reached awakening. I myself was he; I, Shakyamuni, was he then.
“And the monks who were attached to grasping at that time, the nuns, the laymen, and the laywomen who were there then, to whom the wise one announced awakening:
“they too have seen many kotis of buddhas; and these five hundred here, not one missing, are they, the monks and nuns and the laywomen too, here in front of me.

cmp.note: 偈颂里列的是比丘、比丘尼和女居士，和前面散文（五百菩萨、五百比丘尼、五百女居士）不完全对应。白话写成「比丘（尼）们」来兼顾两边；英文照偈颂字面译。
cmp.en: The verse lists monks, nuns, and laywomen, which doesn't quite match the prose above (five hundred bodhisattvas, five hundred nuns, five hundred laywomen). The plain Chinese writes 比丘（尼）们 (“monks (nuns)”) to cover both; the English follows the verse literally.

verses.en: “I have let them all hear the highest Dharma, and I have ripened them all. And after I have entered nirvana, all these wise ones will keep this supreme sutra.
“In many inconceivable kotis of eons, a Dharma like this is never heard. There are hundreds of kotis of buddhas, and even they do not explain this sutra.
“Therefore, having heard a Dharma like this, proclaimed by the Self-Existent One himself, honor it again and again, and explain this sutra after I have entered nirvana here.”

cmp.note: svayaṃbhū「自生者、自己成就的」，是佛的称号：不靠老师而自己觉悟的人。白话「自生者（佛）」照译；鸠摩罗什这四句改写得较多，没有这个称号，还加了「勿生疑惑」「世世值佛，疾成佛道」。
cmp.en: Svayaṃbhū, “self-existent, self-made,” is an epithet of a buddha: one who awakened by himself without a teacher. The plain Chinese 自生者（佛） (“the self-existent one (the Buddha)”) translates it; Kumarajiva rewrites these lines more freely, drops the epithet, and adds 勿生疑惑 (“do not doubt”) and 世世值佛，疾成佛道 (“meet buddhas life after life and swiftly attain buddhahood”).

verses.en: Here ends the nineteenth chapter, called “Sadaparibhuta,” in the glorious Dharma discourse of the Lotus of the True Dharma.

chapters.title: Chapter 21 · The Tathagata's Display of Supernatural Power

verses.en: Then all those hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas (both are huge numbers) of bodhisattvas who had come up out of the cracks in the earth, as many as the specks of dust in a thousand world systems ground to powder, joined their palms toward the Blessed One and said to him: “Blessed One, after the Tathagata has passed into final nirvana, we will proclaim this Dharma discourse in every buddha-land of the Blessed One, wherever the Blessed One will pass into final nirvana. We ourselves long for this great Dharma discourse, Blessed One: to hold it in memory, to recite it, to teach it, to make it known, and to write it down.”

cmp.note: 梵文只说「世尊的一切佛国土，世尊将在那里入灭的每一处」。鸠摩罗什译成「世尊分身所在国土」，加进了第十一品「分身诸佛」的概念；英文、白话都照梵文，没有「分身」。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says only “in all the Blessed One's buddha-lands, wherever the Blessed One will pass into final nirvana.” Kumarajiva writes 世尊分身所在国土 (Shìzūn fēnshēn suǒzài guótǔ, “the lands where the Blessed One's emanation bodies are”), bringing in the emanation buddhas of the stupa chapter. The English and the plain Chinese follow the Sanskrit and have no emanations here.

verses.en: Then many hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas of bodhisattvas led by Manjushri (the bodhisattva of wisdom), who live in this Saha world (our world of endurance), along with monks, nuns, laymen and laywomen, gods, nagas, yakshas, gandharvas, asuras, garudas, kinnaras, mahoragas, humans and non-humans, and many bodhisattvas, great beings, as many as the grains of sand in the Ganges, said to the Blessed One: “Blessed One, after the Tathagata has passed into final nirvana, we too will proclaim this Dharma discourse, in bodies no one can see. Blessed One, standing in the sky we will make our voices heard, and in beings who have not yet planted roots of goodness we will plant them.”

cmp.note: 「用看不见的身体」：这些本地的菩萨说要隐身在空中说法。这一整段鸠摩罗什本没有，罗什本里文殊等旧住菩萨只出现在下一段，作为看神通的听众。
cmp.en: “With an unseen body”: these bodhisattvas of our own world promise to teach invisibly from the sky. Kumarajiva's version has no such passage; in his text Manjushri and the other resident bodhisattvas appear only in the next paragraph, as the audience watching the miracle.

verses.en: Then at that moment the Blessed One spoke to the foremost of those bodhisattvas, great beings, who had appeared first, those leaders of hosts, leaders of great hosts, teachers of hosts: the bodhisattva, great being, great leader and teacher named Vishishtacharitra (“Excellent Conduct”). “Well done, well done, Vishishtacharitra! This is just what you all should do for the sake of this Dharma discourse. You have been brought to maturity by the Tathagata.”

cmp.note: 名字意思是「殊胜的行持」。鸠摩罗什译「上行」，英文音写并在括号里给出意思。这一段世尊对上行的称赞，罗什本没有译。
cmp.en: The name means “excellent conduct.” Kumarajiva renders it 上行 (Shàngxíng, “superior practice”); the English transliterates it and gives the meaning in parentheses. Kumarajiva does not translate this praise of Vishishtacharitra.

verses.en: Then the Blessed One, the Tathagata Shakyamuni, and the Blessed One, the Tathagata Prabhutaratna (“Many Jewels”), the arhat, the fully awakened buddha who had passed into final nirvana and sat inside the stupa, both seated on lion thrones, smiled, and from their open mouths they put out their tongues. Those two tongues reached all the way to the Brahma world. From those two tongues came many hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas of rays of light, and from each one of those rays came many hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas of bodhisattvas, gold in color, their bodies bearing the thirty-two marks of a great man (the special features of a buddha or a universal king), seated on lion thrones in the heart of lotus flowers. Those bodhisattvas spread out through hundreds of thousands of world systems in the main and in-between directions, and standing in the sky in every direction they taught the Dharma.

cmp.note: 梵文是两位佛一起微笑、伸舌、舌中放光、光中出菩萨。鸠摩罗什本只写释迦牟尼「出广长舌上至梵世，一切毛孔放于无量无数色光」：光从毛孔放出，没有多宝佛伸舌，也没有光中化出的菩萨。伸出长舌在印度是「所说绝无虚假」的证明。
cmp.en: In the Sanskrit both buddhas smile and put out their tongues, light streams from the tongues, and bodhisattvas appear in the light. Kumarajiva has only Shakyamuni putting out his “broad, long tongue” up to the Brahma world, and the light comes from 一切毛孔 (yíqiè máokǒng, “all his pores”): no tongue from Prabhutaratna and no bodhisattvas in the rays. In India a tongue long enough to cover the face was a sign that one's words are never false.

verses.en: Just as the Blessed One, the Tathagata Shakyamuni, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, and the Tathagata Prabhutaratna, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, worked this miracle of supernatural power with their tongues, so did all those Tathagatas, arhats, fully awakened buddhas who had come from hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas of other world systems and sat each on his own lion throne at the foot of a jewel tree: they too worked this miracle with their tongues.

The Blessed One, the Tathagata Shakyamuni, and all those Tathagatas kept up this display of supernatural power for a full hundred thousand years. Then, when the hundred thousand years had passed, those Tathagatas drew their tongues back in, and in one and the same instant, all at once, they all cleared their throats with a great lion's cough and made a single sound of snapping their fingers. With that great cough and that great finger-snap, all the hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas of buddha-lands in the ten directions shook: they quaked, quaked hard, quaked all over; they swayed, swayed hard, swayed all over; they trembled, trembled hard, trembled all over.

cmp.note: 「清嗓子的咳嗽」和「弹指」。英文 cough、finger-snap 和白话「咳嗽」「弹指」都照字面；鸠摩罗什用「謦欬」，是古汉语里开口说话前轻咳一声的意思，更贴近「要宣布了」的含义。地动梵文列了九种说法，罗什简称「六种震动」。
cmp.en: Utkāsana is a throat-clearing cough and acchaṭā a snap of the fingers. The English “cough” and “finger-snap” and the plain Chinese 咳嗽 (késou, “cough”) and 弹指 (tánzhǐ, “snap the fingers”) are literal; Kumarajiva's 謦欬 (qǐngkài) is the polite little cough before speaking, which better catches the sense of “an announcement is coming.” The Sanskrit lists nine words for the shaking; Kumarajiva sums them up as 六种震动 (liù zhǒng zhèndòng, “the six kinds of quaking”).

verses.en: And all the beings in all those buddha-lands, gods, nagas, yakshas, gandharvas, asuras, garudas, kinnaras, mahoragas, humans and non-humans, through the power of the Buddha saw this Saha world from where they were. They saw those hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas of Tathagatas, each seated on a lion throne at the foot of a jewel tree; they saw the Blessed One, the Tathagata Shakyamuni, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, and the Blessed One, the Tathagata Prabhutaratna, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, who had passed into final nirvana, seated on the lion throne in the middle of the great jewel stupa together with the Blessed One, the Tathagata Shakyamuni; and they saw the three assemblies. When they saw this they were struck with wonder, amazement and great joy.

And they heard a voice from the sky saying: “Friends, beyond immeasurable, countless hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas of world systems there is a world system called Saha. In it is the Tathagata named Shakyamuni, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha. Right now he is proclaiming to the bodhisattvas, great beings, the Dharma discourse called the Lotus of the True Dharma, a great and far-reaching sutra, an instruction for bodhisattvas, held dear by all buddhas. Rejoice in it with all your heart, and pay homage to the Blessed One, the Tathagata Shakyamuni, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, and to the Blessed One, the Tathagata Prabhutaratna, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha.”

cmp.note: 「诸位贤友」，是天神之间互相称呼的客气话。鸠摩罗什写成「诸天于虚空中高声唱言」，直接说出是谁在喊；梵文只说「空中有声音」。罗什本也只让众生礼敬释迦牟尼，没提多宝佛。
cmp.en: Mārṣāḥ, “friends, good sirs,” is how gods politely address one another. Kumarajiva says 诸天于虚空中高声唱言 (zhū tiān yú xūkōng zhōng gāoshēng chàng yán, “the gods called out loudly in the sky”), naming who shouts; the Sanskrit only says a voice came from the sky. Kumarajiva also has the beings honor only Shakyamuni, leaving out Prabhutaratna.

verses.en: When all those beings heard such a voice from the sky, they joined their palms right where they were and said, “Homage to the Blessed One, the Tathagata Shakyamuni, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha!” And toward this Saha world they threw all kinds of flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, scented powders, robes, parasols, flags, banners and victory pennants; they threw all kinds of ornaments and jewelry too, necklaces, half-necklaces and precious gems, as an offering to the Blessed One Shakyamuni and to the Tathagata Prabhutaratna, and to this Dharma discourse, the Lotus of the True Dharma. And those flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, flags, banners and pennants, and those necklaces, half-necklaces and gems, once thrown, came to this Saha world.

cmp.note: 「礼敬世尊释迦牟尼」。鸠摩罗什译成「南无释迦牟尼佛」并重复两次；「南无」就是 namo 的音译。英文照意思译成 Homage to。
cmp.en: “Homage to the Blessed One Shakyamuni.” Kumarajiva writes 南无释迦牟尼佛 (nāmó Shìjiāmóuní fó) and repeats it twice; 南无 (nāmó) is simply a transliteration of namo. The English translates the meaning as “Homage to.”

verses.en: And with those heaps of flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, flags, banners and pennants, with the necklaces, half-necklaces and gems, a vast canopy of flowers took shape in the open sky above all the Tathagatas seated in this Saha world, which had now become one with those hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas of other world systems.

cmp.note: 「合为一体」：娑婆世界与其他无数世界连成一片。鸠摩罗什把这一点放在句末，说得更明白：「十方世界通达无碍，如一佛土」。
cmp.en: Ekībhūtaiḥ, “become one”: the Saha world merges with countless other worlds. Kumarajiva puts this at the end and says it more plainly: 十方世界通达无碍，如一佛土 (“the worlds of the ten directions opened into one another without obstruction, like a single buddha-land”).

verses.en: Then the Blessed One spoke to the bodhisattvas, great beings, led by Vishishtacharitra: “Sons of good family, the power of the Tathagatas, the arhats, the fully awakened buddhas, is beyond imagining. Sons of good family, even if I went on for many hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas of eons (kalpas), entrusting this Dharma discourse to you and describing its many benefits from the angle of one teaching after another, I would never reach the end of its virtues. To put it briefly, sons of good family: all the mastery of the buddhas, all the secrets of the buddhas, all the deepest ground of the buddhas, I have taught in this Dharma discourse. So, sons of good family, after the Tathagata has passed into final nirvana, you should respectfully hold this Dharma discourse in memory, teach it, write it down, recite it, make it known, cultivate it and honor it.

cmp.note: vṛṣabhitā 字面是「公牛般的地位」，指佛像牛群领头的公牛那样的威德、主宰。英文 mastery、白话「威德」都是意译。鸠摩罗什把这一句扩成四句：「如来一切所有之法、一切自在神力、一切秘要之藏、一切甚深之事」，是汉地最常被引的一段。
cmp.en: Vṛṣabhitā literally means “bull-ness,” the standing of the lead bull of the herd, i.e. the buddhas' commanding power. The English “mastery” and the plain Chinese 威德 (wēidé, “majestic power”) both translate the sense. Kumarajiva expands the sentence into four phrases, 如来一切所有之法…一切自在神力…一切秘要之藏…一切甚深之事 (“all the Tathagata's teachings, all his free supernatural powers, all his secret treasuries, all his profound matters”), one of the most quoted passages in Chinese Buddhism.

verses.en: “And sons of good family, in any spot on earth where this Dharma discourse is recited, made known, taught, written down, thought about, spoken of or chanted, or where it is kept as a book, whether in a monastery park, a dwelling for monks, a house, a forest, a city, at the foot of a tree, in a palace, a shelter or a cave, in that spot a shrine (chaitya) should be built in honor of the Tathagata. Why? Because that spot should be known as the seat of awakening of all the Tathagatas. In that spot, you should know, all the Tathagatas, arhats, fully awakened buddhas, have awakened to unsurpassed, perfect awakening; in that spot all the Tathagatas have turned the wheel of the Dharma; and in that spot, you should know, all the Tathagatas have passed into final nirvana.”

cmp.note: caitya 是供奉用的纪念建筑，英文用 shrine 并附原词，白话「塔庙」，鸠摩罗什「起塔」。bodhimaṇḍa 是佛成道的地方（菩提树下那块地），罗什译「道场」；后来中文「道场」泛指修行场所，原意窄得多。
cmp.en: A caitya is a memorial structure for worship; the English uses “shrine” with the Sanskrit word, the plain Chinese 塔庙 (tǎmiào, “stupa-temple”), Kumarajiva 起塔 (qǐ tǎ, “raise a stupa”). Bodhimaṇḍa is the exact spot where a buddha awakens (the ground under the bodhi tree); Kumarajiva's 道场 (dàochǎng) later came to mean any place of practice, which is much broader than the original.

verses.en: Then at that moment the Blessed One spoke these verses:

The nature of the buddhas, who work for the good of the world and stand firm in higher knowledge, is beyond imagining. Those with boundless eyes display their supernatural powers here to bring joy to all embodied beings.
Their tongues reaching the Brahma world, sending out thousands of rays, they displayed wondrous powers here for the sake of all who have set out for the highest awakening.
The buddhas clear their throats and make the single sound of a finger-snap, and so they make it known to the whole world, to this world system in the ten directions.

These and other miracles the kind ones, who care for others' good, display as a sign of the virtues: so that people, delighted, will hold this sutra after the Well-Gone One (Sugata, a title of the Buddha) has passed into nirvana.

cmp.note: 字面是「他们怎样才会欢喜地受持此经」，意思是佛显神通，是为了让人在佛灭后欢喜受持。白话译成感叹句「这些人在那时会多么欢喜地受持这部经啊」，语气不同，意思相近。
cmp.en: Literally “how might they, delighted, hold the sutra”: the buddhas show miracles so that people will gladly hold it after the Buddha's nirvana. The plain Chinese turns it into an exclamation, 会多么欢喜地受持这部经啊 (“how joyfully they will hold this sutra!”), a different tone with a similar sense.

verses.en: Even if for many thousands of kotis of eons I spoke the praises of the Well-Gone One's children who will hold this supreme sutra after the Guide of the World has passed into nirvana,
there would be no end to their virtues, just as space has no end in any direction. Beyond imagining are the virtues of those who always hold this lovely sutra.
I have been seen by him, and all these leaders, and this Guide of the World who has passed into nirvana, and all these many bodhisattvas, and the four assemblies: all have been seen by him.

cmp.note: 「被他看见了」：这句没有说「他」是谁，要接上下文才知道是受持此经的人。白话直接补出「受持此经的人」；英文照梵文写 him，读者需要往下读。鸠摩罗什写「能持是经者，则为已见我」，也补出了主语。
cmp.en: “Seen by him”: the line never says who “he” is; context shows it is the person who holds this sutra. The plain Chinese supplies 受持此经的人 (“the one who holds this sutra”); the English keeps the Sanskrit's bare “him.” Kumarajiva also supplies the subject: 能持是经者，则为已见我 (“whoever can hold this sutra has thereby seen me”).

verses.en: Today here he has pleased me, and pleased all these leaders, and this Victor-Lord who has passed into nirvana, and the others in the ten directions as well.
And the buddhas of the future and the past, and those who live in the ten directions: all of them will have been seen and well honored by whoever holds this sutra.
The secret knowledge of the highest of persons, which they pondered on the seat of awakening, he too will soon come to understand, whoever holds this sutra of the true Dharma.
His eloquence too will be endless, like the wind that catches on nothing anywhere. He will know the Dharma, its meaning and its explanation, whoever holds this excellent sutra.

cmp.note: 法、义、词三项，是佛教讲「四无碍解」（法、义、词、辩）里的前三项，最后的「辩」就是句首的 pratibhāna（辩才）。英文、白话都照字面译；鸠摩罗什「诸法之义，名字及言辞，乐说无穷尽」也是这四项。
cmp.en: Dharma, meaning and explanation are the first three of the four “unobstructed knowledges” (of dharma, meaning, language and eloquence); the fourth, pratibhāna, “eloquence,” opens the verse. The English and the plain Chinese translate literally; Kumarajiva's 诸法之义，名字及言辞，乐说无穷尽 (“the meaning of the dharmas, names and words, endless joy in speaking”) covers the same four.

verses.en: He will always understand how the sutras connect, and the intent behind what the guides have said. Even after the Guide has passed into nirvana, he will know the true meaning of the sutras.

cmp.note: saṃdhāya-bhāṣita 是佛教术语「密意说」：话里有更深的用意，不能只看字面。白话「说话时的深层用意」译得准；英文 the intent behind what … said 也是这个意思。鸠摩罗什译成「因缘及次第」，偏向经文的来由和次序。
cmp.en: Saṃdhāya-bhāṣita is a technical term for “intentional speech,” words with a deeper purpose that should not be read only at face value. The plain Chinese 说话时的深层用意 (“the deeper intention when speaking”) is accurate, as is the English “the intent behind what … said.” Kumarajiva's 因缘及次第 (yīnyuán jí cìdì, “causes and sequence”) leans toward the background and order of the sutras.

verses.en: He shines like the moon, like the sun; he becomes a giver of light and radiance. Wandering over the earth here and there, he rouses many bodhisattvas.
So the wise bodhisattvas who have heard of these benefits should hold this sutra after I have passed into nirvana. They will have no doubt about awakening.
Here ends the twentieth chapter, called “The Tathagata's Display of Supernatural Power,” in the glorious Dharma discourse of the Lotus of the True Dharma.

cmp.note: 梵本自己的编号是「第二十品」。本站把开经算作一章、把提婆达多品并入见宝塔品，所以这里是第 21 章；鸠摩罗什本是第二十一品。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit manuscript numbers this the twentieth chapter. This site counts the opening as a chapter and merges the Devadatta chapter into the stupa chapter, so here it is Chapter 21; in Kumarajiva's version it is the twenty-first.

verses.en: Then the bodhisattva, great being Bhaishajyaraja (the Medicine King) rose from his seat, put his upper robe over one shoulder, set his right knee on the ground, bowed toward the Blessed One with joined palms, and said to the Blessed One: “Blessed One, how much merit would a son of good family or a daughter of good family produce by holding this Dharma discourse, the Lotus of the True Dharma, whether by learning it by heart or by having it as a book?” When he had said this, the Blessed One said to the bodhisattva, great being Bhaishajyaraja: “Bhaishajyaraja, suppose some son or daughter of good family were to respect, revere, honor and make offerings to hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas (both huge numbers) of Tathagatas, as many as the grains of sand in eighty Ganges rivers. What do you think, Bhaishajyaraja: how much merit would that son or daughter of good family produce from that?” The bodhisattva, great being Bhaishajyaraja said: “A great deal, Blessed One; a great deal, Well-Gone One.” The Blessed One said: “I tell you, Bhaishajyaraja, I make it known to you: if some son or daughter of good family were to hold from this Dharma discourse, the Lotus of the True Dharma, even a single verse of four lines, recite it, master it and put it into practice, then, Bhaishajyaraja, that son or daughter of good family would produce far more merit from that.”

cmp.note: 「放在身上或放在书里」：kāyagata 字面是「进入身体」，指背下来、记在心里；pustakagata 是写成书本。英文 learning it by heart / having it as a book、白话「记在心里，或者抄写成经卷」都译出了。鸠摩罗什改成「读诵通利，若书写经卷」。
cmp.en: “Gone into the body or gone into a book”: kāyagata literally means “gone into the body,” i.e. memorized; pustakagata means written as a book. The English “learning it by heart … having it as a book” and the plain Chinese 记在心里，或者抄写成经卷 (“keep it in the heart, or copy it into a scroll”) both convey this. Kumarajiva says 读诵通利，若书写经卷 (“reciting it fluently, or copying it as a scroll”).

verses.en: Then at that moment the bodhisattva, great being Bhaishajyaraja said to the Blessed One: “Blessed One, to the sons and daughters of good family who have this Dharma discourse, the Lotus of the True Dharma, by heart or as a book, we will give the words of a dharani spell (dharani, a string of sacred syllables that holds and protects) for their protection, shelter and safekeeping. It goes like this:”

cmp.note: dhāraṇī 来自 dhṛ「持」，本义是「能持住的东西」：既指过耳不忘的记忆力，也指护身的咒语。这一品取后一个意思。中文音译「陀罗尼」，意译「总持」；英文没有对等的词，保留 dharani 并在括号里解释。
cmp.en: Dhāraṇī comes from dhṛ, “to hold”: it means “that which holds,” both a memory that retains everything heard and a protective spell. This chapter uses the second sense. Chinese transliterates it 陀罗尼 (tuóluóní) or translates it 总持 (zǒngchí, “holding all”); English has no equivalent word, so the English keeps “dharani” with a gloss.

verses.en: (The dharani follows. Like every dharani it is recited in its original sounds, not translated.) anye manye mane mamane citte carite same samitā viśānte mukte muktatame same aviṣame samasame jaye kṣaye akṣaye akṣiṇe śānte samite dhāraṇi ālokabhāṣe pratyavekṣaṇi nidhiru abhyantaraniviṣṭe abhyantarapāriśuddhimutkule araḍe paraḍe sukāṅkṣi asamasame buddhavilokite dharmaparīkṣite saṃghanirghoṣaṇi nirghoṇi bhayābhayaviśodhani mantre mantrākṣayate rute rutakauśalye akṣaye akṣayavanatāye vakkule valoḍra amanyanatāye svāhā

cmp.note: 陀罗尼照例只念原音，不翻译，所以英文照录梵文音节。其中一部分是看得懂的梵文词的呼格形式，如 citte「心」、mukte「解脱」、śānte「寂静」、buddhavilokite「佛所观照」、saṃghanirghoṣaṇi「僧团的声音」，但连起来不成句子。鸠摩罗什用汉字逐音节音写，并给每句编号（安尔、曼尔、摩祢……），读音还按当时的汉语注了反切；他的底本音节和这个梵本也不全相同。结尾的 svāhā 是咒语的收尾词，鸠摩罗什译本里这里没有对应。
cmp.en: Dharanis are recited in their original sounds and not translated, so the English reproduces the Sanskrit syllables. Some are recognizable Sanskrit words in vocative form, such as citte (“mind”), mukte (“freed”), śānte (“calm”), buddhavilokite (“seen by the Buddha”), saṃghanirghoṣaṇi (“voice of the Sangha”), but together they do not form sentences. Kumarajiva writes the syllables out in Chinese characters, numbering each phrase (安尔 ānʼěr, 曼尔 mànʼěr, 摩祢 mómí …) and adding pronunciation hints for the Chinese of his day; his source text's syllables are not quite the same as this manuscript's. The closing svāhā is the customary ending word of a spell.

verses.en: “Blessed One, these words of the spell, the dharani, have been spoken by buddhas, blessed ones, as many as the grains of sand in sixty-two Ganges rivers. Anyone who would attack such Dharma teachers, such holders of the sutra, would be doing harm to all those buddhas, the blessed ones.”

Then the Blessed One gave his approval to the bodhisattva, great being Bhaishajyaraja: “Well done, well done, Bhaishajyaraja! You have done something good for beings. Out of compassion for beings you have spoken the words of a dharani, and you have given them protection, shelter and safekeeping.”

Then the bodhisattva, great being Pradanashura (“Hero of Giving”) said to the Blessed One: “Blessed One, I too will give the words of a dharani for the sake of such Dharma teachers, so that no one who watches for a weak spot in them, who hunts for a weak spot, will find one: no yaksha (a nature spirit, often hostile), no rakshasa (a man-eating demon), no putana, no kritya, no kumbhanda, no preta (hungry ghost), watching for a weak spot, hunting for a weak spot, will find one.”

cmp.note: 这几类都是印度民间信仰里的鬼魅：pūtana 是使人（尤其小儿）生病的恶鬼，kṛtya 是巫术召来的害人精，kumbhāṇḍa 字面是「瓮形睾丸」，是一类丑怪的鬼。英文、白话和鸠摩罗什都只音译（富单那、吉遮、鸠槃荼），没有解释。
cmp.en: These are all spirits of Indian folk belief: a pūtana is a demon that brings sickness, especially to children; a kṛtya is a harmful being conjured by witchcraft; a kumbhāṇḍa (literally “pot-testicled”) is a grotesque kind of goblin. The English, the plain Chinese and Kumarajiva all simply transliterate them, as 富单那 (fùdānnà), 吉遮 (jízhē) and 鸠槃荼 (jiūpántú), without explanation.

verses.en: Then at that moment the bodhisattva, great being Pradanashura spoke these words of the dharani spell. It goes like this:
jvale mahājvale ukke tukke mukke aḍe aḍāvati nṛtye nṛtyāvati iṭṭini viṭṭini ciṭṭini nṛtyani nṛtyāvati svāhā

cmp.note: 照原音录出，不译。看得懂的只有 jvale「燃烧的（女神）」、mahājvale「大燃烧的」、nṛtye「舞蹈的」几个，其余是押韵的音节。鸠摩罗什音写为「痤隷、摩诃痤隷、郁枳、目枳……」。
cmp.en: Given in its original sounds, untranslated. The only recognizable words are jvale (“blazing one,” feminine), mahājvale (“greatly blazing one”) and nṛtye (“dancing one”); the rest are rhyming syllables. Kumarajiva writes them as 痤隷 (cuólì), 摩诃痤隷 (móhē cuólì), 郁枳 (yùzhǐ), 目枳 (mùzhǐ) and so on.

verses.en: “Blessed One, these words of the dharani have been spoken, and approved, by Tathagatas, arhats, fully awakened buddhas as many as the grains of sand in the Ganges. Anyone who would attack such Dharma teachers would be doing harm to all those Tathagatas.”

Then the great king Vaishravana (guardian king of the north, one of the four world-protecting kings) said to the Blessed One: “Blessed One, I too will speak the words of a dharani, for the benefit and happiness of those Dharma teachers, out of compassion, for their protection, shelter and safekeeping. It goes like this:”
aṭṭe taṭṭe naṭṭe vanaṭṭe anaḍe nāḍi kunaḍi svāhā

cmp.note: 照原音录出，不译；这几句基本都是没有字面意义的押韵音节。鸠摩罗什音写为「阿梨、那梨、㝹那梨……」。
cmp.en: Given in its original sounds, untranslated; these are almost entirely rhyming syllables with no word meaning. Kumarajiva writes them as 阿梨 (ālí), 那梨 (nàlí), 㝹那梨 (nòunàlí) and so on.

verses.en: “Blessed One, with these words of the dharani I protect those people who teach the Dharma. And for a hundred yojanas (a yojana is a day's march, roughly ten miles) around, I will protect those sons and daughters of good family who hold sutras like this, and bring them safety and well-being.”

cmp.note: 「从一百由旬之外」，即一百由旬的范围之内都护着。由旬是古印度的路程单位，大约一天行军的距离，说法不一，约十几公里。英文附了大致长度；白话只说「古印度路程单位」。
cmp.en: “From a hundred yojanas away,” i.e. within a radius of a hundred yojanas. A yojana is an ancient Indian distance, roughly a day's march; estimates vary, around fifteen kilometers. The English gives an approximate length; the plain Chinese only says 古印度路程单位 (“an ancient Indian unit of distance”).

verses.en: Then the great king Virudhaka (guardian king of the south, another of the four world-protecting kings), who had joined that same assembly and was sitting there surrounded and attended by hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas of kumbhandas, rose from his seat, put his upper robe over one shoulder, bowed toward the Blessed One with joined palms, and said to the Blessed One: “Blessed One, I too will speak the words of a dharani, for the benefit of many people: words of a dharani spell for the protection, shelter and safekeeping of such Dharma teachers, such holders of the sutra. It goes like this:”

cmp.note: 梵本是南方天王增长（Virūḍhaka），带着鸠槃荼众，这正是增长天王手下的鬼众。鸠摩罗什本却是东方的持国天王，带着乾闼婆众。两个底本在这里说的是不同的天王；英文、白话都照梵本。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit has Virūḍhaka, guardian king of the south, with his host of kumbhāṇḍas, which are indeed his traditional followers. Kumarajiva instead has 持国天王 (Chíguó tiānwáng), Dhṛtarāṣṭra, guardian king of the east, with a host of gandharvas. The two source texts name different kings here; the English and the plain Chinese follow the Sanskrit.

verses.en: agaṇe gaṇe gauri gandhāri caṇḍāli mātaṅgi pukkasi saṃkule vrūsali sisi svāhā

cmp.note: 照原音录出，不译。这一段很特别：多是女性的称呼，Gaurī（白肤的，也是女神名）、Gandhārī（犍陀罗女）、Caṇḍālī、Mātaṅgī、Pukkasī 都是最低贱阶层的女子，vrūsali 可能就是 vṛṣalī（首陀罗女）。用贱民女子名入咒，在密教咒语里常见。鸠摩罗什音写为「阿伽祢、伽祢、瞿利、干陀利、旃陀利、摩蹬耆……」。
cmp.en: Given in its original sounds, untranslated. This one is unusual: most of the words are names for women. Gaurī (“fair one,” also a goddess's name), Gandhārī (“woman of Gandhara”), and Caṇḍālī, Mātaṅgī and Pukkasī, all women of the lowest outcaste groups; vrūsali is probably vṛṣalī (“low-caste woman”). Calling on outcaste women's names is common in later tantric spells. Kumarajiva writes them as 阿伽祢 (āqiémí), 伽祢 (qiémí), 瞿利 (qúlì), 干陀利 (gāntuólì), 旃陀利 (zhāntuólì), 摩蹬耆 (módēngqí) and so on.

verses.en: “Blessed One, these are the words of the dharani spell spoken by forty-two kotis of buddhas. Anyone who would attack such Dharma teachers would be doing harm to all of them.”

Then the rakshasa women named Lamba, Vilamba, Kutadanti (“Crooked Teeth”), Pushpadanti (“Flower Teeth”), Makutadanti (“Crown Teeth”), Keshini (“Hairy One”), Achala (“Unmoving”), Maladhari (“Garland Bearer”), Kunti, and Sarvasattvojohari (“Stealer of the Vital Force of All Beings”), and Hariti with her sons and her retinue, all these rakshasa women came to where the Blessed One was. When they arrived, all these rakshasa women said to the Blessed One with one voice: “Blessed One, we too will give protection, shelter and safekeeping to such Dharma teachers, such holders of the sutra, and bring them well-being, so that no one watching for a weak spot in those Dharma teachers, hunting for a weak spot, will find one.”

cmp.note: Hārītī 原是专吃人家小孩的女鬼，后来被佛感化，成为保护孩子的神，中文称「鬼子母」。十罗刹女的名字鸠摩罗什有几个和梵本对不上：makuṭadantī「冠齿」他作「黑齿」，acalā「不动」作「无厌足」，mālādhārī「持花鬘」作「持璎珞」，kuntī 音写作「睾帝」，可能底本不同。
cmp.en: Hārītī was originally a demoness who devoured other people's children; won over by the Buddha, she became a protector of children, called in Chinese 鬼子母 (Guǐzǐmǔ, “Mother of Demon Children”). Several of Kumarajiva's names for the ten rakshasa women do not match this manuscript: for makuṭadantī (“crown teeth”) he has 黑齿 (hēichǐ, “black teeth”), for acalā (“unmoving”) 无厌足 (wú yànzú, “never satisfied”), for mālādhārī (“garland bearer”) 持璎珞 (chí yīngluò, “wearing jewel strings”), and Kuntī appears as 睾帝 (gāodì); his source may have differed.

verses.en: Then all those rakshasa women, chanting together in one voice, offered the Blessed One these words of the dharani spell. It goes like this:
iti me iti me iti me iti me iti me | nime nime nime nime nime | ruhe ruhe ruhe ruhe ruhe | stuhe stuhe stuhe stuhe stuhe svāhā

cmp.note: 照原音录出，不译。四组音节各重复五遍，基本没有字面意义。鸠摩罗什的音写（伊提履、伊提泯、泥履、楼醯、多醯、兜醯……）重复次数和音节都和这个梵本稍有不同。
cmp.en: Given in its original sounds, untranslated. Four syllable groups, each repeated five times, with little or no word meaning. Kumarajiva's transcription (伊提履 yītílǚ, 伊提泯 yītímǐn, 泥履 nílǚ, 楼醯 lóuxī, 多醯 duōxī, 兜醯 dōuxī …) differs slightly from this manuscript in both syllables and number of repetitions.

verses.en: “Even if they climb up onto our heads, let no one harm the Dharma teachers: no yaksha, rakshasa, preta, pishacha (a flesh-eating ghoul), putana, kritya, vetala (a spirit that animates corpses), kumbhanda, stabdha, omaraka, ostaraka or apasmaraka (a demon of epilepsy); no spell cast by a yaksha, by a non-human or by a human; no fever that comes every day, every second day, every third day or every fourth day, no constant fever, no irregular fever. Even when he is dreaming, that anyone in the form of a woman, a man, a boy or a girl should trouble him: this cannot happen.

cmp.note: 「登上这个头」，意思大概是「哪怕骑到我们头上」，表示宁可自己受辱也要护住法师。鸠摩罗什译「宁上我头上，莫恼于法师」，意思更清楚。英文照字面译成 climb up onto our heads。stabdha（僵直）、omāraka、ostāraka 这几类鬼的含义已不清楚，英文只音写。
cmp.en: “Having climbed onto this head”: probably meaning “even if they climb onto our heads,” i.e. we would rather suffer the insult ourselves than let the teachers be harmed. Kumarajiva's 宁上我头上，莫恼于法师 (“rather climb on my head than trouble the Dharma teacher”) makes this clearer. The English renders it literally. What kinds of spirit stabdha (“stiff”), omāraka and ostāraka were is no longer clear, so the English only transliterates them.

verses.en: Then those rakshasa women, chanting together in one voice, addressed the Blessed One with these verses:
“Whoever hears this spell and still attacks a Dharma teacher, his head will split into seven pieces, like the blossom-cluster of the arjaka plant.”

cmp.note: arjaka 是一种罗勒类的植物，花穗成熟时会裂开。鸠摩罗什译「如阿梨树枝」，把花穗（mañjarī）换成了「树枝」。「头破七分」后来成了中文俗语。
cmp.en: Arjaka is a basil-like plant whose flower spike splits apart when ripe. Kumarajiva's 如阿梨树枝 (rú ālí shùzhī, “like a branch of the arjaka tree”) turns the flower spike (mañjarī) into a “branch.” 头破七分 (tóu pò qī fēn, “head split in seven”) later became a Chinese idiom.

verses.en: “The fate of those who kill their mothers, the fate of those who kill their fathers: that fate will come to whoever attacks a Dharma teacher.”
“The fate of those who crush sesame seeds, and the fate of those who cheat with sesame: that fate will come to whoever attacks a Dharma teacher.”

cmp.note: 榨芝麻油要压死芝麻里的小虫，所以被看作有罪的行业。tilakūṭa 可能指在芝麻买卖上作假，也可能读作「芝麻堆」，意思不太确定。鸠摩罗什只译「亦如压油殃」。
cmp.en: Pressing sesame for oil crushes the tiny insects inside the seeds, so it was considered a sinful trade. Tilakūṭa may mean cheating in the sesame trade, or simply “a heap of sesame”; the sense is not certain. Kumarajiva has only 亦如压油殃 (“like the calamity of pressing oil”).

verses.en: “The fate of those who cheat with scales, the fate of those who cheat with brass measures: that fate will come to whoever attacks a Dharma teacher.”

cmp.note: 短斤缺两的秤和量器。鸠摩罗什在这里多加了一句梵本没有的「调达破僧罪」——调达即提婆达多，分裂僧团是佛教最重的罪之一。
cmp.en: Rigged scales and short measures. Here Kumarajiva adds a phrase the Sanskrit lacks, 调达破僧罪 (Tiáodá pò sēng zuì, “the sin of Devadatta splitting the Sangha”); splitting the monastic community is among the gravest offenses in Buddhism.

verses.en: Having said this, the rakshasa women led by Kunti said to the Blessed One: “Blessed One, we too will protect such Dharma teachers; we will bring them well-being, keep the rod of punishment away from them, and neutralize poison.” When they had said this, the Blessed One said to the rakshasa women: “Well done, well done, sisters! You will give protection, shelter and safekeeping to those Dharma teachers who hold even just the name of this Dharma discourse.

“How much more, then, those who hold this Dharma discourse complete and entire, or who honor it as a book, with flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, scented powders, robes, parasols, flags, banners and victory pennants, with oil lamps, ghee lamps, lamps of scented oil, lamps of champaka oil, lamps of varshika oil, lamps of blue-lotus oil, lamps of sumana oil: those who honor and revere it with hundreds of thousands of kinds of offering like these. Kunti, you and your retinue should protect them.”

cmp.note: 世尊在这里点名叮嘱的是孔蒂（Kuntī），鸠摩罗什音写为「睾帝」。白话把灯的种类列成「酥油灯、香油灯……」，漏了梵文排在最前面的普通油灯（tailapradīpa）；英文照梵文全列。
cmp.en: The Blessed One addresses Kuntī by name here; Kumarajiva transliterates it 睾帝 (gāodì). The plain Chinese lists the lamps starting from 酥油灯 (“ghee lamps”) and leaves out the plain oil lamps (tailapradīpa) that the Sanskrit lists first; the English gives the full Sanskrit list.

verses.en: While this chapter on dharanis was being taught, sixty-eight thousand living beings gained the acceptance that things are unborn.

cmp.note: 「对诸法不生的忍」：kṣānti 本义是「忍耐、接受」，这里指心能安然接受「一切法本来没有生起」这个道理，是菩萨修行的一个重要阶位。中文「无生法忍」的「忍」容易被读成「忍受」；英文 acceptance 更接近原意。
cmp.en: “Acceptance of the non-arising of things”: kṣānti originally means “patience, acceptance,” and here it is the mind's calm acceptance that no thing has ever truly come into being, an important stage on the bodhisattva path. The Chinese 无生法忍 (wúshēng fǎ rěn) uses 忍 (rěn), which readers easily take as “endure”; the English “acceptance” is closer to the original.

verses.en: Here ends the twenty-first chapter, called “Dharanis,” in the glorious Dharma discourse of the Lotus of the True Dharma.

cmp.note: 梵本自己编为第二十一品；本站算法是第 22 章，鸠摩罗什本是第二十六品——罗什本把陀罗尼品放在观世音品之后，次序和梵本不同。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit numbers this the twenty-first chapter; on this site it is Chapter 22, and in Kumarajiva's version it is the twenty-sixth, since he places the dharani chapter after the Avalokiteshvara chapter, a different order from the Sanskrit.

chapters.title: Chapter 23 · The Former Life of Bhaishajyaraja, the Medicine King

verses.en: Then the bodhisattva, great being Nakshatrarajasamkusumitabhijna (roughly “One Whose Higher Powers Blossom Like the King of Stars”) said to the Blessed One: “Blessed One, why does the bodhisattva, great being Bhaishajyaraja (the Medicine King) wander about in this Saha world (our world of endurance)? And, Blessed One, many hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas (both huge numbers) of hard deeds are seen in him. Please, Blessed One, Tathagata, arhat, fully awakened buddha, tell us even a small part of the conduct of the bodhisattva, great being Bhaishajyaraja, so that gods, nagas, yakshas, gandharvas, asuras, garudas, kinnaras, mahoragas, humans and non-humans, the bodhisattvas, great beings, who have come from other world systems, and these great disciples, may all hear it and be pleased, satisfied, uplifted and glad at heart.”

cmp.note: 名字很长，大意是「神通如星宿之王开花般绽放的人」。鸠摩罗什截取前半译为「宿王华」（星宿之王的花）。英文音写全名，括号里给一个大概意思。
cmp.en: A long name meaning roughly “one whose higher powers have blossomed like the king of the stars.” Kumarajiva keeps only part of it: 宿王华 (Sùwánghuá, “Flower of the Star King”). The English transliterates the full name and gives an approximate meaning in parentheses.

cmp.note: 「药之王」，中文「药王」是直译，英文音写并附 Medicine King。这一品讲的是他前世焚身供佛的故事，在中国影响极大，历史上有僧人据此燃指、燃身。
cmp.en: “King of Medicines”; the Chinese 药王 (Yàowáng) is a direct translation, and the English transliterates and adds “Medicine King.” This chapter tells of his former life in which he burned his own body as an offering, a story that had enormous influence in China: historically some monks burned fingers or even their whole bodies in imitation.

verses.en: Then the Blessed One, knowing the request of the bodhisattva, great being Nakshatrarajasamkusumitabhijna, said to him at that moment: “Long ago, son of good family, in the past, as many eons (kalpas, vast ages) ago as there are grains of sand in the Ganges, there was a time when a tathagata named Chandrasuryavimalaprabhasashri (“Glory of the Spotless Light of Sun and Moon”) appeared in the world: an arhat, a fully awakened buddha, perfect in knowledge and conduct, the Well-Gone One, knower of the world, unsurpassed, tamer of those who can be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a buddha, a blessed one.

cmp.note: 「日月无垢光明吉祥」。鸠摩罗什译「日月净明德」，是中文读者熟悉的佛名。后面一串是佛的十个称号，英文逐一译出，鸠摩罗什用「应供、正遍知、明行足……」这套固定译名。
cmp.en: “Glory of the spotless light of sun and moon.” Kumarajiva renders it 日月净明德 (Rìyuè Jìngmíngdé, “Pure Bright Virtue of Sun and Moon”), the name familiar to Chinese readers. The string after it is the standard ten epithets of a buddha; the English translates each, while Kumarajiva uses the fixed Chinese set 应供、正遍知、明行足… (“worthy of offerings, rightly and universally knowing, perfect in clarity and conduct…”).

verses.en: “That Blessed One, Nakshatrarajasamkusumitabhijna, the Tathagata Chandrasuryavimalaprabhasashri, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, had a great assembly of eighty kotis of bodhisattvas, great beings, and an assembly of disciples as many as the grains of sand in seventy-two Ganges rivers. There were no women in his dispensation. That buddha-land had no hells, no animal births, no hungry ghosts and no asuras; it was level and lovely, as flat as the palm of a hand. Its ground was made of heavenly lapis lazuli and adorned with jewel trees and sandalwood trees; it was stirred by nets of jewels, hung with streamers of silk, and scented by jewel incense burners. At the foot of every jewel tree, at the distance of an arrow's flight, stood a jewel pavilion.

cmp.note: 「没有女人」。这是不少大乘经描写理想佛土的固定说法，反映当时的观念；英文、白话都照实译出，不加修饰。鸠摩罗什在这里还插进了佛和菩萨的寿命，梵本放在下一段。
cmp.en: “Free of women.” This is a stock phrase in many Mahayana descriptions of an ideal buddha-land and reflects the attitudes of its time; the English and the plain Chinese translate it as it stands. Kumarajiva also inserts the lifespans of the buddha and bodhisattvas here; the Sanskrit gives them in the next paragraph.

verses.en: “On top of every jewel pavilion a hundred kotis of young gods stood playing instruments, keeping time and singing, as an offering to the Blessed One, the Tathagata Chandrasuryavimalaprabhasashri, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha. And that Blessed One taught this Dharma discourse, the Lotus of the True Dharma, at length to those great disciples and those bodhisattvas, great beings, with the bodhisattva, great being Sarvasattvapriyadarshana (“Delightful to See for All Beings”) as its occasion. The lifespan of that Blessed One, Nakshatrarajasamkusumitabhijna, the Tathagata Chandrasuryavimalaprabhasashri, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, was forty-two thousand eons, and those bodhisattvas, great beings, and those great disciples had the same lifespan.

cmp.note: 「一切众生都乐于见到的人」，鸠摩罗什译「一切众生憙见」。他就是药王菩萨的前身。adhiṣṭhānaṃ kṛtvā 字面是「以他为依据」，白话译「为缘起」，英文译成 as its occasion，意思是佛因他而说此经。
cmp.en: “The one all beings delight to see”; Kumarajiva has 一切众生憙见 (Yíqiè Zhòngshēng Xǐjiàn). He is the former life of Bhaishajyaraja. Adhiṣṭhānaṃ kṛtvā literally means “making him the basis”; the plain Chinese says 为缘起 (“as the occasion”) and the English “as its occasion”: the buddha taught the sutra on his account.

verses.en: “That bodhisattva, great being Sarvasattvapriyadarshana devoted himself to hard practice under that Blessed One's teaching. For twelve thousand years he kept to the walking path (where monks pace up and down in meditation), working at meditation with great energy. After twelve thousand years he gained the concentration (samadhi) called Showing Every Form. As soon as he gained that concentration, the bodhisattva, great being Sarvasattvapriyadarshana was pleased, uplifted, glad at heart, delighted, full of joy and happiness, and at that moment he thought: ‘It is thanks to this Dharma discourse, the Lotus of the True Dharma, that I have gained this concentration of Showing Every Form.’

cmp.note: 「能显现一切形相」的三昧：得到它就能化现成任何样子去度众生。鸠摩罗什译「现一切色身三昧」，这里的「色」是「形体」，不是颜色。下一品妙音菩萨、再下一品观世音菩萨现种种身，都是这个能力。
cmp.en: The samadhi of “showing every form”: one who gains it can appear in any shape to help beings. Kumarajiva calls it 现一切色身三昧 (xiàn yíqiè sèshēn sānmèi), where 色 (sè) means “bodily form,” not “color.” Gadgadasvara in the next chapter and Avalokiteshvara in the one after take many forms by this same power.
