verses.en: “At that moment the bodhisattva, great being Sarvasattvapriyadarshana thought: ‘What if I were to make an offering to the Blessed One, the Tathagata Chandrasuryavimalaprabhasashri, and to this Dharma discourse, the Lotus of the True Dharma?’ At that moment he entered such a concentration that the instant he entered it, a great rain of mandarava and great mandarava flowers poured down from the sky above, a cloud of black sandalwood formed, and a rain of uragasara sandalwood (“snake-essence” sandalwood) poured down. And that kind of perfume, Nakshatrarajasamkusumitabhijna, is such that a single karsha of it (a small weight, roughly a dozen grams) is worth as much as this whole Saha world.

cmp.note: 「蛇心旃檀」，一种名贵的檀香，传说蛇喜欢缠在这种树上。鸠摩罗什译「海此岸栴檀」，和梵文意思不同，可能底本或理解有别。karṣa 是重量单位，罗什换算成「六铢」。
cmp.en: “Snake-essence sandalwood,” a precious sandalwood around which snakes were said to coil. Kumarajiva renders it 海此岸栴檀 (hǎi cǐ'àn zhāntán, “sandalwood from this shore of the sea”), a different meaning, perhaps from a different source or understanding. A karṣa is a unit of weight; Kumarajiva converts it to 六铢 (liù zhū, “six zhu”), a Chinese weight.

verses.en: “Then, Nakshatrarajasamkusumitabhijna, the bodhisattva, great being Sarvasattvapriyadarshana, mindful and fully aware, came out of that concentration. Having come out of it, he thought: ‘Showing supernatural miracles is not as great an offering to the Blessed One as giving up my own body.’ Then, Nakshatrarajasamkusumitabhijna, the bodhisattva, great being Sarvasattvapriyadarshana began at that moment to eat aloeswood, turushka and frankincense resin, and to drink champaka oil. In this way, Nakshatrarajasamkusumitabhijna, while the bodhisattva, great being Sarvasattvapriyadarshana kept eating fragrances and drinking champaka oil without a break, twelve years went by.

cmp.note: 梵本是吃香、喝油「十二年」；鸠摩罗什作「满千二百岁」，一千二百年。白话照梵文。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says he ate fragrances and drank oil for “twelve years”; Kumarajiva has 满千二百岁 (mǎn qiān'èrbǎi suì, “a full twelve hundred years”). The plain Chinese follows the Sanskrit.

verses.en: “Then, Nakshatrarajasamkusumitabhijna, when those twelve years had passed, the bodhisattva, great being Sarvasattvapriyadarshana wrapped his own body in heavenly cloth, soaked it in scented oil, and made his own solemn resolve. Having made his resolve, he set his own body alight, as an offering to the Tathagata and in honor of this Dharma discourse, the Lotus of the True Dharma. And, Nakshatrarajasamkusumitabhijna, the flames and light of that lamp that was the body of the bodhisattva, great being Sarvasattvapriyadarshana filled world systems as many as the grains of sand in eighty Ganges rivers.

cmp.note: adhiṣṭhāna 有「誓愿、加持之力」的意思：他先立下自己的誓愿，再点火。白话「发起自己的誓愿之力」、英文 made his own solemn resolve 都是这个意思；鸠摩罗什译「以神通力愿而自然身」。注意梵文 kāyapradīpa「身体之灯」：他把自己当成供佛的灯。
cmp.en: Adhiṣṭhāna means a resolve or empowering vow: he first makes his own vow, then lights the fire. The plain Chinese 发起自己的誓愿之力 (“brought forth the power of his own vow”) and the English “made his own solemn resolve” say the same; Kumarajiva has 以神通力愿而自然身 (“by the power of his supernatural vow he burned his own body”). Note the Sanskrit kāyapradīpa, “body-lamp”: he makes himself a lamp offered to the buddha.

verses.en: “In those world systems, buddhas, blessed ones as many as the grains of sand in eighty Ganges rivers all gave their approval: ‘Well done, well done, son of good family! Well done indeed, son of good family! This is the true energy of bodhisattvas, great beings. This is the true offering to the Tathagata, the offering of the Dharma. An offering of flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, scented powders, robes, parasols, flags and banners is not like this, nor an offering of food, nor an offering of snake-essence sandalwood. This, son of good family, is the highest gift. Giving up a kingdom is not like it, nor giving up beloved sons and wives. This, son of good family, giving up one's own body, is the distinguished, highest, best, most excellent, most exquisite offering of the Dharma.’ And, Nakshatrarajasamkusumitabhijna, when those buddhas, blessed ones, had spoken these words, they fell silent.

cmp.note: 「舍弃自身」被诸佛称为最高的「法供养」。这一段是后世燃身、燃指供佛的主要经典依据，也一直有争议。英文、白话都照字面翻，不加评论；鸠摩罗什本基本相同。
cmp.en: “Giving up one's own body” is praised by the buddhas as the highest “offering of the Dharma.” This passage became the main scriptural basis for later practices of burning the body or fingers as an offering, and it has long been debated. The English and the plain Chinese translate it literally without comment; Kumarajiva's version says essentially the same.

verses.en: “And, Nakshatrarajasamkusumitabhijna, while the body of Sarvasattvapriyadarshana was blazing, twelve hundred years went by, and it did not die down. Only after twelve hundred years did it go out. And, Nakshatrarajasamkusumitabhijna, after making such an offering to the Tathagata and such an offering of the Dharma, the bodhisattva, great being Sarvasattvapriyadarshana passed away from there and, under the teaching of that same Blessed One, the Tathagata Chandrasuryavimalaprabhasashri, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, was reborn in the house of King Vimaladatta (“Spotless Gift”), born spontaneously: he appeared sitting cross-legged in the king's lap. And the moment he was born, the bodhisattva, great being Sarvasattvapriyadarshana spoke to his mother and father in a verse:

cmp.note: 「化生」，不经母胎、忽然出现的出生方式。梵文说他盘腿出现在（父王的）怀中，并对「父母」说偈；鸠摩罗什写「即为其父而说偈言」，只对父亲说，后面也都只称「大王」。
cmp.en: Aupapādika means “spontaneously born,” appearing suddenly without a womb. The Sanskrit says he appeared cross-legged in the king's lap and spoke to his “mother and father”; Kumarajiva writes 即为其父而说偈言 (“he spoke a verse to his father”), addressing only the father, and afterwards only says 大王 (“Great King”).

verses.en: “‘Best of kings, this is my walking path, where I stood and gained concentration. I took on firm energy and a great vow, and gave up my own dear body.’

“Then, Nakshatrarajasamkusumitabhijna, the bodhisattva, great being Sarvasattvapriyadarshana, having spoken this verse, said to his mother and father: ‘Mother, father, that Blessed One, the Tathagata Chandrasuryavimalaprabhasashri, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, is still here even now, living, carrying on, teaching the Dharma. By making offerings to that Blessed One, the Tathagata Chandrasuryavimalaprabhasashri, I gained the dharani of skill in all languages, and in that Blessed One's presence I heard this Dharma discourse, the Lotus of the True Dharma, in eighty hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas of verses, and in kankaras, vivaras and akshobhyas of verses (all names of enormous numbers). Well then, mother, father: I will go to that Blessed One, and when I get there I will make offerings to him once more.’

cmp.note: 三个都是古印度极大的数目名称。鸠摩罗什音写为「甄迦罗、频婆罗、阿閦婆」，白话沿用；英文音写并说明是大数。
cmp.en: All three are names of huge numbers in ancient India. Kumarajiva transliterates them 甄迦罗 (zhēnjiāluó), 频婆罗 (pínpóluó), 阿閦婆 (āchùpó), and the plain Chinese keeps those; the English transliterates them and notes that they are large numbers.

verses.en: “Then, Nakshatrarajasamkusumitabhijna, at that moment the bodhisattva, great being Sarvasattvapriyadarshana rose into the air to the height of seven palm trees and, sitting cross-legged in a pavilion made of the seven precious things, went to where that Blessed One was. When he arrived, he bowed his head to the Blessed One's feet, walked around the Blessed One seven times keeping him on his right, bowed toward the Blessed One with joined palms, paid him homage, and praised him with this verse:

“‘Your face is spotless, lord of men, steadfast one; your radiance shines in the ten directions. Well-Gone One, I once made you the highest offering, and now I have come back here to see you, protector.’

“Then, Nakshatrarajasamkusumitabhijna, the bodhisattva, great being Sarvasattvapriyadarshana spoke this verse at that moment to that Blessed One Chandrasuryavimalaprabhasashri (the Sanskrit is garbled here) … and that Blessed One, the Tathagata Chandrasuryavimalaprabhasashri, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, said to the bodhisattva, great being Sarvasattvapriyadarshana: ‘Son of good family, the time of my final nirvana has come; son of good family, the time of my ending has come. So go, son of good family, and set out my couch: I am going to pass into final nirvana.’

cmp.note: 梵本这一句缺了动词、名字也被截断，意思不完整，白话和英文都标出残缺。鸠摩罗什本在这里多一句菩萨的话：「世尊！世尊犹故在世」，句子是通顺的；还多了「我于今夜当般涅槃」的「今夜」。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit sentence here is missing its verb and part of a name, so the sense is incomplete; the plain Chinese and the English both mark the gap. Kumarajiva's version reads smoothly here, with an extra line from the bodhisattva, 世尊！世尊犹故在世 (“Blessed One! You are still in the world”), and the buddha adds 今夜 (jīnyè, “tonight”) to “I will pass into nirvana.”

verses.en: “Then, Nakshatrarajasamkusumitabhijna, that Blessed One, the Tathagata Chandrasuryavimalaprabhasashri, said to the bodhisattva, great being Sarvasattvapriyadarshana: ‘Son of good family, I entrust this teaching to you. These bodhisattvas, great beings, these great disciples, this awakening of a buddha, this world system, these jewel pavilions, these jewel trees, and these young gods who wait on me, I entrust to you. And the relics that will remain after my final nirvana, son of good family, I entrust to you. You yourself, son of good family, should make great offerings to my relics. You should spread these relics far and wide, and build many thousands of stupas.’

cmp.note: dhātu 本义是「元素、成分」，这里指火化后留下的遗骨，中文音译「舍利」（来自另一个词 śarīra）。英文 relics 是通行译法。
cmp.en: Dhātu basically means “element, constituent”; here it means the bones left after cremation. Chinese calls them 舍利 (shèlì), a transliteration of a different word, śarīra. The English “relics” is the usual rendering.

verses.en: “Then, Nakshatrarajasamkusumitabhijna, having instructed the bodhisattva, great being Sarvasattvapriyadarshana in this way, that Blessed One, the Tathagata Chandrasuryavimalaprabhasashri, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, passed into final nirvana in the last watch of that same night, into the realm of nirvana in which nothing at all is left behind.

cmp.note: 「无余依涅槃界」：连身体这最后的依托也不留下的涅槃，即佛的入灭。白话「不留任何余依的涅槃界」照字面；英文 in which nothing at all is left behind 意思一样。鸠摩罗什只写「入于涅槃」。
cmp.en: “The nirvana-realm with no remainder of support”: nirvana in which even the body, the last support, is left behind, i.e. a buddha's death. The plain Chinese 不留任何余依的涅槃界 (“nirvana-realm leaving no remaining support”) is literal, and the English “in which nothing at all is left behind” means the same. Kumarajiva simply says 入于涅槃 (“entered nirvana”).

verses.en: “Then, Nakshatrarajasamkusumitabhijna, the bodhisattva, great being Sarvasattvapriyadarshana, knowing that the Blessed One, the Tathagata Chandrasuryavimalaprabhasashri, had passed into final nirvana, built a pyre of snake-essence sandalwood and burned the Tathagata's body. Knowing that the Tathagata's body had burned and the fire had died down, he gathered the relics and wept, cried out and lamented. Then, Nakshatrarajasamkusumitabhijna, after weeping, crying out and lamenting, the bodhisattva, great being Sarvasattvapriyadarshana had eighty-four thousand urns made of the seven precious things, put the Tathagata's relics into them, and set up eighty-four thousand stupas made of the seven precious things, as high as the Brahma world, adorned with rows of parasols and stirred with silk streamers and bells.

cmp.note: 梵文说塔「高达梵天世界」；鸠摩罗什写「高三世界」。八万四千塔这个数字，后来也用在阿育王造塔的传说里。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says the stupas reached “up to the Brahma world”; Kumarajiva says 高三世界 (gāo sān shìjiè, “as high as three worlds”). The number eighty-four thousand stupas also appears in the later legend of King Ashoka's stupa building.

verses.en: “When he had set up those stupas, he thought: ‘I have made an offering to the relics of that Blessed One, the Tathagata Chandrasuryavimalaprabhasashri. But I will go further still and make an even more distinguished offering to the Tathagata's relics.’ Then, Nakshatrarajasamkusumitabhijna, the bodhisattva, great being Sarvasattvapriyadarshana called together that whole host of bodhisattvas, those great disciples, and those hosts of gods, nagas, yakshas, gandharvas, asuras, garudas, kinnaras, mahoragas, humans and non-humans: ‘Pay close attention, all of you, sons of good family. We are going to make an offering to that Blessed One's relics.’

“Then, Nakshatrarajasamkusumitabhijna, at that moment, in front of those eighty-four thousand stupas holding the Tathagata's relics, the bodhisattva, great being Sarvasattvapriyadarshana set alight his own arm, adorned with the marks of a hundred merits. Having set it alight, he made offerings to those stupas of the Tathagata's relics for seventy-two thousand years. And while he was making the offering, countless hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas of disciples in that assembly were trained, and all those bodhisattvas gained the concentration of Showing Every Form.

cmp.note: 梵文是「无数声闻被调伏、教化」。鸠摩罗什改成「令无数求声闻众……发阿耨多罗三藐三菩提心」：让求声闻果的人转而发心成佛，更贴合法华经「一乘」的主旨。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says countless disciples “were trained.” Kumarajiva has 令无数求声闻众……发阿耨多罗三藐三菩提心 (“caused countless seekers of the disciple's path… to aspire to unsurpassed, perfect awakening”): those aiming at the disciples' goal turn toward buddhahood, which fits the Lotus Sutra's “one vehicle” theme more closely.

verses.en: “Then, Nakshatrarajasamkusumitabhijna, that whole host of bodhisattvas and all those great disciples, seeing the bodhisattva, great being Sarvasattvapriyadarshana missing a limb, wept with tears streaming down their faces, cried out and lamented, and said to one another: ‘This bodhisattva, great being Sarvasattvapriyadarshana is our teacher, the one who instructs us. And now he has lost a limb, he has lost his arm.’ Then, Nakshatrarajasamkusumitabhijna, the bodhisattva, great being Sarvasattvapriyadarshana spoke to those bodhisattvas, those great disciples and those young gods: ‘Sons of good family, do not weep, do not cry out, do not lament because you see me missing a limb.

cmp.note: 梵文这里说他失去的是「手臂」（单数），前一段也是燃「自己的手臂」。鸠摩罗什在下一段写「我舍两臂」，变成了两条手臂；英文、白话都照梵文是一条。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says he has lost his “arm” (singular), and the previous paragraph too has him burning “his own arm.” In the next paragraph Kumarajiva writes 我舍两臂 (wǒ shě liǎng bì, “I gave up both arms”); the English and the plain Chinese follow the Sanskrit's single arm.

verses.en: ‘Look, sons of good family: I call to witness all the buddhas, the blessed ones, who are living, carrying on and staying in the endless, boundless world systems of the ten directions, and before them I make an act of truth. By this truth, by these true words, that I gave up my own arm as an offering to the Tathagata, my body will become the color of gold. By this truth, by these true words, may this arm of mine be as it was before, may this great earth shake in the six ways, and may the young gods in the sky rain down a great rain of flowers.’

cmp.note: 「以真实为依凭的誓言」：古印度相信，只要说的是绝对真实的话，就能凭这真实的力量使愿望成真，英文称为 act of truth。白话「真实的誓言」「真实语」、鸠摩罗什「若实不虚」都是这个意思。
cmp.en: An “empowerment by truth”: in ancient India it was believed that a statement of absolute truth has the power to make a wish come true, and this is known in English as an “act of truth.” The plain Chinese 真实的誓言 (“a vow of truth”) and 真实语 (“true words”), and Kumarajiva's 若实不虚 (“if this is true and not false”), all express the same idea.

verses.en: “Then, Nakshatrarajasamkusumitabhijna, the instant the bodhisattva, great being Sarvasattvapriyadarshana had made this act of truth, this great trichiliocosm (a universe of a billion worlds) shook in the six ways, and a great rain of flowers poured down from the sky above. And the arm of the bodhisattva, great being Sarvasattvapriyadarshana was restored as it had been before, through the power of that bodhisattva, great being's own knowledge and the power of his merit. Now, Nakshatrarajasamkusumitabhijna, you may have some doubt, uncertainty or hesitation: was the bodhisattva, great being Sarvasattvapriyadarshana at that time and on that occasion someone else? But, Nakshatrarajasamkusumitabhijna, you should not see it like that.

“Why? Because, Nakshatrarajasamkusumitabhijna, this bodhisattva, great being Bhaishajyaraja was at that time and on that occasion the bodhisattva, great being Sarvasattvapriyadarshana. That is how many hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas of hard deeds the bodhisattva, great being Bhaishajyaraja performs, Nakshatrarajasamkusumitabhijna, and how he gives up his own body. And, Nakshatrarajasamkusumitabhijna, a son or daughter of good family who has set out on the bodhisattva path and longs for this unsurpassed, perfect awakening, and who sets alight a big toe at the shrines of the Tathagata, or a single finger, a single toe, a single limb, or an arm: that son or daughter of good family who has set out on the bodhisattva path produces far more merit

cmp.note: 这里直说「在如来的塔庙前点燃自己的大脚趾、一根手指……」的福德胜过舍弃王位。英文、白话照译。这是中国佛教「燃指供佛」的直接经文依据，历来有人照做，也有许多高僧批评这是误读。
cmp.en: The text says plainly that setting alight one's big toe, a finger and so on at a Tathagata's shrine brings more merit than giving up a kingdom. The English and the plain Chinese translate it as is. This is the direct scriptural source of the Chinese Buddhist practice of 燃指供佛 (rán zhǐ gòng fó, “burning a finger as an offering to the Buddha”); some have followed it literally, and many eminent monks have criticized that as a misreading.

verses.en: than from giving up a kingdom, from giving up beloved sons, daughters and wives, or from giving up a whole great trichiliocosm with its forests, oceans, mountains, springs, lakes, ponds, wells and parks. And, Nakshatrarajasamkusumitabhijna, suppose a son or daughter of good family who has set out on the bodhisattva path were to fill this great trichiliocosm with the seven precious things and give it as a gift to all the buddhas, bodhisattvas, disciples and solitary buddhas (pratyekabuddhas). That son or daughter of good family, Nakshatrarajasamkusumitabhijna, would not produce as much merit as the son or daughter of good family who holds from this Dharma discourse, the Lotus of the True Dharma, even a single verse of four lines. I say this person's store of merit is greater,

cmp.note: 这一句梵文的句法不太顺：字面是「他生的福德有那么多，像受持一偈的人那么多」，接着又说「我说后者更多，而不是那个布施的人」。白话和英文都按上下文理解成「比不上受持一偈的人」。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit syntax is awkward here: literally “he produces as much merit as the one who holds a verse,” followed by “I say the latter's merit is greater, not that of the giver.” The plain Chinese and the English both read it from context as “does not equal the one who holds a single verse.”

verses.en: not that of the one who fills this great trichiliocosm with the seven precious things and gives it as a gift to all the buddhas, bodhisattvas, disciples and solitary buddhas.

“Just as, Nakshatrarajasamkusumitabhijna, the great ocean stands at the top of all springs, lakes and ponds, so too, Nakshatrarajasamkusumitabhijna, this Dharma discourse, the Lotus of the True Dharma, stands at the top of all the sutras spoken by the Tathagata. Just as, Nakshatrarajasamkusumitabhijna, Sumeru, king of mountains, stands at the top of all the Black Mountains, the Chakravala ranges and the Great Chakravala ranges (the iron mountain rings around the world), so too, Nakshatrarajasamkusumitabhijna, this Dharma discourse, the Lotus of the True Dharma, is the king of all the sutras spoken by the Tathagata and stands at the top.

cmp.note: 须弥山是古印度宇宙观里世界中心的大山；铁围山（cakravāla）是围在世界最外圈的山环。英文音写并在括号里说明；白话直接用中文旧名「须弥山」「铁围山」。
cmp.en: Sumeru is the great mountain at the center of the world in ancient Indian cosmology; the Cakravāla are the rings of iron mountains around the world's outer edge. The English transliterates them with a gloss; the plain Chinese uses the old Chinese names 须弥山 (Xūmíshān) and 铁围山 (Tiěwéishān, “iron-ring mountains”).

verses.en: “Just as, Nakshatrarajasamkusumitabhijna, among all the stars the moon, the maker of light, ranks highest, so too, Nakshatrarajasamkusumitabhijna, among all the sutras spoken by the Tathagata this Dharma discourse, the Lotus of the True Dharma, ranks highest, giving more light than hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas of moons. Just as, Nakshatrarajasamkusumitabhijna, the disk of the sun drives away all darkness, so too, Nakshatrarajasamkusumitabhijna, this Dharma discourse, the Lotus of the True Dharma, drives away all the darkness of unwholesome deeds. Just as, Nakshatrarajasamkusumitabhijna, Shakra is lord of the gods among the gods of the Thirty-Three, so too, Nakshatrarajasamkusumitabhijna, this Dharma discourse, the Lotus of the True Dharma, is lord of all the sutras spoken by the Tathagata.

cmp.note: 帝释（Śakra，也叫 Indra），是三十三天（须弥山顶的天界）众神之主。鸠摩罗什在这一串比喻里多了一个梵本没有的「转轮圣王为诸小王第一」。
cmp.en: Śakra (also called Indra) is lord of the gods of the Thirty-Three, the heaven on top of Mount Sumeru. In this string of comparisons Kumarajiva adds one the Sanskrit lacks: 转轮圣王为诸小王第一 (“the wheel-turning king is first among lesser kings”).

verses.en: “Just as, Nakshatrarajasamkusumitabhijna, Brahma Sahampati (“Lord of the Saha World”), king of all the gods of Brahma's retinue, acts as a father in the Brahma world, so too, Nakshatrarajasamkusumitabhijna, this Dharma discourse, the Lotus of the True Dharma, acts as a father to all beings: to learners and to those beyond learning, to all disciples and solitary buddhas, and to those who have set out on the bodhisattva path. Just as, Nakshatrarajasamkusumitabhijna, the stream-enterer, the once-returner, the non-returner, the arhat and the solitary buddha surpass all foolish ordinary people, so too, Nakshatrarajasamkusumitabhijna, this Dharma discourse, the Lotus of the True Dharma, should be known to surpass all the sutras spoken by the Tathagata, rising above them to stand at the top.

cmp.note: 「有学、无学」：还在修学的圣者，和已证阿罗汉、不必再学的人。白话译「还在学的和已学成的人」，英文 learners and those beyond learning。预流、一来、不还、阿罗汉是声闻修行的四个果位。
cmp.en: Śaikṣa and aśaikṣa: noble disciples still in training, and arhats who have nothing further to learn. The plain Chinese says 还在学的和已学成的人 (“those still learning and those who have finished”), the English “learners and those beyond learning.” Stream-enterer, once-returner, non-returner and arhat are the four stages of the disciples' path.

verses.en: “And, Nakshatrarajasamkusumitabhijna, the beings who hold this king of sutras should also be known as standing at the top. Just as, Nakshatrarajasamkusumitabhijna, a bodhisattva is called the foremost of all disciples and solitary buddhas, so too, Nakshatrarajasamkusumitabhijna, this Dharma discourse, the Lotus of the True Dharma, is called the foremost of all the sutras spoken by the Tathagata. Just as, Nakshatrarajasamkusumitabhijna, the Tathagata is the crowned king of the Dharma over all disciples, solitary buddhas and bodhisattvas, so too, Nakshatrarajasamkusumitabhijna, this Dharma discourse, the Lotus of the True Dharma, is like the Tathagata himself to those who have set out on the bodhisattva path.

cmp.note: 「就是如来本身」：这部经对菩萨来说等于如来。鸠摩罗什只写「此经亦复如是，诸经中王」，没有译出「经即是如来」这一层，白话和英文照梵文译出。
cmp.en: “Become the Tathagata himself”: for bodhisattvas this sutra is the Tathagata. Kumarajiva writes only 此经亦复如是，诸经中王 (“so is this sutra king among sutras”) and drops the idea that the sutra is the Tathagata; the plain Chinese and the English translate it from the Sanskrit.

verses.en: “And, Nakshatrarajasamkusumitabhijna, this Dharma discourse, the Lotus of the True Dharma, protects all beings from every fear and frees them from every suffering. It is like a pond to the thirsty, a fire to those suffering from cold, clothing to the naked, a caravan leader to merchants, a mother to her children, a boat to those crossing over, a doctor to the sick, a lamp to those wrapped in darkness, a jewel to those seeking wealth, a universal monarch to all petty kings, the ocean to the rivers, a torch for driving away all darkness. Just so, Nakshatrarajasamkusumitabhijna, this Dharma discourse, the Lotus of the True Dharma, frees from every suffering, cuts off every illness, and frees from every fear, bond and hardship of the round of rebirth (samsara).

“And, Nakshatrarajasamkusumitabhijna, whoever hears this Dharma discourse, the Lotus of the True Dharma, whoever writes it, whoever has it written: the store of merit of these people, Nakshatrarajasamkusumitabhijna, cannot be measured to its end even by a buddha's knowledge, so great is the store of merit that son or daughter of good family will produce.

“Whoever holds this Dharma discourse, or recites it, teaches it, hears it, writes it or makes it into a book, and honors, reveres, respects and makes offerings to it with flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, scented powders, robes, parasols, flags, banners and victory pennants, with music, cloth and joined palms, with ghee lamps, lamps of scented oil, lamps of champaka oil, of sumana oil, of patala oil, of varshika oil, of navamalika oil, and with many kinds of offering shows it honor, reverence, respect and worship: much merit, Nakshatrarajasamkusumitabhijna, will that son or daughter of good family on the bodhisattva path produce who holds, recites or hears this chapter on the former life of Bhaishajyaraja.

cmp.note: 「从前的因缘、前世的事」。鸠摩罗什译作「本事」，品名是《药王菩萨本事品》；英文译 former life。
cmp.en: Pūrvayoga means “former connection, story of a past life.” Kumarajiva renders it 本事 (běnshì, “original deeds”), naming the chapter 药王菩萨本事品; the English says “former life.”

verses.en: “And, Nakshatrarajasamkusumitabhijna, if a woman hears this Dharma discourse, takes it up and holds it, that will be her last birth as a woman. Nakshatrarajasamkusumitabhijna, any woman who hears this chapter on the former life of Bhaishajyaraja in the last five hundred years and practices it will, when she passes away from here, be reborn in the world system Sukhavati (the Land of Bliss), where the Blessed One, the Tathagata Amitayus (“Boundless Life”), the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, lives, carries on and stays, surrounded by a host of bodhisattvas. She will be born there seated on a lion throne in the heart of a lotus. Desire will no longer torment her, nor hatred, nor delusion, nor pride, nor stinginess, nor anger, nor ill will. As soon as she is born she will gain the five higher knowledges, and she will gain the acceptance that things are unborn.

cmp.note: 「这将是她最后一次为女身」，反映古代认为女身不利修行的观念；英文、白话照实译出。这段把读法华经和往生阿弥陀佛的极乐世界连在一起；梵文用 Amitāyus「无量寿」，鸠摩罗什写「阿弥陀佛」，并把「后五百岁」明确为「如来灭后后五百岁」。
cmp.en: “That will be her last existence as a woman” reflects the ancient view that a woman's body is a disadvantage for practice; the English and the plain Chinese translate it as it stands. This passage links reading the Lotus Sutra with rebirth in Amitabha's Land of Bliss: the Sanskrit uses the name Amitāyus (“Boundless Life”), Kumarajiva writes 阿弥陀佛 (Ēmítuó fó, “Amitabha Buddha”), and he spells out “the last five hundred years” as 如来灭后后五百岁 (“the last five hundred years after the Tathagata's passing”).

verses.en: “And that bodhisattva, great being, Nakshatrarajasamkusumitabhijna, having gained the acceptance that things are unborn, will see Tathagatas as many as the grains of sand in seventy-two Ganges rivers. His faculty of sight will become so pure that with that pure faculty of sight he will see those buddhas, the blessed ones. And those buddhas, the blessed ones, will praise him: ‘Well done, well done, son of good family! Having heard the Dharma discourse, the Lotus of the True Dharma, under the teaching of the Blessed One, the Tathagata Shakyamuni, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, you studied it, recited it, cultivated it, reflected on it, took it to heart and made it known to other beings. Son of good family, this store of merit of yours cannot be burned by fire or carried off by water.

cmp.note: 注意梵文这里接着上文的女子，改称「这位菩萨大士」，用的是阳性：往生后她已是菩萨，不再是女身。英文只能用 he，白话用「他」，都跟着梵文。鸠摩罗什的数字是「七百万二千亿那由他恒河沙」，比梵文的「七十二条恒河沙」大得多。
cmp.en: Note that the Sanskrit, continuing about the woman, now calls her “this bodhisattva, great being” in the masculine: after rebirth she is a bodhisattva and no longer in a woman's body. The English has to use “he,” and the plain Chinese uses 他 (tā, “he”), both following the Sanskrit. Kumarajiva's figure, 七百万二千亿那由他恒河沙 (“sands of 7,200,000 hundred-million nayutas of Ganges”), is far larger than the Sanskrit's “seventy-two Ganges rivers.”

verses.en: ‘This store of merit of yours, son of good family, could not be described even by a thousand buddhas. You have struck down Mara, the adversary, son of good family; you have crossed the battlefield of fear and crushed the thorns of your enemies. A hundred thousand buddhas watch over you. Son of good family, in the world with its gods, its Maras and its Brahmas, among all beings with their ascetics and brahmins, there is no one equal to you except the Tathagata alone. There is no other, no disciple, no solitary buddha, no bodhisattva, who can surpass you in merit, in wisdom or in concentration.’ That, Nakshatrarajasamkusumitabhijna, is the power of knowledge that bodhisattva will attain.

cmp.note: 魔（Māra）是佛教里引人执迷、阻碍觉悟的魔王，也泛指一切障碍。英文保留 Mara 并在上下文里说他是「对手」；鸠摩罗什译「破诸魔贼，坏生死军」，多了「生死」二字。
cmp.en: Māra is the tempter in Buddhism who keeps beings deluded and blocks awakening, and by extension any such obstacle. The English keeps “Mara” and calls him “the adversary”; Kumarajiva has 破诸魔贼，坏生死军 (“crushed the demon bandits, destroyed the army of birth and death”), adding the words “birth and death.”

verses.en: “Whoever, Nakshatrarajasamkusumitabhijna, hears this chapter on the former life of Bhaishajyaraja being taught and expresses approval, the scent of the blue lotus will come from his mouth, and the scent of sandalwood from his body. Whoever expresses approval of this Dharma discourse will have, in this very life, such benefits and virtues as I have just described.

“So, Nakshatrarajasamkusumitabhijna, I entrust to you this chapter on the former life of the bodhisattva, great being Sarvasattvapriyadarshana, so that in the last time, the last age, when the last five hundred years are under way, it may spread through this Jambudvipa (our continent, the world of humans) and not disappear; so that Mara the Evil One may find no opening, nor the gods of Mara's retinue, nor nagas, yakshas, gandharvas or kumbhandas. So, Nakshatrarajasamkusumitabhijna, I empower this Dharma discourse here in Jambudvipa. It will be a medicine for beings who are ill, stricken with disease. When they hear this Dharma discourse, disease will not take hold of the body, nor old age, nor untimely death.

cmp.note: 梵文是「不会衰老、不会非时而死」，即不会横死早夭。鸠摩罗什译成「不老不死」，读起来像是长生不死，比原意强得多。白话「衰老和非时横死也不会到来」照梵文。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says “no old age, no untimely death,” i.e. not dying before one's time. Kumarajiva writes 不老不死 (bù lǎo bù sǐ, “no aging, no death”), which reads like immortality and says far more than the original. The plain Chinese, 衰老和非时横死也不会到来 (“neither aging nor untimely violent death will come”), follows the Sanskrit.

verses.en: “And, Nakshatrarajasamkusumitabhijna, if anyone who has set out on the bodhisattva path sees a monk who holds a sutra like this, he should scatter sandalwood powder and blue lotuses over him, and having scattered them, he should think: ‘This son of good family will go to the seat of awakening. He will take up grass. He will spread a grass mat on the seat of awakening. He will defeat the army of Mara and the yakshas. He will blow the conch of the Dharma. He will beat the drum of the Dharma. He will cross the ocean of existence.’ That is how, Nakshatrarajasamkusumitabhijna, a son or daughter of good family on the bodhisattva path should think on seeing a monk who holds a sutra like this. And he will have such benefits and virtues as the Tathagata has described.

cmp.note: 「将拿起草」：释迦牟尼成道前，从割草人手里接过吉祥草，铺在菩提树下作坐垫。这几句是在预言这位比丘将来也会这样成佛。鸠摩罗什译「不久必当取草坐于道场」。
cmp.en: “He will take up grass”: before his awakening, Shakyamuni accepted kusha grass from a grass-cutter and spread it as his seat under the bodhi tree. These lines foretell that this monk will one day become a buddha the same way. Kumarajiva has 不久必当取草坐于道场 (“before long he will surely take grass and sit on the seat of awakening”).

verses.en: While this chapter on the former life of Bhaishajyaraja was being taught, eighty-four thousand bodhisattvas gained the dharani that follows the skill in all languages. And the Blessed One, the Tathagata Prabhutaratna, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, gave his approval: “Well done, well done, Nakshatrarajasamkusumitabhijna! That the Tathagata should have taught you a Dharma of such unimaginable virtues, and that you should have questioned the Tathagata, who is endowed with unimaginable virtues!”

cmp.note: 这一句梵文可以读成「如来为你讲了这样不可思议的功德之法」，也可以读成「你被如来称为具有不可思议功德的人」，不太确定。英文取前一种，与白话一致。白话的「因为你……」是加上去的，梵文只是用「和」把两件事并列。
cmp.en: This Sanskrit sentence can be read as “the Tathagata has taught you such a Dharma of unimaginable virtues” or as “you have been declared by the Tathagata to have unimaginable virtues”; it is not certain. The English takes the first reading, as the plain Chinese does. The plain Chinese 因为你… (“because you…”) adds a cause the Sanskrit lacks: the Sanskrit simply joins the two facts with “and.”

verses.en: Here ends the twenty-second chapter, called “The Former Life of Bhaishajyaraja,” in the glorious Dharma discourse of the Lotus of the True Dharma.

cmp.note: 梵本自编为第二十二品；本站是第 23 章，鸠摩罗什本是第二十三品《药王菩萨本事品》。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit numbers this the twenty-second chapter; on this site it is Chapter 23, and in Kumarajiva's version it is the twenty-third, 药王菩萨本事品 (Yàowáng Púsà Běnshì Pǐn).

verses.en: Then, at that moment, the Blessed One Shakyamuni, the Tathagata, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, sent out a light from the tuft of hair between his brows (the urna, one of the marks of a great man). By that light, in the east, hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas (huge numbers) of buddha-fields, as many as the grains of sand in eighteen Ganges Rivers, were filled with radiance. Beyond those buddha-fields, as many as the sands of eighteen Ganges Rivers, there is a world system called Vairocanarashmipratimandita (Adorned with Rays of Sunlight). There a Tathagata named Kamaladalavimalanakshatrarajasankusumitabhijna (“stainless as a lotus petal, a king among the stars, his higher knowledge in full flower”), an arhat, a fully awakened buddha, lives, abides and carries on, with an immense lifespan. Surrounded and led by an immense community of bodhisattvas, he was teaching the Dharma.

cmp.note: 梵文只说光从眉间白毫放出。鸠摩罗什写「放大人相肉髻光明，及放眉间白毫相光」，多了头顶肉髻的光；数目也不同，梵文是「十八条恒河沙数」的佛土，鸠摩罗什作「百八万亿那由他恒河沙等」。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says only that the light came from the tuft of hair between the brows. Kumarajiva writes that the Buddha sent out light from “the protuberance on his crown and the white tuft between his brows,” adding the crown; the numbers also differ: the Sanskrit has buddha-fields “as many as the sands of eighteen Ganges Rivers,” Kumarajiva 百八万亿那由他恒河沙等 (“as many as the sands of 108 myriad-million nayutas of Ganges Rivers”).

verses.en: The light that the Blessed One Shakyamuni, the Tathagata, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, sent out from the tuft of hair between his brows at that moment filled the world system Vairocanarashmipratimandita with a great radiance. And in that world system Vairocanarashmipratimandita there lived a bodhisattva, great being named Gadgadasvara, who had planted roots of goodness. He had seen rays of light like this from many Tathagatas, arhats, fully awakened buddhas before. And this bodhisattva, great being Gadgadasvara had attained many concentrations.

cmp.note: gadgada 是「结结巴巴、哽咽」，svara 是「声音」，梵文名字字面是「结巴之声」或「哽咽之声」，为什么这样命名，学者说法不一。鸠摩罗什译作「妙音」，意思完全不同，有学者推测他依据的本子里名字不同。白话只写了「妙音」加梵名，没有提字面意思；英文保留梵名不译。
cmp.en: Gadgada means “stammering, choked with emotion” and svara means “voice,” so the Sanskrit name literally means “Stammering Voice” or “Voice Choked with Feeling”; scholars disagree on why he is named this way. Kumarajiva calls him 妙音 (Miàoyīn, “Wonderful Sound”), a completely different meaning, some scholars suggest because his source text had a different name. The plain Chinese gives only 妙音 plus the Sanskrit name without mentioning its literal sense; the English keeps the Sanskrit name untranslated.

verses.en: For example, he had attained the concentration called Armlet on the Top of the Banner, the concentration called Lotus of the True Dharma, the concentration called Given by the Stainless, the concentration called Play of the King of Stars, the concentration called Without Support, the concentration called Seal of Knowledge, the concentration called Moon Lamp, the concentration called Skill in All Sounds, the concentration called Gathering of All Merit, the concentration called Full of Clear Faith, the concentration called Play of Supernatural Power, the concentration called Torch of Knowledge, the concentration called King of Arrays, the concentration called Stainless Radiance, the concentration called Stainless Womb, the concentration called All-Pervading Water, and the concentration called Turning of the Sun. And so on: the bodhisattva, great being Gadgadasvara had attained hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas of concentrations, as many as the grains of sand in the Ganges.

cmp.note: anilambha 字面「无所依、无所执」（白话「无所缘」）；apkṛtsna 是「水遍处」，一种以水为对象、观想水充满一切的禅修。鸠摩罗什把后者作「不共三昧」，和梵文不对应。名单里各三昧的名字多是意译，三种语言之间难免有出入。
cmp.en: Anilambha literally means “without support, not grasping” (the plain Chinese has 无所缘, “without object”); apkṛtsna is the “water kasina,” a meditation that takes water as its object and pictures water filling everything. Kumarajiva renders the latter as 不共三昧 (bùgòng sānmèi, “unshared samadhi”), which doesn't match the Sanskrit. Most of the concentration names in this list are translated by meaning, so some mismatch among the three languages is unavoidable.

verses.en: That light fell on the body of the bodhisattva, great being Gadgadasvara.

Then the bodhisattva, great being Gadgadasvara rose from his seat, draped his upper robe over one shoulder, set his right knee on the ground, joined his palms toward the Blessed One, and said to the Blessed One Kamaladalavimalanakshatrarajasankusumitabhijna, the Tathagata, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha: “Blessed One, I will go to that Saha world (our world of endurance) to see the Blessed One Shakyamuni, the Tathagata, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, to bow to him and wait on him; and to see Manjushri, the Prince (Kumarabhuta, “in the form of a youth”); to see the bodhisattva Bhaishajyaraja; to see the bodhisattva Pradanashura; to see the bodhisattva Nakshatrarajasankusumitabhijna; to see the bodhisattva Vishishtacharitra; to see the bodhisattva Vyuharaja; and to see the bodhisattva Bhaishajyarajasamudgata.”

cmp.note: kumārabhūta 字面是「作童子身的」，是文殊的固定称号，意思是他永远以少年的样子出现。鸠摩罗什译作「法王子」，强调他是法王（佛）的继承人；白话沿用「法王子」。英文用 the Prince 并加括号解释字面。
cmp.en: Kumārabhūta literally means “in the form of a youth,” Manjushri's standard title, meaning he always appears as a young man. Kumarajiva renders it 法王子 (fǎ wángzǐ, “prince of the Dharma King”), stressing that he is heir to the Dharma King (the Buddha); the plain Chinese keeps 法王子. The English uses “the Prince” and gives the literal meaning in parentheses.

verses.en: Then the Blessed One Kamaladalavimalanakshatrarajasankusumitabhijna, the Tathagata, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, said to the bodhisattva, great being Gadgadasvara: “Son of good family, when you go to that Saha world, don't start thinking little of it. That world, son of good family, is full of ups and downs, made of earth, strewn with black mountains and full of filth. And that Blessed One Shakyamuni, the Tathagata, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, is short in body, and those bodhisattvas are short in body too. But your body, son of good family, is 4,200,000 yojanas tall (a yojana is a day's journey, roughly ten kilometers), and my body, son of good family, is 6,800,000 yojanas tall.

cmp.note: 梵文是「四十二个十万由旬」，即四百二十万由旬，白话照算。鸠摩罗什作「四万二千由旬」，比梵文小一百倍；佛身六百八十万由旬两本倒一致。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says “forty-two hundred-thousands of yojanas,” that is, 4,200,000 yojanas, and the plain Chinese does the arithmetic correctly. Kumarajiva writes 四万二千由旬 (“42,000 yojanas”), a hundred times smaller than the Sanskrit; for the buddha's own body of 6,800,000 yojanas the two versions agree.

verses.en: And you, son of good family, are graceful, beautiful to look at, handsome, perfect in the loveliness of your supremely fine complexion, with a splendor beyond hundreds of thousands of merits. So, son of good family, when you go to that Saha world, don't start thinking little of the Tathagata, or of the bodhisattvas, or of that buddha-field.”

When he had said this, the bodhisattva, great being Gadgadasvara said to the Blessed One Kamaladalavimalanakshatrarajasankusumitabhijna, the Tathagata, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha: “Blessed One, I will do as the Tathagata commands. Blessed One, I will go to that Saha world through the Tathagata's empowering blessing, through the Tathagata's strength, through the Tathagata's play of powers, through the Tathagata's array, through the Tathagata's surpassing knowledge.”

Then, at that moment, without stirring from that buddha-field and without rising from his seat, the bodhisattva, great being Gadgadasvara entered a concentration of such a kind that the very moment he entered it, here in the Saha world, on Vulture Peak (Gridhrakuta), in front of the Tathagata's Dharma seat, there appeared eighty-four hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas of lotuses, with golden stalks and silver leaves, the color of kimshuka flowers (a bright red blossom).

cmp.note: 梵文是「八十四个百千俱胝那由他」朵莲花，白话照译；鸠摩罗什作「八万四千众宝莲华」，数目小了许多，还加了「金刚为须，甄叔迦宝以为其台」等细节。kiṃśuka 在梵文是一种开红花的树，梵文说莲花是这种花的颜色；鸠摩罗什把它变成一种宝石做的莲台。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit has “eighty-four hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas” of lotuses, and the plain Chinese follows it; Kumarajiva has 八万四千众宝莲华 (“84,000 jeweled lotuses”), a much smaller number, and adds details such as stamens of diamond. Kiṃśuka is a tree with bright red flowers, and the Sanskrit says the lotuses were that color; Kumarajiva turns it into a jewel, 甄叔迦宝 (zhēnshūjiā bǎo, “kimshuka gem”), forming the lotus seat.

verses.en: Then Manjushri the Prince, seeing this array of lotuses appear, said to the Blessed One Shakyamuni, the Tathagata, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha: “Blessed One, whose sign is this, that these eighty-four hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas of lotuses can be seen, with golden stalks and silver leaves, the color of kimshuka flowers?”

When he had said this, the Blessed One said to Manjushri the Prince: “Manjushri, from the eastern quarter, from the world system Vairocanarashmipratimandita, from the buddha-field of the Blessed One Kamaladalavimalanakshatrarajasankusumitabhijna, the Tathagata, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, the bodhisattva, great being Gadgadasvara, surrounded and led by eighty-four hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas of bodhisattvas, is coming to this Saha world to see me, to bow to me and to wait on me, and to hear this Dharma discourse, the Lotus of the True Dharma.” Then Manjushri the Prince said to the Blessed One: “Blessed One, what stock of good deeds has that son of good family built up, that through the good deeds he has done and accumulated he has attained such distinction?

And in what concentration, Blessed One, does that bodhisattva practice? Blessed One, may we hear about that concentration, so that we too, Blessed One, may practice in that concentration. And may we see that bodhisattva, great being, Blessed One: what his complexion is like, what his form is like, what his marks are, what his build is, how he conducts himself. So please, Blessed One, may the Tathagata make a sign of such a kind that, urged on by that sign, that bodhisattva, great being may come to this Saha world.”

Then the Blessed One Shakyamuni, the Tathagata, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, said to the Blessed One Prabhutaratna (“Many Jewels”), the Tathagata, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, who had entered final nirvana: “May the Blessed One make a sign of such a kind that the bodhisattva, great being Gadgadasvara may come to this Saha world.” Then, at that moment, the Blessed One Prabhutaratna, the Tathagata, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, who had entered final nirvana, made such a sign appear to urge on the bodhisattva, great being Gadgadasvara: “Come, son of good family, to this Saha world. Manjushri the Prince here would be glad to see you.”

cmp.note: 多宝如来早已般涅槃，却坐在宝塔中听法（见第 12 章），所以梵文特意加上「已般涅槃的」。这里梵文是释迦牟尼直接请多宝显瑞；鸠摩罗什写成释迦牟尼告诉文殊「多宝如来当为汝等而现其相」。
cmp.en: Prabhutaratna entered final nirvana long ago, yet sits in his jeweled stupa listening to the Dharma (see Chapter 12), which is why the Sanskrit pointedly adds “who had entered final nirvana.” Here in the Sanskrit Shakyamuni asks Prabhutaratna directly to make the sign; in Kumarajiva, Shakyamuni instead tells Manjushri that 多宝如来当为汝等而现其相 (“the Tathagata Prabhutaratna will show the sign for you”).

verses.en: Then the bodhisattva, great being Gadgadasvara bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One Kamaladalavimalanakshatrarajasankusumitabhijna, the Tathagata, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, walked around him three times keeping him on his right, and, together with those eighty-four hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas of bodhisattvas, surrounded and led by them, vanished from that world system Vairocanarashmipratimandita and came to this Saha world. The lands shook, lotuses rained down, and hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas of instruments played. His face had eyes like the petals of a blue lotus, his body was the color of gold, his whole person was adorned with hundreds of thousands of merits; he blazed with glory and shone with splendor, his limbs were patterned with the marks, and his body was as firm as Narayana's (a mighty god).

cmp.note: Nārāyaṇa 是毗湿奴的别名，以力大坚固著称，佛经常用「那罗延身」形容金刚不坏的身体。白话、鸠摩罗什都音译为「那罗延」，英文保留原名并注明是大力神。
cmp.en: Nārāyaṇa is another name of Vishnu, famous for strength and firmness; Buddhist texts often use “a body like Narayana's” for an indestructible body. The plain Chinese and Kumarajiva both transliterate it as 那罗延 (Nàluóyán), and the English keeps the name with a note that he is a mighty god.

verses.en: Mounted on a pavilion made of the seven precious substances, he came through the air at the height of seven palm trees, surrounded and led by a host of bodhisattvas. He approached this Saha world and Vulture Peak, the king of mountains. When he got there, he came down from the pavilion, took a pearl necklace worth a hundred thousand, and went to the Blessed One. When he came to him, he bowed his head at the Blessed One's feet, walked around him seven times keeping him on his right, and presented that pearl necklace to the Blessed One as an offering. Having presented it, he said to the Blessed One: “The Blessed One Kamaladalavimalanakshatrarajasankusumitabhijna, the Tathagata, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, asks after the Blessed One: whether you are free of illness and free of trouble, whether you get up easily, whether you are getting along, whether you are strong, whether you are living at ease.

And that Blessed One said this: 'Blessed One, are things bearable for you? Are you getting by? Are the elements of your body in balance? Are your living beings well behaved, easy to train, easy to heal? Are they pure in body? Are they not too driven by greed, not too driven by hatred, not too driven by delusion? Blessed One, are the beings not envious, not stingy, not lacking respect for mother and father, not lacking respect for renunciants and brahmins, not holding wrong views, not untamed in mind, not unguarded in their senses? Blessed One, have these beings of yours defeated Mara, the enemy? Blessed One, has Prabhutaratna, the Tathagata, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, who entered final nirvana, come to this Saha world to hear the Dharma, sitting inside the stupa made of the seven precious substances?'

cmp.w: kaccit te bhagavan kṣamaṇīyam, kaccid yāpanīyam
cmp.note: 这是佛经里比丘见面互相问候的固定套话：「还忍得住吗？还过得去吗？」英文 are things bearable / are you getting by 保留了这种家常口吻；鸠摩罗什作「世事可忍不」，也保留了。白话「您还能忍受吗」稍显生硬，但意思不错。
cmp.en: This is the stock greeting monks exchange in the sutras: “Is it bearable? Are you getting by?” The English “are things bearable / are you getting by” keeps the homely tone, and so does Kumarajiva's 世事可忍不 (shìshì kě rěn fǒu, “are worldly affairs bearable?”). The plain Chinese 您还能忍受吗 (“can you still endure?”) is a little stiff, but the meaning is right.

verses.en: And that Blessed One asks after the Blessed One Prabhutaratna, the Tathagata, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha: 'Blessed One, are things bearable for the Blessed One Prabhutaratna, the Tathagata, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha? Is he getting by? Blessed One, will Prabhutaratna, the Tathagata, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, remain for a long time?' Blessed One, we too would like to see the relic body of Prabhutaratna, the Tathagata, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha. So please, may the Blessed One, the Tathagata, show us the relic body of the Blessed One Prabhutaratna, the Tathagata, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha.”

cmp.note: dhātu 在这里是「舍利、遗骨」，vigraha 是「身形」，合起来是「舍利之身」：多宝如来已经涅槃，坐在塔中的是他的遗身。白话「舍利之身」、英文 relic body 都照字面；鸠摩罗什只说「欲见多宝佛身」。
cmp.en: Dhātu here means “relics, bodily remains,” and vigraha means “form, figure,” so together “relic body”: Prabhutaratna has entered nirvana, and what sits in the stupa is his preserved body. The plain Chinese 舍利之身 (shèlì zhī shēn, “relic body”) and the English “relic body” are both literal; Kumarajiva says only 欲见多宝佛身 (“wish to see Prabhutaratna Buddha's body”).

verses.en: Then the Blessed One Shakyamuni, the Tathagata, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, said to the Blessed One Prabhutaratna, the Tathagata, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, who had entered final nirvana: “Blessed One, this bodhisattva, great being Gadgadasvara wishes to see the Blessed One Prabhutaratna, the Tathagata, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, who has entered final nirvana.” Then the Blessed One Prabhutaratna, the Tathagata, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, said to the bodhisattva, great being Gadgadasvara: “Well done, well done, son of good family, that you have come here wishing to see the Blessed One Shakyamuni, the Tathagata, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, to hear this Dharma discourse, the Lotus of the True Dharma, and to see Manjushri the Prince.”

Then the bodhisattva, great being Padmashri (Lotus Glory) said to the Blessed One: “Blessed One, what kind of roots of goodness did the bodhisattva, great being Gadgadasvara plant in the past, and in the presence of which Tathagata?” Then the Blessed One Shakyamuni, the Tathagata, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, said to the bodhisattva, great being Padmashri: “Son of good family, long ago in the past, an eon countless, more than countless, vast, immeasurable, beyond measure ago, at that time a Tathagata named Meghadundubhisvararaja (King of the Sound of the Cloud Drum), an arhat, a fully awakened buddha, appeared in the world, perfect in knowledge and conduct, the Sugata (Well-Gone One), knower of the world, unsurpassed, trainer of people who can be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a buddha, a blessed one, in the world system called Sarvarupasamdarshana (Showing All Forms), in the eon called Priyadarshana (Lovely to See).

cmp.note: 字面是「云鼓音王」：megha 是云，dundubhi 是大鼓，合起来像「云中雷鼓」。鸠摩罗什作「云雷音王」，把鼓声译成雷声；白话沿用。英文译出字面 Cloud Drum。
cmp.en: Literally “King of the Sound of the Cloud Drum”: megha is “cloud” and dundubhi a great drum, so something like thunder drumming in the clouds. Kumarajiva writes 云雷音王 (Yún Léiyīn Wáng, “King of Cloud Thunder Sound”), turning the drum into thunder, and the plain Chinese keeps that name. The English gives the literal “Cloud Drum.”

verses.en: Son of good family, the bodhisattva, great being Gadgadasvara honored that Blessed One Meghadundubhisvararaja, the Tathagata, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, with the playing of a hundred thousand instruments for 1,200,000 years, and gave him eighty-four thousand vessels made of the seven precious substances. It was there, son of good family, under the teaching of the Tathagata Meghadundubhisvararaja, that the bodhisattva, great being Gadgadasvara gained the glory he has now.

cmp.note: 梵文是「十二个十万年」，即一百二十万年，白话照算；鸠摩罗什作「万二千岁」（一万二千年），少了一百倍。上文妙音的身高也是这样，鸠摩罗什的数字常比梵本小。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says “twelve hundred-thousands of years,” that is, 1,200,000 years, and the plain Chinese does the arithmetic correctly; Kumarajiva has 万二千岁 (“12,000 years”), a hundred times less. The same happened with Gadgadasvara's height above: Kumarajiva's numbers are often smaller than the Sanskrit's.

verses.en: Now, son of good family, you may have some doubt, uncertainty or hesitation: was the bodhisattva, great being named Gadgadasvara at that time, who made those offerings to the Blessed One Meghadundubhisvararaja, the Tathagata, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, and gave those eighty-four thousand vessels, someone else? Son of good family, you should not see it that way. Why? It was this very bodhisattva, great being Gadgadasvara, son of good family, who made those offerings to the Blessed One Meghadundubhisvararaja, the Tathagata, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, and gave those eighty-four thousand vessels. That is how, son of good family, the bodhisattva, great being Gadgadasvara has waited on many buddhas, has planted roots of goodness with many hundreds of thousands of buddhas, and has done the preparatory work for buddhahood.

And this bodhisattva, great being Gadgadasvara has seen buddhas, blessed ones, as many as the grains of sand in the Ganges. Padmashri, do you see this bodhisattva, great being Gadgadasvara?” Padmashri said: “I see him, Blessed One. I see him, Sugata.” The Blessed One said: “Padmashri, this bodhisattva, great being Gadgadasvara has taught this Dharma discourse, the Lotus of the True Dharma, in many forms.

For example: sometimes in the form of Brahma, sometimes in the form of Rudra (Shiva), sometimes in the form of Shakra (Indra, king of the gods), sometimes in the form of Ishvara (“the Lord,” a great god), sometimes in the form of a general, sometimes in the form of Vaishravana (god of wealth and guardian of the north), sometimes in the form of a wheel-turning king (a world emperor), sometimes in the form of a local king, sometimes in the form of a guild master, sometimes in the form of a householder, sometimes in the form of a townsman, sometimes in the form of a brahmin, he taught this Dharma discourse, the Lotus of the True Dharma. Sometimes in the form of a monk, sometimes in the form of a nun, sometimes in the form of a layman, sometimes in the form of a laywoman, sometimes in the form of a guild master's wife, sometimes in the form of a householder's wife, sometimes in the form of a townsman's wife, sometimes in the form of a boy, sometimes in the form of a girl, the bodhisattva, great being Gadgadasvara taught this Dharma discourse, the Lotus of the True Dharma, to living beings.

cmp.note: 梵文名单里有楼陀罗（湿婆），鸠摩罗什没有，改成「自在天、大自在天」两项；naigama 是城镇里的商人或市民，鸠摩罗什译成「宰官」（官员），中国读者熟悉的「宰官身」在梵文这一品其实是市民。这份名单和下一章观世音的「三十三身」很像，英文、白话都照梵文。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit list includes Rudra (Shiva), whom Kumarajiva omits, giving instead two entries, 自在天 and 大自在天 (“Ishvara” and “Maheshvara”); naigama means a townsman or merchant, which Kumarajiva renders as 宰官 (zǎiguān, “official”), so the “official's body” familiar to Chinese readers is, in the Sanskrit of this chapter, a townsman. This list closely resembles Avalokiteshvara's thirty-three forms in the next chapter; the English and the plain Chinese follow the Sanskrit.

verses.en: Son of good family, through this many displays of form the bodhisattva, great being Gadgadasvara taught this Dharma discourse, the Lotus of the True Dharma, to living beings. To some he even taught it in the form of a yaksha; to some in the form of a god, to some in the form of a garuda, to some in the form of a kinnara, to some in the form of a mahoraga, the bodhisattva, great being Gadgadasvara taught this Dharma discourse, the Lotus of the True Dharma, to living beings. Even for beings born in the hells, in animal wombs, in the world of Yama (lord of the dead), or in places where there is no chance to practice, the bodhisattva, great being Gadgadasvara becomes a rescuer by teaching this Dharma discourse, the Lotus of the True Dharma.

cmp.note: 录文是 sura「天神」，白话译作「阿修罗」，等于把它读成 asura。按语法，keṣāṃcit 后若接 asura 应写作 keṣāṃcid asura，所以录文本身是 sura。英文照录文译作 god；但前后都是夜叉、迦楼罗等八部众，读成 asura 也说得通。
cmp.en: The transcription reads sura, “god,” whereas the plain Chinese has 阿修罗 (āxiūluó, “asura”), reading it as asura. By the rules of Sanskrit sound-joining, keṣāṃcit followed by asura would be written keṣāṃcid asura, so the transcription itself says sura. The English follows the transcription with “god”; but since the surrounding list is yakshas, garudas and the other classes of non-human beings, reading asura is also defensible.

cmp.note: akṣaṇa「没有时机」，指生在无法遇佛闻法的处境（汉译「八难」）。白话「没有修行机会之处」、英文 places where there is no chance to practice 都译出了意思；鸠摩罗什作「众难处」。
cmp.en: Akṣaṇa, “no right moment,” means being born where one cannot meet a buddha or hear the Dharma (in Chinese the 八难, bā nàn, “eight difficult places”). The plain Chinese 没有修行机会之处 (“places with no chance to practice”) and the English both convey this; Kumarajiva writes 众难处 (zhòng nàn chù, “the many places of difficulty”).

verses.en: He even took on the form of a woman to teach this Dharma discourse, the Lotus of the True Dharma, to beings living in the inner palace (the women's quarters). He taught the Dharma to beings in this Saha world. Padmashri, the bodhisattva, great being Gadgadasvara is indeed a rescuer of the beings born in the Saha world. Right here in this Saha world, the bodhisattva, great being Gadgadasvara teaches this Dharma discourse, the Lotus of the True Dharma, to living beings through this many forms and appearances, and yet this good man loses none of his supernatural power and none of his wisdom. Son of good family, through this many lights of knowledge the bodhisattva, great being Gadgadasvara is known in this Saha world.

cmp.note: antaḥpura 是王宫的内宫，也就是后妃女眷住的地方，男子不能进入，所以菩萨化作女身进去说法。白话「内宫」、英文 inner palace 加了括号说明女眷住处，鸠摩罗什作「王后宫」。
cmp.en: Antaḥpura is the inner palace, the women's quarters where the queens and court ladies live and men may not enter, which is why the bodhisattva takes a woman's form to teach there. The plain Chinese says 内宫 (nèigōng, “inner palace”), the English adds a note in parentheses about the women's quarters, and Kumarajiva writes 王后宫 (wáng hòugōng, “the king's rear palace”).

verses.en: And in other world systems, as many as the grains of sand in the Ganges, he teaches the Dharma in the form of a bodhisattva to beings who are to be trained by a bodhisattva. He teaches the Dharma in the form of a disciple (shravaka) to beings who are to be trained by a disciple. He teaches the Dharma in the form of a solitary buddha (pratyekabuddha) to beings who are to be trained by a solitary buddha. He teaches the Dharma in the form of a Tathagata to beings who are to be trained by a Tathagata. He even shows a Tathagata's relics to beings who are to be trained by a Tathagata's relics. He even shows himself in final nirvana to beings who are to be trained by final nirvana. Padmashri, that is the power of knowledge the bodhisattva, great being Gadgadasvara has attained.

cmp.note: vaineya 是「应被调伏、可以教化的」。这一句「应以某身得度者，即现某身」的格式，正是下一章观世音菩萨普门品「三十三应身」的原型。白话「应以……调伏教化」，英文 who are to be trained by，都按梵文的被动意味译出。
cmp.en: Vaineya means “to be trained, open to guidance.” This pattern, “to those who are to be trained by such-and-such a form, he shows that form,” is the model for Avalokiteshvara's “thirty-three responsive forms” in the next chapter. The plain Chinese 应以……调伏教化 (“ought to be tamed and taught by”) and the English “who are to be trained by” both keep the passive sense of the Sanskrit.

verses.en: Then the bodhisattva, great being Padmashri said to the Blessed One: “Blessed One, this bodhisattva, great being Gadgadasvara has planted roots of goodness indeed. Blessed One, what is this concentration, abiding in which the bodhisattva, great being Gadgadasvara has trained so many beings?” When he had said this, the Blessed One Shakyamuni, the Tathagata, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, said to the bodhisattva, great being Padmashri: “Son of good family, it is the concentration called Showing All Forms. Abiding in this concentration, the bodhisattva, great being Gadgadasvara has done such immeasurable good for living beings.”

While this chapter on Gadgadasvara was being taught, all of the eighty-four hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas of bodhisattvas who had come to this Saha world with the bodhisattva, great being Gadgadasvara attained the concentration called Showing All Forms. And in this Saha world, bodhisattvas, great beings beyond counting attained the concentration called Showing All Forms.

Then the bodhisattva, great being Gadgadasvara, having made vast and abundant offerings to the Blessed One Shakyamuni, the Tathagata, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, and to the relic stupa of the Blessed One Prabhutaratna, the Tathagata, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, mounted the pavilion made of the seven precious substances again. As the lands shook, lotuses rained down, and hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas of instruments played, he went back to his own buddha-field, surrounded and led by those eighty-four hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas of bodhisattvas. When he arrived, he said to the Blessed One Kamaladalavimalanakshatrarajasankusumitabhijna, the Tathagata, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha: “Blessed One, I have done good for living beings in the Saha world.

I have seen the relic stupa of the Blessed One Prabhutaratna, the Tathagata, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, and bowed to it. I have seen the Blessed One Shakyamuni, the Tathagata, and bowed to him. I have seen Manjushri the Prince. I have seen the bodhisattva, great being Bhaishajyaraja, who has attained the strength and speed of energy, and the bodhisattva, great being Pradanashura. And all those eighty-four hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas of bodhisattvas have attained the concentration called Showing All Forms.”

cmp.note: 梵文这个词是药王菩萨的形容语「得精进力与迅捷的」，白话、英文都这样译。鸠摩罗什把它当成另一位菩萨的名字「得勤精进力菩萨」，于是名单里多了一位菩萨。
cmp.en: In the Sanskrit this word describes Bhaishajyaraja, “who has attained the strength and speed of energy,” and the plain Chinese and the English both take it that way. Kumarajiva treats it as the name of a separate bodhisattva, 得勤精进力菩萨 (Dé Qín Jīngjìn Lì Púsà, “Bodhisattva Who Has Gained the Power of Diligent Effort”), so his list has one bodhisattva more.

verses.en: While this chapter on the coming and going of the bodhisattva, great being Gadgadasvara was being taught, forty-two thousand bodhisattvas gained acceptance of the truth that things do not arise (anutpattika-dharma-kshanti, the calm certainty that nothing truly comes into being), and the bodhisattva, great being Padmashri gained the concentration called Lotus of the True Dharma.

cmp.note: 汉译「无生法忍」，kṣānti 本义是「忍耐」，在这里是「安然接受、确信」：对「诸法本来不生」这件事心里完全安住。英文 acceptance 比中文的「忍」更接近原意；中文读者容易把「忍」理解成咬牙忍受。另外，得忍的人梵文是「菩萨」，鸠摩罗什作「天子」。
cmp.en: In Chinese this is 无生法忍 (wúshēng fǎ rěn, “forbearance regarding the unborn nature of things”). Kṣānti originally means “patience,” but here it means calm acceptance and certainty: the mind settles completely on the truth that nothing truly arises. The English “acceptance” is closer to the original than the Chinese 忍 (rěn), which readers easily take as gritting one's teeth and bearing it. Also, those who gain it are “bodhisattvas” in the Sanskrit and 天子 (tiānzǐ, “sons of the gods”) in Kumarajiva.

verses.en: Here ends the twenty-third chapter, called “Gadgadasvara,” in the glorious Dharma discourse of the Lotus of the True Dharma.

cmp.note: 梵本把这一品算作第二十三品，本站算第 24 章，鸠摩罗什本也是第二十四品「妙音菩萨品」。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit counts this as the twenty-third chapter; this site counts it as Chapter 24, which is also its place in Kumarajiva's version, as chapter 24, “The Bodhisattva Wonderful Sound.”

chapters.title: Chapter 25 · Avalokiteshvara, the Gateway Facing Every Direction

verses.en: Then the bodhisattva Akshayamati (“Endless Mind”), a great being, rose from his seat, put his upper robe over one shoulder, set his right knee on the ground, joined his palms toward the Blessed One, and said to him: “Blessed One, why is the bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara, the great being, called Avalokiteshvara (“the Lord Who Looks Down on the world”)?” When he had said this, the Blessed One said to the bodhisattva Akshayamati, the great being: “Son of good family, here in this world, however many hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas of beings (kotis and nayutas are both enormous numbers) are going through sufferings, if they hear the name of the bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara, the great being, they will all be freed from that whole mass of suffering.”

cmp.note: 梵文是 avalokita「观看、俯视」加 īśvara「主、自在者」，字面是「俯视（世间）的主」。玄奘译「观自在」就是照这个形式。鸠摩罗什译「观世音」，对应的是更早的一种写法 avalokitasvara（svara 是「声音」），中亚出土的梵文残卷里见过这个形式。英文照现存梵文译 the Lord Who Looks Down；白话沿用华人熟悉的「观世音」，括号里注了玄奘的「观自在」。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit is avalokita, “looking, looking down,” plus īśvara, “lord, master”: literally “the lord who looks down (on the world).” Xuanzang's 观自在 (Guānzìzài, “the one who observes with mastery”) follows this form. Kumarajiva's 观世音 (Guānshìyīn, “the one who observes the world's sounds”) matches an older spelling, avalokitasvara, where svara means “sound”; that form turns up in Sanskrit manuscript fragments from Central Asia. The English follows the surviving Sanskrit; the plain Chinese keeps the familiar 观世音 and mentions Xuanzang's 观自在 in brackets.

cmp.note: 梵文只说「听到他的名号」就能解脱，这里没有解释名字的由来。鸠摩罗什本写「一心称名，观世音菩萨即时观其音声，皆得解脱」，多了「一心称名」和「观其音声」，把「观世音」讲成「观看世间的声音」。这是华人最熟的一句，但梵文里没有。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says only that hearing his name sets beings free; it doesn't explain the name here. Kumarajiva adds 一心称名 (yìxīn chēng míng, “call his name with a single mind”) and 观其音声 (guān qí yīnshēng, “he observes the sound of their voices”), which turns the name into “the one who observes the world's sounds.” It is the line Chinese readers know best, but it isn't in the Sanskrit.

verses.en: “Son of good family, those beings who keep in mind the name of the bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara, the great being, even if they fall into a great mass of fire, will all be freed from that great mass of fire by the radiant power of the bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara, the great being. And again, son of good family, if beings being swept away by rivers cry out to the bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara, the great being, every one of those rivers will give those beings a place to stand.”

“And again, son of good family, suppose hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas of beings had boarded a ship in the middle of the ocean, carrying the treasures they had gathered: raw gold and worked gold, gems, pearls, diamonds, beryl, conch shell, crystal, coral, emerald, musaragalva (a precious stone, perhaps agate), red pearls and more. Suppose a black storm wind threw their ship onto the island of the rakshasis (man-eating demonesses), and among them there was even one single being who cried out to the bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara, the great being. They would all be freed from that island of the rakshasis. Son of good family, it is for this reason that the bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara, the great being, is called Avalokiteshvara.”

cmp.note: 梵文是「罗刹女之岛」，rākṣasī 是阴性，指吃人的女鬼。英文 rakshasis、白话「罗刹女」都保留了性别；鸠摩罗什写「罗刹鬼国」，看不出是女鬼。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit is “the island of the rākṣasīs,” a feminine form meaning man-eating demonesses. The English “rakshasis” and the plain Chinese 罗刹女 (luóchà nǚ, “rakshasa women”) both keep the gender; Kumarajiva writes 罗刹鬼国 (luóchà guǐ guó, “land of rakshasa ghosts”), where it disappears.

verses.en: “Son of good family, if someone who has been handed over for execution cries out to the bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara, the great being, the swords of the executioners will shatter. And again, son of good family, if this great trichiliocosm (a vast universe of a billion worlds) were full of yakshas and rakshasas (two kinds of fierce spirits), then once someone takes up the name of Avalokiteshvara, the great being, those spirits, for all their malice, would not even be able to see him. And again, son of good family, if some being were bound with shackles and fetters of wood or iron, whether guilty or innocent, then once he takes up the name of the bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara, the great being, those shackles and fetters quickly open up. Son of good family, such is the power of the bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara, the great being.”

cmp.note: 梵文是恶鬼「连看都看不见他」。鸠摩罗什写「尚不能以恶眼视之，况复加害」，变成「连用恶眼看他都做不到，何况加害」，多了「恶眼」和后半句的推论。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says the evil spirits “cannot even see him.” Kumarajiva writes 尚不能以恶眼视之，况复加害 (“they cannot even look at him with evil eyes, let alone harm him”), adding the “evil eyes” and the “let alone” that follows.

verses.en: “Son of good family, suppose this great trichiliocosm were full of swindlers, enemies and robbers with swords in their hands, and a caravan leader set out through it with a great caravan, rich in priceless jewels. As they went along they would see those robbers, swindlers and enemies with swords in hand, and seeing them they would be frightened and terrified, and feel they had nowhere to turn. Then the caravan leader would say to the caravan: ‘Don't be afraid, sons of good family, don't be afraid! All of you, with one voice, call out to the bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara, the great being, the Giver of Fearlessness. Then you will quickly be freed from this danger of robbers, this danger of enemies.’”

cmp.note: 梵文是商队首领自己开口，叫大家一齐呼喊「施予无畏者」（abhayaṃdada，观世音的一个称号）。鸠摩罗什写「其中一人作是唱言」，说话的是商人中的某一个；称号也化成一句解释「是菩萨能以无畏施于众生」。
cmp.en: In the Sanskrit it is the caravan leader himself who speaks, telling everyone to call out to “the Giver of Fearlessness” (abhayaṃdada, one of Avalokiteshvara's titles). Kumarajiva writes 其中一人作是唱言 (“one of them called out”), so the speaker is just one of the merchants, and the title becomes an explanation: 是菩萨能以无畏施于众生 (“this bodhisattva can give fearlessness to beings”).

verses.en: “Then the whole caravan, with one voice, would cry out to Avalokiteshvara: ‘Homage, homage to him, the Giver of Fearlessness, Avalokiteshvara, the bodhisattva, the great being!’ Just by taking up his name, the caravan would be freed from every fear. Son of good family, such is the power of the bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara, the great being.”

cmp.note: 梵文 namo「礼敬」在这里连说两遍，后面还带着「施予无畏者」的称号。鸠摩罗什把 namo 音译成「南无」，只说一遍，于是有了华人最熟的那句「南无观世音菩萨」。英文 Homage、白话「礼敬」是意译。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says namo, “homage,” twice, followed by the title “Giver of Fearlessness.” Kumarajiva transliterates namo as 南无 (nāmó), says it once, and so produced the phrase Chinese speakers know best: 南无观世音菩萨 (nāmó Guānshìyīn púsà, “homage to the bodhisattva Guanshiyin”). The English “homage” and the plain Chinese 礼敬 (lǐjìng, “pay respects”) translate the meaning instead.

verses.en: “Son of good family, beings driven by desire become free of desire by paying homage to the bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara, the great being. Beings driven by hatred become free of hatred by paying homage to the bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara, the great being. Beings driven by delusion become free of delusion by paying homage to the bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara, the great being. Son of good family, that is how great the supernatural power of the bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara, the great being, is.”

cmp.note: rāga 字面是「染色」，指广义的贪爱、执着，不只是性欲。鸠摩罗什译「婬欲」，把范围缩到了性欲；白话「贪欲」、英文 desire 都取广义。另外梵文说的是「礼敬」，鸠摩罗什写「常念恭敬」，多了「常念」。
cmp.en: Rāga literally means “coloring, dye” and covers craving and attachment in general, not just sexual desire. Kumarajiva renders it 婬欲 (yínyù, “lust”), narrowing it to sex; the plain Chinese 贪欲 (tānyù, “greed, craving”) and the English “desire” both keep the broad sense. Also, the Sanskrit says “paying homage,” while Kumarajiva writes 常念恭敬 (cháng niàn gōngjìng, “constantly keep him in mind and revere him”), adding the “constantly keep in mind.”

verses.en: “Son of good family, if a woman who wants a son pays homage to the bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara, the great being, a son will be born to her: handsome, lovely, good to look at, with all the marks of a fine boy, loved by many, charming, and one who has planted roots of goodness. If she longs for a daughter, a daughter will be born to her: beautiful, lovely, good to look at, with the finest, most radiant complexion, with all the marks of a fine girl, loved by many, charming, and one who has planted roots of goodness. Son of good family, such is the power of the bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara, the great being.”

cmp.note: 梵文形容儿子和女儿的话几乎一样：都俊美可爱、人人喜爱、种下了善根，女儿还多了「容貌极其美好」。鸠摩罗什写成「福德智慧之男」「端正有相之女」：儿子有福德、有智慧，女儿只剩端正好看。这个分别是汉译带进来的，梵文里没有；英文、白话照梵文。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit describes the son and the daughter in almost the same words: both are good-looking, loved by many, and have planted roots of goodness, and the daughter is also given “the finest complexion.” Kumarajiva writes 福德智慧之男 (“a son with merit and wisdom”) and 端正有相之女 (“a daughter who is well-formed and good-looking”): the son gets merit and wisdom, the daughter only looks. That difference comes from the Chinese translation, not the Sanskrit; the English and the plain Chinese follow the Sanskrit.

verses.en: “Son of good family, for those who pay homage to the bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara, the great being, and keep his name in mind, the result is never in vain. Son of good family, suppose one person pays homage to the bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara, the great being, and keeps his name in mind; and another pays homage to buddhas, blessed ones, as many as the grains of sand in sixty-two Ganges rivers, and keeps their names in mind, and honors that many buddhas, blessed ones, while they are alive and present in the world, with robes, alms food, beds and seats, and medicines and supplies for the sick. What do you think, son of good family: how much merit would that son or daughter of good family produce from this?”

cmp.note: 梵文是「六十二条恒河沙数那么多的佛世尊」。鸠摩罗什写「六十二亿恒河沙菩萨」：佛变成了菩萨，数目也多了「亿」。英文、白话照梵文。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says “buddhas, blessed ones, as many as the sands of sixty-two Ganges rivers.” Kumarajiva writes 六十二亿恒河沙菩萨 (“bodhisattvas as many as the sands of six billion two hundred million Ganges rivers”): the buddhas become bodhisattvas, and the number gains a “hundred million.” The English and the plain Chinese follow the Sanskrit.

verses.en: When he had said this, the bodhisattva Akshayamati, the great being, said to the Blessed One: “A great deal, Blessed One; a great deal, Sugata (“Well-Gone One,” a title of the Buddha). That son or daughter of good family would produce a great deal of merit from this.” The Blessed One said: “Son of good family, the merit made by honoring that many buddhas, blessed ones, and the merit of someone who pays homage even just once to the bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara, the great being, and keeps his name in mind, are equal on both sides: neither is more, neither is greater.”

“The one who honors those buddhas, blessed ones, as many as the sands of sixty-two Ganges rivers, and keeps their names in mind, and the one who pays homage to the bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara, the great being, and keeps his name in mind: these two heaps of merit could not easily be used up even in hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas of eons (an eon, or kalpa, is an immense stretch of cosmic time). Son of good family, that is how immeasurable the merit is of keeping in mind the name of the bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara, the great being.”

Then the bodhisattva Akshayamati, the great being, said to the Blessed One: “Blessed One, how does the bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara, the great being, move about in this Saha world (our world, “the world of endurance”)? How does he teach the Dharma to beings? And what is the range of the skillful means of the bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara, the great being?” When he had said this, the Blessed One said to the bodhisattva Akshayamati, the great being: “Son of good family, there are world systems in which the bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara, the great being, teaches the Dharma to beings in the form of a buddha. There are world systems in which the bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara, the great being, teaches the Dharma to beings in the form of a bodhisattva. To some beings the bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara, the great being, teaches the Dharma in the form of a solitary buddha (pratyekabuddha, one who awakens on his own).”

cmp.note: rūpa 是「形象、样子」，「以佛的 rūpa 说法」就是现出佛的样子来说法。鸠摩罗什译「现佛身」，用「身」字；白话「形象」、英文 in the form of 都照梵文。
cmp.en: Rūpa means “form, appearance”: teaching “in the rūpa of a buddha” means appearing as a buddha to teach. Kumarajiva renders it 现佛身 (xiàn fó shēn, “manifests a buddha body”), using the word “body”; the plain Chinese 形象 (xíngxiàng, “form, image”) and the English “in the form of” follow the Sanskrit.

verses.en: “To some beings the bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara, the great being, teaches the Dharma in the form of a disciple (shravaka). To some he teaches the Dharma in the form of Brahma (king of the Brahma heavens). To some he teaches the Dharma in the form of Shakra (Indra, king of the gods of the Thirty-Three). To some he teaches the Dharma in the form of a gandharva (a heavenly musician). To beings who are to be trained by a yaksha, he teaches the Dharma in the form of a yaksha. To beings to be trained by Ishvara (“the Lord,” a great god), he teaches in the form of Ishvara; to beings to be trained by Maheshvara (“the Great Lord,” that is, Shiva), he teaches the Dharma in the form of Maheshvara. To beings to be trained by a wheel-turning king (an ideal king who rules the whole world), he teaches the Dharma in the form of a wheel-turning king.”

cmp.note: 梵文本里「以乾闼婆的形象为众生说法」这一句一字不差地重复了两遍，应是抄写时的重复。英文、白话都只译一次。
cmp.en: In the Sanskrit text the sentence “teaches the Dharma to beings in the form of a gandharva” appears twice, word for word, most likely a copying slip. The English and the plain Chinese translate it only once.

cmp.note: vaineya 是「可以被（某种身份的人）调伏、教化的」。从夜叉开始，梵文改用「对该由夜叉教化的众生，就以夜叉的形象说法」这个句式。鸠摩罗什全段统一成「应以……身得度者，即现……身而为说法」，从头到尾都是这个句式。
cmp.en: Vaineya means “able to be trained or guided (by someone of a given kind).” From the yaksha onward the Sanskrit switches to the pattern “to beings to be trained by a yaksha, he teaches in the form of a yaksha.” Kumarajiva uses one pattern for the whole list: 应以……身得度者，即现……身而为说法 (“to those who should be saved by a ... body, he shows a ... body and teaches them”).

verses.en: “To beings to be trained by a pishacha (a flesh-eating goblin), he teaches the Dharma in the form of a pishacha. To beings to be trained by Vaishravana (the guardian king of the north), he teaches the Dharma in the form of Vaishravana. To beings to be trained by a general, he teaches the Dharma in the form of a general. To beings to be trained by a brahmin (a member of the Indian priestly class), he teaches the Dharma in the form of a brahmin. To beings to be trained by Vajrapani (the protector who holds the vajra, the thunderbolt), he teaches the Dharma in the form of Vajrapani.
