Son of good family, that is how the bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara, the great being, is endowed with qualities beyond thought. So then, sons of good family, honor the bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara, the great being. Son of good family, this bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara, the great being, gives fearlessness to beings who are afraid. That is why, here in this Saha world, he is called the Giver of Fearlessness.”

cmp.note: 梵文从第 12 段到这里一共列出十六种形象：佛、菩萨、独觉、声闻、梵天、帝释、乾闼婆、夜叉、自在天、大自在天、转轮圣王、毕舍遮、毗沙门、将军、婆罗门、执金刚。鸠摩罗什本列的是后来中文里说的「三十三身」：多了小王、长者、居士、宰官、比丘比丘尼、优婆塞优婆夷、妇女、童男童女、天龙八部等，梵文里的转轮圣王、毕舍遮却没有。英文、白话照梵文。
cmp.en: From verse 12 to here the Sanskrit lists sixteen forms: buddha, bodhisattva, solitary buddha, disciple, Brahma, Shakra, gandharva, yaksha, Ishvara, Maheshvara, wheel-turning king, pishacha, Vaishravana, general, brahmin and Vajrapani. Kumarajiva's list is the one later known in Chinese as the 三十三身 (sānshísān shēn, “thirty-three bodies”): it adds lesser kings, elders, householders, officials, monks and nuns, laymen and laywomen, wives, boys and girls, the eight kinds of gods and spirits and more, while the Sanskrit's wheel-turning king and pishacha are missing. The English and the plain Chinese follow the Sanskrit.

verses.en: Then the bodhisattva Akshayamati, the great being, said to the Blessed One: “Blessed One, we will give the bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara, the great being, a gift for the Dharma, a cloth offering for the Dharma.” The Blessed One said: “Son of good family, do so whenever you think the time is right.” Then the bodhisattva Akshayamati, the great being, took from his own neck a pearl necklace worth a hundred thousand and offered it to the bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara, the great being, as a Dharma offering, saying: “Good man, accept this Dharma offering from me.” But he would not accept it. Then the bodhisattva Akshayamati, the great being, said to the bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara, the great being: “Son of good family, accept this pearl necklace out of compassion for us.”

cmp.note: ācchāda 原义是「覆盖物、衣料」，dharmācchāda 就是为了谢法而献上的衣料，泛指谢法的礼物。白话「法的赠衣」、英文 a cloth offering for the Dharma 都照字面；鸠摩罗什译「法施」，衣料的意思不见了。
cmp.en: Ācchāda originally means “covering, cloth,” so dharmācchāda is a gift of cloth offered in thanks for the Dharma, and by extension any such thank-offering. The plain Chinese 法的赠衣 (“a garment given for the Dharma”) and the English “a cloth offering for the Dharma” are literal; Kumarajiva renders it 法施 (fǎ shī, “Dharma gift”), and the cloth disappears.

verses.en: Then the bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara, the great being, accepted the pearl necklace from the bodhisattva Akshayamati, the great being, out of compassion for the bodhisattva Akshayamati, the great being, and out of compassion for the four assemblies (monks, nuns, laymen and laywomen) and for the gods, nagas, yakshas, gandharvas, asuras, garudas, kinnaras and mahoragas (various divine beings and spirits), humans and non-humans. Having accepted it, he divided it into two portions. He gave one portion to the Blessed One Shakyamuni, and brought the second portion to the jeweled stupa of the Blessed One Prabhutaratna (“Many Jewels,” a buddha of the distant past whose stupa appeared in Chapter 12), the Tathagata, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha. “Son of good family, it is with such miraculous displays that the bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara, the great being, moves about in this Saha world.”

cmp.note: 梵文是观世音自己出于怜悯收下璎珞。鸠摩罗什本多了一句佛的吩咐：「当愍此无尽意菩萨及四众……受是璎珞」，观世音是听了佛的话才收下的。
cmp.en: In the Sanskrit, Avalokiteshvara accepts the necklace on his own, out of compassion. Kumarajiva adds an instruction from the Buddha, 当愍此无尽意菩萨及四众……受是璎珞 (“have compassion on Akshayamati and the four assemblies ... and accept this necklace”), so Avalokiteshvara accepts because the Buddha told him to.

verses.en: Then, at that time, the Blessed One spoke these verses:

cmp.note: 梵文说下面的偈颂是世尊说的。鸠摩罗什本是「无尽意菩萨以偈问」，变成一问一答。另外，鸠摩罗什最初译的这一品没有偈颂；现在流通本里的偈颂，一般认为是隋代阇那崛多等人补译后编进去的。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says the Blessed One spoke the verses that follow. Kumarajiva's text has 无尽意菩萨以偈问 (“the bodhisattva Akshayamati asked in verse”), making them a question and answer. Also, Kumarajiva's original translation of this chapter had no verses at all; the verses in today's common edition are generally thought to have been translated later, in the Sui dynasty, by Jnanagupta and others, and added in.

verses.en: Akshayamati, wanting to know the reason, asked Chitradhvaja (“Bright Banner”) about this: “For what cause is this son of the Victor (that is, a bodhisattva) called Avalokiteshvara?”

cmp.note: 偈颂的梵文语法松散，这一句也可读成「妙幢问无尽意」；但下一段明说是妙幢开口作答，所以白话、英文都读成无尽意问妙幢。鸠摩罗什本的偈颂里没有「妙幢」这个名字，写成「世尊妙相具，我今重问彼」，问的对象成了世尊；「妙相」或许就是从 citradhvaja「彩色的幢」来的。
cmp.en: The grammar of the verses is loose, and this line could also be read as “Chitradhvaja asked Akshayamati.” But the next verse says plainly that Chitradhvaja is the one who answers, so the plain Chinese and the English both read it as Akshayamati asking Chitradhvaja. Kumarajiva's verses have no Chitradhvaja at all: they say 世尊妙相具，我今重问彼 (“World-Honored One, endowed with wonderful marks, I now ask again about him”), so the question goes to the Buddha. The “wonderful marks” may come from citradhvaja, “bright-colored banner.”

verses.en: Then Chitradhvaja looked around in every direction and said to Akshayamati, that ocean of vows: “Listen to the practice of Avalokiteshvara.”

cmp.note: 梵文「誓愿之海」紧挨着无尽意的名字，白话、英文都把它当作称呼无尽意。鸠摩罗什写「弘誓深如海」，放在下一首里，说的是观世音的誓愿。
cmp.en: In the Sanskrit, “ocean of vows” sits right next to Akshayamati's name, so the plain Chinese and the English take it as describing him. Kumarajiva writes 弘誓深如海 (hóng shì shēn rú hǎi, “his great vow is as deep as the sea”) in the next stanza, where it describes Avalokiteshvara's vow.

verses.en: “Through many hundreds of kotis of eons beyond thought, in the presence of many thousands of kotis of buddhas, how he purified his vow: hear that from me in brief.”
“Hearing of him, and seeing him too, and remembering him in due order: for living beings here, none of this is ever in vain. It destroys all suffering and the sorrows of existence.”
“If someone with a mind full of hate pushes him into a pit of fire to kill him, when he remembers Avalokiteshvara the fire dies down, as if doused with water.”

cmp.note: 梵文只说火「像被浇了水一样熄灭」。鸠摩罗什作「火坑变成池」，后来民间说成「火坑变莲池」；变成池子的画面是汉译的，梵文没有。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says only that the fire “dies down as if sprinkled with water.” Kumarajiva writes 火坑变成池 (huǒkēng biàn chéng chí, “the fire pit turns into a pool”), which popular Chinese later turned into “the fire pit becomes a lotus pond.” The image of the pool comes from the Chinese translation, not the Sanskrit.

verses.en: “If someone throws him into the perilous ocean, the home of nagas, sea monsters (makaras), asuras and ghosts, when he remembers Avalokiteshvara he never sinks in that king of waters.”

“If someone with a mind full of hate pushes him off the top of Mount Meru (the great mountain at the center of the world) to kill him, when he remembers Avalokiteshvara he stays up in the sky like the sun.”
“If, to kill him, someone brings a mountain of diamond (vajra) down on his head, when he remembers Avalokiteshvara it cannot harm even one pore of his skin.”

cmp.note: 梵文是金刚做的山砸到他头上。鸠摩罗什作「或被恶人逐，堕落金刚山」，变成人被追赶、从金刚山上掉下来。
cmp.en: In the Sanskrit a mountain made of vajra is brought down on his head. Kumarajiva writes 或被恶人逐，堕落金刚山 (“or, chased by evil men, he falls from a vajra mountain”), so the person falls off the mountain instead.

verses.en: “If he is surrounded by bands of enemies with swords in hand, set on hurting him, when he remembers Avalokiteshvara they turn kind-hearted in that very moment.”
“If he has been brought to the execution ground and has fallen into the executioner's hands, when he remembers Avalokiteshvara the swords break into pieces.”
“If he is bound here with shackles and fetters of wood or of iron, when he remembers Avalokiteshvara the bonds split apart at once.”
“Spells, powers, charms and herbs, ghosts and vetalas (spirits that bring corpses to life) that destroy the body: when he remembers Avalokiteshvara, they go back to where they were sent from.”

cmp.note: 中文读者常讨论这句：害人的咒和毒「还著于本人」，回到施放的人身上。梵文字面就是「它们回到被放出来的地方去」，鸠摩罗什译得很准；白话、英文照译，不另加解释。oṣadhī 本义是「草药」，鸠摩罗什译「毒药」，取的是用来害人的药草。
cmp.en: Chinese readers often discuss this line: harmful spells and poisons 还著于本人 (huán zhuó yú běnrén, “return to the one who sent them”). The Sanskrit literally says “they go back to where they were set going from,” and Kumarajiva translates it accurately; the plain Chinese and the English translate it as it is, without adding an explanation. Oṣadhī basically means “herbs”; Kumarajiva renders it 毒药 (dúyào, “poison”), taking it as herbs used to harm.

verses.en: “If he is surrounded by nagas, yakshas, asuras, ghosts and rakshasas that steal a person's vital strength, when he remembers Avalokiteshvara they cannot harm even one pore of his skin.”
“If he is surrounded by wild beasts, terrifying, with sharp fangs and claws, when he remembers Avalokiteshvara they quickly run off in every direction, endlessly far.”
“If he is surrounded by snakes whose very glance is poison, fierce and dreadful, blazing with flames and fire, when he remembers Avalokiteshvara they at once lose their poison.”

cmp.note: dṛṣṭiviṣa 字面是「目光有毒的」，印度传说里有看人一眼就能把人毒死的蛇。鸠摩罗什写成「蚖蛇及蝮蝎，气毒烟火燃」，结果是「寻声自回去」，听到念诵声自己退走；梵文的结果是「立刻没了毒」。
cmp.en: Dṛṣṭiviṣa literally means “whose glance is poison”: Indian lore tells of snakes that can kill with a single look. Kumarajiva writes 蚖蛇及蝮蝎，气毒烟火燃 (“lizards, snakes, vipers and scorpions, their poison breath burning like smoke and fire”), and the outcome is 寻声自回去 (“at the sound they turn and leave”); in the Sanskrit the outcome is that “they at once lose their poison.”

verses.en: “Deep thunder with lightning flashing out, thunderbolts from the clouds, pouring rain: when he remembers Avalokiteshvara, they quickly die down in that very moment.”
“Seeing beings beset by hundreds of sufferings, tormented by many pains, he whose strength is pure knowledge looked on them, and so became the protector of this world with its gods.”

cmp.note: vilokiyā「看了之后」和 avalokita「观看」同出一个词根 lok「看」，偈颂在这里扣着观世音的名字。英文 looked on them、白话「看见」只剩「看」，扣名字的意味没了；鸠摩罗什「观音妙智力」用「观」字，倒还暗合。
cmp.en: Vilokiyā, “having looked,” comes from the same root lok, “to look,” as avalokita, so the verse is playing on Avalokiteshvara's name here. The English “looked on them” and the plain Chinese 看见 (kànjiàn, “saw”) keep only the looking, and the wordplay is lost; Kumarajiva's 观音妙智力 (“the wondrous wisdom-power of Guanyin”) still echoes it through the word 观 (guān, “observe”).

verses.en: “He has gone to the far shore of supernatural power, and is trained in vast knowledge and skillful means. Everywhere in the ten directions of the world, in every land without exception, he is seen.”

“The bad states that leave no chance to hear the Dharma, the terrors of the hells, of the animal realm and of Yama's rule (Yama is the king of the dead), and the torments of birth, old age and sickness: one by one he calms them for living beings.”

cmp.note: akṣaṇa 字面是「不是时候」，指生在听不到佛法的处境，汉译佛经一般叫「八难」。鸠摩罗什写「种种诸恶趣」，概括掉了这层意思；他还多了一个「死」字，「生老病死苦」，梵文只说生、老、病。
cmp.en: Akṣaṇa literally means “not the right moment”: being born where one has no chance to hear the Dharma, usually called 八难 (bā nàn, “the eight difficult states”) in Chinese translations. Kumarajiva writes 种种诸恶趣 (“all the various evil destinies”), which blurs that sense, and he adds “death” to make 生老病死苦 (“the suffering of birth, old age, sickness and death”); the Sanskrit names only birth, old age and sickness.

verses.en: Then Akshayamati, glad and delighted at heart, spoke these verses:

cmp.note: 梵文在这里换了说话的人，下面是无尽意赞颂观世音。鸠摩罗什本没有这一句，「真观清净观」那几首在中文本里仍算妙幢（世尊）答话的一部分。
cmp.en: Here the Sanskrit changes speaker: what follows is Akshayamati praising Avalokiteshvara. Kumarajiva's text has no such line, so the stanzas beginning 真观清净观 (“true seeing, pure seeing”) are still part of the answer in the Chinese.

verses.en: “Eyes that are lovely, eyes full of kindness, eyes made excellent by wisdom and knowledge; eyes of compassion, pure eyes: you are dear and beautiful, with a lovely face and lovely eyes.”

cmp.note: 梵文一连串 locana「眼睛」：好眼、慈眼、慧眼、悲眼、净眼。鸠摩罗什把「眼」全换成「观」：真观、清净观、广大智慧观、悲观、慈观，从「长着怎样的眼睛」变成「用怎样的方式观看」，正好扣住观世音的「观」。英文 eyes、白话「眼睛」照梵文。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit strings together locana, “eyes”: lovely eyes, kind eyes, eyes of wisdom, eyes of compassion, pure eyes. Kumarajiva turns every “eye” into 观 (guān, “seeing, contemplation”): 真观、清净观、广大智慧观、悲观、慈观 (“true seeing, pure seeing, the seeing of vast wisdom, compassionate seeing, kind seeing”). What kind of eyes he has becomes what kind of seeing he does, which ties neatly to the 观 in Guanshiyin. The English “eyes” and the plain Chinese 眼睛 (yǎnjing, “eyes”) follow the Sanskrit.

verses.en: “Your light is stainless, spotless, utterly pure, without darkness, the light of the sun of knowledge, a light that sweeps away the disasters of wind and fire. Blazing, you shine over the world.”

“Compassion, true virtue and kindness are your thunder; with lovely virtues and a kind mind, you are a great cloud. You put out the fire of the afflictions (kleshas, the passions that burn the mind) for living beings, and rain down the deathless rain of the Dharma.”

cmp.note: amṛta 字面是「不死」，指使人不死的甘露。中文译「甘露」，取的是「甜美的露水」这一面，「不死」的意思淡了；英文 deathless 照字面。
cmp.en: Amṛta literally means “deathless,” the nectar that makes one immortal. The Chinese 甘露 (gānlù, “sweet dew”) keeps the sweetness and loses most of the “deathless”; the English “deathless” is literal.

verses.en: “In quarrels, disputes and fights, in the great terror of men at war, when one remembers Avalokiteshvara the wicked mobs of enemies calm down.”

“His voice is the voice of a cloud, the voice of a drum, the roar of a rain cloud, the lovely voice of Brahma. He has reached the far shore of the whole range of sound. Avalokiteshvara is the one to remember.”

cmp.note: 梵文是「雨云的轰鸣」（jala-dhara 字面「载水者」，指雨云）。鸠摩罗什作「海潮音」，可能把「载水者」理解成了大海。「妙音、梵音、海潮音」后来成了中文赞颂观音的常用语。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit is “the roar of the rain cloud” (jala-dhara, literally “water-bearer,” means a rain cloud). Kumarajiva writes 海潮音 (hǎicháo yīn, “the sound of the ocean tide”), perhaps taking the “water-bearer” as the sea. 妙音、梵音、海潮音 (“wondrous sound, Brahma's sound, sound of the ocean tide”) later became a standard phrase in Chinese praise of Guanyin.

verses.en: “Remember him, remember him, have no doubts about Avalokiteshvara, that pure being. In death, in disaster, in calamity, he becomes a protector, a refuge, a final resting place.”

cmp.note: 梵文是命令式「要忆念，要忆念」。鸠摩罗什作「念念勿生疑」，「念念」后来常被理解成「每一个念头」，意思从叮嘱变成了「念念之间都不要怀疑」。英文 Remember him, remember him、白话「忆念吧，忆念吧」照梵文。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit is an imperative: “remember, remember!” Kumarajiva writes 念念勿生疑 (niànniàn wù shēng yí), and 念念 was later often understood as “every single thought,” so the urging became “do not doubt in any moment of thought.” The English “Remember him, remember him” and the plain Chinese 忆念吧，忆念吧 follow the Sanskrit.

verses.en: “He has gone to the far shore of every good quality; his eyes look on all beings with compassion and kindness. He is goodness itself, a great ocean of good qualities: Avalokiteshvara is the one to bow to.”
“He who has compassion for the world will become a buddha in a time to come. He destroys all suffering, fear and grief: I bow to Avalokiteshvara.”

cmp.note: 从这一段到第 51 段，鸠摩罗什本（连后来补译的偈颂）都没有，是梵文本多出来的部分，讲观世音将来成佛，以及他侍立在阿弥陀佛身边、阿弥陀佛的极乐世界。
cmp.en: From this verse to verse 51, nothing appears in Kumarajiva's text, not even in the verses added later. This is extra material in the Sanskrit: it tells that Avalokiteshvara will become a buddha, that he attends the Buddha Amitabha, and describes Amitabha's Land of Bliss.

verses.en: “Lokeshvararaja was the guide, and the monk Dharmakara (the name Amitabha bore before he became a buddha), honored by the world, practiced for many hundreds of eons and reached stainless, unsurpassed awakening.”

“Standing at his right and at his left, he fans the guide Amitabha (“Infinite Light”). Through the samadhi (meditative absorption) of seeing all things as like a magic show, he went to every land and honored the Victors.”
“In the west, a source of happiness, lies the stainless world Sukhavati (the Land of Bliss), where this guide Amitabha now lives, the charioteer of beings.”

“No women are born there, and there is no sexual union of any kind. Those true sons of the Victor are born spontaneously (appearing without parents) and, stainless, sit within the hearts of lotus flowers.”

cmp.note: 梵文直说「那里没有女人出生」，英文、白话都照字面译，不改写。jinorasa 字面是「胜者亲生的儿子」，aurasa 指从胸怀所生的嫡子，英文 true sons、白话「胜者之子」都比原词弱一点。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says plainly that “no women are born there,” and the English and the plain Chinese translate it literally, without softening it. Jinorasa literally means “the Victor's own sons,” aurasa being a son born of one's own breast, a legitimate son; the English “true sons” and the plain Chinese 胜者之子 (shèngzhě zhī zǐ, “sons of the Victor”) are both a little weaker than the original.

verses.en: “And that guide Amitabha, seated on a lion throne in the heart of a stainless, lovely lotus, shines like a king of sala trees.”

“He too is a guide of the world in the same way, with no equal in the three worlds (the realms of desire, of form and of formlessness). By the merit I have gathered in praising you, may I quickly become like you, best of men!”
Thus end the verses.

Then the bodhisattva Dharanimdhara (“Holder of the Earth”), a great being, rose from his seat, put his upper robe over one shoulder, set his right knee on the ground, joined his palms toward the Blessed One, and said to him: “Blessed One, those beings who hear this chapter of the Dharma discourse about the bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara, the great being, will not be people with only meager roots of goodness: this teaching on the miraculous transformations of the bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara, the great being, the chapter called ‘The Gateway Facing Every Direction,’ the miracle of the transformations of the bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara.”

cmp.note: samanta「周遍、四面八方」加 mukha「脸、口、门口」，意思是「面向一切方向的」，也可解成「向一切方向敞开的门」。鸠摩罗什取「门」的意思译「普门」；英文 the Gateway Facing Every Direction 想把「门」和「面向」两层都留住。
cmp.en: Samanta, “all around, in every direction,” plus mukha, “face, mouth, entrance”: “facing every direction,” or “a door open on every side.” Kumarajiva takes the “door” sense and renders it 普门 (pǔmén, “universal gate”); the English “the Gateway Facing Every Direction” tries to keep both the door and the facing.

verses.en: While the Blessed One was teaching this chapter, The Gateway Facing Every Direction, eighty-four thousand living beings in that assembly set their minds on unsurpassed, perfect awakening, the equal of the unequaled.

cmp.note: asama-sama 字面是「与无可比者相等的」，只有诸佛彼此相等，别的都比不上。鸠摩罗什译「无等等」，是逐字对应；白话「无与伦比」只留下「比不上」这一半，英文 the equal of the unequaled 照字面。
cmp.en: Asama-sama literally means “equal to the unequaled”: only the buddhas are equal to one another, and nothing else compares. Kumarajiva's 无等等 (wú děng děng, “unequaled-equal”) matches it word for word; the plain Chinese 无与伦比 (wú yǔ lún bǐ, “incomparable”) keeps only the “unequaled” half, and the English “the equal of the unequaled” is literal.

verses.en: Here ends the twenty-fourth chapter, called “The Gateway Facing Every Direction,” the teaching on the transformations of Avalokiteshvara, in the glorious Dharma discourse of the Lotus of the True Dharma.

cmp.note: 梵本把这一品算作第二十四品。本站把开经算作一章、把提婆达多品并入见宝塔品，所以排在第 25 章；鸠摩罗什本里它也正好是第二十五品，不过罗什本的品次和梵本并不一样（例如陀罗尼品排在这一品之后）。英文这句照梵文写 twenty-fourth。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit counts this as the twenty-fourth chapter. The site counts the opening section as a chapter and folds the Devadatta chapter into the stupa chapter, so this is Chapter 25 here; in Kumarajiva’s version it also happens to be the twenty-fifth, though his chapter order differs from the Sanskrit (for instance, the dharani chapter comes after this one). The English of this line follows the Sanskrit with “twenty-fourth.”

chapters.title: Chapter 26 · The Former Life of King Shubhavyuha

verses.en: Then the Blessed One addressed the whole assembly of bodhisattvas: “Sons of good family, long ago in the past, countless eons ago, more than countless eons (kalpas, cosmic ages), there was a time when a Tathagata named Jaladharagarjitaghoshasusvaranakshatrarajasankusumitabhijna (“his voice like the thunder of rain clouds, his sound beautiful, a king among the stars, his higher knowledge in full flower”) appeared in the world: an arhat, a fully awakened buddha, perfect in knowledge and conduct, the Sugata (Well-Gone One), knower of the world, unsurpassed, the trainer of people who can be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a buddha, a blessed one. It was in the eon called Priyadarshana (Lovely to See), in the world system called Vairocanarashmipratimandita (Adorned with Rays of Sunlight). Sons of good family, under the teaching of that Tathagata Jaladharagarjitaghoshasusvaranakshatrarajasankusumitabhijna there was a king named Shubhavyuha (Beautiful Array). And, sons of good family, King Shubhavyuha had a wife named Vimaladatta (Given by the Stainless).

cmp.note: 这个佛号在梵文里是一个长复合词，英文只能照音写出再加括号解释，读起来很吃力；鸠摩罗什浓缩成「云雷音宿王华智」七个字，每个字对一段意思（云、雷音、宿王、华、智），汉字读者反而容易记。
cmp.en: This buddha's name is one long compound in Sanskrit. The English can only spell it out and explain it in parentheses, which makes for heavy reading; Kumarajiva condenses it into seven characters, 云雷音宿王华智 (Yún Léiyīn Sùwáng Huázhì, “cloud, thunder-sound, king of stars, flower, knowledge”), each matching one piece of the meaning, so a Chinese reader actually finds it easy to remember.

verses.en: Sons of good family, King Shubhavyuha had two sons: one named Vimalagarbha (Stainless Womb), the other named Vimalanetra (Stainless Eye). These two boys had supernatural powers. They were wise, full of merit and knowledgeable, and devoted to the bodhisattva practice; that is, devoted to the perfection of giving, the perfection of moral conduct, the perfection of patience, the perfection of effort, the perfection of meditation, the perfection of wisdom, and the perfection of skillful means; to loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy and equanimity; and so on up to the thirty-seven qualities that lead to awakening.

cmp.note: garbha 有「胎、子宫、内藏」几层意思。鸠摩罗什译「净藏」，取「内藏」义；英文 Stainless Womb 取字面。两种都说得通。
cmp.en: Garbha means “womb, embryo, inner store.” Kumarajiva's 净藏 (Jìngzàng, “pure store”) takes the sense “inner store”; the English “Stainless Womb” takes the literal sense. Both are defensible.

verses.en: They had gone all the way to the far shore in everything: they had mastered the concentration called Stainless, the concentration called Sun of the King of Stars, the concentration called Stainless Radiance, the concentration called Stainless Light, the concentration called Beauty of Adornment, and the concentration called Store of Great Splendor. At that time that Blessed One taught this Dharma discourse, the Lotus of the True Dharma, out of compassion for living beings and out of compassion for King Shubhavyuha. Then, sons of good family, the boy Vimalagarbha and the boy Vimalanetra went to their own mother, the one who bore them.

When they came to her, they joined their palms, ten fingers together, and said to their mother: “Come, Mother, let's go to the Blessed One Jaladharagarjitaghoshasusvaranakshatrarajasankusumitabhijna, the Tathagata, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, to see that Blessed One, to bow to him and to wait on him. Why? Because, Mother, that Blessed One Jaladharagarjitaghoshasusvaranakshatrarajasankusumitabhijna, the Tathagata, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, is explaining in full, before the world and its gods, the Dharma discourse called the Lotus of the True Dharma. Let's go and hear it.”

Sons of good family, when they said this, Queen Vimaladatta said to the boy Vimalagarbha and the boy Vimalanetra: “My sons, your father, King Shubhavyuha, is devoted to the brahmins. So you won't be allowed to go and see that Tathagata.” Then, sons of good family, the boy Vimalagarbha and the boy Vimalanetra joined their palms, ten fingers together, and said to their own mother: “Have we really been born into this family of wrong views? We are sons of the King of the Dharma!” Then, sons of good family, Queen Vimaladatta said to the two boys: “Good, good, my sons. Out of compassion for your father, King Shubhavyuha, show him some miracle. Perhaps he will come to have faith because of you,

cmp.note: 梵文只说国王「信奉婆罗门」，原因是他不放孩子去见佛。鸠摩罗什写「信受外道，深着婆罗门法」，又加一句「汝等应往白父，与共俱去」，母亲先叫孩子去求父亲；梵文里母亲直接说「你们去不成」。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says only that the king “is devoted to the brahmins,” which is why the boys can't go to see the Buddha. Kumarajiva writes 信受外道，深着婆罗门法 (“believes in outside paths and is deeply attached to brahmin teachings”) and adds a line in which the mother tells the boys to go and ask their father to come along; in the Sanskrit she simply says, “you won't be allowed to go.”

verses.en: and, his heart won over, he will let us go to that Blessed One Jaladharagarjitaghoshasusvaranakshatrarajasankusumitabhijna, the Tathagata, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha.”

Then, sons of good family, the boy Vimalagarbha and the boy Vimalanetra at once rose into the air to the height of seven palm trees and, out of compassion for their father, King Shubhavyuha, performed the twin miracles that the Buddha allows. Up there in the sky they lay down as if on a bed; up there in the sky they walked up and down; up there in the sky they shook off dust; up there in the sky they let streams of water pour from the lower half of their bodies and blazed with masses of fire from the upper half; then they let streams of water pour from the upper half of their bodies and blazed with masses of fire from the lower half. There in the sky they grew huge and then became tiny; having become tiny, they grew huge again. They vanished there in the sky and came up out of the earth; having come up out of the earth, they came up out of the sky.

cmp.note: 「双神变」，身上同时出水又出火，是佛教传说里佛陀在舍卫城示现过的有名神通。白话译「双重神变」，英文 twin miracles；鸠摩罗什只写「种种神变」，「双」的意思没有译出来。
cmp.en: The “twin miracle,” with water and fire coming from the body at once, is a famous wonder that Buddhist legend says the Buddha himself performed at Shravasti. The plain Chinese says 双重神变 (“double miracle”) and the English “twin miracles”; Kumarajiva writes only 种种神变 (“all kinds of miracles”), so the “twin” is lost.

verses.en: Sons of good family, with this many miracles of supernatural power the two boys won over their father, King Shubhavyuha. And, sons of good family, when King Shubhavyuha saw the boys' miracles of supernatural power, he was at once satisfied, elated, glad and delighted, full of joy and happiness. He joined his palms, ten fingers together, and said to the two boys: “My sons, who is your teacher? Whose disciples are you?” Then, sons of good family, the two boys said to King Shubhavyuha: “Great king, the Blessed One Jaladharagarjitaghoshasusvaranakshatrarajasankusumitabhijna, the Tathagata, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, is living right now, seated on a Dharma seat at the foot of a jeweled tree of awakening,

cmp.note: 梵文说国王反过来向两个儿子合掌，这是很强烈的姿态：父亲向孩子行礼。白话、英文都照译；鸠摩罗什也有「合掌向子」，保留了这个细节。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit has the king join his palms toward his own two sons, a striking gesture: a father saluting his children. The plain Chinese and the English both keep it, and so does Kumarajiva with 合掌向子 (hézhǎng xiàng zǐ, “joined his palms toward his sons”).

verses.en: and he is explaining in full, before the world and its gods, the Dharma discourse called the Lotus of the True Dharma. That Blessed One is our teacher, great king; we are his disciples.” Then, sons of good family, King Shubhavyuha said to the two boys: “My sons, we will see this teacher of yours. We will go to that Blessed One.”

Then, sons of good family, the two boys came down from the sky and went to their own mother. They joined their palms, ten fingers together, and said to their mother: “Mother, we have won our father over to unsurpassed, perfect awakening. We have done for our father what a teacher does. So now you should let us go. We will go forth (leave home to become monks) under that Blessed One.”
Then, sons of good family, the boy Vimalagarbha and the boy Vimalanetra at once spoke to their mother in two verses:
“Mother, give us leave to go forth into the homeless life. We will go forth, for a Tathagata is hard to meet.
Even harder to find than the udumbara flower is a Victor (a buddha). We will leave everything behind and go forth, for such a fortunate moment is rare.”

cmp.note: kṣaṇa 是「刹那、时机」，kṣaṇasaṃpad 指「生在能遇佛闻法的好时机」，与此相对的是「八难」（生在没机会修行的处境）。白话「遇上好时机」、英文 fortunate moment 都译出了意思；鸠摩罗什作「脱诸难亦难」，是从反面说。
cmp.en: Kṣaṇa means “moment, opportunity,” and kṣaṇasaṃpad is “the good fortune of being born at a time when one can meet a buddha and hear the Dharma,” the opposite of being born into one of the circumstances where practice is impossible. The plain Chinese 遇上好时机 (“meeting a good moment”) and the English “fortunate moment” both convey this; Kumarajiva says it from the other side: 脱诸难亦难 (tuō zhū nàn yì nán, “escaping all the hindrances is also hard”).

verses.en: Queen Vimaladatta said:
“Today I let you go. Go, my boys, and go well. We too will go forth, for a Tathagata is hard to meet.”
(End of the verses.)

Then, sons of good family, when the two boys had spoken these verses, they said to their mother and father: “Come on, Mother and Father! Let's all go together to the Blessed One Jaladharagarjitaghoshasusvaranakshatrarajasankusumitabhijna, the Tathagata, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha. Let's go to see that Blessed One, to bow to him, to wait on him and to hear the Dharma. Why? Because, Mother and Father, it is rare for a buddha to appear. It is like the udumbara flower, or like a turtle in the great ocean putting its neck through the hole in a floating yoke. Mother, buddhas, blessed ones, rarely appear. So, Mother and Father, it is by the support of the highest merit that we have been born under such a teaching. So please, Mother and Father, let us go. We two will go.

cmp.note: 「像大海中的乌龟把脖子伸进轭木的孔」：茫茫大海里漂着一块有孔的轭木，一只乌龟偶然把头伸进孔中，比喻遇佛之难。鸠摩罗什作「一眼之龟，值浮木孔」，乌龟变成独眼的，这是汉地流传的版本。
cmp.en: “Like a turtle in the great ocean putting its neck into the hole of a yoke”: in the vast sea floats a yoke with a hole in it, and a turtle happens to put its head through, an image for how rare it is to meet a buddha. Kumarajiva writes 一眼之龟，值浮木孔 (yī yǎn zhī guī, zhí fúmù kǒng, “a one-eyed turtle meeting the hole in a floating log”); the turtle becoming one-eyed is the version that spread in China.

verses.en: We will go forth under that Blessed One Jaladharagarjitaghoshasusvaranakshatrarajasankusumitabhijna, the Tathagata, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha. For, Mother and Father, it is hard to get to see the Tathagatas. A time like today is hard to come by; so is such a King of the Dharma; such a fortunate moment is extremely rare.”

Sons of good family, at that time eighty-four thousand women of King Shubhavyuha's inner palace became vessels fit for this Dharma discourse, the Lotus of the True Dharma. The boy Vimalanetra had practiced this Dharma discourse thoroughly. The boy Vimalagarbha had practiced for many hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas (huge numbers) of eons in the concentration called Removing the Evil of All Beings, thinking, “How can all beings give up all evil?” And the boys' mother, Queen Vimaladatta, understood the chanting of all the buddhas and the secret places of all the buddhas' teachings. Then, sons of good family, King Shubhavyuha was trained by the two boys in the Tathagata's teaching, brought into it and brought to maturity, together with all his relatives and household.

cmp.note: saṃgīti 可以是「合诵、齐唱」，也可以是「结集、集会」。白话取「集会」，英文取 chanting；鸠摩罗什作「诸佛集三昧」，把它当成一种三昧的名字。确切所指不很清楚。
cmp.en: Saṃgīti can mean “chanting together, recitation” or “council, assembly.” The plain Chinese takes 集会 (jíhuì, “assembly”), the English “chanting”; Kumarajiva writes 诸佛集三昧 (zhū fó jí sānmèi, “the samadhi of the assembly of all buddhas”), treating it as the name of a concentration. Exactly what is meant is not very clear.

verses.en: Queen Vimaladatta with all her relatives and household, and the two boys, King Shubhavyuha's sons, with forty-two thousand people, along with the women of the palace and the ministers, all together and of one mind, went to the Blessed One Jaladharagarjitaghoshasusvaranakshatrarajasankusumitabhijna, the Tathagata, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha. When they got there they bowed their heads at that Blessed One's feet, walked around that Blessed One three times keeping him on their right, and stood to one side.

Then, sons of good family, that Blessed One Jaladharagarjitaghoshasusvaranakshatrarajasankusumitabhijna, the Tathagata, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, knowing that King Shubhavyuha had come with his household, instructed him with a talk on the Dharma, encouraged him, inspired him and delighted him.

Then, sons of good family, King Shubhavyuha, having been well and truly instructed, encouraged, inspired and delighted by that Blessed One with a talk on the Dharma, was at once satisfied, elated, glad and delighted, full of joy and happiness. He tied the royal headband on his younger brother and set him on the throne. Then he with his sons, relatives and household, Queen Vimaladatta with all her women, and the two boys with those forty-two thousand people, all together and of one mind, went forth in faith from home into the homeless life under the teaching of that Blessed One Jaladharagarjitaghoshasusvaranakshatrarajasankusumitabhijna, the Tathagata, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha.

cmp.note: paṭṭa 是系在额上的丝带，古印度立王时为新王系上，相当于加冕。白话「系上王冠头带」、英文 tied the royal headband 都保留了这个动作；鸠摩罗什只说「以国付弟」。
cmp.en: A paṭṭa is a silk band tied around the forehead; in ancient India tying it on a new king was the equivalent of crowning him. The plain Chinese 系上王冠头带 (“tied on the royal headband”) and the English keep this act; Kumarajiva says only 以国付弟 (yǐ guó fù dì, “handed the kingdom to his younger brother”).

verses.en: After going forth, King Shubhavyuha and his household lived for eighty-four thousand years devoted to practice, reflecting on this Dharma discourse, the Lotus of the True Dharma, cultivating it and purifying it. Then, sons of good family, when those eighty-four thousand years had passed, King Shubhavyuha gained the concentration called Array of the Adornment of All Good Qualities. And the moment he gained that concentration, he rose into the air to the height of seven palm trees.

Then, sons of good family, King Shubhavyuha, standing in the sky, said to the Blessed One Jaladharagarjitaghoshasusvaranakshatrarajasankusumitabhijna, the Tathagata, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha: “Blessed One, these two sons of mine are my teachers. By their miracles of supernatural power they turned me back from those deep-seated wrong views, set me in the Tathagata's teaching, brought me to maturity, brought me in, and urged me to come and see the Tathagata. Blessed One, those two boys are my good friends (kalyanamitra, spiritual friends who lead one to the good); they were born in my house in the form of sons so that I would remember the roots of goodness I planted in the past.”

cmp.note: kalyāṇamitra 字面是「善的朋友」，指带人走上正道的良师益友，汉译「善知识」。英文 good friend 照字面，但在英文里太平常，所以加了括号解释；中文的「善知识」现代读者也未必一看就懂。
cmp.en: Kalyāṇamitra literally means “good friend,” a mentor or companion who leads you onto the right path; Chinese renders it 善知识 (shàn zhīshi, “good acquaintance”). The English “good friend” is literal but too ordinary in English, so a parenthetical explanation is added; for that matter, a modern Chinese reader may not understand 善知识 at a glance either.

verses.en: When he had said this, the Blessed One Jaladharagarjitaghoshasusvaranakshatrarajasankusumitabhijna, the Tathagata, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, said to King Shubhavyuha: “So it is, great king, it is just as you say. Great king, sons and daughters of good family who have planted roots of goodness, wherever they are born, in whatever realm of existence, path, death and rebirth, easily find good friends, who stand by them doing what a teacher does, who instruct them in unsurpassed, perfect awakening, bring them into it and bring them to maturity. Great king, it is a lofty thing to be taken in hand by a good friend who urges one to see the Tathagata. Great king, do you see these two boys?” He said: “I see them, Blessed One. I see them, Sugata.”

The Blessed One said: “Great king, these two sons of good family will make offerings in the presence of Tathagatas, arhats, fully awakened buddhas as many as the grains of sand in sixty-five Ganges Rivers, and will hold this Dharma discourse, the Lotus of the True Dharma, out of compassion for living beings, and to stir up energy so that beings with wrong views may come to right view.”

cmp.note: 梵文用将来时：两位王子「将会」供养六十五恒河沙数的佛。白话、英文照译；鸠摩罗什作「已曾供养」，变成过去的事。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit uses the future tense: the two princes “will” make offerings to buddhas as many as the sands of sixty-five Ganges Rivers. The plain Chinese and the English follow it; Kumarajiva writes 已曾供养 (yǐ céng gòngyǎng, “have already made offerings”), putting it in the past.

verses.en: Then, sons of good family, King Shubhavyuha came down from the sky, joined his palms, ten fingers together, and said to the Blessed One Jaladharagarjitaghoshasusvaranakshatrarajasankusumitabhijna, the Tathagata, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha: “Please, Blessed One, may the Tathagata explain: what kind of knowledge does a Tathagata, an arhat, a fully awakened buddha have, that the protuberance on the crown of his head (the ushnisha) shines, that the Blessed One's eyes are so clear, that the tuft of white hair between his brows (the urna) shines white as the moon or a conch shell, that the even, close-set row of teeth gleams in his mouth, that the Blessed One's lips are red as the bimba fruit, and the Sugata's eyes so lovely?”

cmp.note: uṣṇīṣa 是佛头顶隆起的肉髻，ūrṇā 是眉间一缕白毛（白毫），都属于佛的三十二相。英文没有对应词，保留梵文并加括号解释；汉译「肉髻」「白毫」是意译，汉字读者容易明白。
cmp.en: The uṣṇīṣa is the rounded protuberance on top of a buddha's head, and the ūrṇā is a tuft of white hair between the eyebrows; both belong to the thirty-two marks of a buddha. English has no equivalent words, so the translation keeps the Sanskrit with an explanation; the Chinese 肉髻 (ròujì, “flesh topknot”) and 白毫 (báiháo, “white hair”) translate the meaning and are easy for a Chinese reader to grasp.

verses.en: Then, sons of good family, having praised the Blessed One Jaladharagarjitaghoshasusvaranakshatrarajasankusumitabhijna, the Tathagata, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, for these good qualities, and having praised that Blessed One for hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas of other good qualities, King Shubhavyuha at that moment said to that Blessed One: “It is wonderful, Blessed One, how greatly meaningful this teaching of the Tathagata is, how the Dharma and discipline made known by the Tathagata are endowed with inconceivable good qualities, how well laid down the Tathagata's training is.

From this day on, Blessed One, we will no longer be ruled by our own minds, no longer be ruled by wrong views, no longer be ruled by anger, no longer be ruled by evil thoughts as they arise. Blessed One, carrying so many unwholesome things as I do, I don't wish to come close to the Blessed One.” He bowed his head at the feet of that Blessed One Jaladharagarjitaghoshasusvaranakshatrarajasankusumitabhijna, the Tathagata, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, and stayed where he was, up in the sky.

cmp.note: 国王说自己身上带着这么多不善法，不想走近世尊，所以礼完佛就留在空中。这句也可以读成过去式「（以前）我带着这些不善法，不愿去见世尊」。鸠摩罗什没有这句，结尾作「礼佛而出」。
cmp.en: The king says that, carrying so many unwholesome things, he does not wish to come near the Blessed One, which is why after bowing he stays up in the sky. The line could also be read in the past tense: “(before,) burdened with these unwholesome things, I had no wish to go and see the Blessed One.” Kumarajiva lacks this sentence and ends with 礼佛而出 (lǐ fó ér chū, “bowed to the Buddha and left”).

verses.en: Then King Shubhavyuha and Queen Vimaladatta tossed a pearl necklace worth a hundred thousand into the air above the Blessed One. As soon as it was tossed, the pearl necklace took shape above that Blessed One's head as a pavilion of pearls: square, with four pillars, well proportioned, nicely divided, beautiful to look at. In that pavilion a couch appeared, spread with many hundreds of thousands of fine cloths, and on that couch could be seen the figure of a Tathagata seated cross-legged. Then King Shubhavyuha thought: “How mighty this buddha-knowledge is, and how inconceivable the good qualities of the Tathagata! For here this figure of a Tathagata appears inside the pavilion, graceful, beautiful to look at, perfect in the loveliness of his supremely fine complexion.”

Then the Blessed One Jaladharagarjitaghoshasusvaranakshatrarajasankusumitabhijna, the Tathagata, addressed the four assemblies: “Monks, do you see King Shubhavyuha standing in the sky, roaring a lion's roar?” They said: “We see him, Blessed One.” The Blessed One said: “Monks, this King Shubhavyuha, having become a monk under my teaching, will become a Tathagata in the world named Shalendraraja (King of Sal Trees), an arhat, a fully awakened buddha, perfect in knowledge and conduct, the Sugata, knower of the world, unsurpassed, trainer of people who can be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a buddha, a blessed one, in the world system called Vistirnavati (Wide). That eon will be called Abhyudgataraja (Lofty King).

cmp.note: 梵文国名是「广大」，白话照译；鸠摩罗什作「大光」，和梵文不同，可能他依据的本子不一样。英文照梵文。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit name of the world means “wide,” and the plain Chinese follows it; Kumarajiva has 大光 (Dàguāng, “Great Light”), which differs from the Sanskrit, perhaps because his source text was different. The English follows the Sanskrit.

verses.en: Monks, that Tathagata Shalendraraja, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, will have an immeasurable community of bodhisattvas and an immeasurable community of disciples (shravakas). That world system Vistirnavati will be level as the palm of a hand and made of lapis lazuli. That is how inconceivable that Tathagata, arhat, fully awakened buddha will be. Now, sons of good family, you may have some doubt, uncertainty or hesitation: was the king named Shubhavyuha at that time someone else? Sons of good family, you should not see it that way. Why? This very bodhisattva, great being Padmashri (Lotus Glory) was at that time the king named Shubhavyuha.

Sons of good family, you may have some doubt, uncertainty or hesitation: was the queen named Vimaladatta at that time someone else? Sons of good family, you should not see it that way. Why? The bodhisattva, great being named Vairocanarashmipratimanditadhvajaraja (Banner King Adorned with Rays of Sunlight) was at that time the queen named Vimaladatta. Out of compassion for King Shubhavyuha and for those beings, he took on the role of King Shubhavyuha's wife. Sons of good family, you may have some doubt, uncertainty or hesitation: were the two boys at that time someone else? Sons of good family, you should not see it that way. Why?

cmp.note: 梵文说这位菩萨（语法上是阳性）为了怜悯国王而「甘愿成为」王后。白话、英文都照译，英文用 he；鸠摩罗什只说「于彼中生」，看不出前生的王后今世是男身菩萨这一层。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says this bodhisattva (grammatically masculine) “took on being the wife” of the king out of compassion. The plain Chinese and the English both follow this, the English using “he”; Kumarajiva says only 于彼中生 (yú bǐ zhōng shēng, “was born among them”), so the point that the former queen is now a male bodhisattva doesn't come through.

verses.en: These two, Bhaishajyaraja (Medicine King) and Bhaishajyasamudgata (Medicine Rising), were at that time the sons of King Shubhavyuha. Sons of good family, such are the inconceivable good qualities of the bodhisattvas, great beings Bhaishajyaraja and Bhaishajyasamudgata. They have planted roots of goodness with many hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas of buddhas; both of these good men have inconceivable qualities. And all who hold the names of these two good men will deserve to be honored by the world and its gods.
While this chapter about former lives was being taught, the pure eye of the Dharma, free of dust and stain, opened to things for eighty-four thousand living beings.

cmp.note: 「法眼净」是早期佛经的固定说法，指初次看清「凡是生起的都会灭去」，即证得初果。白话、英文都照字面译，读者未必知道这是专门术语。
cmp.en: “The pure Dharma eye” is a stock phrase in early Buddhist texts for the first clear seeing that “whatever arises will pass away,” that is, reaching the first stage of awakening (stream-entry). The plain Chinese and the English both translate it literally, so readers may not realize it is a technical term.

verses.en: Here ends the twenty-fifth chapter, called “The Former Life of King Shubhavyuha,” in the glorious Dharma discourse of the Lotus of the True Dharma.

cmp.note: 梵本把这一品算作第二十五品，本站算第 26 章，鸠摩罗什本是第二十七品。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit counts this as the twenty-fifth chapter; this site counts it as Chapter 26, and in Kumarajiva's version it is chapter 27.

verses.en: Then, in the east, the bodhisattva, great being Samantabhadra (his name means “good in every way”) set out, surrounded and led by bodhisattvas, great beings, beyond all counting. The lands he passed through shook, lotuses rained down, and hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas (both huge numbers) of musical instruments played. He came with a bodhisattva's great power, a bodhisattva's great transformations, a bodhisattva's great supernatural ability, a bodhisattva's great majesty, a bodhisattva's great concentration, a bodhisattva's great blazing radiance, a bodhisattva's great vehicle, a bodhisattva's great wonders, surrounded and led by a great host of gods, nagas, yakshas, gandharvas, asuras, garudas, kinnaras, mahoragas, humans and non-humans (all kinds of beings, divine and otherwise). With such inconceivable wonders of supernatural power, the bodhisattva, great being Samantabhadra arrived in this world system.

cmp.note: samanta 是「周遍、各方面」，bhadra 是「吉祥、贤善」，合起来是「处处都好」。英文名字照梵文不译，第一次出现时加了解释；汉译「普贤」是意译，汉字读者一看就懂，英文读者只看到一串音。
cmp.en: Samanta means “all around, in every respect” and bhadra means “auspicious, good,” so together “good in every way.” The English keeps the Sanskrit name and explains it on first use; the Chinese 普贤 (Pǔxián, “universally good”) translates the meaning, so a Chinese reader understands it at a glance while an English reader sees only a string of sounds.

verses.en: He went to Vulture Peak (Gridhrakuta, the king of mountains, where the Buddha was teaching this sutra), to where the Blessed One was. When he got there, he bowed his head at the Blessed One's feet, walked around him seven times keeping him on his right, and said to the Blessed One: “Blessed One, I have come here from the buddha-field (a buddha's world) of the Blessed One Ratnatejobhyudgataraja, the Tathagata, because I heard that here, Blessed One, in this Saha world (our world of endurance), this Dharma discourse, the Lotus of the True Dharma, is being taught. I have come to the Blessed One, the Tathagata Shakyamuni, to hear it. And, Blessed One, all these hundreds of thousands of bodhisattvas have also come to hear this Dharma discourse, the Lotus of the True Dharma. So please, may the Blessed One, the Tathagata, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, teach this Dharma discourse, the Lotus of the True Dharma, to these bodhisattvas, great beings, in full.”

When he had said this, the Blessed One said to the bodhisattva, great being Samantabhadra: “Son of good family, these bodhisattvas, great beings, understand at a hint. Even so, this Dharma discourse, the Lotus of the True Dharma, is suchness (things just as they are) undivided.” The bodhisattvas said: “That is so, Blessed One. That is so, Sugata (Well-Gone One).” Then, so as to establish in the Lotus of the True Dharma the monks, nuns, laymen and laywomen who had gathered in that assembly, the Blessed One spoke again to the bodhisattva, great being Samantabhadra: “Son of good family, when a woman has four qualities, this Dharma discourse, the Lotus of the True Dharma, will come into her hands. What are the four?

cmp.note: mātṛgrāma 字面是「母亲之群」，是梵文佛经里「女人」的惯用说法。梵本这里专说女人得到这部经的条件，英文、白话都照译；鸠摩罗什改成「若善男子、善女人」，男女都包括了，还加了「于如来灭后」。
cmp.en: Mātṛgrāma literally means “the class of mothers,” the usual word for “women” in Sanskrit Buddhist texts. The Sanskrit here speaks specifically of the conditions under which a woman will receive this sutra, and both the English and the plain Chinese follow it; Kumarajiva changes it to 若善男子、善女人 (ruò shàn nánzǐ, shàn nǚrén, “if a good man or good woman”), covering both sexes, and adds “after the Tathagata's passing.”

cmp.note: tathatā 是「如此性」，即事物本来的样子，汉译「真如」；asaṃbhinna 是「未被分割、无差别」。这句鸠摩罗什本没有。英文 suchness 是佛学英文的惯用词，加了括号解释。
cmp.en: Tathatā means “thusness,” things just as they are, rendered in Chinese as 真如 (zhēnrú, “true suchness”); asaṃbhinna means “undivided, without distinction.” Kumarajiva's version lacks this sentence. “Suchness” is the standard Buddhist English term, so the English adds a brief explanation in parentheses.

verses.en: They are: she will be watched over by the buddhas, the blessed ones; she will have planted roots of goodness; she will be placed in the group that is certain (of liberation); and she will set her mind on unsurpassed, perfect awakening in order to rescue all living beings. Son of good family, when a woman has these four qualities, this Dharma discourse, the Lotus of the True Dharma, will come into her hands.”

cmp.note: 录文写的是 niraya-rāśi，字面是「地狱聚」，放在这里讲不通，应当是 niyata-rāśi「正定聚」（必定得解脱的一群）的抄误。白话、英文都按 niyata 译，鸠摩罗什的「入正定聚」也支持这个读法。
cmp.en: The transcription reads niraya-rāśi, literally “the hell group,” which makes no sense here; it is almost certainly a copying error for niyata-rāśi, “the group that is certain” (of liberation). Both the plain Chinese and the English translate it as niyata, and Kumarajiva's 入正定聚 (rù zhèngdìng jù, “enters the group certain of the right path”) supports that reading.

verses.en: Then the bodhisattva, great being Samantabhadra said to the Blessed One: “Blessed One, in the last age, the last time, when the last five hundred years are under way, I will protect monks who hold sutras like this. I will bring them blessings, keep punishment away from them, and neutralize poisons, so that no one who watches for a weak spot in these Dharma teachers, who looks for an opening, will find one. Mara the Evil One (the tempter who blocks the spiritual path) will watch for a weak spot and look for an opening and not find one; nor will Mara's sons, nor the gods of Mara's host, nor Mara's daughters, nor Mara's followers; no one will ever again be possessed by Mara. Neither gods, nor yakshas, nor hungry ghosts, nor putanas, nor krityas, nor vetalas (various kinds of demons) who watch for a weak spot in that Dharma teacher and look for an opening will find one.

cmp.note: 梵文「伺察空隙、寻找空隙」，是佛经里形容魔伺机下手的固定说法。英文 watch for a weak spot / look for an opening、白话「钻空子」都译出来了；鸠摩罗什浓缩成「伺求得其便」。
cmp.en: “Watching for an opening, searching for an opening” is a stock phrase in the sutras for Mara waiting for his chance. The English “watch for a weak spot, look for an opening” and the plain Chinese 钻空子 (zuān kòngzi, “slip through a gap”) both render it; Kumarajiva compresses it to 伺求得其便 (sìqiú dé qí biàn, “lie in wait to get their chance”).

verses.en: Blessed One, I will protect that Dharma teacher constantly, at all times. And when that Dharma teacher, absorbed in reflecting on this Dharma discourse, is walking up and down in meditation, then, Blessed One, I will mount the white king of elephants with six tusks and, surrounded by a host of bodhisattvas, come to that Dharma teacher's walking hut to guard this Dharma discourse. And if, while that Dharma teacher is absorbed in reflecting on this Dharma discourse, even a single word or syllable of it slips from his memory, then I will ride that white six-tusked king of elephants, show myself face to face to that Dharma teacher, and recite this Dharma discourse back to him complete.

cmp.note: caṃkrama 是「经行」，在一小段路上来回慢走的禅修。梵文说普贤在说法师经行时来；鸠摩罗什写「若行、若立读诵此经」，白话照梵文。
cmp.en: Caṃkrama is walking meditation, pacing slowly back and forth along a short path. The Sanskrit says Samantabhadra comes while the teacher is doing walking meditation; Kumarajiva writes 若行、若立读诵此经 (“whether walking or standing, reciting this sutra”). The English and the plain Chinese follow the Sanskrit.

verses.en: When that Dharma teacher sees my form and hears this Dharma discourse complete from me, he will be satisfied, elated, glad and delighted, full of joy and happiness, and will put even more effort into this Dharma discourse. Glad and delighted, full of joy and happiness, he will put even more effort into this Dharma discourse. And as soon as he sees me he will gain concentration, and he will gain the dharani (a power to hold everything in memory; also a spell) called Turning of Dharanis, the dharani called Hundred Thousand Kotis of Turnings, and the dharani called Turning of Skill in All Sounds.

cmp.note: 梵文是「善解一切声音之旋」，指懂得一切众生语言的能力。白话照译；鸠摩罗什作「法音方便陀罗尼」，意思偏到「法的声音」上去了。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit means “the turning of skill in all sounds,” the ability to understand the languages of all beings. The plain Chinese follows it; Kumarajiva writes 法音方便陀罗尼 (fǎyīn fāngbiàn tuóluóní, “dharani of skill in the sound of the Dharma”), shifting the sense toward “the sound of the Dharma.”

verses.en: Blessed One, in the last age, the last time, in the last five hundred years, there will be monks, nuns, laymen or laywomen who hold sutras like this, copy sutras like this, seek out sutras like this, recite sutras like this. If, in the last age, the last time, in the last five hundred years, they practice this Dharma discourse diligently in walking meditation for three weeks, twenty-one days, then I will show them my form that all beings love to see. Riding that same white six-tusked king of elephants, surrounded by a host of bodhisattvas, I will come on the twenty-first day to where those Dharma teachers do their walking meditation. And when I come, I will gladden those Dharma teachers, encourage them, inspire them and delight them.

cmp.note: 「一切众生乐见的身形」。这也是第 23 章药王菩萨前生的名字「一切众生喜见」，梵文用的是同一个词。白话、英文、鸠摩罗什都照译。
cmp.en: “A form that all beings love to see.” It is the same word as the name of the Medicine King's former self in Chapter 23, Sarvasattvapriyadarshana. The plain Chinese, the English and Kumarajiva all translate it directly.

verses.en: I will give them a dharani, so that no one will be able to harm those Dharma teachers. Neither humans nor non-humans will find an opening in them, and women will not lead them astray. I will protect them, bring them blessings, keep punishment away from them, and neutralize poisons. Blessed One, we will give those Dharma teachers these dharani phrases. Blessed One, these are the dharani phrases:

(The dharani is left untranslated, as is customary; only its sounds are given:) adaṇḍe daṇḍapati daṇḍāvartani daṇḍakuśale daṇḍasudhāri sudhārapati buddhapaśyane sarvadhāraṇi āvartani saṃvartani saṃghaparīkṣite saṃghanirghātani dharmaparīkṣite sarvasattvarutakauśalyānugate siṃhavikrīḍite anuvarte vartani vartāli svāhā.

cmp.note: 陀罗尼一般不译，只录音。这一串里有些词看得出意思，如 daṇḍa「杖、刑罚」、buddhapaśyane「见佛者」、siṃhavikrīḍite「狮子游戏」、svāhā「成就、吉祥」，但整串不是连贯的句子。鸠摩罗什用汉字音译，句数比梵本多，两本的咒文对不齐。
cmp.en: Dharanis are traditionally not translated, only transcribed. Some words in this string are recognizable, such as daṇḍa (“staff, punishment”), buddhapaśyane (“one who sees the Buddha”), siṃhavikrīḍite (“lion's play”) and svāhā (“hail, may it be so”), but the string as a whole is not a coherent sentence. Kumarajiva transliterates it with Chinese characters, and his version has more phrases than the Sanskrit, so the two spells don't line up.

verses.en: Blessed One, whichever bodhisattva, great being, these dharani phrases reach the ear of, it should be known that this is the empowering blessing of the bodhisattva, great being Samantabhadra.

And, Blessed One, as this Dharma discourse, the Lotus of the True Dharma, circulates in this Jambudvipa (the continent we live on, that is, the human world), whichever bodhisattvas, great beings, it comes into the hands of, those Dharma teachers, Blessed One, should understand: 'It is through the power of the bodhisattva, great being Samantabhadra, through the radiance of the bodhisattva, great being Samantabhadra, that this Dharma discourse has come into our hands.' Blessed One, those beings will have a share in the practice of the bodhisattva, great being Samantabhadra. Those beings will have planted roots of goodness with many buddhas. And, Blessed One, those beings will have their heads stroked by the Tathagata's hand. Blessed One, those who copy and hold this sutra will have done something that pleases me.

cmp.note: 「头顶被如来的手抚摸过的」。第 28 章开头，梵文是佛握菩萨的手，鸠摩罗什译成摩顶；这里梵文本身就是「摩顶」，三种译法一致。
cmp.en: “Whose heads have been stroked by the Tathagata's hand.” At the start of Chapter 28 the Sanskrit has the Buddha clasp the bodhisattvas' hands where Kumarajiva has him stroke their heads; here the Sanskrit itself speaks of head-stroking, and all three versions agree.

verses.en: Those who copy this sutra and understand its meaning, Blessed One, will, after copying this sutra and passing away from here, be reborn among the gods of the Thirty-Three (a heaven on the summit of Mount Meru). As soon as they are reborn, eighty-four thousand celestial maidens (apsarases) will come to them. Those sons of the gods will stand among those maidens wearing crowns as big as drums. Sons of good family, such is the mass of merit from copying this Dharma discourse alone. How much more for those who teach it, recite it, reflect on it and take it to heart! So, sons of good family, this Dharma discourse, the Lotus of the True Dharma, should be copied with respect and with full attention.

cmp.note: 「像鼓一样大的冠」。白话照译；鸠摩罗什作「七宝冠」，把大小换成了材质。英文照梵文。
cmp.en: “With a crown the size of a drum.” The plain Chinese follows this; Kumarajiva writes 七宝冠 (qībǎo guān, “a crown of the seven precious substances”), trading size for material. The English follows the Sanskrit.

verses.en: Whoever copies it with undistracted attention, a thousand buddhas will reach out a hand to him, and at the time of his death a thousand buddhas will appear before him face to face. He will not go to a bad destiny or a fall into lower realms. Passing away from here, he will be reborn among the Tushita gods (the heaven where Maitreya lives), where the bodhisattva, great being Maitreya (the bodhisattva who will be the next buddha) dwells, with the thirty-two marks of excellence, surrounded by a host of bodhisattvas and attended by hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas of celestial maidens, teaching the Dharma. So, sons of good family, a wise son or daughter of good family should copy this Dharma discourse, the Lotus of the True Dharma, with respect, teach it with respect, recite it with respect and take it to heart with respect.

Sons of good family, by copying this Dharma discourse, teaching it, reciting it, cultivating it and taking it to heart, one will have such immeasurable good qualities. So, Blessed One, a wise son or daughter of good family should hold this Dharma discourse, the Lotus of the True Dharma; that is how great its benefits will be. And so, Blessed One, I too will empower this Dharma discourse, so that through my empowering blessing, Blessed One, this Dharma discourse will circulate in this Jambudvipa.”

cmp.note: adhiṣṭhāna 是佛菩萨以自己的力量「站在背后撑着」，汉译「加持」。英文没有现成的词，这里用 empower 加 empowering blessing。鸠摩罗什作「以神通力故，守护是经」。
cmp.en: Adhiṣṭhāna is a buddha's or bodhisattva's power “standing behind” something and sustaining it, rendered in Chinese as 加持 (jiāchí, “adding support”). English has no ready word, so the translation uses “empower” and “empowering blessing.” Kumarajiva writes 以神通力故，守护是经 (“by my supernatural power, I will guard this sutra”).

verses.en: Then, at that moment, the Blessed One, Shakyamuni, the Tathagata, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, applauded the bodhisattva, great being Samantabhadra: “Well done, well done, Samantabhadra! You have set out to act like this for the good of many people, for the happiness of many people, out of compassion for the world, for the welfare, good and happiness of a great multitude. You have such inconceivable qualities, with a resolve held by great compassion and an aspiration held by the inconceivable, that you yourself give your empowering blessing to those Dharma teachers. Sons of good family, whoever holds the name of the bodhisattva, great being Samantabhadra should know that they have seen the Tathagata Shakyamuni, and that they have heard this Dharma discourse, the Lotus of the True Dharma, from the Blessed One Shakyamuni himself.

cmp.note: 梵文说受持「普贤名号」的人等于见过释迦牟尼。鸠摩罗什把这两件事分开：「守护能受持普贤菩萨名者」，而「见释迦牟尼佛」的是受持、读诵、书写《法华经》的人。白话、英文照梵文。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says that those who hold “Samantabhadra's name” have in effect seen Shakyamuni. Kumarajiva splits this in two: the Buddha will protect those who hold Samantabhadra's name, while it is those who hold, recite and copy the Lotus Sutra who 见释迦牟尼佛 (jiàn Shìjiāmóuní fó, “see Shakyamuni Buddha”). The plain Chinese and the English follow the Sanskrit.

verses.en: They have honored the Tathagata Shakyamuni with offerings. They have applauded the Tathagata Shakyamuni as he taught the Dharma. They will rejoice in this Dharma discourse, the Tathagata Shakyamuni will lay his hand on their heads, and the Blessed One Shakyamuni will cover them with his robes. Samantabhadra, these sons and daughters of good family should be known as people who uphold the Tathagata's teaching. They will have no taste for Lokayata (the materialist school that trusts only this world and the senses), they will not care for people who spend their lives on poetry, nor for dancers, wrestlers, actors, liquor sellers, sheep butchers, poultry dealers, pig butchers or pimps. Once they have heard, copied, held or recited sutras like this, nothing else will appeal to them.

cmp.note: 这几个词指以羊、鸡、猪为业的人，在印度通常是屠宰贩卖牲畜的行业，所以被列为不宜亲近。白话译「养羊的、养鸡的、养猪的」，听起来像普通农户；英文译成 butchers / dealers，鸠摩罗什也写「屠儿、畜猪羊鸡狗」。
cmp.en: These words refer to people who make a living from sheep, chickens and pigs, in India usually the trades of slaughtering and selling livestock, which is why they are listed as people to keep away from. The plain Chinese 养羊的、养鸡的、养猪的 (“people who raise sheep, chickens, pigs”) sounds like ordinary farmers; the English uses “butchers” and “dealers,” and Kumarajiva likewise writes 屠儿 (túr, “butchers”).

verses.en: These beings should be known as people who live by their own true nature. They will think things through properly, each in their own heart. They will rely on the strength of their own merit, and living beings will love to see them. Monks who hold sutras like this will not be troubled by greed, nor by hatred, delusion, envy, stinginess, hypocrisy, pride, conceit or false pride. Samantabhadra, these Dharma teachers will be content with what they receive.

cmp.note: 字面「具备自性之法的」，意思不很确定，大约是「本性正直、天然有德」。白话「具备本性之法」照字面；英文取 live by their own true nature；鸠摩罗什作「心意质直」，是意译。
cmp.en: Literally “endowed with the dharma of their own nature”; the meaning is not quite certain, perhaps “upright by nature, naturally virtuous.” The plain Chinese 具备本性之法 (“endowed with the law of their own nature”) stays literal; the English takes it as “live by their own true nature”; Kumarajiva paraphrases as 心意质直 (xīnyì zhízhí, “straightforward in mind”).

verses.en: Samantabhadra, in the last age, the last time, when the last five hundred years are under way, whoever sees a monk who holds this Dharma discourse, the Lotus of the True Dharma, should think: 'This son of good family will go to the seat of awakening. This son of good family will defeat the wheel of Mara's dark army. He will turn the wheel of the Dharma, beat the drum of the Dharma, blow the conch of the Dharma, rain down the rain of the Dharma, and mount the lion throne of the Dharma.' Monks who hold this Dharma discourse in the last age, the last time, when the last five hundred years are under way, will not be greedy; they will not crave robes or bowls. Those Dharma teachers will be straightforward.

cmp.note: kali 是「争斗、恶运」，kalicakra 是「争斗之轮」，指魔的军阵。白话「魔的军阵」、英文 wheel of Mara's dark army 都是意译；鸠摩罗什作「破诸魔众」。
cmp.en: Kali means “strife, ill luck,” and kalicakra is “the wheel of strife,” meaning Mara's battle array. The plain Chinese 魔的军阵 (mó de jūnzhèn, “Mara's battle lines”) and the English “wheel of Mara's dark army” both interpret; Kumarajiva writes 破诸魔众 (“defeat the hosts of Mara”).

verses.en: Those Dharma teachers will obtain the three gates of liberation (emptiness, signlessness and wishlessness), and will see results in this very life (meaning partly unclear). Those who lead astray monks who are Dharma teachers holding sutras like this will be born blind. Those who spread ill reports about monks who hold sutras like this will have blotched skin in this very life. Those who jeer at and mock people who copy sutras like this will have broken teeth and gappy teeth, ugly lips, flat noses, twisted hands and feet, crossed eyes, foul-smelling bodies, and bodies covered with boils, pustules, scabs, ringworm and itch.

cmp.note: 字面是「他们的现世之事将会转回/止息」，确切意思不明。白话「在现世就会得到回报」是跟着鸠摩罗什「亦于现世得其福报」来理解的；英文同样这样译，但标了意思不全明。
cmp.en: Literally “what belongs to this present life will turn back / cease for them”; the exact meaning is unclear. The plain Chinese 在现世就会得到回报 (“will be rewarded in this life”) follows Kumarajiva's 亦于现世得其福报 (“also receives blessings in this present life”); the English reads it the same way but marks it as partly unclear.

cmp.note: 字面「给予愚痴」，可以是「蒙蔽、欺骗」，也可以是「说他们愚痴」。白话取「蒙蔽」，英文 lead astray 意思相近；鸠摩罗什写的是骂他们「汝狂人耳」，更接近后一种读法。
cmp.en: Literally “give delusion,” which can mean “deceive, mislead” or “call them deluded.” The plain Chinese takes 蒙蔽 (méngbì, “deceive”) and the English “lead astray” is close to it; Kumarajiva has people abuse them with 汝狂人耳 (“you're just a madman”), closer to the second reading.

verses.en: Those who say unkind things, true or false, about people who copy sutras like this, recite sutras like this, hold sutras like this and teach sutras like this, should know that this is an even heavier bad karma. So, Samantabhadra, when you see from far away monks who hold this Dharma discourse, you should rise to meet them. The reverence you would show in the presence of the Tathagata is the reverence you should show these monks who hold this sutra.”

While this chapter, Samantabhadra's Encouragement, was being taught, bodhisattvas, great beings, as many as the grains of sand in the Ganges River gained the dharani called Hundred Thousand Kotis of Turnings.
Here ends the twenty-sixth chapter, called “Samantabhadra's Encouragement,” in the glorious Dharma discourse of the Lotus of the True Dharma.

cmp.note: 梵本把这一品算作第二十六品，本站算第 27 章；鸠摩罗什本这是最后一品（第二十八品），所以他的经末总结「一切大会，皆大欢喜，作礼而去」放在这里，梵本的这类结尾则在下一章「嘱累品」末尾。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit counts this as the twenty-sixth chapter; this site counts it as Chapter 27. In Kumarajiva's version it is the last chapter (the twenty-eighth), so his closing line for the whole sutra, 一切大会，皆大欢喜，作礼而去 (“the whole great assembly rejoiced, bowed, and departed”), comes here, whereas the Sanskrit's equivalent closing comes at the end of the next chapter, “The Entrusting.”

verses.en: Then the Blessed One, Shakyamuni, the Tathagata, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, rose from his Dharma seat. He gathered all those bodhisattvas together and, with a right hand brought into being by his supernatural power, took hold of their right hands, and at that moment said: “Sons of good family, this unsurpassed, perfect awakening, which I gathered over countless hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas of eons (kotis and nayutas are both huge numbers), I now place in your hands. I hand it over, I hand it on, I lay it down with you, I leave it in your keeping. Sons of good family, you must make it spread far and wide.”

cmp.note: 梵文是佛用右手「握住」菩萨们的右手，像郑重地把东西交到对方手里。英文、白话都照译；鸠摩罗什译成「以右手摩无量菩萨摩诃萨顶」，变成摸顶，这是汉传佛教里「摩顶授记」最熟悉的画面，和梵文的握手不同。
cmp.en: In the Sanskrit the Buddha takes hold of the bodhisattvas' right hands with his own right hand, like solemnly placing something into someone's hands. The English and the plain Chinese follow this; Kumarajiva writes 以右手摩无量菩萨摩诃萨顶 (yǐ yòushǒu mó wúliàng púsà móhēsà dǐng, “with his right hand stroked the crowns of the heads of countless bodhisattvas”), the head-touching gesture so familiar in Chinese Buddhism, which is a different picture from the handclasp.

cmp.note: 梵文连用四个近义动词「交付、转交、放下、寄存」，层层加重。英文用四个短句保留了叠用的语气；鸠摩罗什只用一个「付嘱」，这一品的汉名「嘱累」就从这里来。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit piles up four near-synonymous verbs, “hand over, hand on, lay down, deposit,” each adding weight. The English keeps the repetition with four short clauses; Kumarajiva uses a single 付嘱 (fùzhǔ, “entrust”), which is where the Chinese chapter name 嘱累 (zhǔlěi, “entrusting”) comes from.

verses.en: A second time and a third time, the Blessed One took hold of the whole assembly of bodhisattvas with his right hand and said: “Sons of good family, this unsurpassed, perfect awakening, which I gathered over countless hundreds of thousands of kotis of nayutas of eons, I now place in your hands. I hand it over, I hand it on, I lay it down with you, I leave it in your keeping. Sons of good family, you must take it up, hold on to it, recite it, master it, teach it and make it clear, and let all living beings hear it. Sons of good family, I am not stingy. My mind clings to nothing, I am without fear, and I am a giver of the buddha-knowledge, a giver of the Tathagata's knowledge, the self-arisen knowledge (knowledge that arises on its own, without a teacher). Sons of good family, I am a great lord of giving. Sons of good family, you too should learn from me and do the same.

cmp.note: dānapati 字面是「布施之主」，指出钱供养的大施主。佛在这里拿世俗的施主自比，说他施舍的是智慧。英文 great lord of giving、白话「伟大的施主」都保留了这个比喻；鸠摩罗什加了「如来有大慈悲」，梵文这里没有「慈悲」。
cmp.en: Dānapati literally means “lord of giving,” the wealthy patron who funds offerings. The Buddha compares himself to such a patron, except that what he gives is knowledge. The English “great lord of giving” and the plain Chinese 伟大的施主 (wěidà de shīzhǔ, “great donor”) keep the comparison; Kumarajiva adds 如来有大慈悲 (“the Tathagata has great compassion”), and “compassion” is not in the Sanskrit here.

verses.en: “Free of stinginess, you should let the sons and daughters of good family who come to you hear this Dharma discourse, this knowledge and vision of the Tathagata, this great skillful means. And living beings who have no faith should be encouraged to take up this Dharma discourse. Sons of good family, by doing this you will have repaid the Tathagatas.”

cmp.w: ye ca aśrāddhāḥ sattvāste 'smin dharmaparyāye samādāpayitavyāḥ
cmp.note: 梵文说：对没有信心的人，也要劝他们接受「这部」法门。鸠摩罗什的说法相反：不信这部经的人，「当于如来余深法中，示教利喜」，也就是改用如来别的深法去教。英文、白话照梵文。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says that even people without faith should be encouraged to take up “this” Dharma discourse. Kumarajiva says the opposite: those who don't accept this sutra should be taught 于如来余深法中 (yú rúlái yú shēn fǎ zhōng, “through the Tathagata's other profound teachings”). The English and the plain Chinese follow the Sanskrit.

verses.en: When the Blessed One, Shakyamuni, the Tathagata, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, had said this, those bodhisattvas, great beings, were flooded with great joy and delight. Filled with deep reverence, they bowed toward the Blessed One Shakyamuni, the Tathagata, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha: they bent their bodies, bowed their bodies, lowered their bodies, bowed their heads, and with palms joined they all said to him with one voice: “Blessed One, we will do just as the Tathagata commands. We will carry out the commands of all the Tathagatas and fulfill them. Let the Blessed One have no worry, and live at ease as he pleases.” A second time and a third time the whole assembly of bodhisattvas said with one voice: “Let the Blessed One have no worry, and live at ease as he pleases.

cmp.note: alpotsuka 字面是「少操心的」，是请对方放下心来的客气话。英文 have no worry、白话「不要挂心」、鸠摩罗什「愿不有虑」意思一致。
cmp.en: Alpotsuka literally means “of little concern,” a polite way of asking someone to set their mind at rest. The English “have no worry,” the plain Chinese 不要挂心 (búyào guàxīn, “don't be anxious”), and Kumarajiva's 愿不有虑 (yuàn bù yǒu lǜ, “may you have no worry”) all agree.

verses.en: Blessed One, we will do just as the Tathagata commands. We will fulfill the commands of all the Tathagatas.”

Then the Blessed One, Shakyamuni, the Tathagata, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, sent off all the Tathagatas, arhats, fully awakened buddhas who had come from other world systems, and wished those Tathagatas well, saying: “May the Tathagatas, arhats, fully awakened buddhas, live at ease as they please.” He set the jeweled stupa of the Blessed One Prabhutaratna, the Tathagata, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha, back in its place, and wished that Tathagata, too, to live at ease as he pleased.

cmp.note: 梵文只说这些如来「从其他世界来」。鸠摩罗什写成「十方来诸分身佛」，明说他们是释迦牟尼的分身（见第 12 章），梵文这里没有「分身」二字。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit says only that these Tathagatas “had come from other world systems.” Kumarajiva writes 十方来诸分身佛 (shífāng lái zhū fēnshēn fó, “the emanation buddhas who came from the ten directions”), stating outright that they are Shakyamuni's own emanations (see Chapter 12); the word “emanation” is not in the Sanskrit here.

verses.en: This is what the Blessed One said, with a glad heart. And the immeasurable, countless Tathagatas, arhats, fully awakened buddhas who had come from other world systems and were seated on lion thrones at the feet of jeweled trees; and Prabhutaratna, the Tathagata, the arhat, the fully awakened buddha; and the whole assembly of bodhisattvas; and the immeasurable, countless bodhisattvas, great beings, led by Vishishtacharitra, who had risen up out of the cracks in the earth; and the great disciples; and the four assemblies (monks, nuns, laymen and laywomen); and the world with its gods, humans, asuras and gandharvas, all rejoiced at what the Blessed One had said.
Here ends the twenty-seventh chapter, called “The Entrusting,” in the glorious Dharma discourse of the Lotus of the True Dharma.

cmp.note: 梵本把这一品算作第二十七品，本站算第 28 章（本站第 1 章是开经，又把提婆达多品并入第 12 章）。梵本里「嘱累品」放在全经最后；鸠摩罗什本则放在第二十二品，后面还有药王、妙音、普门等六品。
cmp.en: The Sanskrit counts this as the twenty-seventh chapter; this site counts it as Chapter 28 (the site's Chapter 1 is an opening section, and the Devadatta chapter is merged into Chapter 12). In the Sanskrit, “The Entrusting” comes at the very end of the sutra; in Kumarajiva's version it is chapter 22, followed by six more chapters, including the Medicine King, Wonderful Sound and Avalokiteshvara chapters.

verses.en: Of all things that arise from a cause, the Tathagata has told the cause, and also how they cease. This is what the great renunciant teaches.

cmp.note: 这首偈不是《法华经》本文，是抄经人常附在经末的「缘起偈」，相传舍利弗就是听了这首偈而出家的。鸠摩罗什本没有。śramaṇa 是出家修行者，白话「大沙门」、英文 great renunciant 都是在译这个词。
cmp.en: This verse is not part of the Lotus Sutra itself; it is the “verse of dependent arising” that copyists often added at the end of a scripture, and tradition says it was on hearing this verse that Shariputra left home. Kumarajiva's version doesn't have it. Śramaṇa means a wandering renunciant; the plain Chinese 大沙门 (dà shāmén, “great shramana”) and the English “great renunciant” both render that word.
